title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試錄序
上萬曆之十年四川當論秀士於
鄉巡按御史宋〔仕〕秉憲度而
監臨之兢兢翼翼如也先是
馳檄徵四方文學博士至則
以〔應科〕及教諭戴〔震亨〕司考
試教諭湯〔欽聞〕王〔顯先〕張〔道〕
===
〔深〕訓導李〔輿杜〕孫〔紀〕吳〔中禎〕
〔章〕司同考試提調則左布
政使蔡〔汝賢〕右叅議萬〔一貫〕
監試則按察使鄭〔旻〕副使范
〔崙〕百執事慎簡惟其人比入
闈御史申㦤要束矢精白以
從事諰諰懇懇如也於是進
punctuated:
四川鄉試錄序
上萬曆之十年，四川當論秀士於鄉。巡按御史宋〔仕〕秉憲度而監臨之，兢兢翼翼如也。先是，馳檄徵四方文學博士，至則以〔應科〕及教諭戴〔震亨〕司考試，教諭湯〔欽聞〕、王〔顯先〕、張〔道深〕，訓導李〔輿杜〕、孫〔紀〕、吳〔中禎〕、〔章〕司同考試。提調則左布政使蔡〔汝賢〕、右叅議萬〔一貫〕，監試則按察使鄭〔旻〕、副使范〔崙〕，百執事慎簡惟其人。比入闈，御史申㦤要束，矢精白以從事，諰諰懇懇如也。於是進
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

In the tenth year of the Wanli reign of His Majesty (1582), Sichuan was due to evaluate and select cultivated talents in the Provincial Examination. Regional Inspector Censor Song Shi 宋仕 upheld the constitutional norms and served as Supervising Official over it, acting with the utmost caution and reverence. Prior to this, dispatches had been sent out by courier to summon erudite instructors of literature from all quarters. Upon their arrival, I, Yingke 應科, together with Instructor Dai Zhenheng 戴震亨, were appointed to take charge as Examiners; Instructors Tang Qinwen 湯欽聞, Wang Xianxian 王顯先, and Zhang Daoshen 張道深, along with Assistant Instructors Li Yudu 李輿杜, Sun Ji 孫紀, Wu Zhongzhen 吳中禎, and [?] Zhang 章 [?], were appointed to take charge as Associate Examiners. As for the Proctors, they were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Cai Ruxian 蔡汝賢 and Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Wan Yiguan 萬一貫; as for the Surveillance Officials of the Examination, they were Surveillance Commissioner Zheng Min 鄭旻 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Fan Lun 范崙; and for all the various functionaries, only the right men were carefully selected. When the time came to enter the examination compound, the Censor reiterated his admirable regulations and restraints, and all swore an oath to carry out their duties with pure integrity, acting with earnestness and scrupulous care. Thereupon, there were brought forward…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
提學副使楊〔節〕今署提學事
左叅議王〔儱祥〕先後所選士
二千有奇三試之得儁者七
十人詩鹿鳴而賓興之濟濟
顒顒如也士當籍
奏〔應科〕不佞宜首颺言以諗諸
士始〔應科〕讀上林甘泉之賦
緬焉慕之以爲蜀士翩翩文
章鉅麗雖其人之贍辭哉儻
亦山川奇秀之助乎而無從
覯之也頃幸而攬名都之勝
岷峨表其鎮大江濬其源是
帝以會昌而神聖所爲鍾毓也扶
輿淳淑之氣洋洋乎攸萃矣
punctuated:
提學副使楊〔節〕、今署提學事左叅議王〔儱祥〕先後所選士二千有奇，三試之，得儁者七十人，詩《鹿鳴》而賓興之，濟濟顒顒如也。士當籍奏，〔應科〕不佞，宜首颺言以諗諸士。
始〔應科〕讀《上林》、《甘泉》之賦，緬焉慕之，以爲蜀士翩翩，文章鉅麗，雖其人之贍辭哉，儻亦山川奇秀之助乎？而無從覯之也。頃幸而攬名都之勝，岷、峨表其鎮，大江濬其源，是帝以會昌，而神聖所爲鍾毓也，扶輿淳淑之氣，洋洋乎攸萃矣。
translation_en:
… the more than two thousand scholars successively selected by the Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education Yang Jie 楊節 and the Left Assistant Administration Commissioner presently acting as Education Intendant Wang Longxiang 王儱祥 [?], and tested them in three sessions, obtaining seventy men of outstanding talent. We chanted the ode "Deer Cry" (Luming) and raised them up as honored guests; how numerosos, dignified, and reverent they were! Now that the roster of scholars is to be presented to the throne, I, Yingke 應科, though untalented, ought to be the first to offer words of counsel to the scholars.

Previously, when I, Yingke, read the rhapsodies on the Shanglin Park and the Ganquan Palace, I admired them from afar, thinking how refined were the scholars of Shu (Sichuan) and how grand and magnificent their writings! Even if this was due to the rich eloquence of the men themselves, might it not also have been aided by the wondrous beauty of their mountains and rivers? Yet I had no way to witness it in person. Recently, I have had the good fortune to take in the scenic splendors of this famed metropolis, where Mount Min and Mount Emei stand forth as its guardian peaks and the Great River (Yangzi) dredges its source. This is whereby the Sovereign meets with flourishing fortune and what the sacred and divine have concentrated and nurtured; the pure, auspicious vital energy (qi) of the cosmos is gathered here in vast abundance!

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
既有事校𢎥則又瞿然嘆蜀
士本實醲粹不第扶疎於枝
葉信斌斌兼有其質文焉而
嚮之豔慕卿雲爲黼黻河漢
者曾未睹大方之全也
本朝用經術取士士斟酌道德
之淵源以效諸實旣其稍渝
===
則有繡鞶悅剽諸子百家以
炫衆驚愚者蜀人士顧獨斤
斤先民是程蓋其愼也邇歲
明詔沛然屢下匠鑄文體歸之雅
正海內操觚之徒意製騁馳
猶然躍溢於治而今諸士之
業則皆規摹矱矩允哉知言
punctuated: 既有事校𢎥，則又瞿然嘆蜀士本實醲粹，不第扶疎於枝葉，信斌斌兼有其質文焉。而嚮之豔慕卿、雲爲黼黻河漢者，曾未睹大方之全也。本朝用經術取士，士斟酌道德之淵源，以效諸實。旣其稍渝，則有繡鞶悅，剽諸子百家以炫衆驚愚者。蜀人士顧獨斤斤先民是程，蓋其愼也。邇歲明詔沛然屢下，匠鑄文體，歸之雅正。海內操觚之徒，意製騁馳，猶然躍溢於治；而今諸士之業，則皆規摹矱矩，允哉知言…
translation_en:
Once I became engaged in grading the examination papers, I marveled in astonishment at how the scholars of Shu are fundamentally solid, rich, and pure—not merely luxuriant in branches and leaves, but truly possessing a harmonious balance of both substance and refinement. My earlier envious admiration of Sima Xiangru 司馬相如 and Yang Xiong 揚雄 as embroidered ceremonial robes or the Milky Way had never glimpsed the entirety of their great accomplishment.

Our dynasty selects scholars through the study of the Classics, and scholars draw upon the fountainheads of morality and virtue to apply them to practical realities. Once this standard slightly deteriorated, there arose those who embroidered belt-pouches and kerchiefs [i.e., engaged in petty, ornate writing], plagiarizing the Various Masters and Hundred Schools to dazzle the crowd and startle the ignorant. Yet the scholars of Shu alone remained scrupulously attentive, taking the ancients as their model—such is their prudence. In recent years, the enlightened imperial decrees have been abundantly issued time and again, forging and molding literary style to return it to elegance and correctness. Throughout the realm, those who wield the writing tablet let their conceptions and compositions gallop unrestrained, still leaping and overflowing out of the mold; yet the essays of the scholars here today all conform to compass and square—truly the selection of those who understand words…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
之選已非夫乘
昌會而濟聖眞也抑何其涵煦
純懿靡然顧化之捷如此哉且非
獨於辭也馬之探前趹後蹄
間三尋者非梁益所産也乃
江源龍湖之種步驟中繩無
佚銜轡者多有冰紈霧縠文
犀翠翰明璣紫貝蜀鮮稱哉
而深山長谷楩柟松栢往往
勝
===
廟堂之棟幹唯士亦然今天下儆
儻異倫秀蔚有美者奚譆至
足要以小心奉法樸茂良實
稱任使蜀人士亦有足多者
punctuated: 之選已。非夫乘昌會而濟聖眞也，抑何其涵煦純懿、靡然顧化之捷如此哉！且非獨於辭也。馬之探前趹後、蹄間三尋者，非梁、益所産也；乃江源、龍湖之種，步驟中繩、無佚銜轡者多有。冰紈霧縠、文犀翠翰、明璣紫貝，蜀鮮稱哉；而深山長谷，楩柟松栢，往往勝廟堂之棟幹。唯士亦然。今天下儆儻異倫、秀蔚有美者，奚譆至足；要以小心奉法、樸茂良實、稱任使，蜀人士亦有足多者
translation_en: …a selection of [those who truly know words]. Were it not for taking advantage of this prosperous epoch to aid the sagely truth, how else could their being nurtured in pure excellence and bending with the wind toward transformation be as swift as this! Moreover, this is not true of literary expression alone. Horses that stretch forward and kick backward, covering three xun in a single stride, are not produced in Liang and Yi [Sichuan]; yet among the breeds of Jiangyuan and Longhu, there are many whose paces conform to the marking-line and that never throw off bit and bridle. Ice-white silk and mist-fine gauze, patterned rhinoceros horn and kingfisher plumes, bright pearls and purple cowries—Sichuan is rarely praised for these; yet in its deep mountains and long valleys, the pian, nan, pine, and cypress trees are often equal to serving as ridgepoles and pillars for the imperial court. And so it is with scholars as well. In the empire today, those who are extraordinary and peerless, flourishing and refined in beauty, are indeed abundant enough [?]; yet in essence, when it comes to upholding the laws with careful circumspection, being simple, substantial, upright, and sincere, and proving equal to official commissions, the scholars and gentlemen of Sichuan also have much to be commended for…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
焉前代無論焉耳
高皇帝天造草昧劉文成爲帷幄
子房而蚤授妙略以垂開濟
之勳者非蜀士也乎
文皇帝鼎建鴻基總銓衡之任而
謀謩太平者又蜀士也
肅皇帝中興景運首鉉台而斧藻
===
維新之化者又蜀士也蓋至
于今而炯聲茂實表樹
當世者軏躅相望此亦足明士適
用之效已且夫二三君子所
謂鉅儒元工故皆繇縫掖起
而諸士鳩山川之靈粹比肩
聯翩而興於
punctuated: 焉。前代無論焉耳。高皇帝天造草昧，劉文成爲帷幄子房，而蚤授妙略以垂開濟之勳者，非蜀士也乎？文皇帝鼎建鴻基，總銓衡之任而謀謩太平者，又蜀士也。肅皇帝中興景運，首鉉台而斧藻維新之化者，又蜀士也。蓋至于今，而炯聲茂實表樹當世者，軏躅相望，此亦足明士適用之效已。且夫二三君子，所謂鉅儒元工，故皆繇縫掖起，而諸士鳩山川之靈粹，比肩聯翩而興於
translation_en: … therein. Not to mention previous dynasties, when the August Emperor [Taizu] created the empire out of chaos, while Liu Wencheng [Liu Ji 劉基] served as the Zifang [Zhang Liang 張良] inside the command tent, was not the one who early on imparted wondrous strategies to leave behind merits of founding and ordering the realm [i.e., Wang Guangyang 汪廣洋 or Daotong 道同 /趙汸/王克己/韓成/or rather Ba Yu / Sichuan scholar like Yang/etc. — literally: a scholar of Shu] a scholar of Shu? When the Cultured Emperor [Chengzu] established the great foundation, the one who took overall charge of the responsibility of personnel selection and evaluation [Minister of Personnel, i.e., Jian Yi 蹇義] and planned for grand peace was again a scholar of Shu. When the Reverent Emperor [Shizong] revived the glorious destiny in a dynastic restoration, the one who headed the Grand Secretariat [i.e., Yang Tinghe 楊廷和] and adorned the transformative rule of renewal was again a scholar of Shu. Down to the present day, those with brilliant reputations and flourishing achievements who stand out as models in the current age follow closely in one another's wheel-tracks in unbroken succession; this too suffices to demonstrate the efficacy of scholars being suited for practical use. Moreover, those two or three gentlemen, the so-called great Confucians and premier statesmen, all originally rose from the ranks of humble scholars in wide-sleeved robes. Now all you scholars gather the numinous essence of the mountains and rivers, standing shoulder to shoulder and rising in succession at…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
文明之旦寧渠無傑然自期許以
前哲者哉〔應科〕誠望之矣不
聞賢者在治其若鳳乎止則
梧棲而竹食飛則翽羽而喈
鳴故處奥濮而稱良士則學
有檢押必不爲雕蔓離奇以
詭正資適逢時而稱良臣則
===
業有衡量必不爲駘蕩儇巧
以踰節夫爲臣者亦奚以加
于士哉直取居平所誦法設
誠致行之道如是足也諸士
醇脩而敏迪徵諸辭華實相
章則信乎蜀之良也已方將
濯清流翔天衢耀
punctuated: 文明之旦，寧渠無傑然自期許以前哲者哉？〔應科〕誠望之矣。不聞賢者在治，其若鳳乎？止則梧棲而竹食，飛則翽羽而喈鳴。故處奥濮而稱良士，則學有檢押，必不爲雕蔓離奇以詭正；資適逢時而稱良臣，則業有衡量，必不爲駘蕩儇巧以踰節。夫爲臣者，亦奚以加于士哉？直取居平所誦法，設誠致行之道，如是足也。諸士醇脩而敏迪，徵諸辭，華實相章，則信乎蜀之良也已！方將濯清流、翔天衢，耀
translation_en: … the dawn of an enlightened era, how could there be none among them who stand out in holding themselves to the standard of those former worthies? I, [Yingke], truly hope for this. Have you not heard that a worthy man in an age of good governance is like the phoenix? When at rest, it roosts in the parasol tree and feeds on bamboo seed; when in flight, its wings rustle and its cry rings out harmoniously. Therefore, when one dwells in a secluded corner [?] by the Pu River and is praised as a fine scholar, his learning is governed by discipline and restraint, and he will certainly not engage in ornate, sprawling, or bizarre compositions that deviate from orthodoxy; when one's talents happen to meet the right time and he is praised as a fine minister, his achievements are guided by due measure, and he will certainly not engage in dissolute, lax, or slickly clever conduct that oversteps the bounds of propriety. How, indeed, does being a minister add anything beyond what is already in the scholar? It is simply a matter of taking the principles that one has ordinarily recited and modeled oneself upon, establishing sincerity, and putting them into practice—that much is sufficient. You scholars cultivate yourselves with purity and advance swiftly in understanding; as evidenced in your writings, literary elegance and solid substance mutually illuminate one another, so you are truly the finest talents of Shu! You are just about to bathe in the clear stream, soar along the heavenly thoroughfare, and shine in …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
日月之末光以展寀錯事殫精悉
忠激卬名世之烈斯自雅志
素所蓄也其何讓哉雖然〔應科〕
懔懔懼焉周地賤媒非謂
其爲訑而偏於譽耶今主司
於諸士之升輒津津曰良士
良士誠中心愛之信之猶列
===
眉乃不量其譽之過也太阿
剖犁觀者神竦燕石緹緗客
乃盧胡士或索之實而無益
主上之理與今所稱詡相繆盩則
安歸責乎諸士朂矣脩爾邦
人之素毋異趣以爲高寧範
我馳驅毋詭遇而關入以捷
punctuated: 日月之末光，以展寀錯事，殫精悉忠，激卬名世之烈，斯自雅志素所蓄也，其何讓哉？雖然，〔應科〕懔懔懼焉。周地賤媒，非謂其爲訑而偏於譽耶？今主司於諸士之升，輒津津曰：「良士，良士。」誠中心愛之、信之，猶列眉，乃不量其譽之過也。太阿剖犁，觀者神竦；燕石緹緗，客乃盧胡。士或索之實而無益主上之理，與今所稱詡相繆盩，則安歸責乎？諸士朂矣！脩爾邦人之素，毋異趣以爲高；寧範我馳驅，毋詭遇而關入以捷；
translation_en: … the faintest rays of the sun and moon, so as to assume official duties and manage affairs, exhausting your energies and giving your utmost loyalty, roused to achieve accomplishments famed throughout the age—this is naturally what you have long cherished in your lofty ambitions; why then should you yield to anyone? Even so, I, Yingke, am filled with awe and trepidation. Among the officials of the Rites of Zhou, the Matchmaker (Dijian, "Earth's Lowly") was held in low esteem—was this not because he was given to boastful exaggeration and partiality in his praise? Now, as the examiners promote you gentlemen, we cannot help exclaiming with delight: "Fine scholars! Fine scholars!" Truly, from the bottom of our hearts we cherish and trust you, as clearly as seeing the eyebrows lined up on a face, and so we do not stop to measure whether our praise may be excessive. When the great sword Tai'e slices through a calf, onlookers are struck with awe; when a mere stone from Yan is wrapped in fine orange and yellow silk, the guest covers his mouth and laughs. Should a scholar, when tested for substance, prove of no benefit to His Majesty's governance, contradicting what we now so warmly extol, then upon whom will the blame fall? Exert yourselves, gentlemen! Cultivate the longstanding virtues of the worthy men of your native land, and do not pursue aberrant paths in a bid to appear lofty. Rather drive your chariot strictly according to the rules than resort to devious intercepts and illicit entry for the sake of a quick…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
寧爲楩柟松栢需其成于久
大毋若譁嚚之玩取衒目睫
庶幾哉前哲可企以爲爾山
川重而主司竊徼榮附於以
人事
君追訑者之誚幸矣夫語有之信
言不華凡〔應科〕所切磋度諸
士能行者具以質告亦猶以
奉
===
明詔也毋姍曰卑卑無甚高論哉
是舉也巡撫右副都御史今
陞吏部右侍郎候代張〔士佩〕
飭治經文聲敎布濩巡撫貴
州兼督湖北川東右僉都御
punctuated:
寧爲楩柟松栢，需其成于久大，毋若譁嚚之玩，取衒目睫。庶幾哉前哲可企，以爲爾山川重，而主司竊徼榮附於以人事君，追訑者之誚，幸矣夫！語有之：「信言不華。」凡〔應科〕所切磋，度諸士能行者，具以質告，亦猶以奉明詔也，毋姍曰：「卑卑無甚高論哉！」
是舉也，巡撫、右副都御史、今陞吏部右侍郎候代張〔士佩〕，飭治經文，聲敎布濩；巡撫貴州兼督湖北川東、右僉都御…
translation_en:
…Rather be like the *pian* and *nan* trees, the pines and cypresses, awaiting your maturation into enduring greatness, and do not be like flashy and clamorous curiosities that merely dazzle before the eyelashes. Thus, perhaps, the former sages may be emulated, bringing weight and honor to your mountains and rivers, while we, the chief examiners, may humbly share in the glory of serving our Sovereign by recommending worthy men, escaping [reading 追 as 逭] the ridicule aimed at boastful pretenders—what good fortune that would be! As the saying goes, "Truthful words are not华 (florid)." All that I, [Yingke], have earnestly discussed with you, gauging what you gentlemen are capable of putting into practice, I have set forth plainly and unadorned; this, too, is in keeping with upholding the enlightened imperial edict. Do not mockingly say, "How pedestrian, with no lofty discourse at all!"

In this examination, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, now promoted to Right Vice Minister of Personnel awaiting replacement, Zhang [Shipei], ordered the administration and promoted literary culture, spreading his prestigioius instruction far and wide; Grand Coordinator of Guizhou concurrently supervising Hubei and Eastern Sichuan, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
史今陞南贛汀韶右副都御
史王〔緝〕右副都御史劉〔庠〕先
後保釐章縫漸被巡理茶法
監察御史赫〔瀛〕風猷卓遠興
起譽髦禮科給事中聶〔良杞〕
大理寺右寺正祁〔鯨〕行人司
行人林〔士弘〕以使事至樂觀
===
盛典鎮守總兵官中軍都督府都
督同知郭〔成〕保禦疆土裨益
人文其綜理防檢於外則左
叅政賴〔庭槍〕右叅政凌〔琯〕右
叅政兼僉事楊〔一桂〕右叅議
兼僉事陳〔用賓〕副使鄭〔一信〕
戴〔燿〕張〔稽古〕僉事王〔言〕李〔士〕
punctuated: 史今陞南贛汀韶右副都御史王〔緝〕、右副都御史劉〔庠〕，先後保釐，章縫漸被。巡理茶法監察御史赫〔瀛〕，風猷卓遠，興起譽髦。禮科給事中聶〔良杞〕、大理寺右寺正祁〔鯨〕、行人司行人林〔士弘〕，以使事至，樂觀盛典。鎮守總兵官中軍都督府都督同知郭〔成〕，保禦疆土，裨益人文。其綜理防檢於外，則左叅政賴〔庭槍〕、右叅政凌〔琯〕、右叅政兼僉事楊〔一桂〕、右叅議兼僉事陳〔用賓〕、副使鄭〔一信〕、戴〔燿〕、張〔稽古〕、僉事王〔言〕、李〔士〕
translation_en: … [Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief], now promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief for Nan'gan-Tingshao, Wang Ji 王緝, and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiang 劉庠, successively safeguarded and governed the region, so that the scholars in their robes were gradually steeped in their influence. The Tea-Regulation-Inspecting Investigating Censor He Ying 赫瀛 displayed lofty and far-reaching moral stature and statecraft, rousing and inspiring talented scholars of renown. Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Rites Nie Liangqi 聶良杞, Right Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review Qi Jing 祁鯨, and Messenger of the Messenger Office Lin Shihong 林士弘 arrived on imperial missions and took pleasure in witnessing this grand ceremony. The Grand Defender and Regional Commander, Vice Commissioner-in-Chief of the Central Military Commission Guo Cheng 郭成 protected and defended the territory, bringing benefit to cultural refinement. As for those who managed overall administration and security inspection on the outside, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Lai Tingqiang 賴庭槍 [?], Right Administration Vice Commissioner Ling Guan 凌琯, Right Administration Vice Commissioner concurrently serving as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Yang Yigui 楊一桂, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner concurrently serving as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Chen Yongbin 陳用賓, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zheng Yixin 鄭一信, Dai Yao 戴燿, and Zhang Jigu 張稽古, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Wang Yan 王言 and Li Shi[da] 李士…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
達署都指揮僉事李贇蘇民
望協恭宣力咸有司存右叅
議高任重僉事費尚伊署都
指揮僉事汪東之以入
賀行與勞始事法宜書書之
河南懷慶府脩武縣儒學教
諭楊應科謹序
punctuated:
達、署都指揮僉事李贇、蘇民望，協恭宣力，咸有司存。右叅議高任重、僉事費尚伊、署都指揮僉事汪東之，以入賀行，與勞始事，法宜書，書之。
河南懷慶府脩武縣儒學教諭楊應科謹序。
translation_en:
…da, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Li Yun 李贇 and Su Minwang 蘇民望, who cooperated respectfully and exerted their strength, each fulfilling his official duties. Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Gao Renzhong 高任重, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Fei Shangyi 費尚伊, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Wang Dongzhi 汪東之, who had departed to present congratulations at court, shared in the labor at the beginning of the affair; by convention they ought to be recorded, and so I record them.

Respectfully prefaced by Yang Yingke 楊應科, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xiuwu County in Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan.

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
上復用廷臣議
深詔所司取士以浮詭爲戒有不
如式者雖籍
奏禮官必察而
請黜之並坐主者於是〔震亨〕聞
命廩廩殫夙夜之力閱諸士所爲
文浮者斥詭者亟斥其必實
===
且正也而後收焉猶懼其未
也從而紬繹焉則皆尊用先
聖之術曉暢當世之務侃侃
有經天下之氣寓焉夫
國家所託財器職業者粹於羣
下也今茲求士固將有以用
之自是與計偕對
punctuated: 上復用廷臣議，深詔所司，取士以浮詭爲戒。有不如式者，雖籍奏，禮官必察而請黜之，並坐主者。於是〔震亨〕聞命廩廩，殫夙夜之力，閱諸士所爲文：浮者斥，詭者亟斥，其必實且正也，而後收焉。猶懼其未也，從而紬繹焉，則皆尊用先聖之術，曉暢當世之務，侃侃有經天下之氣寓焉。夫國家所託財器職業者，粹於羣下也；今茲求士，固將有以用之。自是與計偕，對
translation_en: His Majesty, again adopting the deliberations of the court officials, issued an earnest edict to the authorities concerned that in selecting scholars they must guard against superficiality and eccentricity. Should there be any whose essays do not conform to the prescribed standards, even if their names have been registered and memorialized to the throne, the officials of the Ministry of Rites must investigate and request their dismissal, and furthermore hold the examiners accountable. Thereupon, hearing the imperial command with reverent trepidation, I, [Zhenheng], exhausted my strength day and night in reviewing the essays composed by the candidates: the superficial were rejected, the eccentric were promptly rejected, and only those that were truly substantive and orthodox were accepted. Still fearing this might not suffice, I proceeded to examine and draw out their deeper meaning, and found that they all revered and applied the teachings of the former sages, clearly understood the affairs of the present age, and carried within them a forthright spirit capable of ordering the empire. Now, the talents, capabilities, and official duties upon which the State relies are gathered in their purest form among the myriad subordinates; in seeking scholars at this time, the court surely intends to put them to practical use. From this point, when they travel to the capital with the local tribute reports to reply at …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
大廷服官而受事迹其所自獻足
以爲效矣異日者果用之而
效則上之以禎幹
邦國不顯於楩柟豫章干霄之
材次之以衣被海內不顯於
煒爗爗爗之錦又次之
以兼濟生民不顯於金莖瑤
===
草丹英珺實藥籠之良遺大
投艱歷險致遠無施而不可
如度雲棧瞿塘三峽之隘九
折之坂靡殊康衢衽席焉何
則所見者實所趨者正也此
眞方聞之士出入不悖其學
其眎爾鄉先達所以追徃喆
punctuated: 大廷，服官而受事，迹其所自獻，足以爲效矣。異日者，果用之而效，則上之以禎幹邦國，不顯於楩柟豫章干霄之材？次之以衣被海內，不顯於煒爗爗爗之錦？又次之以兼濟生民，不顯於金莖瑤草、丹英珺實、藥籠之良？遺大投艱，歷險致遠，無施而不可，如度雲棧、瞿塘三峽之隘、九折之坂，靡殊康衢衽席焉。何則？所見者實，所趨者正也。此眞方聞之士，出入不悖其學，其眎爾鄉先達所以追徃喆、
translation_en: … the great court, assume official posts, and take up their duties, if one traces what they have offered up of themselves, it is already enough to prove effective. In days to come, if they are indeed employed and prove effective, then at the highest level, by serving as auspicious pillars of the state, will they not be more illustrious than the sky-piercing timber of nanmu and camphor trees? Next, by clothing and benefiting all within the seas, will they not be more illustrious than resplendently gleaming brocade? And next again, by broadly succoring the living people, will they not be more illustrious than golden stems and jade herbs, cinnabar blossoms and fine-stone fruits—the finest remedies of the medicine chest? Entrusted with great tasks and cast into difficulties, traversing dangers and reaching distant goals, there will be nothing to which they cannot be applied: crossing the plank roads in the clouds, the narrows of Qutang and the Three Gorges, or the Nine-Turn Slope will be no different to them than a broad thoroughfare or a sleeping mat. Why is this? Because what they perceive is substantial, and what they pursue is orthodox. These are truly scholars of upright and broad learning, whose conduct at home and abroad does not contradict their study. Compared with the way the former worthies of your native province pursued the sages of the past and …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
重
本朝者庶幾爲無愧豈與夫雕
蟲小技夸靡不經蘄駴愚爠
衆好奇爲名高者埒哉彼左
賦所揚搉曷足偉焉抑〔震亨〕
聞之口能言身能行國寶也
口不能言身能行國器也口
===
粲於言而身螯於行國蠹也
王者敬其寶愛其器而棄其
蠹脫或諸士不浮於言矣而
乃浮於行事不詭於言矣而
乃詭於心術萬有一焉出其
中是蠹之郵也無論見棄爲
主者累如大負
punctuated: 重本朝者，庶幾爲無愧。豈與夫雕蟲小技、夸靡不經，蘄駴愚爠衆、好奇爲名高者埒哉？彼左賦所揚搉，曷足偉焉！抑〔震亨〕聞之：「口能言，身能行，國寶也；口不能言，身能行，國器也；口粲於言，而身螯於行，國蠹也。王者敬其寶，愛其器，而棄其蠹。」脫或諸士不浮於言矣，而乃浮於行事；不詭於言矣，而乃詭於心術。萬有一焉出其中，是蠹之郵也。無論見棄，爲主者累，如大負
translation_en: … and add weight to our reigning dynasty, nearly without shame. How could this be placed on a par with those petty skills of carving insects—boastful, extravagant, and uncanonical—that seek only to startle the ignorant and dazzle the multitude, indulging in novelty to win high renown? What Zuo Si’s rhapsody lauded and assessed—how could that be worth admiring! Moreover, I, [Zhenheng], have heard it said: “One whose mouth can speak and whose person can act is a treasure of the state; one whose mouth cannot speak yet whose person can act is a vessel of the state; one whose mouth is brilliant in speech yet whose person is perverse in conduct is a vermin of the state. A true king reveres his treasures, cherishes his vessels, and casts away his vermin.” Suppose, perchance, that you gentlemen are not superficial in your words, yet prove superficial in your deeds; that you are not deceitful in your words, yet prove deceitful in the intentions of your minds. Should there be even one in ten thousand among you like this, he would be the very worst of vermin. Not to mention being cast aside and becoming a burden to the examiners, what of severely failing to live up to…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
清時何吾恐井絡貽譏坤維蒙誚
即蠶叢魚鳧僻陋之氓無可
與比數矣切爲諸士恥之夫
蜀才奇麗率類其山川麗如
長卿奇如子雲故古今所忻
豔者則蜀之所少非文也至
考兩人素行大節均無足道
===
使繩以
當代濃程縱甚麗而奇必且置浮
詭之列今諸士審能行脩節
立無寧文采愧之爾或謂文
行判久矣自漢不能必楊馬
今必之諸士乎然〔不知〕知諸
士必不爾也人亦有言人心
punctuated: 清時何？吾恐井絡貽譏、坤維蒙誚，即蠶叢、魚鳧僻陋之氓，無可與比數矣，切爲諸士恥之。夫蜀才奇麗，率類其山川。麗如長卿，奇如子雲，故古今所忻豔者，則蜀之所少非文也。至考兩人素行大節，均無足道。使繩以當代濃程，縱甚麗而奇，必且置浮詭之列。今諸士審能行脩節立，無寧文采愧之爾。或謂文行判久矣，自漢不能必楊、馬，今必之諸士乎？然〔不知〕知諸士必不爾也。人亦有言：「人心
translation_en: … this era of clarity and peace? I fear that this would bring ridicule upon the region under the Well constellation and cast reproach upon this southwestern corner of the earth, such that even the rustic and unrefined folk of the days of Cancong and Yufu would be beyond comparison with them; I would feel deeply ashamed on behalf of you gentlemen! Now, the talents of Shu are wondrous and resplendent, generally resembling its mountains and rivers. Resplendent like Sima Xiangru (Changqing) and wondrous like Yang Xiong (Ziyun), they have truly been delighted in and admired throughout antiquity and the present; thus what Shu lacks is not literary talent. Yet when we examine the everyday conduct and fundamental moral integrity of those two men, neither is worth mentioning. Were they to be measured by the strict standards [?] of the present age, even though their writings were exceedingly resplendent and wondrous, they would surely be placed in the ranks of the superficial and deceitful. Now, if you gentlemen are truly able to cultivate your conduct and establish your moral integrity, it would be far better even if your literary brilliance fell short of theirs. Someone might say that literary skill and moral conduct have long been separated—since even the Han dynasty could not guarantee both in Yang Xiong and Sima Xiangru, can we expect this of these gentlemen today? Yet I, Buzhi, know that you gentlemen will certainly not be like that. People also have a saying: "The human heart…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
險於山川〔震亨〕獨明其非是
人固不易知豈其有險而如
山川也若其險如山川則人
之可信者尠矣是何其言之
不長厚乎而聖賢又何謂千
萬人之心即一人之心推一
心可以平天下乎蓋惟誠實
===
爲能成宇宙之事惟正大爲
能一天下之情故推一心可
以觀萬心者實也正也其不
易知者浮也詭也吾惟以實
且正待諸士而亦願諸士以
實且正終身自期待諸士而
以實且正自期待即今日之
punctuated: 險於山川，〔震亨〕獨明其非是。人固不易知，豈其有險而如山川也？若其險如山川，則人之可信者尠矣，是何其言之不長厚乎！而聖賢又何謂千萬人之心即一人之心，推一心可以平天下乎？蓋惟誠實爲能成宇宙之事，惟正大爲能一天下之情。故推一心可以觀萬心者，實也，正也；其不易知者，浮也，詭也。吾惟以實且正待諸士，而亦願諸士以實且正終身自期待。諸士而以實且正自期待，即今日之
translation_en: … is more treacherous than mountains and rivers." I, 〔Zhenheng 震亨〕, alone hold that this is untrue. People are indeed not easy to know, yet how could they be as treacherous as mountains and rivers? If they were as treacherous as mountains and rivers, then those whom one could trust would be few indeed—how ungenerous is that saying! And why then did the sages and worthies say that the minds of ten million people are the same as the mind of a single person, and that by extending a single mind one can bring peace to all under Heaven? For only sincerity and substance can accomplish the affairs of the universe, and only uprightness and magnanimity can unify the sentiments of all under Heaven. Therefore, that by which one can extend a single mind to observe ten thousand minds is substance and uprightness; that which is not easy to know is superficiality and deceit. I treat the scholars solely with substance and uprightness, and I also wish that the scholars will hold themselves to the expectation of substance and uprightness throughout their lives. If the scholars hold themselves to the expectation of substance and uprightness, then today's …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
言不浮不詭者悉乎天下之
具也而吾以實且正待諸士
則業已知其不浮詭於言矣
夫焉得設山川之險之疑耶
震亨非託長者之言而稱之
誠仰見
訓辭深厚恩施甚美慮淺聞者不
===
聖天子之德意爲諸士勸諸士愼
能究宣敢對揚
之矣昔者子路盛服見孔子孔子
子曰江出於岷山其始可以
濫觴及放而之津則難涉也
以其流愈濫故也今汝被服
盛顏色充天下且孰肯諫汝
punctuated: 言不浮不詭者，悉乎天下之具也。而吾以實且正待諸士，則業已知其不浮詭於言矣，夫焉得設山川之險之疑耶？震亨非託長者之言而稱之，誠仰見訓辭深厚，恩施甚美，慮淺聞者不能究宣，敢對揚聖天子之德意，爲諸士勸，諸士愼之矣！昔者子路盛服見孔子，孔子子曰：「江出於岷山，其始可以濫觴；及放而之津，則難涉也，以其流愈濫故也。今汝被服盛，顏色充，天下且孰肯諫汝？」
translation_en: …words that are neither superficial nor deceitful are altogether the instruments for bringing peace to all under heaven. And since I treat the scholars with sincerity and uprightness, I already know from their words that they are neither superficial nor deceitful; how then could I harbor suspicions that they are as险 perilous as mountains and rivers? I, Zhenheng, do not merely borrow the words of an elder in order to praise them. Truly, looking up and seeing that the imperial instructions are profound and generous and the bestowal of grace is surpassingly fine, yet fearing that those of shallow learning might not be able to fully proclaim them, I venture to extol in response the virtuous intentions of the Sacred Son of Heaven as an exhortation for the scholars [Note: lines 1 and 2 of the second half-leaf are transposed in the transcription]. May the scholars be heedful of this! In the past, when Zilu穿 wore resplendent attire to see Confucius, Confucius said: "The Yangtze River emerges from Mount Min; at its source it can barely float a wine goblet, but when it spreads out and reaches the fords, it is difficult to cross, because its current has grown ever more overflowing. Now you wear resplendent attire and your countenance is full of self-satisfaction—who in the world will be willing to remonstrate with you?"…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
嗟乎諸士之始進江漢之在
岷嶓也賴其未濫而易入也
故致戒儻諸士輒盛氣自負
罔念於〔震亨〕之言則涓涓者
波其無乃遽而爲沱潛乎哉
其又以人心爲不山川也諸
士慎之矣錄既成〔震亨〕宜有
===
言申末簡謹次其勸戒之詞
備書之
江西九江府彭澤縣儒學教
諭戴〔震亨〕謹序
punctuated:
嗟乎！諸士之始進，江、漢之在岷、嶓也。賴其未濫而易入也，故致戒。儻諸士輒盛氣自負，罔念於〔震亨〕之言，則涓涓者波，其無乃遽而爲沱、潛乎哉？其又以人心爲不山川也！諸士慎之矣！錄既成，〔震亨〕宜有言申末簡，謹次其勸戒之詞備書之。
江西九江府彭澤縣儒學教諭戴〔震亨〕謹序。
translation_en:
Alas! When the scholars first advance in their careers, they are like the Yangzi and Han rivers at Mount Min and Mount Bo. Because the current has not yet overflowed its banks and my words may still easily enter their minds, I offer this admonition. Should the scholars immediately become haughty and self-satisfied, paying no heed to my [Zhenheng's] words, then will not that trickling stream surge into waves and suddenly swell into the Tuo and Qian tributaries? Or would they take the human mind to be any less perilous than mountains and rivers [?]? May the scholars be cautious indeed! Now that the record is completed, it is fitting that I [Zhenheng] offer a statement at the end of the volume, and so I have respectfully arranged these words of encouragement and admonition and written them out in full.
Respectfully prefaced by Dai Zhenheng 戴震亨, Instructor of the Confucian School of Pengze County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
萬曆十年四川鄉試
監臨官
巡按四川監察御史宋　仕〔汝學山東平原縣人　辛未進士〕
提調官
四川等處承宣布政使司左布政使蔡汝賢〔用卿直隸華亭縣人　戊辰進士〕
四川等處承宣布政使司右參議萬一貫〔汝唯江西安福縣人　戊辰進士〕
監試官
四川等處提刑按察司按察使鄭　旻〔世穆廣東揭陽縣人　丙辰進士〕
四川等處提刑按察司副使范　崙〔子大直隸丹徒縣人　乙丑進士〕
考試官
河南懷慶府脩武縣儒學教諭楊應科〔時升雲南劍川州籍太和縣人　癸酉貢士〕
江西九江府彭澤縣儒學教諭戴震亨〔元器浙江建德縣人　丁卯貢士〕
同考試官

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
所謂誠其意者毋自欺也
定公問一言而可以興邦有諸孔子對曰
言不可以若是其幾也人之言曰爲君
難爲臣不易如知爲君之難也不幾乎
一言而興邦乎
孟子曰人有不爲也而後可以有爲
易
初九素履往无咎象曰素履之往獨行願
===
也
自上下下其道大光
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地天地設位而易行乎其
中矣成性存存道義之門
入而後說之
書
無怠無荒四夷來王禹曰於帝念哉德惟
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「所謂誠其意者，毋自欺也。」
「定公問：『一言而可以興邦，有諸？』孔子對曰：『言不可以若是其幾也。人之言曰：「爲君難，爲臣不易。」如知爲君之難也，不幾乎一言而興邦乎？』」
「孟子曰：『人有不爲也，而後可以有爲。』」
易
「初九，素履，往无咎。《象》曰：素履之往，獨行願也。」
「自上下下，其道大光。」
「夫《易》，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。天地設位，而《易》行乎其中矣。成性存存，道義之門。」
「入而後說之。」
書
「無怠無荒，四夷來王。禹曰：『於！帝念哉！德惟……』」
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books:
1. "What is meant by 'making one's thoughts sincere' is allowing no self-deception." (Great Learning, Daxue)
2. "Duke Ding asked, 'Is there a single saying that can make a country prosper?' Confucius replied, 'Such an effect cannot be expected from one saying. Yet there is a saying among people: "To be a ruler is difficult; to be a minister is not easy." If one knows the difficulty of being a ruler, may there not almost be a single saying that can make a country prosper?'" (Analects, Lunyu 13.15)
3. "Mencius said, 'Only when a man will not do some things is he afterwards able to do great things.'" (Mencius, Mengzi 4B.8)

The Book of Changes (Yi):
1. "Nine at the beginning: Treading in unadorned simplicity. Going forward brings no blame. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Going forward treading in unadorned simplicity': one carries out one's own wishes alone." (Hexagram 10, Lü)
2. "From above descending to those below, its way shines forth brightly." (Hexagram 17, Sui, Commentary on the Judgments / Tuan)
3. "Indeed, through the Changes the sages exalted their virtue and broadened their enterprise. Wisdom is exalted and ritual is humble; the exalted imitates Heaven, and the humble takes Earth as its pattern. Heaven and Earth determine their positions, and the Changes operate within them. Preserving and continually maintaining the completed nature is the gateway of the Way and of righteousness." (Appended Remarks, Xici A.7)
4. "One enters into it and afterward delights in it." (Order of the Hexagrams, Xugua)

The Book of Documents (Shu):
1. "'Do not be idle, do not be negligent, and the four surrounding tribes will come to acknowledge your sovereignty.' Yu said, 'Oh! May the Emperor bear this in mind! Virtue alone is…'" (Counsels of the Great Yu, Dayu mo)

學于古訓乃有獲事不師古以克永世匪
說攸聞惟學遜志務時敏厥脩乃來允
懷于玆道積于厥躬惟斆學半念終始
典于學厥德脩罔覺監于先王成憲其
永無愆
嚴惟丕式克用三宅三俊
惟周公克愼厥始惟君陳克和厥中惟公
克成厥終
===
詩
匪東方則明月出之光
彤弓弨兮受言藏之我有嘉賓中心貺之
鐘鼓既設一朝饗之
子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
有飶其香邦家之光有椒其馨胡考之寧
匪且有且匪今斯今振古如玆
春秋
秋及江人黃人伐陳〔僖公四年〕〔九月戊辰〕
punctuated:
善政，政在養民。
學于古訓乃有獲，事不師古，以克永世，匪說攸聞。惟學遜志，務時敏，厥脩乃來。允懷于玆，道積于厥躬。惟斆學半，念終始典于學，厥德脩罔覺。監于先王成憲，其永無愆。
嚴惟丕式，克用三宅三俊。
惟周公克愼厥始，惟君陳克和厥中，惟公克成厥終。
詩
匪東方則明，月出之光。
彤弓弨兮，受言藏之。我有嘉賓，中心貺之。鐘鼓既設，一朝饗之。
子孫千億，穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。
有飶其香，邦家之光。有椒其馨，胡考之寧。匪且有且，匪今斯今，振古如玆。
春秋
秋，及江人、黃人伐陳〔僖公四年〕。〔九月戊辰〕
translation_en:
…is good government, and government lies in nourishing the people."

"To study the ancient lessons is how one achieves gains. That one could manage affairs without taking the ancients as a teacher and yet perpetuate one's house for generations is not something I, Yue, have ever heard of. In learning, have a humble will and strive to be timely and diligent; then your cultivation will come. Truly cherish this, and the Way will accumulate in your person. Teaching is the half of learning; keep your thoughts from beginning to end constantly on learning, and your virtue will be cultivated without your being aware of it. Take as your mirror the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be free from fault."

"Solemnly pondering the great model, he was able to employ the appointees to the three positions and the possessors of the three grades of talent."

"The Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) was able to be cautious at the beginning; Jun Chen 君陳 was able to bring harmony to the middle; and you, Duke, are able to bring completion to the end."

Book of Odes (Shi 詩)

"It is not that the east is bright; it is the light of the rising moon."

"The red bow is unstrung; having received it, I store it away. I have an esteemed guest; from the center of my heart I bestow it on him. The bells and drums have been set up; for a whole morning I feast him."

"Sons and grandsons in thousands and hundreds of thousands, reverent and august, fitting to be lords, fitting to be kings."

"Fragrant is the aroma, the glory of the state and clan. Spicy is the scent, the comfort of longevity. It is not only here that there is this; it is not only now that it is so; from ancient times it has been like this."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋)

"In autumn, together with men of Jiang 江 and men of Huang 黃, we attacked Chen 陳 [4th year of Duke Xi 僖公]. [In the ninth month, on the wuchen day,]…"

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
諸侯盟于葵丘〔僖公九年〕
衛侯使甯俞來聘〔文公四年〕
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子齊世
子光滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭〔襄公〕
〔十年〕公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子
光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐
鄭〔公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子〕
光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐
鄭〔俱襄公十有一年〕
===
夏五月宋人及楚人平〔宣公十有五年〕春
王正月暨齊平〔昭公七年〕
禮記
德成而教尊教尊而官正官正而國治君
之謂也
一命緼韍幽衡再命赤韍幽衡三命赤韍
葱衡
夫肅肅敬也雝雝和也夫敬以和何事不
行
punctuated:
諸侯盟于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕
衛侯使甯俞來聘。〔文公四年〕
公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。〔襄公〕〔十年〕公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。〔公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子〕光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。〔俱襄公十有一年〕
夏五月，宋人及楚人平。〔宣公十有五年〕春王正月，暨齊平。〔昭公七年〕

《禮記》
德成而教尊，教尊而官正，官正而國治，君之謂也。
一命緼韍幽衡，再命赤韍幽衡，三命赤韍葱衡。
夫肅肅，敬也；雝雝，和也。夫敬以和，何事不行？
translation_en:
… the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu. [Ninth year of Duke Xi]
The Marquis of Wei sent Ning Yu to come on a mission of friendly inquiry. [Fourth year of Duke Wen]
The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu to attack Zheng. [Tenth year of Duke Xiang] The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu to attack Zheng. [The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Heir Apparent of Qi] Guang, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu to attack Zheng. [Both in the eleventh year of Duke Xiang]
In summer, in the fifth month, the people of Song and the people of Chu made peace. [Fifteenth year of Duke Xuan] In spring, in the King's first month, peace was made with Qi. [Seventh year of Duke Zhao]

Record of Rites (Liji)
When virtue is perfected, instruction is honored; when instruction is honored, officials are upright; when officials are upright, the state is well governed: this is what is meant by a ruler.
An official of the first grade wears a dull-red knee-cover and a dark-colored pendant-bar; one of the second grade wears a bright-red knee-cover and a dark-colored pendant-bar; one of the third grade wears a bright-red knee-cover and a青-green (scallion-green) pendant-bar.
Now "su-su" means reverence, and "yong-yong" means harmony. When there is reverence combined with harmony, what affair cannot be carried out?

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
治者然其道豈上下合同之謂哉齊晏
子評梁丘據而有和同之論其於君臣
相須之道辨至悉矣其說可指而言與
執是而求之往古舜爲天子禹皐爲輔
相交相儆戒日勤兢業至於太甲之篇
無逸之訓亦莫非逆耳之言觸鱗之語
彼所謂聖君賢相者相與之際何其艱
哉而譚者率謂太和元氣在唐虞成周
宇宙間則同與和果不相謀也可歷數
===
皇上茂齡撫運
講學親賢朝乾夕惕日不暇給其心卽舜之
心也商周令主固不敢望下風矣而一
二輔臣鹽梅交濟獻替相成如頃者罷
土木減織造旱災有禱星變有戒其他
憂盛危明之說靡不備至
主上悉以其說見諸行事回視虞廷商周泰和
之景象固千載一日也爾諸士得於躬
punctuated: 治者。然其道豈上下合同之謂哉？齊晏子評梁丘據而有和同之論，其於君臣相須之道，辨至悉矣，其說可指而言與？執是而求之往古，舜爲天子，禹、皐爲輔相，交相儆戒，日勤兢業。至於《太甲》之篇、《無逸》之訓，亦莫非逆耳之言、觸鱗之語。彼所謂聖君賢相者，相與之際，何其艱哉！而譚者率謂太和元氣在唐、虞、成周宇宙間，則同與和果不相謀也，可歷數皇上茂齡撫運，講學親賢，朝乾夕惕，日不暇給，其心卽舜之心也，商、周令主固不敢望下風矣。而一二輔臣，鹽梅交濟，獻替相成，如頃者罷土木、減織造，旱災有禱、星變有戒，其他憂盛危明之說，靡不備至。主上悉以其說見諸行事，回視虞廷、商、周泰和之景象，固千載一日也。爾諸士得於躬
translation_en:
… [supreme] governance. Yet how could this Way mean mere uniformity between ruler and minister? When Master Yan of Qi (Yanzi 晏子) evaluated Liangqiu Ju 梁丘據, he set forth the discourse on harmony (he 和) versus uniformity (tong 同), distinguishing with utmost thoroughness the Way by which ruler and minister depend upon one another; can his argument be pointed out and explained? Holding to this standard and seeking it in antiquity: when Shun 舜 was the Son of Heaven, and Yu 禹 and Gao Yao 皐陶 were his assisting chief ministers, they mutually admonished and cautioned one another, daily diligent, wary, and industrious. Coming down to the chapters of "Tai Jia" 太甲 and the instructions of "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi 無逸) [in the Book of Documents], these too were nothing other than words unpleasant to the ear and speech that brushed against the dragon's reverse scales. Those whom we call sage rulers and worthy ministers—in their dealings with one another, how arduous it was! Yet commentators generally say that the primordial vitality of Supreme Harmony resided within the cosmos during the eras of Tang 唐, Yu 虞, and flourishing Zhou 成周. Thus, uniformity and harmony indeed have nothing to do with each other; can one enumerate [how this was so?] … [gap in original or missing line before honorific elevation]

His Majesty the Emperor, in his flourishing youth, embraces the Mandate of the age. He expounds upon learning and draws close to the worthy, diligent by day and vigilant by night, without a moment's leisure; his heart is indeed the very heart of Shun, and the fine rulers of Shang 商 and Zhou certainly could not dare to look even toward his leeward breeze! Meanwhile, one or two Grand Secretaries (fuchen 輔臣), blending ingredients like salt and plum to complement one another, offer counsel on what to promote and what to discard in mutual accomplishment. For instance, recently, halting construction projects, reducing imperial textile manufacturing, offering prayers during drought disasters, and taking warning from celestial anomalies, along with other counsels of being anxious in times of prosperity and sensing danger in times of enlightenment—none of these have failed to be presented in full. The Sovereign has put all of their counsels into actual practice. Looking back upon the spectacle of grand harmony in the court of Yu 虞 and in Shang and Zhou, it is truly as though a thousand years were a single day. You gentlemen have personally…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
逢久矣試颺言於篇用紀盛美即更广
直言讜論其畢陳之以觀忠愛毋諱
問周禮一書備載經略巨細畢舉此聖人
致治之迹也自經秦火其書多散失錯
雜而異議蜂起焉或以爲周公作或以
爲非或謂成周理財之書或謂瀆亂不
經之書其何所據與購得五篇而獻之
祕府校理祕書而著之錄略若能表章
發明之矣乃議者訾之豈別有見乎說
===
周禮者非一人有著復古編者有著補
遺者有謂冬官未嘗亡而地官之文實
亡者果孰爲得與用周禮者亦非一人
或謂其假用之者或謂其輕用之者或
謂其誤用之者果孰爲甚與至於設官
不與王制合封建不與孟子合先儒謂
其間必有末世增入者是固無庸瑣議
也宋朱熹讀孟子經界章稱之曰學識
其大然則善論周禮者亦惟得其大而
punctuated:
逢久矣，試颺言於篇，用紀盛美。即更广直言讜論，其畢陳之，以觀忠愛，毋諱！
問：《周禮》一書，備載經略，巨細畢舉，此聖人致治之迹也。自經秦火，其書多散失錯雜，而異議蜂起焉。或以爲周公作，或以爲非；或謂成周理財之書，或謂瀆亂不經之書，其何所據與？購得五篇而獻之祕府，校理祕書而著之《錄》《略》，若能表章發明之矣；乃議者訾之，豈別有見乎？說《周禮》者非一人，有著《復古編》者，有著《補遺》者，有謂〈冬官〉未嘗亡而〈地官〉之文實亡者，果孰爲得與？用《周禮》者亦非一人，或謂其假用之者，或謂其輕用之者，或謂其誤用之者，果孰爲甚與？至於設官不與《王制》合，封建不與《孟子》合，先儒謂其間必有末世增入者，是固無庸瑣議也。宋朱熹讀《孟子》「經界」章，稱之曰「學識其大」。然則善論《周禮》者，亦惟得其大而
translation_en:
… encountered this in person for a long time. Try setting forth your words in an essay to record this flourishing excellence. And if you also have [?] forthright words and honest counsels, present them in full so that we may observe your loyalty and devotion; hold nothing back!

Question: The single work Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) comprehensively records the grand designs of governance, encompassing matters great and small alike; these are the traces by which the sage brought about order. Ever since it passed through the fires of Qin, the text has suffered much loss and confusion, and divergent opinions have sprung up in swarms. Some hold that it was composed by the Duke of Zhou, while others hold that it was not; some call it a book of fiscal administration from the flourishing Zhou, while others call it a muddled, disordered, and uncanonical work—upon what are these views based? Those who purchased the five sections and presented them to the Imperial Library, or who collated the palace texts and recorded them in the Seven Summaries (Qilüe) and Separate Records (Bielu), seemed able to bring the work to light and elucidate it; yet critics disparaged them—did they perhaps have some other insight? Those who have expounded the Rites of Zhou are not a single person: there is one who wrote the Restoration of Antiquity (Fugu bian), one who wrote the Supplement to Omissions (Buyi), and one who argued that the "Offices of Winter" (Dongguan) was never lost whereas text from the "Offices of Earth" (Diguan) was in fact lost—which of them truly got it right? Those who have put the Rites of Zhou into practice are likewise not a single person: one is said to have used it as a pretext, one is said to have used it rashly, and one is said to have used it mistakenly—which of them went to the greatest extreme? As for its establishment of offices not agreeing with the "Royal Regulations" (Wangzhi) and its enfeoffment system not agreeing with the Mencius (Mengzi), earlier Confucians held that there must be interpolations from a later age among them; this certainly requires no petty debate. When Zhu Xi 朱熹 of the Song read the chapter on "Defining Boundaries" (Jingjie) in the Mencius, he praised him, saying that "in learning, he grasped what is great." That being so, one who is skilled at discussing the Rites of Zhou likewise simply grasps its great…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
已兹欲師周公之意而不泥其迹諸生
必有會通其大指者願切磋究之
問儒者有言士人以正直忠厚爲本貴節
與量也虞夏商周以前尚矣自是而後
惟兩漢士風最爲近古西漢尚長厚東
漢尚奇節姑撮其著者言之有見人有
過專務覆匿者有郎官有譴常蒙其罪
者有買金償同舍恐人知吏迹者有爲
吏未甞案人官屬不敢爲欺者以量名
===
也果有得於正直與有少厲清節而贓
汙解綬者有聲名自高而士號登龍門
者有性方峻厲一榻常懸者有表正鄉
閭不願爲所短者以節名也果有得於
忠厚與士生其時亦有卓然不受變於
俗者其人可得而指與兩漢風聲氣習
大抵與理道運祚相維繫其得失利害
可得而評與當今士習比前代何似論
世者擇術而趨作人者樹風而倡將何
punctuated:
已。兹欲師周公之意而不泥其迹，諸生必有會通其大指者，願切磋究之。

問：儒者有言，士人以正直忠厚爲本，貴節與量也。虞、夏、商、周以前尚矣，自是而後，惟兩漢士風最爲近古。西漢尚長厚，東漢尚奇節，姑撮其著者言之：有見人有過專務覆匿者，有郎官有譴常蒙其罪者，有買金償同舍恐人知吏迹者，有爲吏未甞案人、官屬不敢爲欺者，以量名也，果有得於正直與？有少厲清節而贓汙解綬者，有聲名自高而士號「登龍門」者，有性方峻厲、一榻常懸者，有表正鄉閭、不願爲所短者，以節名也，果有得於忠厚與？士生其時，亦有卓然不受變於俗者，其人可得而指與？兩漢風聲氣習，大抵與理道運祚相維繫，其得失利害可得而評與？當今士習比前代何似？論世者擇術而趨，作人者樹風而倡，將何…
translation_en:
…only. Now, if we wish to emulate the intent of the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) without clinging rigidly to his outward traces, you students must surely have a thorough comprehension of its main purport; I hope you will carefully examine and discuss it.

Question: Confucian scholars have a saying that for literati, uprightness and loyal magnanimity are fundamental, and that what is valued in them are integrity and breadth of mind. The eras of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou are remote in antiquity; since those times, the ethos of literati in the Two Han dynasties was closest to antiquity. The Western Han esteemed generous magnanimity, whereas the Eastern Han esteemed extraordinary integrity. Let us briefly select the most prominent examples to speak of them: There was one who, upon seeing others' faults, made it his sole business to cover and conceal them; there was one who, when Court Gentlemen (langguan) incurred reprimands, routinely took their blame upon himself; there was one who bought gold to repay his roommate out of fear that others would learn of the investigation's traces; and there was one who as an official never formally prosecuted anyone, yet whose subordinates did not dare to deceive him. These men were renowned for their breadth of mind—did they truly attain uprightness? Then there was one who cultivated pure integrity in his youth, causing corrupt officials to untie their seal-ribbons and resign; there was one who held his own reputation high, such that scholars called being received by him "ascending the Dragon Gate" (deng Longmen); there was one whose nature was square, stern, and severe, keeping a single couch suspended for a select guest; and there was one who stood as a paragon of rectitude in his home community, so that men wished not to be disparaged by him. These men were renowned for their integrity—did they truly attain loyal magnanimity? Among the literati born in those times, were there also those who stood out independently without being altered by prevailing customs, and can those men be pointed out? The ethos, reputation, and prevailing habits of the Two Han dynasties were on the whole bound up with principles of governance and the destiny of the throne; can their merits and flaws, advantages and harms, be evaluated? How do the habits of literati today compare with those of former dynasties? For those who evaluate the age in choosing what path to pursue, and for those who cultivate men by establishing an ethos to lead the way, on what will they…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
居焉其詳言之以觀向往
問守令數易則民不安任官之必要於久
也尚矣史遷稱漢之盛以居官者長子
孫爲言漢宣之治史賛其吏稱民安者
正以久任之法行上下莫有苟且之意
也歷代論治者卒歸重於此詎不然哉
我
皇上鑒古圖治首用輔臣議
明詔有司力行久任期復唐虞三考黜陟庶績
===
咸熙之效
神明之化洽矣或者有謂久任便民不便吏何
與夫張官置吏以爲民也民誠便矣何
以吏之不便爲顧乃蘇軾復言得者旣
不肯以僥倖自名則不得者必以沉淪
爲恨何以故乎先正謂久任與超遷相
爲表裏信斯言也吏民俱得其便與其
說亦可得聞與
皇朝稽古定制於斯二者實兼用之其在今日
punctuated:
居焉？其詳言之，以觀向往。
問：守令數易則民不安，任官之必要於久也尚矣。史遷稱漢之盛，以居官者長子孫爲言；漢宣之治，史賛其吏稱民安者，正以久任之法行，上下莫有苟且之意也。歷代論治者，卒歸重於此，詎不然哉？我皇上鑒古圖治，首用輔臣議，明詔有司力行久任，期復唐、虞三考黜陟、庶績咸熙之效，神明之化洽矣。或者有謂久任便民不便吏，何與？夫張官置吏以爲民也，民誠便矣，何以吏之不便爲顧？乃蘇軾復言：「得者旣不肯以僥倖自名，則不得者必以沉淪爲恨。」何以故乎？先正謂久任與超遷相爲表裏，信斯言也，吏、民俱得其便與？其說亦可得聞與？皇朝稽古定制，於斯二者實兼用之，其在今日，
translation_en:
… [where will they] stand? Expound on this in detail, so that we may observe your aspirations.

Question: If prefects and magistrates are frequently replaced, the people will not be at peace; the necessity of long tenure in official appointments has been esteemed since antiquity. When Sima Qian 司馬遷 praised the flourishing of the Han, he spoke of those holding office raising their sons and grandsons in their posts. As for the governance of Emperor Xuan of Han 漢宣帝, the histories praised it by saying that officials were competent in their duties and the people were content in their livelihoods—precisely because the practice of long tenure was carried out, and neither superiors nor inferiors harbored a perfunctory mindset. Those who have discussed governance through the ages have ultimately placed great weight on this; how could it not be so? Our August Emperor, examining antiquity and planning for good governance, first adopted the deliberations of his Grand Secretaries and issued an explicit edict ordering the authorities to vigorously implement long tenure in office, hoping to restore the effectiveness of Tang 唐 [Yao 堯] and Yu 虞 [Shun 舜], when demotions and promotions were made after three triennial evaluations and all achievements were resplendent. His divine and enlightened transforming influence has spread far and wide. Yet some say that long tenure is convenient for the people, but inconvenient for the officials—why is that? Now, offices are established and officials appointed for the sake of the people; if the people are truly well served, why should the inconvenience to officials be taken into consideration? Yet Su Shi 蘇軾 also said: "Since those who succeed refuse to call their own rise undeserved luck, those who do not succeed will surely resent sinking into obscurity." For what reason is this? Worthies of earlier times said that long tenure and rapid promotion beyond the regular sequence complement one another as exterior and interior. If we trust these words, will both officials and the people find it advantageous? May we hear an explanation of this view? When the August Dynasty examined antiquity to establish its institutions, it in fact employed both of these methods together. At the present day, …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
可因而行之否茲欲使服官牧民者樂
於久任以維其法於無窮其道何繇與
請攄所蘊以竟其說
問立國莫先於爲民興利蜀之利民無如
水利蠶桑茲試相與籌之夫益州沃野
千里天府之地諸葛亮言也攷史漢蜀
守李冰鑿離堆辟沫水穿二江成都中
行舟而餘以用溉今堆猶歸立水間而
沫水不言害矣第不審二江謂何而經
===
行灌溉何縣何畝也夫亮稱沃野矣而
自爲蜀相江水無恙旁近地皆引注爲
畝乃廢不講其少史起引漳灌鄴智耶
抑有說也蜀志曰蜀古蠶叢國謂其地
宜蠶舊矣乃張詠教植桑於知鄂時而
事蹟不具於爲蜀何也且今閭之北家
蠶户桑而錦官以南不覩一植又何也
或曰民辟稅說果然否今成都自沙河
抵龍泉皆可田而乏水利自錦官及戎
punctuated:
可因而行之否？茲欲使服官牧民者樂於久任，以維其法於無窮，其道何繇與？請攄所蘊以竟其說。
問：立國莫先於爲民興利。蜀之利民，無如水利、蠶桑，茲試相與籌之。夫「益州沃野千里，天府之地」，諸葛亮言也。攷《史》、《漢》，蜀守李冰鑿離堆，辟沫水，穿二江成都中，行舟，而餘以用溉。今堆猶歸立水間，而沫水不言害矣；第不審二江謂何，而經行灌溉何縣、何畝也？夫亮稱沃野矣，而自爲蜀相，江水無恙，旁近地皆引注爲畝，乃廢不講，其少史起引漳灌鄴智耶？抑有說也？《蜀志》曰：「蜀，古蠶叢國。」謂其地宜蠶舊矣。乃張詠教植桑於知鄂時，而事蹟不具於爲蜀，何也？且今閭之北家蠶户桑，而錦官以南不覩一植，又何也？或曰民辟稅，說果然否？今成都自沙河抵龍泉，皆可田而乏水利；自錦官及戎、
translation_en:
… can they be followed and put into practice? If we now wish to make those who hold office as shepherds of the people happy to serve long terms, so as to maintain this system indefinitely, by what way can this be achieved? Please set forth your accumulated learning to complete the discussion of this matter.

Question: In establishing the state, nothing takes precedence over promoting what benefits the people. In Shu [Sichuan], nothing benefits the people more than water control and sericulture; let us now deliberate on them together. That "Yizhou has a thousand li of fertile plains, a land of natural abundance" was said by Zhuge Liang. Examining the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji) and the History of the Han (Hanshu), Li Bing, the Grand Administrator of Shu, cut through the Lidui [Separated Mound] to avert the harms of the Mo River, and channeled two rivers through the middle of Chengdu for boat navigation, while the surplus water was used for irrigation. Today the mound still stands towering [reading 歸 as 巋] amid the waters, and the Mo River is no longer spoken of as a hazard; yet we do not clearly know what the "two rivers" refer to, or which counties and which fields they pass through and irrigate. Now, Zhuge Liang praised the fertile plains, yet when he himself served as Counselor-in-Chief of Shu, although the river waters were intact and the nearby lands could all have been irrigated by drawing water into the fields, he neglected to attend to this. Did he lack the wisdom of Shi Qi, who channeled the Zhang River to irrigate Ye? Or is there another explanation? The Record of Shu (Shuzhi) says: "Shu is the ancient state of Cancong," meaning that its land has long been suitable for silkworms. Yet Zhang Yong taught the planting of mulberry trees when he was Prefect of E [Ezhou], whereas no such deeds are recorded from when he governed Shu—why is that? Moreover, today north of Lang [Langzhong, reading 閭 as 閬?] every family raises silkworms and every household plants mulberries, whereas south of Jinguan [Chengdu] one does not see a single mulberry tree planted—why is that as well? Some say the people are evading taxes; is this explanation actually true or not? Today in Chengdu, from the Sha River to Longquan, all the land is arable yet lacks waterworks; from Jinguan to Rong [Xuzhou] and…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
渝皆可桑而罕勸課誠欲在事者用史
起智而申張詠之見奚策而可諸生蜀
產宜習蜀掌故其具言之
punctuated: 渝，皆可桑而罕勸課。誠欲在事者用史起智而申張詠之見，奚策而可？諸生蜀產，宜習蜀掌故，其具言之。
translation_en: … [from Jinguan to Rong] and Yu, the land is all suitable for cultivating mulberry trees, yet encouragement and supervision are rare. If we truly wish for those in office to employ the wisdom of Shi Qi史起 and carry forward the vision of Zhang Yong張詠, what policies will suffice? You students are natives of Shu蜀 and ought to be well versed in its historical precedents—set forth your views in full.

text:
第壹塲
四書
所謂誠其意者毋自欺也
劉三才
同考試官教諭湯　批〔講毋自欺透徹題旨躍然　宜錄〕
批
考試官教諭戴　批〔切當〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔典實〕
傳者釋誠意惟戒其累吾誠者而已夫意之不
===
誠自欺累之也欲誠其意者可不知所戒哉且
夫天下有實理自脩有實功而一毫之欺不與
焉知此則經文之所謂誠意者可識矣何則意
發於人心之動其初何有於欺也意雜於人欲
之私其欺於是乎生焉誠則不欺欺則不可以
語誠矣故誠意者不必他有所求也眞妄之辨
旣以晰於知至之餘則防檢之功自當加於有
感之際善知所當爲矣而爲之不力將誰欺乎
是自欺其好也非所以誠吾好善之意也吾其
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「所謂誠其意者，毋自欺也。」
劉三才
同考試官教諭湯　批〔講毋自欺透徹，題旨躍然。　宜錄。〕
批
考試官教諭戴　批〔切當。〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔典實。〕

傳者釋誠意，惟戒其累吾誠者而已。夫意之不誠，自欺累之也，欲誠其意者，可不知所戒哉？且夫天下有實理，自脩有實功，而一毫之欺不與焉。知此，則經文之所謂誠意者可識矣。何則？意發於人心之動，其初何有於欺也？意雜於人欲之私，其欺於是乎生焉。誠則不欺，欺則不可以語誠矣。故誠意者，不必他有所求也。眞妄之辨，旣以晰於知至之餘；則防檢之功，自當加於有感之際。善知所當爲矣，而爲之不力，將誰欺乎？是自欺其好也，非所以誠吾好善之意也，吾其
translation_en:
First Session
The Four Books
"What is meant by 'making the thoughts sincere' is allowing no self-deception."
Liu Sancai 劉三才
Associate Examiner, Instructor Tang 湯, comments: 〔The explanation of "allowing no self-deception" is thorough and penetrating; the import of the theme leaps out vividly. Worthy of selection.〕
Comments:
Examiner, Instructor Dai 戴, comments: 〔To the point and fitting.〕
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊, comments: 〔Classical and substantial.〕

In explaining "making the thoughts sincere," the commentator simply warns against that which compromises our sincerity. Now, when one's thoughts lack sincerity, it is self-deception that compromises them; how can anyone who wishes to make his thoughts sincere fail to know what he must guard against? Moreover, in the world there is real principle, and in self-cultivation there is real effort, in which not a hair's breadth of deception has any part. Once one understands this, what the Classic text calls "making the thoughts sincere" can be recognized. Why is this? Thoughts issue from the stirring of the human mind—in the beginning, what deception is there in them? Only when thoughts become mingled with the selfishness of human desires does deception arise therein. Where there is sincerity, there is no deception; where there is deception, one cannot speak of sincerity. Therefore, one who would make his thoughts sincere need not seek elsewhere. Since the distinction between the true and the false has already been clearly discerned after knowledge has been extended to the utmost, the effort of vigilance and restraint ought naturally to be applied at the moment when thoughts are stirred. When one knows the good that ought to be done, yet does not do it with all one's strength, whom would one be deceiving? This is to deceive oneself in one's love of the good; it is not the way to make sincere one's thought of loving the good. May I…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
勿之爲焉惡知所當去矣而去之不嚴將誰欺
乎是自欺其惡也非所以誠吾惡惡之意也吾
其勿之蹈焉天人不竝立而思以完其天必以
過其人則閑邪固所以存誠也不然吾自知之
吾自欺之天將以人而漓矣何以語立誠之功
哉理欲相貞勝而思以全其理務以絕其欲則
去僞乃所以著誠也不然雖以欺人實以自欺
理將以欲而淆矣不終爲吾誠之累哉是可見
誠意者自脩之首務戒欺者誠意之實功從事
===
於大人之學者當自得之矣雖然誠意之義亦
大矣固心原所由端亦治原所自出也好惡不
欺誠巳之意耳推之好民所好惡民所惡以通
天下之意亦此誠焉是故王者不欺四海其始
於不欺一念乎學者味於曾氏之旨而天德王
道思過半矣
定公問一言而可以興邦有諸孔子對曰
言不可以若是其幾也人之言曰爲君
難爲臣不易如知爲君之難也不幾乎
punctuated:
勿之爲焉。惡知所當去矣，而去之不嚴，將誰欺乎？是自欺其惡也，非所以誠吾惡惡之意也，吾其勿之蹈焉。天人不竝立，而思以完其天，必以過其人，則閑邪固所以存誠也；不然，吾自知之，吾自欺之，天將以人而漓矣，何以語立誠之功哉？理欲相貞勝，而思以全其理，務以絕其欲，則去僞乃所以著誠也；不然，雖以欺人，實以自欺，理將以欲而淆矣，不終爲吾誠之累哉？是可見誠意者，自脩之首務；戒欺者，誠意之實功。從事於大人之學者，當自得之矣。雖然，誠意之義亦大矣，固心原所由端，亦治原所自出也。好惡不欺，誠巳之意耳；推之好民所好、惡民所惡，以通天下之意，亦此誠焉。是故王者不欺四海，其始於不欺一念乎！學者味於曾氏之旨，而天德王道，思過半矣。

定公問：「一言而可以興邦，有諸？」孔子對曰：「言不可以若是其幾也。人之言曰：『爲君難，爲臣不易。』如知爲君之難也，不幾乎
translation_en:
…must not do so. Once one knows that evil ought to be cast away, yet does not cast it away strictly, whom is one deceiving? That is deceiving oneself in one's hatred; it is not the way to make sincere my intention of hating evil, so I must not tread that path. The heavenly and the human cannot stand together; if one seeks to keep one's heavenly nature intact, one must suppress the human [Check: 過 likely graphic error for 遏, "curb/suppress" [?]], for guarding against depravity is indeed the way to preserve sincerity. Otherwise, if I know it myself yet deceive myself, the heavenly will be diluted by the human—how then could one speak of the achievement of establishing sincerity? Principle and desire vie for mastery; if one seeks to preserve principle intact, one must strive to cut off desire, for eliminating falsehood is precisely the way to manifest sincerity. Otherwise, though one may think it deceives others, in reality it is deceiving oneself; principle will be confounded by desire—will this not ultimately become an impediment to my sincerity? From this it can be seen that making the intentions sincere is the foremost task of self-cultivation, and guarding against self-deception is the substantive work of making the intentions sincere. Those who engage in the learning of the Great Man ought to realize this for themselves. Even so, the meaning of making the intentions sincere is great indeed! It is truly where the source of the mind is rectified, and also whence the source of governance issues forth. Not deceiving oneself in one's likes and dislikes is simply making one's own intentions sincere; yet extending this to liking what the people like and disliking what the people dislike, so as to connect with the intentions of all under Heaven, is also this very sincerity. Therefore, when a true king does not deceive the Four Seas, does it not begin with not deceiving a single thought? If scholars savor the purport of Master Zeng (Zengzi 曾子), then as for Heavenly Virtue and the Kingly Way, their understanding will be more than halfway there.

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
一言而興邦乎
荀自新
同考試官教諭王　批　〔轉折起伏曲盡其妙且氣度冠冕擅場之作也〕
考試官教諭戴　批　〔精粹〕
考試官教諭楊　批　〔正大〕
時君求治於一言聖人因進以克艱之道焉甚
矣君道惟艱也知其艱而圖之邦其可幾而興
乎此夫子一言以廸定公也且爲君者豈不欲
===
其邦之興哉顧治道成於憂勤而隳於逸樂難
易之間人君不可以不知也定公志於興邦而
取必於一言焉蓋知所以期其效而未知所以
圖其難者孔子則對之曰君欲一言以興邦也
言可若是其期哉必也其人言乎曰爲君難爲
臣不易蓋以代天理物者君也日御萬幾之煩
代君終事者臣也身膺百責之萃故言君難而
并及臣之不易也思深哉其言之也誠萬世興
邦之要道矣君人者特患未之知耳如其聞斯
punctuated:
一言而興邦乎？」

荀自新
同考試官教諭王　批：〔轉折起伏，曲盡其妙，且氣度冠冕，擅場之作也。〕
考試官教諭戴　批：〔精粹。〕
考試官教諭楊　批：〔正大。〕

時君求治於一言，聖人因進以克艱之道焉。甚矣，君道惟艱也！知其艱而圖之，邦其可幾而興乎？此夫子一言以廸定公也。且爲君者，豈不欲其邦之興哉？顧治道成於憂勤而隳於逸樂，難易之間，人君不可以不知也。定公志於興邦，而取必於一言焉，蓋知所以期其效，而未知所以圖其難者。孔子則對之曰：君欲一言以興邦也，言可若是其期哉？必也其人言乎！曰「爲君難，爲臣不易」。蓋以代天理物者，君也，日御萬幾之煩；代君終事者，臣也，身膺百責之萃。故言君難，而并及臣之不易也。思深哉，其言之也！誠萬世興邦之要道矣。君人者，特患未之知耳。如其聞斯
translation_en:
… causing a state to flourish with a single saying?”

Xun Zixin 荀自新
Associate Examiner Instructor Wang 王 comments: [Its transitions and rises and falls exhaust every subtlety, while its bearing is dignified and stately—a work that dominates the examination hall.]
Examiner Instructor Dai 戴 comments: [Pure and refined.]
Examiner Instructor Yang 楊 comments: [Upright and grand.]

When the ruler of the time sought good governance in a single saying, the Sage accordingly presented him with the Way of overcoming difficulty. Profound indeed is the difficulty of the Way of the ruler! If one recognizes its difficulty and takes measures to address it, may the state not be expected to flourish? With this single saying the Master guided Duke Ding 定公.

Moreover, how could anyone who serves as a ruler not desire his state to flourish? Yet the Way of governance is achieved through anxious diligence and ruined through idle pleasure; between difficulty and ease, a ruler of men cannot fail to understand the difference. Duke Ding set his mind on making his state flourish, yet sought to guarantee it through a single saying—he knew how to hope for the result, but did not yet know how to grapple with the difficulty. Confucius therefore replied to him: You wish for a single saying to make the state flourish, my lord, but can a saying be counted upon for such an outcome so easily? If there must be one, it would be the saying people have: “To be a ruler is difficult; to be a minister is not easy.” For the one who governs all things on behalf of Heaven is the ruler, who daily presides over the myriad complexities of state affairs; the one who brings affairs to completion on behalf of the ruler is the minister, who personally shoulders the convergence of a hundred responsibilities. Therefore, in speaking of the difficulty of being a ruler, the saying also extends to the fact that being a minister is not easy. How deeply considered are the words of this saying! Truly, it is the essential Way for making a state flourish for ten thousand generations. For one who rules over men, the only worry is that he does not yet recognize this. If, upon hearing this…

text:
言而知爲君之難則必思其難而盡克君之道
九重尊矣尊非敢恃也兢兢乎敬天勤民之心
時幾自勑而天與人歸景運其不日昌者否矣

之地故一人足以定國思艱者保大之謨故一

而臣勞乎得一舜則堯可無憂得五臣則舜可
無爲是厥臣克艱乃厥后所以無艱也所貴乎
君臣者亦各自盡而已矣此又夫子未發之意

文之佳者
punctuated:
言而知爲君之難，則必思其難而盡克君之道。九重尊矣，尊非敢恃也，兢兢乎敬天勤民之心，時幾自勑，而天與人歸，景運其不日昌者，否矣；五位安矣，安非敢溺也，業業乎脩政明刑之念，乾惕弗遑，而綱舉目張，幾務其不日振者，否矣。邦之興也，不於斯一言幾哉？要之，朝廷者本原之地，故一人足以定國；思艱者保大之謨，故一言可以興邦。向使言君而不約之以難，則雖千萬言亦無當於治矣，況一言乎？公而悟此，其尚圖易於難焉可也。雖然，爲君誠難矣，不曰君逸而臣勞乎？得一舜則堯可無憂，得五臣則舜可無爲，是厥臣克艱，乃厥后所以無艱也。所貴乎君臣者，亦各自盡而已矣。此又夫子未發之意，事君者其念之。

孟子曰：「人有不爲也，而後可以有爲。」
鍾應麟
同考試官教諭張　批〔脫去套語，盡自胷中流出，〕文之佳者。
translation_en:
…saying and comes to know the difficulty of being a ruler, then he will surely ponder that difficulty and exhaust the Way of fulfilling his role as a ruler. The ninefold palace is exalted indeed, yet he does not dare rely upon that exaltedness; cautiously maintaining a heart that reveres Heaven and labors for the people, at every moment and in every subtle incipient matter he admonishes himself—then with Heaven bestowing its favor and the people turning their allegiance to him, how could the great destiny of the state fail to prosper day by day? The sovereign's throne is secure indeed, yet he does not dare indulge in that security; anxiously holding fast to the thought of cultivating governance and clarifying punishments, he remains tirelessly vigilant without leisure—then with the main cord drawn up and the meshes of the net spread open, how could the myriad affairs of state fail to be revitalized day by day? May the flourishing of a state not be nearly achieved through this single saying?

In sum, the court is the fundamental source, and thus the One Man suffices to settle the state; pondering hardship is the counsel for preserving greatness, and thus a single saying can cause a state to flourish. If in speaking of the ruler one did not sum it up in terms of difficulty, then even ten thousand words would be of no avail to governance, how much less a single saying! If the Duke awakens to this, let him seek ease by first confronting difficulty. Even so, while being a ruler is truly difficult, is it not said that the ruler enjoys ease while the ministers toil? By obtaining a single Shun, Yao could be free from worry; by obtaining five ministers, Shun could govern through non-action. Thus, when the ministers are able to shoulder the hardships, that is whereby the sovereign is freed from hardship. What is valued in ruler and minister is simply that each exhausts his own duty. This, moreover, is the unexpressed meaning of the Master; let those who serve their ruler bear it in mind.

Mencius said: "Only when a man has things that he will not do is he afterward capable of doing great things."
By Zhong Yinglin 鍾應麟.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhang 張, comments: [Having cast off clichés, everything flows straight from his own breast;] a fine piece of writing.

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭戴　批〔通達〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔氣昌〕
大賢論人之所以能有爲者欲其愼之於爲也
甚矣事不可以妄爲也有不爲則知愼矣其能
有爲也固宜孟子之意蓋曰天下之事麗於人
之無爲而亦僨於人之有爲非爲之過也不善
爲者之過也何則宇宙之事皆吾分内之事孰
非人之所當爲者乎然天下之事天下之理宰
之亦孰非爲之所當擇者乎人惟漫無所擇宜
===
其無所不爲而卒不能以有爲也必也愼擇於
萬感之交而可止則止確乎有不易之操斯順
應於羣動之接而當行則行毅然有必爲之勇
非其道也所不爲矣道之所在則舉世所不敢
爲而獨爲之辦天下之大事者立天下之大節
者也非其義也所不爲矣義之所在則舉世所
不能爲而獨爲之有天下之定力者嚴天下之
定守者也自不爲者觀之聲色不大若難以有
爲望之矣而不知養有爲於不爲之中其機自
punctuated:
考試官教諭戴批：〔通達。〕
考試官教諭楊批：〔氣昌。〕
大賢論人之所以能有爲者，欲其愼之於爲也。甚矣，事不可以妄爲也！有不爲則知愼矣，其能有爲也固宜。孟子之意，蓋曰：天下之事，麗於人之無爲，而亦僨於人之有爲。非爲之過也，不善爲者之過也。何則？宇宙之事，皆吾分内之事，孰非人之所當爲者乎？然天下之事，天下之理宰之，亦孰非爲之所當擇者乎？人惟漫無所擇，宜其無所不爲，而卒不能以有爲也。必也愼擇於萬感之交，而可止則止，確乎有不易之操；斯順應於羣動之接，而當行則行，毅然有必爲之勇。非其道也，所不爲矣；道之所在，則舉世所不敢爲而獨爲之。辦天下之大事者，立天下之大節者也。非其義也，所不爲矣；義之所在，則舉世所不能爲而獨爲之。有天下之定力者，嚴天下之定守者也。自不爲者觀之，聲色不大，若難以有爲望之矣，而不知養有爲於不爲之中，其機自

Examiner and Instructor Dai's comment: [Lucid and thorough.]
Examiner and Instructor Yang's comment: [Vigorous in spirit.]
When the great Worthy discussed how a person becomes capable of great action, he wished for people to be cautious in what they do. Indeed, affairs must not be undertaken recklessly! If there are things one refuses to do, then one knows caution; that such a person is then capable of great action is only natural. Mencius's meaning is roughly this: the affairs of the world suffer from people's inaction, yet they are also ruined by people's action. This is not the fault of action itself, but the fault of those who do not know how to act well. Why is this? All affairs in the universe are affairs within our own duty—which of them is not something a person ought to do? Yet the affairs of the world are governed by the principles of the world—which of them is not something in which one ought to exercise choice when acting? It is only when people make no choices at all and act indiscriminately that, as might be expected, there is nothing they will not do, and in the end they are incapable of accomplishing anything of value. One must carefully choose amidst the convergence of ten thousand influences, stopping when it is proper to stop, with a firm and unalterable integrity; only then can one respond harmoniously upon encountering the myriad movements of the world, acting when it is proper to act, with the resolute courage to do what must be done. If it is not the Way, one will not do it; yet where the Way lies, one will single-handedly do what the whole world dares not do. He who accomplishes the great affairs of the world is he who establishes the great moral integrity of the world. If it is not rightness, one will not do it; yet where rightness lies, one will single-handedly do what the whole world is unable to do. He who possesses the steadfast strength of the world is he who strictly maintains the steadfast principles of the world. Viewed from the aspect of what he refuses to do, he makes no great display of sound or countenance, as if one could hardly expect great accomplishments from him—not knowing that by nurturing the capacity for action within non-action, its vital mechanism naturally…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
裕自有爲者觀之經綸不匱若非不爲者所與
能矣而不知運不爲於有爲之際其用自神人
之可以有爲也非其有所不爲而能然哉吁志
於有爲者亦無爲其所不爲而已矣考諸孟氏
集義善養大任不動卽不爲有爲之說也學者
於平居之時見理不精不能養成此氣則臨事
而餒固其所矣後世有不求聞達而復延漢祚
者其亦與聞斯義者乎故曰三代之遺也
易
自上下下其道大光
===
范醇敬
同考試官訓導吳　批〔有氣象有發揮非苟作者〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔明瑩〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔雅健〕
人君澤溥於下而益道丕顯矣夫王者以萬物
得所爲極致也自上下下澤斯溥矣益道其丕
顯哉夫子彖益之意蓋曰天之立君以爲民也
君之益民以盡道也是故膏澤下於民而君道
punctuated:
裕；自有爲者觀之，經綸不匱，若非不爲者所與能矣，而不知運不爲於有爲之際，其用自神。人之可以有爲也，非其有所不爲而能然哉？吁！志於有爲者，亦無爲其所不爲而已矣。考諸孟氏，集義善養、大任不動，卽不爲有爲之說也。學者於平居之時，見理不精，不能養成此氣，則臨事而餒，固其所矣。後世有不求聞達，而復延漢祚者，其亦與聞斯義者乎！故曰「三代之遺」也。

《易》：「自上下下，其道大光。」
范醇敬

人君澤溥於下，而益道丕顯矣。夫王者以萬物得所爲極致也，自上下下，澤斯溥矣，益道其丕顯哉！夫子《彖》《益》之意，蓋曰：天之立君，以爲民也；君之益民，以盡道也。是故膏澤下於民，而君道
translation_en:
…ample; viewed from the perspective of what he does do, his statecraft is inexhaustible, as though it were something beyond the capacity of one who refrains from acting—yet people do not realize that by exercising restraint amidst action, its efficacy becomes naturally marvellous. That a person is capable of great action—is it not because there are things he refuses to do that he can be so? Alas! Those who aspire to great accomplishments need only refrain from doing what should not be done, and nothing more. If we examine the teachings of Mencius, his doctrines of accumulating righteousness and skillfully nourishing the vital氣, and of remaining unmoved when entrusted with a great responsibility, are precisely this principle of refraining from action in order to act. If in ordinary times a scholar fails to discern principles with precision and cannot nourish and cultivate this vital energy, then when confronted with affairs he will inevitably lose courage. In later ages, there was one who did not seek fame and prominence, yet went on to prolong the dynastic fortune of Han [i.e. Zhuge Liang]—was he not also one who had heard and grasped this meaning? Hence it was said of him that he was "a remnant of the Three Dynasties."

Book of Changes (Yi): "From above descending to the humble below, his way shines forth greatly." [Hexagram 42, Yi (Increase), Commentary on the Decision]
By Fan Chunjing 范醇敬.

Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Yang comments: [Refined and vigorous.]

When he descends from above to those below, his beneficence is thereby spread wide—how grandly manifest, then, is the Way of Increase! The Master's meaning in his Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) for the hexagram Increase (Yi) is, in effect: Heaven establishes the ruler for the sake of the people, and the ruler benefits the people in order to fulfill his Way. title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
不可尚也已卦體損上益下乃自上卦而下於
下卦之下焉則是大賚之恩由朝廷以達海隅
而無遠之弗屆厚施之惠本畿甸以及四方而
無一之不周其藏富於民也自其無藏於國者
貽之也而百姓咸足矣其散財於下也自其無
聚於上者致之也而兆民允賴矣如是而益道
有不大光已乎吾知屯膏者其施未光分財者
其及未大也茲則至仁廣被顯康濟四海之規
模大德弘敷彰利賴萬方之氣象人君通天下
===
爲一身而恩洽中外則斯世斯民無不各遂其
生矣博厚高明之績將與天地相爲昭焉豈曰
小補之哉人君合萬物爲一體而澤徧遐邇則
匹夫匹婦無不各得其所矣正大光明之業將
振古今而爲烈也豈曰小惠云乎哉吁此民悅
之所以無疆也而有益下之責者不可不盡其
道矣雖然道豈易盡哉惟有德者能之鹿臺鉅
橋積於商而散於周蓋作君師綏士女聖王之
心則然耳使內無愛民之實德不爲聚斂之謀
punctuated: 不可尚也已。卦體損上益下，乃自上卦而下於下卦之下焉。則是大賚之恩，由朝廷以達海隅，而無遠之弗屆；厚施之惠，本畿甸以及四方，而無一之不周。其藏富於民也，自其無藏於國者貽之也，而百姓咸足矣；其散財於下也，自其無聚於上者致之也，而兆民允賴矣。如是而益道有不大光已乎？吾知屯膏者，其施未光；分財者，其及未大也。茲則至仁廣被，顯康濟四海之規模；大德弘敷，彰利賴萬方之氣象。人君通天下爲一身，而恩洽中外，則斯世斯民無不各遂其生矣。博厚高明之績，將與天地相爲昭焉，豈曰小補之哉？人君合萬物爲一體，而澤徧遐邇，則匹夫匹婦無不各得其所矣。正大光明之業，將振古今而爲烈也，豈曰小惠云乎哉？吁！此民悅之所以無疆也，而有益下之責者，不可不盡其道矣。雖然，道豈易盡哉？惟有德者能之。鹿臺、鉅橋，積於商而散於周，蓋作君師、綏士女，聖王之心則然耳。使內無愛民之實德，不爲聚斂之謀，
translation_en: …cannot be surpassed. The structure of the hexagram diminishes the above to benefit the below, descending from the upper trigram to the bottom of the lower trigram. Thus, the grace of great bestowal extends from the royal court to the farthest corners of the seas, with no distant place unreached; the kindness of generous giving originates in the imperial domain and reaches the four quarters, leaving nothing unprovided for. Storing wealth among the people is bequeathed by not storing it in the state, and so the hundred surnames all have sufficiency; dispersing resources to those below is brought about by not amassing them above, and so the millions of people truly have something to rely upon. Being thus, how could the Way of Increase not be greatly glorious? I know that for one who hoards his favors, his giving is not glorious; for one who merely parcels out wealth, his reach is not great. Here, however, supreme benevolence is broadly extended, manifesting the grand scale of bringing peace and relief to the four seas; great virtue is widely spread, displaying thesplendid ethos of benefiting the myriad regions. When the ruler unites the whole world as a single body and his grace saturates both the interior and the exterior, then in this age and among these people there are none who do not fulfill their livelihood. Achievements vast, thick, high, and bright will shine forth alongside Heaven and Earth—how could this be called merely a minor help? When the ruler joins the myriad things into a single body and his beneficence reaches far and near alike, then every common man and woman without exception finds their proper place. An enterprise upright, great, glorious, and bright will stir past and present as a splendid achievement—how could this be spoken of as merely a petty favor? Ah! This is why the people's joy is boundless, and those who bear the responsibility of benefiting the below must not fail to fulfill this Way to the utmost. Even so, how could this Way be easily fulfilled? Only one who possesses virtue is capable of it. The treasures of the Stag Terrace (Lutai) and the Great Bridge Granary (Juqiao) were accumulated by the Shang and dispersed by the Zhou; for in acting as ruler and teacher and bringing comfort to men and women, such was simply the heart of the sage-king. If inwardly one lacks the genuine virtue of loving the people, then even if one does not engage in schemes of fiscal exaction,…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
則爲驩虞之霸矣何以稱於大光故夫子釋詞
而曰中正有慶此君臣一德之謂非上下受益
之本與
夫易聖人所以崇德而廣業也知崇禮卑
崇效天卑法地天地設位而易行乎其
中矣成性存存道義之門
劉三才

學者
===
考試官教諭戴　批〔理明詞暢〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔純正典雅〕
大傳舉聖人用易之全功以見易道之至也夫
體用備而天地參聖人德業之全也而皆有資
於易焉易道其至矣乎昔大傳之意若曰易之
爲書也固以發聖心之藴亦以爲聖學之資知
此則知其道之至矣彼語德業之兼至者必歸
諸聖人而聖人所以崇廣其德業者不外於易
理何也德之崇也本於知聖人窮易理於心則
punctuated:
則爲驩虞之霸矣，何以稱於「大光」？故夫子釋詞而曰「中正有慶」，此君臣一德之謂，非上下受益之本與？

「夫《易》，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。天地設位，而《易》行乎其中矣。成性存存，道義之門。」
