《大傳》舉聖人用《易》之全功，以見《易》道之至也。夫體用備而天地參，聖人德業之全也，而皆有資於《易》焉，《易》道其至矣乎！昔《大傳》之意若曰：《易》之爲書也，固以發聖心之藴，亦以爲聖學之資，知此則知其道之至矣。彼語德業之兼至者，必歸諸聖人；而聖人所以崇廣其德業者，不外於《易》理，何也？德之崇也本於知，聖人窮《易》理於心，則
translation_en:
… or else it will be the fleeting joy of a hegemon's rule. How then could it be praised as "greatly glorious"? Therefore, when the Master explained the text, he said, "Through centrality and correctness, there is blessing." This refers to sovereign and minister sharing a single virtue—is it not the foundation by which both above and below receive benefit?

"Now, the Changes (Yi) is that by which the sages exalt their virtue and broaden their enterprise. Wisdom is exalted and propriety is humble; the exalted emulates Heaven, and the humble takes Earth as its model. Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and the Changes operates within them. The completed nature is preserved and preserved again: this is the gate of the Way and of righteousness."
Liu Sancai 劉三才
Associate Examiner, Instructor Tang 湯, comments: [Its logical thread runs seamlessly through, and its thought is fine and meticulous; a scholar profound in the Changes.]
Examiner, Instructor Dai 戴, comments: [The reasoning is clear and the phrasing fluent.]
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊, comments: [Pure, correct, and classically elegant.]

The Great Commentary (Dazhuan) sets forth the complete achievement of the sages' use of the Changes in order to show the perfection of the Way of the Changes. Now, for substance and function to be complete and to form a triad with Heaven and Earth is the totality of the sages' virtue and enterprise; yet all of this draws upon the Changes. How supreme indeed is the Way of the Changes! Formerly, the meaning of the Great Commentary was as if to say: As a book, the Changes certainly serves to bring forth the store of the sage's mind, and it also serves as a resource for sagely learning; if one understands this, one understands the perfection of its Way. Those who speak of the joint perfection of virtue and enterprise must attribute it to the sages; yet that by which the sages exalt and broaden their virtue and enterprise lies nowhere outside the principles of the Changes. Why is this? The exalting of virtue is rooted in wisdom. When the sage exhausts the principles of the Changes in his mind, then…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
識見精明其知崇矣而崇有以效乎天一高明
之不可窮也業之廣也本於禮聖人循易理於
身則踐履篤實其禮卑矣而卑有以法乎地一
博厚之不可極也如是而德業之崇廣也有不
與天地爲一哉吾知天地奠位而變易流行此
固盛德大業之所由出也聖人崇效卑法而知
禮之成性者渾然其常存則體立用行而性眞
之感通者沛然其莫禦率之而爲道性外無道
也而時出不窮矣不爲道之門耶裁之而爲義
===
性外無義也而時措不匱矣不爲義之門耶其
與天地位而易行焉者何以異哉是道義之根
心即德之所以崇也道義之發外即業之所以
廣也而皆於易書資之易道之至也斷可識矣
雖然易不外於心也心者知禮之原三極之奧
也善用易者求之於吾心而不泥於法象之粗
迹則成性存而德業備直可以與天地參矣故
曰齋戒神明聖人之心易也其得於畫前者與
書
punctuated:
識見精明，其知崇矣，而崇有以效乎天，一高明之不可窮也。業之廣也本於禮，聖人循易理於身，則踐履篤實，其禮卑矣，而卑有以法乎地，一博厚之不可極也。如是，而德業之崇廣也，有不與天地爲一哉？吾知天地奠位而變易流行，此固盛德大業之所由出也。聖人崇效卑法，而知禮之成性者，渾然其常存；則體立用行，而性眞之感通者，沛然其莫禦。率之而爲道，性外無道也，而時出不窮矣，不爲道之門耶？裁之而爲義，性外無義也，而時措不匱矣，不爲義之門耶？其與天地位而易行焉者，何以異哉？是道義之根心，即德之所以崇也；道義之發外，即業之所以廣也。而皆於《易》書資之，易道之至也，斷可識矣。雖然，易不外於心也。心者，知禮之原，三極之奧也。善用《易》者，求之於吾心，而不泥於法象之粗迹，則成性存而德業備，直可以與天地參矣。故曰：「齋戒神明，聖人之心易也。」其得於畫前者與！

《書》
translation_en:
… his insight is refined and clear, so his knowledge is lofty; and in its loftiness it emulates Heaven—utterly high and bright, never to be exhausted. The breadth of accomplishments is rooted in ritual propriety: when the sage follows the principles of the Changes (Yi) in his own person, his practical conduct is earnest and substantial, so his ritual propriety is humble; and in its humility it models itself on Earth—utterly broad and thick, never to be fathomed. Being thus, in the loftiness and breadth of his virtue and accomplishments, how could he not be one with Heaven and Earth? I know that Heaven and Earth establish their positions and transformation and change flow through them—this is assuredly whence flourishing virtue and great accomplishments arise. When the sage emulates the lofty and models himself on the humble, the perfected nature of his knowledge and ritual propriety abides in渾然 (undivided) constancy; thus substance is established and function is carried out, and the sympathetic resonance of his true nature flows forth abundantly with nothing able to check it. Followed naturally, it becomes the Way—there is no Way outside of human nature—and as it issues forth at every moment without exhaustion, is it not the gateway of the Way? Regulated and measured, it becomes righteousness—there is no righteousness outside of human nature—and as it is applied at every moment without deficiency, is it not the gateway of righteousness? How does this differ from Heaven and Earth establishing their positions and the Changes operating within them? Therefore, the Way and righteousness taking root in the mind is precisely whereby virtue becomes lofty; the Way and righteousness manifesting on the outside is precisely whereby accomplishments become broad. And since all of this is drawn from the Book of Changes, the perfection of the Way of the Changes can be known beyond a doubt. Even so, the Changes are not external to the mind. The mind is the source of knowledge and ritual propriety, and the profound mystery of the Three Ultimates. One who is skilled at using the Changes seeks them within his own mind and does not cling to the coarse traces of models and images; then perfected nature is preserved and virtue and accomplishments are complete, so that he can directly form a triad with Heaven and Earth. Hence it is said: "Fasting and vigilance to spiritually illumine one's virtue—this is the Changes of the sage's mind." Is this not what is grasped prior to the drawing of the hexagrams!

Book of Documents (Shu)

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
無怠無荒四夷來王禹曰於帝念哉德惟
善政政在養民
董孚毓
同考試官訓導李　批〔益禹同心而其言意各有所重是文有照應而不牽强極爲得旨錄之以式多士〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔詞潔意透得禹益交儆之意〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔脫灑中有關鍵取之〕
大臣期君以保治之極功而同列因推其要焉
蓋治以格遠爲極功而養民其要也宜禹益以
===
之交相戒勉於君歟且帝舜之時無虞之世也
外夷服矣內治脩矣禹益之心猶未已也益旣
陳儆戒於帝矣猶以爲人君之心睹承平則易
怠也帝其誠之於思而所存者皆兢業之至意
人君之事撫盈成則易荒也帝其守之於爲而
所發者皆勵精之良圖斯則德盛而化益以神
文命所敷施及於蠻貊矣邇安而遠由以格聲
教所訖四夷咸歸嚮矣儆戒至是斯無虞可保
益之心卽禹祗承之心也故禹美其言之當念
punctuated:
「無怠無荒，四夷來王。」禹曰：「於！帝念哉！德惟善政，政在養民。」

董孚毓

同考試官訓導李　批〔益、禹同心，而其言意各有所重。是文有照應而不牽强，極爲得旨。錄之以式多士。〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔詞潔意透，得禹、益交儆之意。〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔脫灑中有關鍵，取之。〕

大臣期君以保治之極功，而同列因推其要焉。蓋治以格遠爲極功，而養民其要也，宜禹、益以之交相戒勉於君歟！

且帝舜之時，無虞之世也。外夷服矣，內治脩矣，禹、益之心猶未已也。益旣陳儆戒於帝矣，猶以爲人君之心，睹承平則易怠也，帝其誠之於思，而所存者皆兢業之至意；人君之事，撫盈成則易荒也，帝其守之於爲，而所發者皆勵精之良圖。斯則德盛而化益以神，文命所敷，施及於蠻貊矣；邇安而遠由以格，聲教所訖，四夷咸歸嚮矣。儆戒至是，斯無虞可保，益之心卽禹祗承之心也。故禹美其言之當念，
translation_en:
"Do not beindolent, do not be negligent, and the four distant tribes will come to acknowledge your sovereignty." Yu said, "Oh! May the Emperor bear this in mind! Virtue lies in good governance, and governance lies in nourishing the people."

Dong Fuyu 董孚毓

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Li 李, comments: [Yi 益 and Yu 禹 shared the same mind, yet the thrust of their words each had its own emphasis. This essay maintains mutual correspondence between the two parts without being forced, grasping the main purport exceedingly well. I record it to serve as a model for the many scholars.]
Examiner, Instructor Dai 戴, comments: [The diction is clean and the meaning penetrating; it captures the intent of Yu and Yi joining in admonition.]
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊, comments: [Amidst its free and unrestrained style, it holds fast to the crucial points. Selected.]

A great minister expects of his sovereign the ultimate achievement in preserving good order, and his colleague thereupon deduces its essential basis. Indeed, while good order takes winning over the distant as its ultimate achievement, nourishing the people is its essential basis; how fitting it was that Yu and Yi used these ideas to join in admonishing and encouraging their sovereign!

Moreover, the time of Emperor Shun 舜 was an age free of cause for anxiety. The outer tribes had submitted, and internal governance had been put in order; yet the minds of Yu and Yi were still not at rest. After Yi had set forth his admonition regarding vigilance to the Emperor, he still considered that the mind of a ruler, upon witnessing peace and order, easily grows indolent: may the Emperor make his thoughts sincere, so that all he harbors within is the utmost intention of cautious diligence; and that the affairs of a ruler, when presiding over fullness and completion, easily fall into negligence: may the Emperor guard his actions, so that all he puts forth are sound plans of vigorous dedication. Thus virtue will flourish and transformation will grow ever more miraculous, and the civilizing mandate that is spread abroad will extend even to the Man and Mo tribes; those near at hand will be at peace and through them the distant will be won over, and wherever his renown and teachings reach, the four distant tribes will all turn to him in allegiance. When vigilance and admonition reach this point, then freedom from anxiety can be preserved; the mind of Yi was none other than Yu's own mind of reverent compliance. Therefore Yu praised his words as worthy of being borne in mind…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
而曰至治固足以來遠而出治必先於安民人
君之居於民上者孰不有德乎然非徒善已也
嘗以美意而行良法焉亦孰不有政乎然非徒
法已也在以一人而養天下焉外之以養其身
是爲因天之政而德澤由此其播也內之以養
其心是爲長人之政而德教由此其宣也不是
之務則中土且有未安矣將何以來四夷乎德
政且有未脩矣安在其無怠荒乎是養民者又
儆戒之實功而無虞之所由臻也帝其念之哉
===
吁益之言來王要其成也禹之言養民原其始
也以舜在上而禹益惓惓交警如此無爲而治
有由然與雖然此自帝德罔愆者言耳後之人
君莫要於脩德焉德立則政舉內之順治外之
威嚴胥此致也否則粉飾治具耳誇功絕域耳
奚安攘之足云故曰有天德乃可語王道
嚴惟丕式克用三宅三俊
鍾應麟
同考試官教諭張　批〔此題全重在君能用宅俊上旣〕
punctuated:
而曰：至治固足以來遠，而出治必先於安民。人君之居於民上者，孰不有德乎？然非徒善已也，嘗以美意而行良法焉。亦孰不有政乎？然非徒法已也，在以一人而養天下焉。外之以養其身，是爲因天之政，而德澤由此其播也；內之以養其心，是爲長人之政，而德教由此其宣也。不是之務，則中土且有未安矣，將何以來四夷乎？德政且有未脩矣，安在其無怠荒乎？是養民者，又儆戒之實功，而無虞之所由臻也，帝其念之哉！吁！益之言來王，要其成也；禹之言養民，原其始也。以舜在上，而禹、益惓惓交警如此，無爲而治，有由然與！雖然，此自帝德罔愆者言耳。後之人君，莫要於脩德焉。德立則政舉，內之順治，外之威嚴，胥此致也。否則粉飾治具耳，誇功絕域耳，奚安攘之足云？故曰：有天德，乃可語王道。

嚴惟丕式克用三宅三俊
鍾應麟
同考試官教諭張　批〔此題全重在君能用宅俊上。旣〕
translation_en:
… and said: Perfect governance is indeed sufficient to draw the distant near, yet producing good governance must begin with giving peace to the people. Among rulers who dwell above the people, who does not possess virtue? Yet it is not mere goodness alone; one must implement fine laws with benevolent intent. And who does not have governance? Yet it is not mere laws alone; it lies in one man nourishing all under Heaven. Externally, nourishing their bodies is governance that accords with Heaven, and through this, virtuous bounty is spread; internally, nourishing their minds is governance that nurtures humanity, and through this, virtuous instruction is proclaimed. If one does not attend to this, even the central lands will not yet be at peace—how then could one bring the four barbarian tribes to come in submission? Virtue and governance will not yet be cultivated—where then would be the freedom from idleness and neglect? Thus, nourishing the people is the substantive work of vigilance and caution, and the means by which freedom from anxiety is attained. May the Emperor keep this in mind!

Alas! When Yi spoke of the coming of the barbarian kings, he was summing up the ultimate achievement; when Yu spoke of nourishing the people, he was tracing the original root. With Shun above, and Yu and Yi earnestly admonishing one another like this, was there not a reason that he governed through non-action? Even so, this was spoken with reference to an Emperor whose virtue was already without fault. For rulers of later ages, nothing is more essential than cultivating virtue. When virtue is established, governance is upheld; Domestic harmony and order within, and awe-inspiring dignity abroad, are both brought about by this. Otherwise, one is merely glossing over the instruments of governance, or boasting of achievements in remote regions—how could that be worthy of being called pacifying within and repelling without? Therefore it is said: Only when one possesses Heavenly virtue can one speak of the Kingly Way.

"Strictly contemplating and greatly emulating, he was able to employ the three appointees to office and the three men of eminence." [Book of Documents, "Li zheng"]
Zhong Yinglin 鍾應麟
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhang, comments: [The entire emphasis of this topic lies on the ruler's ability to employ the appointees and men of eminence. Since …]

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
士子只以盡職者才講多失本意是作融會體貼不襲常套取之
考試官教諭戴　批〔發得成湯克用之意透徹可玩〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔莊重典麗雅有理趣〕
聖王純於任賢斯有以盡其用矣蓋任賢貴於
勿貳也嚴恩而大法之則純矣謂不有以盡宅
俊之用乎周公舉湯之知恤者告成王曰君必
資賢以弘化賢則資君以效用此相須之甚殷
而其機實係之君者湯既即宅即俊矣使存之
心者有未專焉非所以能用也湯則精神心術
===
日與宅俊相孚契焉而一話一言皆紬繹之不
忘蓋上帝之臣本簡在于帝心而思之敢不敬
與使發之事者有或違焉未見其能用也湯則
經綸設施日與宅俊相依據焉而一猷一為務
則效之無外蓋上帝之事本資理于帝臣而法
之敢不大與斯則內外一致而信任之篤自有
以發其靖獻之忠心迹俱融而知遇之殊自有
以觸其啓沃之良賢臣以心效之君常懼君不
我信耳茲惟思之者敬焉則得君行志此其時
punctuated:
士子只以盡職者才講，多失本意。是作融會體貼，不襲常套，取之。
考試官教諭戴　批〔發得成湯克用之意透徹，可玩。〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔莊重典麗，雅有理趣。〕
聖王純於任賢，斯有以盡其用矣。蓋任賢貴於勿貳也，嚴恩而大法之，則純矣，謂不有以盡宅俊之用乎？周公舉湯之知恤者告成王曰：君必資賢以弘化，賢則資君以效用，此相須之甚殷，而其機實係之君者。湯既即宅、即俊矣，使存之心者有未專焉，非所以能用也。湯則精神心術，日與宅俊相孚契焉，而一話一言，皆紬繹之不忘，蓋上帝之臣，本簡在于帝心，而思之敢不敬與？使發之事者有或違焉，未見其能用也。湯則經綸設施，日與宅俊相依據焉，而一猷一為，務則效之無外，蓋上帝之事，本資理于帝臣，而法之敢不大與？斯則內外一致，而信任之篤，自有以發其靖獻之忠；心迹俱融，而知遇之殊，自有以觸其啓沃之良。賢臣以心效之君，常懼君不我信耳；茲惟思之者敬焉，則得君行志，此其時
translation_en:
… the candidates merely expound upon their fulfilling their duties and manifesting their talents [?], mostly missing the original intent. This essay synthesizes and closely grasps the meaning without following common clichés; I select it.]
Examiner and Instructor Dai comments: [It brings out the meaning of Tang the Successful being able to employ them thoroughly and is worthy of appreciation.]
Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: [Dignified and classically elegant, with refined philosophical appeal.]

When the sage king is pure in employing the worthy, he thereby exhausts their usefulness. Indeed, in employing the worthy, what is valued is having no doubts; when one reverently contemplates them [reading 恩 as 思] and grandly emulates them, one is pure in doing so—could it be said that he does not thereby exhaust the usefulness of those in the three positions and the men of the three grades of ability? The Duke of Zhou cited how Tang knew to show solicitude in order to instruct King Cheng, saying: The ruler must rely on the worthy to broaden transformation, and the worthy rely on the ruler to render their service; this mutual need is most earnest, yet its pivot truly rests with the ruler. Once Tang had approached those in the positions and approached the men of ability, had what he held in his mind been less than undivided, it would not have been the way to be able to employ them. Instead, Tang in his spirit and mental dispositions daily accorded in mutual trust with those in the positions and the men of ability, and every word and utterance he drew out and pondered without forgetting; for the ministers of the Supreme Lord were originally selected in the mind of the Lord—in contemplating them, how could he dare not be reverent? Had what was manifested in affairs ever run counter to them, it would not have shown that he was able to employ them. Instead, Tang in his governance and measures daily relied upon those in the positions and the men of ability, and in every plan and action he strove to model himself upon them without exception; for the affairs of the Supreme Lord originally depended on the ministers of the Lord for their ordering—in emulating them, how could he dare not do so grandly? Thus inside and outside were one, and the earnestness of his trust naturally sufficed to call forth their loyalty in calmly offering their service; mind and outward traces were both harmonized, and the exceptional nature of his recognition naturally sufficed to stir their goodness in enlightening and enriching his mind. When worthy ministers offer their minds in service to the ruler, they always fear only that the ruler will not trust them; now, since he contemplated them with reverence, this was the very time to win the ruler's confidence and carry out their aspirations…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
也曰宅曰俊咸將精白自矢以共圖耿命之釐
矣有不傾心報國者誰與賢臣以身許之君常
懼君不我任耳茲惟法之者大焉則秉時底績
此其會也若宅若俊率皆寅恭自盡以協釐上
帝之命矣有不竭力從王者誰與是或效其職
或著其才固宅俊之各盡所用也而職之得效
才之得著詎非成湯之能盡其用哉吁湯之知
恤如此其登于至治宜矣成王尚其鑒茲噫用
賢急矣純心要焉一有不純則聲色貨利將貳
之矣嚴思之論旨哉言也彼不冠不見者敬而
實疎謙讓未遑者悅而不繹皆心之不純耳故
曰心純則賢才輔
===
詩
子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
荀自新
同考試官訓導孫　批　〔子孫衍而德位隆正周臣頌君〕
〔至意是篇不尚雕飾典雅和平宜錄以式〕
考試官教諭戴　批　〔溫雅中鋪敘明白得施經義者〕
punctuated:
也。曰宅曰俊，咸將精白自矢，以共圖耿命之釐矣，有不傾心報國者誰與？賢臣以身許之君，常懼君不我任耳；茲惟法之者大焉，則秉時底績，此其會也。若宅若俊，率皆寅恭自盡，以協釐上帝之命矣，有不竭力從王者誰與？是或效其職，或著其才，固宅、俊之各盡所用也；而職之得效，才之得著，詎非成湯之能盡其用哉？吁！湯之知恤如此，其登于至治宜矣，成王尚其鑒茲！噫！用賢急矣，純心要焉；一有不純，則聲色貨利將貳之矣。嚴思之論，旨哉言也！彼不冠不見者，敬而實疎；謙讓未遑者，悅而不繹，皆心之不純耳。故曰：心純則賢才輔。

《詩》
「子孫千億，穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。」
荀自新
同考試官訓導孫　批：〔子孫衍而德位隆，正周臣頌君至意。是篇不尚雕飾，典雅和平，宜錄以式。〕
考試官教諭戴　批：〔溫雅中鋪敘明白，得施經義者。〕
translation_en:
…! Those called the holders of office and the men of eminence will all pledge themselves in pure devotion to jointly plan the ordering of the bright mandate; who among them would not pour out his heart to repay the state? Worthy ministers dedicate their persons to their ruler, ever fearing only that the ruler will not entrust them with responsibility. Now, since his emulation of them is so great, this is the very opportunity to seize the moment and achieve results. Both the holders of office and the men of eminence will all exhaust themselves in reverent diligence to harmoniously order the mandate of the Supreme Sovereign; who among them would not exert all his strength to follow the king? Thus, whether by fulfilling their duties or by displaying their talents, the holders of office and men of eminence indeed each exhaust their usefulness; yet that their duties are fulfilled and their talents displayed—is this not because Tang the Successful was able to employ them to the fullest? Alas! Since Tang knew how to show such solicitous care, it was fitting that he ascended to the summit of governance; may King Cheng take this as his mirror! Ah! Employing the worthy is urgent, and keeping a pure heart is essential. Once there is the slightest impurity, sensual pleasures and material gain will divide it. How profound are the words of Yan Si's discourse! Those who would not receive a minister without putting on a cap showed respect yet were actually distant; those who pleaded modesty and lack of leisure were pleased with advice yet failed to follow it through—all because their hearts were not pure. Therefore it is said: When the ruler's heart is pure, worthy talents will assist him.

Book of Odes (Shijing)
"His sons and grandsons are a hundred thousand million; reverent and august, fit to be lords, fit to be kings."
By Xun Zixin
Associate Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: [That descendants multiply and both virtue and position are exalted is precisely the ultimate meaning of the Zhou ministers' eulogy to their ruler. This essay does not prize ornate embellishment; it is classical, elegant, and harmonious, and ought to be recorded as a model.]
Examiner Dai, Instructor, comments: [Amidst gentle elegance, the exposition is clear and plain—one who has grasped how to unfold the meaning of the Classic.]

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭楊　批〔詞旨冠冕忠愛藹然〕
詩人願王之多嗣有德以宜其位焉夫王嗣係
天下之重也有敬美之德宜君王之位王者之
福於是乎全矣此公尸所以答鳧鷖也若曰人
君統天下以爲治自當斂天下以爲福王之千
祿而獲百福也何如蓋福于一身而不及于子
孫非福也福于子孫而不隆其德位非全福也
吾願和氣攸鍾毓之爲多男之慶自子而孫蓋
有千焉天潢之派此其承之矣明德所感錫之
===
爲繼曜之祥由子而孫蓋有億焉雲仍之秀此
其衍之矣然是子孫也莫不至德淵微而形迹
之俱泯玄機密勿而朕兆之莫窺穆穆然邃以
密焉一緝熙執競之遺風也金玉完其質而至
善之無瑕追琢成其章而衆美之咸備皇皇然
瑩以粹焉一徽柔於皇之遺範也吾見以是德
而爲君則必乃心王室日嚴祇敬之謨恪守侯
封懋宣亮釆之績無有不宜者矣視吾王以顯
德而宜民人者不爲之媲美也耶以是德而爲
punctuated:
考試官教諭楊　批〔詞旨冠冕，忠愛藹然〕

詩人願王之多嗣，有德以宜其位焉。夫王嗣，係天下之重也。有敬美之德，宜君王之位，王者之福於是乎全矣，此公尸所以答《鳧鷖》也。若曰：人君統天下以爲治，自當斂天下以爲福。王之千祿而獲百福也何如？蓋福于一身而不及于子孫，非福也；福于子孫而不隆其德位，非全福也。吾願和氣攸鍾，毓之爲多男之慶，自子而孫，蓋有千焉，天潢之派此其承之矣；明德所感，錫之爲繼曜之祥，由子而孫，蓋有億焉，雲仍之秀此其衍之矣。然是子孫也，莫不至德淵微，而形迹之俱泯；玄機密勿，而朕兆之莫窺。穆穆然邃以密焉，一緝熙執競之遺風也。金玉完其質，而至善之無瑕；追琢成其章，而衆美之咸備。皇皇然瑩以粹焉，一徽柔於皇之遺範也。吾見以是德而爲君，則必乃心王室，日嚴祇敬之謨；恪守侯封，懋宣亮釆之績，無有不宜者矣。視吾王以顯德而宜民人者，不爲之媲美也耶？以是德而爲
translation_en:
Examiner, Instructor Yang, comments: [The diction and purport are dignified and noble, brimming with loyalty and affection.]

The poet wishes for the king to have abundant heirs who possess the virtue to befit their positions. Now, the royal heirs bear the weight of all under heaven. When they possess reverent and admirable virtue and are well-suited to the positions of feudal lords and king, the blessings of a true king are thereby made complete. This is how the impersonator of the dead responds in the ode "Wild Ducks" (Fu yi). It is as if to say: since a ruler unifies all under heaven to govern, he naturally ought to gather the blessings of all under heaven as his own. How is it that the king, in seeking emolument [read 干祿 for 千祿], obtains a hundred blessings? For blessing that rests in one's own person alone and does not extend to one's sons and grandsons is no true blessing; and blessing that extends to one's sons and grandsons without exalting their virtue and position is no complete blessing. I wish that where harmoniousvitality concentrates, it may nurture the joyous fortune of many sons, so that from sons to grandsons there may be a thousand—by this the lineage of the heavenly clan shall be carried on! And that what is moved by bright virtue may bestow the auspicious sign of succeeding brilliance, so that from sons to grandsons there may be a hundred million—by this the flower of distant descendants shall be propagated! Yet of these sons and grandsons, there is none whose supreme virtue is not deep and subtle, with all outward traces obliterated, and whose profound workings are not assiduous and secret, with no sign or omen to be glimpsed. Deeply reverent (mumu), profound and mysterious, this is wholly the bequeathed ethos of radiant continuity and steadfast strength. Like gold and jade, they perfect their substance so that their supreme goodness is without flaw; carved and polished, they complete their pattern so that every excellence is fully present. Splendidly majestic (huanghuang), lustrous and pure, this is wholly the bequeathed model of gentle mildness and august majesty. I see that if with such virtue one serves as a feudal lord, he will surely set his heart on the royal house, daily holding in awe the counsels of reverent respect, and faithfully guard his enfeoffed domain, strenuously manifesting achievements that brighten governance—in nothing will he fail to be fitting! Compared with our king, who by his illustrious virtue is fitting to the common people and officers, does he not rival him in beauty? And if with such virtue one serves as…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
王則必建其有極南面顯恭己之容嗣守丕基
四海仰圭璋之德無有不宜者矣視吾王以令
德而宜民人者不爲之匹休也耶必如是而後
爲君福之全必如是而後滿吾人之願所謂自
天申之者申此而已吁詩人忠愛之情寧有既
哉雖然猶未已也曰不愆不忘守法度也曰無
怨無惡親賢才也終之曰不懈于位有深慮焉
蓋有初鮮終人主之恒患必至于匪懈民安而
社稷靈長之慶終賴之矣然則假樂之詩固萬
===
世君天下者所當繹哉
有飶其香邦家之光有椒其馨胡考之寧
匪且有且匪今斯今振古如茲
李遇春
同考試官訓導龔 批〔士子講豐年類襲浮詞此作獨 昌明典重發出成周太和氣象錄之〕
考試官教諭戴 批〔摘寫周人燕饗報賽處詞旨朗然〕
考試官教諭楊 批〔典嚴莊重亦有豐年穰穰氣象〕
周人敘農事之慶而遡其由來之遠焉夫尊賢
punctuated:
王，則必建其有極，南面顯恭己之容，嗣守丕基，四海仰圭璋之德，無有不宜者矣。視吾王以令德而宜民人者，不爲之匹休也耶？必如是，而後爲君福之全；必如是，而後滿吾人之願。所謂「自天申之」者，申此而已。吁！詩人忠愛之情，寧有既哉？雖然，猶未已也。曰「不愆不忘」，守法度也；曰「無怨無惡」，親賢才也；終之曰「不懈于位」，有深慮焉。蓋有初鮮終，人主之恒患；必至于匪懈民安，而社稷靈長之慶，終賴之矣。然則《假樂》之詩，固萬世君天下者所當繹哉！
有飶其香，邦家之光；有椒其馨，胡考之寧。匪且有且，匪今斯今，振古如茲。
李遇春
同考試官訓導龔批：〔士子講豐年類襲浮詞，此作獨昌明典重，發出成周太和氣象，錄之。〕
考試官教諭戴批：〔摘寫周人燕饗報賽處，詞旨朗然。〕
考試官教諭楊批：〔典嚴莊重，亦有豐年穰穰氣象。〕
周人敘農事之慶，而遡其由來之遠焉。夫尊賢
translation_en:
… a king, then he will surely establish the Supreme Ultimate, displaying a demeanor of self-reverence while facing south, succeeding to and guarding the great foundation, while the Four Seas look up to his jade-like virtue—in nothing will he not be fitting. Compared with our king who through his admirable virtue is fitting toward the common people and officials, does he not match his glory? Only when it is necessarily like this is the ruler's blessing complete; only when it is necessarily like this are our wishes fulfilled. What is meant by "from Heaven it is renewed" is simply the renewal of this. Alas! Could the loyal and affectionate feelings of the poet ever come to an end? Even so, it is not yet finished. When it says "neither erring nor forgetting," that refers to observing the laws and regulations; when it says "neither resented nor disliked," that refers to drawing close to the worthy and talented; and when it concludes by saying "never怠 [remiss] in his position," there is deep forethought in it. For having a good beginning but rarely a good end is the constant malady of rulers; only when it reaches the point of untiring diligence and the peace of the people will the long-enduring felicity of the altars of soil and grain ultimately depend upon it. If so, then the ode "Jia le" (Felicitous and Joyous) is indeed something that those who rule All under Heaven for ten thousand generations ought to ponder!

"Fragrant is the aroma, the glory of the state and family; / Aromatic is the pepper-scent, the peace of the aged and long-lived. / Not only here is it thus, not only now is it so; / From remote antiquity it has been like this." [Classic of Poetry, "Zai shan"]

Li Yuchun

Examiner Instructor Yang comments: [Classical, rigorous, and dignified; it also possesses the abundant, flourishing atmosphere of a bountiful year.]

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
養老皆農事之慶也遡諸古而有然焉神既之
厚何如哉宜周人歌之以報賽也以為國以有
年為瑞而禮以報本為先乃今利之所獲豈徒
烝祖妣而已哉彼國有仁賢饗禮所當舉也茲
以飶然其香者燕我嘉賓焉則明良胥接而樽
俎增輝上下泰交而廟廊生色人文煥而帝載
熙矣邦家不以之光乎國有老成養禮不可廢
也茲以椒然其馨者供我耆老焉則太和保合
而逸豫無期元氣滋培而康寧永錫高年尊而
===
眉壽介矣胡考不以之寧乎凡此固穡事所由
成而豐年所由致矣然匪且有之匪今見之也
蓋我周以農事為重修此稼穡之圖上天以率
育為心貽此豐穰之利言乎肇基同此芟柞亦
同此收成若是有常憲焉神之敷錫者蓋有年
矣則夫嘉會之典不過率由之耳向使不原於
古而何經畫之詳如此哉言乎守成均此耕耘
亦均此收穫若是有成規焉我之利賴者非一
日矣則夫尊養之禮不過率循之耳向使古奉
punctuated: 養老，皆農事之慶也，遡諸古而有然焉，神既之厚何如哉！宜周人歌之以報賽也。以為國以有年為瑞，而禮以報本為先。乃今利之所獲，豈徒烝祖妣而已哉？彼國有仁賢，饗禮所當舉也。茲以飶然其香者，燕我嘉賓焉，則明良胥接而樽俎增輝，上下泰交而廟廊生色，人文煥而帝載熙矣，邦家不以之光乎？國有老成，養禮不可廢也。茲以椒然其馨者，供我耆老焉，則太和保合而逸豫無期，元氣滋培而康寧永錫，高年尊而眉壽介矣，胡考不以之寧乎？凡此固穡事所由成，而豐年所由致矣。然匪且有之，匪今見之也。蓋我周以農事為重，修此稼穡之圖；上天以率育為心，貽此豐穰之利。言乎肇基，同此芟柞，亦同此收成，若是有常憲焉，神之敷錫者蓋有年矣，則夫嘉會之典，不過率由之耳，向使不原於古，而何經畫之詳如此哉？言乎守成，均此耕耘，亦均此收穫，若是有成規焉，我之利賴者非一日矣，則夫尊養之禮，不過率循之耳，向使古奉
translation_en:
… and nourishing the aged are both celebrations arising from agricultural labors. Tracing this back to antiquity, it has ever been so—how generous are the blessings [?] of the spirits! Fittingly did the people of Zhou sing of this in their thanksgiving sacrifices.

They considered that a state takes an abundant year as an auspicious sign, while ritual puts repaying one's origins first. Yet with the bounty harvested today, how could it merely be for making winter offerings to the ancestors and ancestresses? When a state possesses benevolent and worthy men, the rite of feasting ought to be held. Now, taking that which is so richly fragrant, we feast our honored guests: thus enlightened ruler and worthy ministers meet together and the goblets and sacrificial stands gain luster; superior and inferior commune in harmony and the court takes on a vibrant air; human culture shines forth and the sovereign's undertakings prosper—is not the state thereby made glorious? When a state possesses experienced elders, the rite of nourishing the aged cannot be neglected. Now, taking that which has a peppery aroma, we provide for our aged elders: thus supreme harmony is preserved in union and leisure and joy are boundless; the vital氣 (vital energy) is nurtured and health and tranquility are eternally bestowed; advanced years are honored and longevity is aided—are not the aged thereby brought peace?

All of this is indeed brought to completion through the work of husbandry and brought about by an abundant year. Yet it is not merely here that this exists, nor merely today that this is seen. For our Zhou holds agriculture to be of utmost importance, cultivating these plans for sowing and reaping; High Heaven takes universal nurture as its heart, bequeathing this benefit of abundant harvests. Speaking of the founding of the dynasty, there was this same clearing of weeds and felling of trees, and likewise this same harvesting of crops, as if there were an invariable statute; what the spirits have spread and bestowed has indeed lasted for many years. Thus the ceremonies of auspicious assembly do no more than follow along with them. Had they not originated in antiquity, how could the planning and arrangement be so detailed as this? Speaking of the preservation of the heritage, there is equally this plowing and weeding, and equally this reaping and harvesting, as if there were an established rule; what we have profited from and relied upon is not of a single day. Thus the rites of honoring the worthy and nourishing the aged do no more than conform to them. Had antiquity [not?]…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
有行而何儀制之備如此哉夫以今觀古旣能
修遺典於不匱則以後視今亦將衍成法於不
窮神錫之釐厚矣報賽其容已乎大抵周以農
事開國君臣上下罔不憂勤周公以成王未知
稼穡艱難故訓無逸陳豳風尤惓惓焉老成之
愛君固若此厥後臣工有嗟噫嘻有戒甚矣成
王重農之心有似乎先公也乃今讀載芟良耜
不獨頌成王之德而稱周公之功不衰
春秋
秋及江人黃人伐陳〔僖公四年九月戊辰〕
諸侯盟于葵丘〔僖公九年〕
鄧應祈
考試官教諭戴　批〔春秋予桓全爲攘夷尊王此作〕
發揮明悉宜錄以式
考試官教諭楊　批〔嚴整明切〕
===
伯主之攘夷而尊王春秋兩驗之焉此卽伐陳
而知攘楚不可無桓卽盟葵丘而知尊王不可
無桓也自采薇遠而爲侁之橫恣陽穀有會誠
punctuated:
有行，而何儀制之備如此哉？夫以今觀古，旣能修遺典於不匱；則以後視今，亦將衍成法於不窮。神錫之釐厚矣，報賽其容已乎？大抵周以農事開國，君臣上下罔不憂勤。周公以成王未知稼穡艱難，故訓《無逸》，陳《豳風》，尤惓惓焉，老成之愛君固若此。厥後《臣工》有嗟，《噫嘻》有戒，甚矣，成王重農之心有似乎先公也！乃今讀《載芟》、《良耜》，不獨頌成王之德，而稱周公之功不衰。

《春秋》
「秋，及江人、黃人伐陳。」〔僖公四年〕「九月戊辰，諸侯盟于葵丘。」〔僖公九年〕
鄧應祈
考試官教諭戴　批：〔《春秋》予桓，全爲攘夷尊王。此作〕發揮明悉，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭楊　批：〔嚴整明切。〕

translation_en:
… [if it were not already] practiced [in antiquity], how could the ritual regulations be so complete as this? Now, looking at antiquity from the present, since we have been able to cultivate the inherited canons without fail, then when future generations look back at the present, they too will extend these established laws without end. The blessings bestowed by the spirits are generous indeed; how could the thanksgiving sacrifices be allowed to cease?

In general, the Zhou founded its state upon agriculture, and from sovereign and ministers above to those below, there were none who did not labor with anxious diligence. Because King Cheng did not yet know the hardships of sowing and reaping, the Duke of Zhou instructed him with "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) and set forth the "Airs of Bin" (Binfeng) with particular earnestness; such was the seasoned statesman's love for his ruler. Thereafter, there were the exhortations in "Ministers and Officers" (Chengong) and the admonitions in "Oh, Yes!" (Yixi)—profound indeed was the way King Cheng's mind in valuing agriculture resembled that of the former dukes! And so today, when reading "Clearing the Grass" (Zaishan) and "Good Plowshares" (Liangsi), one not only praises the virtue of King Cheng, but also celebrates the unceasing merit of the Duke of Zhou.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"In autumn, [Qi and others] together with the men of Jiang and the men of Huang invaded Chen" [Fourth year of Duke Xi]; "In the ninth month, on the wuchen day, the feudal lords covenanted at Kuiqiu" [Ninth year of Duke Xi].

Deng Yingqi 鄧應祈

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
攘夷之一大機也或謂江黄未同伐楚也何以
知爲謀楚而予桓君子曰蓋至伐陳而桓之攘
夷驗矣夫有正有奇軍之善政也桓惟始會陽
穀也誓及江黄而伏奇之謀定焉則不待威申
列國之衆款納兩廣之雄已先楚而奪之氣矣
而今之連兵伐陳也非以終陽穀之謀乎蓋惟
昔同其謀故今同其力而兵之先聲後實良有
以耳其視武王師牧野而遠及者八國不庶幾
撻伐之殊勳哉故觀伐陳而思陽穀之謀不能
===
不爲世道幸也自天保微而惠王之愛私首止
有會誠尊王之一大機也或謂襄王尚未踐祚
也何以知爲定襄而予桓君子曰蓋至盟葵丘
而桓之尊王驗矣夫彌縫匡救伯之良圖也桓
惟始會首止也協力襄王而輔正之舉倡焉則
不待前星奠位于北極東宮繼體于南面已戴
王而卽之安矣而今之易樹申禁也非以宣首
止之事乎蓋惟昔定王儲故今申王禁而事之
先行後言良有以耳其視太公勤夾輔而錫履
punctuated:
攘夷之一大機也。或謂江、黄未同伐楚也，何以知爲謀楚而予桓？君子曰：「蓋至伐陳，而桓之攘夷驗矣。」夫有正有奇，軍之善政也。桓惟始會陽穀也，誓及江、黄，而伏奇之謀定焉；則不待威申列國之衆，款納兩廣之雄，已先楚而奪之氣矣。而今之連兵伐陳也，非以終陽穀之謀乎？蓋惟昔同其謀，故今同其力；而兵之先聲後實，良有以耳。其視武王師牧野，而遠及者八國，不庶幾撻伐之殊勳哉？故觀伐陳而思陽穀之謀，不能不爲世道幸也。
自《天保》微而惠王之愛私，首止有會，誠尊王之一大機也。或謂襄王尚未踐祚也，何以知爲定襄而予桓？君子曰：「蓋至盟葵丘，而桓之尊王驗矣。」夫彌縫匡救，伯之良圖也。桓惟始會首止也，協力襄王，而輔正之舉倡焉；則不待前星奠位于北極，東宮繼體于南面，已戴王而卽之安矣。而今之易樹申禁也，非以宣首止之事乎？蓋惟昔定王儲，故今申王禁；而事之先行後言，良有以耳。其視太公勤夾輔，而錫履
translation_en:
… one great turning point in repelling the barbarians. Someone might say that Jiang and Huang did not join in the campaign against Chu; how then can one know that it was a plot against Chu and thus grant credit to Duke Huan? The gentleman says: "Only when it came to the campaign against Chen was Duke Huan's repelling of the barbarians verified." Now, having both regular and surprise forces is the sound administration of an army. Only because Duke Huan first met at Yanggu did his oath extend to Jiang and Huang, thereby fixing the strategy of laying a surprise force in ambush; thus, without waiting to extend his awe over the multitudes of the various states, by winning the allegiance of the powers of those two distant realms [? 兩廣], he had already preempted Chu and robbed it of its spirit. And when now they joined forces to attack Chen, was this not to bring the strategy of Yanggu to completion? Indeed, only because they previously shared in the strategy did they now share in the effort; and that military action puts reputation first and reality after truly has its reason. Compared to King Wu leading his army at Muye and reaching as far as eight distant states, does this not come close to such extraordinary merit in punitive campaigning? Therefore, observing the campaign against Chen and reflecting upon the strategy of Yanggu, one cannot help but rejoice for the Way of the world.

Ever since the ode "Tianbao" (Heaven Protects) declined and King Hui indulged in private favoritism, the meeting at Shouzhi was truly one great turning point in honoring the King. Someone might say that King Xiang had not yet ascended the throne; how then can one know that it was to establish King Xiang and thus grant credit to Duke Huan? The gentleman says: "Only when it came to the covenant at Kuiqiu was Duke Huan's honoring of the King verified." Now, patching up flaws and rectifying errors is the sound plan of a hegemon. Only because Duke Huan first met at Shouzhi did they unite their strength for King Xiang, thereby initiating the act of assisting the rightful heir; thus, without waiting for the Fore-star to settle its position at the Northern Pole or the Eastern Palace to succeed to the body of the state facing south, they had already upheld the King and brought him to security. And when now the prohibition against changing the established heir was proclaimed, was this not to declare the enterprise of Shouzhi? Indeed, only because he previously settled the royal heir did he now proclaim the royal prohibition; and that in affairs action comes first and words after truly has its reason. Compared to Grand Duke Lü diligently rendering supporting assistance and being granted territory to tread upon…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
者四至不同一尊獎之偉績哉故觀葵丘而嘉
首止之功不能不爲王室幸也抑伐楚得矣何
驕于伐陳尊王得矣何怠于救衛得非齊桓假
之遂歸而仲鮮格心之學耶故民受其賜聖門
則不道其事
衛侯使甯俞來聘〔文公四年〕
朱炳然
考試官教諭戴　批〔就名分上發知禮最爲得嘉〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔詞雄調古〕
〔詞更犻〕〔愷可誦〕
===
春秋于外臣脩好而深予其知禮焉夫禮莫大
于名分之辨也甯俞其得之可謂曰知矣且甯
俞之聘衛侯以脩好遣也夫睦鄰非禮之常乎
胡以知禮予之君子曰蓋至甯俞而可與言禮
也已夫先王觀象于履而制之爲禮以敎敬也
亦以謹節也自夫其志不敬者不能達禮之原
而其節不具者不能飭禮之儀而禮斯爲天下
裂矣何幸于俞而見之深知天冠地履之分不
punctuated:
者四至，不同一尊獎之偉績哉？故觀葵丘而嘉首止之功，不能不爲王室幸也。抑伐楚得矣，何驕于伐陳？尊王得矣，何怠于救衛？得非齊桓假之遂歸，而仲鮮格心之學耶？故民受其賜，聖門則不道其事。
「衛侯使甯俞來聘」〔文公四年〕
朱炳然
考試官教諭戴批：〔就名分上發知禮，最爲得嘉。〕
考試官教諭楊批：〔詞雄調古。〕
〔詞更犻〕〔愷可誦。〕
春秋于外臣脩好，而深予其知禮焉。夫禮莫大于名分之辨也。甯俞其得之，可謂曰知矣。且甯俞之聘，衛侯以脩好遣也。夫睦鄰非禮之常乎？胡以知禮予之？君子曰：蓋至甯俞而可與言禮也已。夫先王觀象于《履》，而制之爲禮，以敎敬也，亦以謹節也。自夫其志不敬者，不能達禮之原；而其節不具者，不能飭禮之儀，而禮斯爲天下裂矣。何幸于俞而見之！深知天冠地履之分，不
translation_en:
… [Compared with the Grand Duke Tai, who labored as an assistant and was granted territory] reaching to the four boundaries, is this not equally a magnificent achievement in honoring and supporting [the royal house]? Therefore, looking at Kuiqiu and praising the merit of Shouzhi, one cannot help but rejoice for the royal house. Yet while the campaign against Chu was right, why was he arrogant in attacking Chen? While honoring the King was right, why was he lax in rescuing Wei? Could it not be that Duke Huan of Qi merely borrowed [righteousness] without truly returning to it, and that Guan Zhong lacked the learning that rectifies the ruler's heart? Thus, although the people received his benefactions, the school of the Sage did not speak of his affairs.

"The Marquis of Wei sent Ning Yu to come on a mission of friendly inquiries" [Fourth Year of Duke Wen].
By Zhu Bingran.
Examiner and Instructor Dai comments: [Developing "understanding ritual" on the basis of status and duty is most commendable.]
Examiner and Instructor Yang comments: [The diction is vigorous and the tone ancient.]
[The diction is even more forceful [?]] [and lucid, worthy of recitation.]

In recording a foreign minister cultivating friendly relations, the Spring and Autumn Annals deeply praises him for understanding ritual propriety. Now, in ritual propriety, nothing is greater than the distinction of status and duty. Ning Yu grasped this, and so he may truly be called one who understood it. Moreover, as for Ning Yu's mission of friendly inquiries, the Marquis of Wei sent him to cultivate friendly relations. Is not harmony with neighboring states an ordinary rule of ritual propriety? Why then praise him specifically for understanding ritual propriety? The gentleman says: It is only when we come to Ning Yu that one can speak of ritual propriety! Now, the former kings observed the image in the hexagram Treading (Lü) and instituted ritual propriety in order to teach reverence, and also to maintain careful restraint. Once those whose intentions lack reverence cannot penetrate the source of ritual propriety, and those whose restraint is incomplete cannot regulate the ceremonies of ritual propriety, ritual propriety is thereby torn apart throughout the world. How fortunate to see it in Yu! He deeply understood that the distinction between heaven as the cap above and earth as the shoes below must not…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
可一日而或踰而天尊地卑之等不以聲詩而
可忽始而湛露有賦則曰此天子嘉羣臣而燕
樂之者也我非朝正之侯也敢紊上下以僭彝
章乎由是雖賦而有不辭也旣而彤弓有歌則
曰此諸侯獻天子而錫予之者也我無敵愾之
功也敢干大禮以自取戾乎由是雖歌而有不
荅也蓋以魯而僭天子俞之所不安也以已而
僭諸侯俞之所深懼也是故行人之辭肄業之
對有凜乎無敢踰者而一宴享間君臣名分秩
===
如矣噫穆叔聘而辭肆夏君子稱爲秉禮之臣
也士匄聘而拜彤弓君子稱爲守官之嗣也若
俞之辭賦殆庶幾焉其誠春秋之賢大夫也哉
經故以知禮予之予之者重其志也而可以風
天下矣雖然俞可予也而魯則何爲者周禮在
魯聲稱舊矣乃以王朝樂章而寵一諸侯使臣
則所謂禮者安在耶卒之歌雍舞佾禮盡出于
大夫非有所啓而效之者乎昔人謂魯有名而
無情此亦足以觀矣
punctuated: 可一日而或踰，而天尊地卑之等不以聲詩而可忽。始而《湛露》有賦，則曰：「此天子嘉羣臣而燕樂之者也。我非朝正之侯也，敢紊上下以僭彝章乎？」由是雖賦而有不辭也。旣而《彤弓》有歌，則曰：「此諸侯獻天子而錫予之者也。我無敵愾之功也，敢干大禮以自取戾乎？」由是雖歌而有不荅也。蓋以魯而僭天子，俞之所不安也；以已而僭諸侯，俞之所深懼也。是故行人之辭、肄業之對，有凜乎無敢踰者，而一宴享間，君臣名分秩如矣。噫！穆叔聘而辭《肆夏》，君子稱爲秉禮之臣也；士匄聘而拜《彤弓》，君子稱爲守官之嗣也。若俞之辭賦，殆庶幾焉，其誠春秋之賢大夫也哉！經故以知禮予之；予之者，重其志也，而可以風天下矣。雖然，俞可予也，而魯則何爲者？周禮在魯，聲稱舊矣，乃以王朝樂章而寵一諸侯使臣，則所謂禮者安在耶？卒之歌《雍》舞佾，禮盡出于大夫，非有所啓而效之者乎？昔人謂魯有名而無情，此亦足以觀矣。
translation_en:
… may be transgressed for even a single day, and the hierarchy of noble heaven and humble earth must not be neglected even in musical odes. At first, when "Heavy Dew" (Zhanlu) was recited, he thought: "This is how the Son of Heaven commends his assembled ministers and entertains them at banquets. I am not a feudal lord attending the New Year court audience; how dare I confound superior and inferior by usurping the constant statutes?" Thus, although it was recited, he declined to accept the compliment. Thereafter, when "The Red Bow" (Tonggong) was sung, he thought: "This is what the Son of Heaven bestows upon feudal lords when they present captives and tribute. I do not possess the merit of withstanding what the king hates; how dare I infringe upon the great ritual and bring guilt upon myself?" Thus, although it was sung, he did not reply in kind. Indeed, for Lu to usurp the prerogatives of the Son of Heaven was something Ning Yu could not bear with ease; and for himself to usurp the status of the feudal lords was something Ning Yu deeply feared. Therefore, in his words regarding the envoy's duties and his reply about practicing the odes, there was an awe-inspiring resolve never daring to overstep, so that during a single banquet, the nominal statuses of ruler and minister remained in perfect order.

Alas! When Mushu went on a mission of friendly inquiry and declined the "Sixia" hymn, the gentleman praised him as a minister who upheld ritual; when Shi Gai went on a mission of friendly inquiry and bowed in acceptance of "The Red Bow," the gentleman praised him as a descendant who guarded his official duty. As for Ning Yu's declining of the recited odes, he came close to them indeed—truly a worthy grand master of the Spring and Autumn period! The Classic therefore commends him as knowing ritual; in commending him, it values his intent, which could serve to influence the whole world. Even so, while Ning Yu is worthy of commendation, what was Lu doing? That the rituals of Zhou were preserved in Lu had long been its renowned reputation; yet to favor an envoy of a feudal lord with the musical pieces of the royal court—where then was this so-called ritual? In the end, with the singing of the "Yong" ode and the dancing of the eight rows of pantomimes, ritual privileges came entirely from the grand masters; was this not because a precedent had been opened for them to imitate? Men of the past said that Lu had the name of ritual without the reality—from this one may sufficiently observe it.

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
禮記
夫肅肅敬也雝雝和也夫敬以和何事不
行
梁祖齡
考試官教諭戴　批〔發明肅雝和敬之義精絜〕
浮
考試官教諭楊　批〔暢達〕
賢者釋詩之論樂而推其用之裕焉夫事以和
敬爲本也樂之肅雝備是焉其裕於用也宜哉
===
子夏語文侯意曰大哉樂乎幽固足以格神明
而明亦可以通治理者也要不外於和敬焉耳
嘗於詩之詠肅雝者有取焉彼樂貴敬不肅則
慢非敬也詩言肅肅云者蓋以人心之敬發爲
聲音之敬而其廉直勁正者常敬而未嘗慢焉
是故觀於敬而肅肅之義可知矣樂貴和不雝
則乖非和也詩言雝雝云者蓋以人心之和融
爲聲音之和而其欣喜懽愛者常和而未嘗戾
焉是故觀於和而雝雝之義可知矣夫和不徒
punctuated:
《禮記》
「夫肅肅，敬也；雝雝，和也。夫敬以和，何事不行？」
梁祖齡
考試官教諭戴　批：〔發明肅雝和敬之義，精絜。〕
浮
考試官教諭楊　批：〔暢達。〕
賢者釋《詩》之論樂，而推其用之裕焉。夫事以和敬爲本也，樂之肅雝備是焉，其裕於用也宜哉！子夏語文侯意曰：大哉樂乎！幽固足以格神明，而明亦可以通治理者也，要不外於和敬焉耳。嘗於《詩》之詠「肅雝」者有取焉。彼樂貴敬，不肅則慢，非敬也。《詩》言「肅肅」云者，蓋以人心之敬，發爲聲音之敬，而其廉直勁正者，常敬而未嘗慢焉。是故觀於敬，而「肅肅」之義可知矣。樂貴和，不雝則乖，非和也。《詩》言「雝雝」云者，蓋以人心之和，融爲聲音之和，而其欣喜懽愛者，常和而未嘗戾焉。是故觀於和，而「雝雝」之義可知矣。夫和不徒…
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji)

"Now 'solemn, solemn' (susu) means reverence; 'harmonious, harmonious' (yongyong) means harmony. With reverence and harmony, what affair cannot be carried out?"

By Liang Zuling 梁祖齡

Examiner, Instructor Dai 戴 comments: [It elucidates the meaning of solemnity, harmony, concord, and reverence with refined clarity.]
[Marginalia/printer's mark:] Fu 浮 [?]
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊 comments: [Fluent and expressive.]

The worthy explains the discussion of music in the Book of Odes (Shi) and extends it to the abundance of its application. Indeed, affairs take harmony and reverence as their foundation; since the solemnity and harmony of music encompass these, how fitting it is that music is abundant in its application!

The purport of Zixia's 子夏 words to Marquis Wen 文侯 is as follows: Great indeed is music! In the unseen realm it is truly sufficient to reach the spirits and gods, and in the manifest world it can also penetrate the principles of governance; in essence, it goes no further than harmony and reverence. I have drawn meaning from where the Odes sing of "solemnity and harmony." Now, music values reverence; if it is not solemn, it becomes negligent, which is not reverence. When the Odes speak of "solemn, solemn," it is because the reverence of the human heart is expressed as the reverence of sound and tone, and that which is upright, direct, firm, and correct remains constantly reverent and is never negligent. Therefore, by observing reverence, the meaning of "solemn, solemn" can be known. Music values harmony; if it is not harmonious, it becomes discordant, which is not harmony. When the Odes speak of "harmonious, harmonious," it is because the harmony of the human heart blends into the harmony of sound and tone, and that which is joyful, delighted, and affectionate remains constantly harmonious and is never perverse. Therefore, by observing harmony, the meaning of "harmonious, harmonious" can be known. Now, harmony is not merely…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
和也而有敬以主之則雝雝者爲不流矣敬不
徒敬也而有和以濟之則肅肅者爲不離矣恭
敬溫文相須以竝用而推之何所不通中正和
平相待以成能而達之何所不順以之脩身則
動正履和而德行之所由默成者此也以之爲
家國天下則合敬同愛而風俗之所由移易者
此也蓋不淫色不害德而感通之本旣立於肅
雝之中是以措則正施則行而功用之大自溢
於和敬之外非但先祖是聽而已君欲興古樂
===
以爲臣民之極乎毋曰聽之而恐臥也嘗謂治
化之隆固原於樂哉然而樂之所由生又吾心
以爲之本也誠能主敬以立其極審一以定其
和則帝世直溫剛簡之德吾其備之而和敬流
通天地且爲昭矣事無不行云乎哉故曰先王
愼其所以感之者
臣儀行不重辭
舒九江
考試官教諭戴　批〔詞理俱精深達人臣事君〕
punctuated:
和也，而有敬以主之，則「雝雝」者爲不流矣；敬不徒敬也，而有和以濟之，則「肅肅」者爲不離矣。恭敬溫文相須以竝用，而推之何所不通？中正和平相待以成能，而達之何所不順？以之脩身，則動正履和，而德行之所由默成者此也；以之爲家、國、天下，則合敬同愛，而風俗之所由移易者此也。蓋不淫色、不害德，而感通之本旣立於肅雝之中；是以措則正、施則行，而功用之大自溢於和敬之外，非但「先祖是聽」而已。君欲興古樂以爲臣民之極乎？毋曰聽之而恐臥也。嘗謂治化之隆，固原於樂哉！然而樂之所由生，又吾心以爲之本也。誠能主敬以立其極，審一以定其和，則帝世直溫、剛簡之德吾其備之，而和敬流通，天地且爲昭矣，事無不行云乎哉！故曰：「先王愼其所以感之者。」

臣儀行，不重辭。
舒九江
考試官教諭戴　批〔詞理俱精，深達人臣事君〕
translation_en:
… merely harmonious; when there is reverence to govern it, that which is "harmonious, harmonious" (yongyong) does not degenerate into license. Reverence is not merely reverent; when there is harmony to temper it, that which is "solemn, solemn" (susu) does not lead to alienation. Respectful reverence and gentle refinement depend on each other to function together—when extended outward, what will they not penetrate? Central correctness and harmonious peace rely on each other to achieve their efficacy—when carried forward, what will not follow smoothly? Applied to cultivating the self, one's actions are upright and one's conduct harmonious; it is through this that virtuous conduct is silently perfected. Applied to ordering the family, the state, and All under Heaven, it unites people in reverence and joins them in affection; it is through this that customs and mores are transformed. Indeed, neither indulging in licentious sights nor harming virtue, the root of moral resonance and communication is already established within solemnity and harmony. Therefore, when set in place it is upright, and when put into practice it succeeds; the greatness of its efficacy naturally overflows beyond harmony and reverence—it is not merely that "the ancestors hearken to it." Does my lord wish to revive ancient music to set the supreme standard for his ministers and people? Do not say that listening to it makes you fear falling asleep! It has been said that the flourishing of transformative governance truly originates in music! Yet that from which music arises takes our own mind as its root. If one can truly hold to reverence to establish its supreme standard, and examine unity to settle its harmony, then we shall fully possess the virtues of the age of the sage emperors—straightforwardness yet mildness, firmness yet simplicity—and as harmony and reverence flow freely, even Heaven and Earth will be made radiant! Need we speak merely of affairs never failing to be carried out? Therefore it is said: "The former kings were cautious about that by which they moved men's hearts."

"Ministers model themselves on conduct and do not attach weight to words."
Shu Jiujiang 舒九江
Examiner and Confucian Instructor (jiaoyu) Dai comments: [Both diction and principle are refined; it deeply grasps the… of how a minister serves his ruler.]…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
之道
考試官教諭楊　批〔意極斟酌詞亦足以發之〕
人臣之事君尚行而不尚言也夫臣之自效於
君者行也行可儀而辭不重臣道其克盡乎且
世之事君者孰不欲逸其君哉而卒不免於勞
焉者以事之不知所重耳自今觀之臣之所以
啓沃君心者存乎辭辭固不可廢也而所以弼
成君德者存乎行行尤不可忽也不務行而重
辭則行與言違而臣之心有未易知者君斯勞
===
矣是必慎行以爲感通之本而儀範之克端寡
言以據引導之忠而辭說之不事體道以行而
行不過則儼然一有道之儀刑矣至於闡道之
辭非不可爲獻替之助而要非其所重也迪德
以行而行不踰矩凝然一有德之表儀矣至於
論德之辭非不可爲啓對之資而要非其所重
也自靖自獻雖不敢以有隱而潛移默奪之功
得於身體者多焉若曰脩辭以悟君特翼吾行
之不及耳豈得已者哉嘉謨嘉猷雖未嘗以不
punctuated:
之道。
考試官教諭楊　批〔意極斟酌，詞亦足以發之。〕
人臣之事君，尚行而不尚言也。夫臣之自效於君者，行也。行可儀而辭不重，臣道其克盡乎！且世之事君者，孰不欲逸其君哉？而卒不免於勞焉者，以事之不知所重耳。自今觀之，臣之所以啓沃君心者存乎辭，辭固不可廢也；而所以弼成君德者存乎行，行尤不可忽也。不務行而重辭，則行與言違，而臣之心有未易知者，君斯勞矣。是必慎行以爲感通之本，而儀範之克端；寡言以據引導之忠，而辭說之不事。體道以行而行不過則，儼然一有道之儀刑矣。至於闡道之辭，非不可爲獻替之助，而要非其所重也。迪德以行而行不踰矩，凝然一有德之表儀矣。至於論德之辭，非不可爲啓對之資，而要非其所重也。自靖自獻，雖不敢以有隱，而潛移默奪之功，得於身體者多焉。若曰脩辭以悟君，特翼吾行之不及耳，豈得已者哉？嘉謨嘉猷，雖未嘗以不
translation_en:
… [the way a minister serves his ruler].

Examiner Instructor Yang 楊 comments: "The ideas are thoroughly weighed, and the diction is well suited to bring them out."

When a minister serves his ruler, he values conduct rather than speech. Indeed, that by which a minister devotes himself to his ruler is conduct. When his conduct is worthy of emulation and he does not place weight on rhetoric, is the way of the minister not fully realized? Moreover, among those in the world who serve their rulers, who does not wish to give his ruler ease? Yet in the end they cannot save him from toil, simply because in serving him they do not know where to place the emphasis. Viewed from the present, that by which a minister enlightens and enriches his ruler's mind lies in words—so words certainly cannot be discarded; yet that by which he assists in perfecting his ruler's virtue lies in conduct—so conduct can even less be neglected. If he does not apply himself to conduct and instead places weight on words, then conduct and speech will diverge; the minister's mind will not be easy to fathom, and the ruler will thereby be burdened with toil. Therefore, he must be circumspect in his conduct as the basis for inspiring and moving others, so that his exemplary deportment is truly upright; and he must be sparing in speech so as to hold fast to the loyalty that guides his sovereign, without busying himself with verbal disquisitions. When he embodies the Way in his conduct and his conduct does not overstep the rule, he stands with grave dignity as a model of one who possesses the Way. As for words that expound the Way, it is not that they cannot serve as an aid in offering counsel on what to adopt and what to reject, yet in the main they are not where he places his emphasis. When he pursues virtue in his conduct and his conduct does not transgress the square, he stands in steadfast composure as a paragon of one who possesses virtue. As for words that discuss virtue, it is not that they cannot serve as a resource for enlightening replies to the throne, yet in the main they are not where he places his emphasis. In composing himself in peace to offer his devotion to his sovereign, although he dares not hold anything back, the achievement of imperceptibly transforming and silently winning over the ruler is gained mostly through personal practice. If he speaks of cultivating words in order to awaken his ruler, this is merely to supplement what his conduct fails to reach—how could it be something done except out of necessity? As for admirable counsels and admirable plans, although he never fails to…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
告而輔弼賛襄之力得於行脩者大焉若曰陳
言以明志特匡吾行之未逮耳豈所欲者哉夫
惟可儀在行則行無僞行必君之力所能及者
也惟不重在辭則言無虛辭必君之智所能知
者也下無難知如此君可不勞矣抑君臣交儆
上世所不廢也臣可以行而廢辭乎葢處其實
不處其華臣之厚也類如此漢申公無取多言
而欲其君力行老成之慮遠矣要之吾心言行
之本事君以心則辭亦行也又何輕重之有
===
第貳場
論
人君以天之心爲心
劉三才
同考試官教諭湯　批〔天之愛君至欲人君爲善以安天〕
下君承此意即是心天之心是作發揮殆盡氣充詞健錄之
考試官教諭戴　批〔有筆力有理致〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔意正詞暢〕
人君之事天也必純吾心之天于天下而後可
punctuated:
告，而輔弼賛襄之力，得於行脩者大焉；若曰陳言以明志，特匡吾行之未逮耳，豈所欲者哉！夫惟可儀在行，則行無僞行，必君之力所能及者也；惟不重在辭，則言無虛辭，必君之智所能知者也。下無難知如此，君可不勞矣。抑君臣交儆，上世所不廢也，臣可以行而廢辭乎？葢處其實，不處其華，臣之厚也，類如此。漢申公無取多言，而欲其君力行，老成之慮遠矣！要之，吾心，言行之本；事君以心，則辭亦行也，又何輕重之有！

第貳場
論
《人君以天之心爲心》
劉三才
同考試官教諭湯　批：〔天之愛君，至欲人君爲善以安天〕下。君承此意，即是心天之心。是作發揮殆盡，氣充詞健，錄之。
考試官教諭戴　批：〔有筆力，有理致。〕
考試官教諭楊　批：〔意正詞暢。〕

人君之事天也，必純吾心之天于天下，而後可
translation_en:
… inform him, the power to assist and support him is gained in greater measure through the cultivation of conduct; if one speaks of setting forth words to clarify one's intentions, that merely rectifies where one's conduct has not yet reached—how could that be what one desires! Now, only because what makes one worthy of emulation lies in conduct will there be no false conduct in one's actions, and they will surely be what the ruler's strength can attain; only because emphasis is not placed on words will there be no empty rhetoric in one's speech, and it will surely be what the ruler's wisdom can comprehend. When those below present nothing difficult to understand like this, the ruler need not toil. Yet mutual admonition between ruler and minister was not abandoned in high antiquity; can a minister dispense with words on account of conduct? Indeed, dwelling in the substantial and not in the华麗 (superficial ornament)—the honest thickness of a minister is generally like this. Master Shen (Shen Gong 申公) of the Han saw no value in much talk, desiring instead that his ruler earnestly practice; the foresight of that veteran elder was far-reaching! In sum, our mind is the root of speech and conduct; if one serves the ruler with the mind, then words too are conduct—what relative weight could there be between them?

Second Session
Discourse
"The Ruler Takes the Mind of Heaven as His Mind"
Liu Sancai 劉三才
Associate Examiner, Instructor Tang 湯, comments: "Heaven's love for the ruler goes so far as desiring that the ruler do good in order to bring peace to All Under Heaven. For the ruler to uphold this intention is none other than taking the mind of Heaven as his mind. This composition develops the theme exhaustively; its vital breath is full and its diction vigorous. Selected for inclusion."
Examiner, Instructor Dai 戴, comments: "Possesses vigor of brush and soundness of principle."
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊, comments: "The thought is upright and the phrasing fluent."

When a ruler serves Heaven, he must make pure the Heaven of his own mind throughout All Under Heaven, and only then can he…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
以託天下夫天天下大器也天以託之我而吾以
眇然之身承之當必有以副其託者况天之示
我以禨祥顯我以法象無非以重其託而仁愛
我也而吾不思體其心以荅其旣其如天之託
我何哉然所謂體其心者非徒求之在天之天
而從事乎虛文之崇也亦惟勉于爲善以純吾
心之天而已吾心之天純則天下安天下安則
天之所以託我者始副而後天心以格此之謂
善承天者西山眞氏以災祥爲天之愛君而曰
===
爲君者可不以天之心爲心誠有味哉其言也
夫天之于君猶父母之于子也父母之于子其
撫而鞠育之固愛也有時怒而教戒之亦愛也
父母不以其怒且敎也而廢慈而爲之子者能
懼其怒而率其教焉則父母且煦育之愈加矣
然則人君固天之宗子也天心之仁愛者何所
不至而况以宗廟之大百神之靈億兆生民之
衆內夏外夷之遠咸于君乎託之豈不欲常示
祥而顧示異哉乃善則祥應不善則災應若是
punctuated:
以託天下。夫天，天下大器也。天以託之我，而吾以眇然之身承之，當必有以副其託者。况天之示我以禨祥，顯我以法象，無非以重其託而仁愛我也。而吾不思體其心以荅其旣，其如天之託我何哉？然所謂體其心者，非徒求之在天之天，而從事乎虛文之崇也；亦惟勉于爲善，以純吾心之天而已。吾心之天純，則天下安；天下安，則天之所以託我者始副，而後天心以格。此之謂善承天者。

西山眞氏以災祥爲天之愛君，而曰：「爲君者可不以天之心爲心？」誠有味哉其言也！夫天之于君，猶父母之于子也。父母之于子，其撫而鞠育之，固愛也；有時怒而教戒之，亦愛也。父母不以其怒且敎也而廢慈，而爲之子者，能懼其怒而率其教焉，則父母且煦育之愈加矣。然則人君固天之宗子也，天心之仁愛者何所不至？而况以宗廟之大、百神之靈、億兆生民之衆、內夏外夷之遠，咸于君乎託之，豈不欲常示祥而顧示異哉？乃善則祥應，不善則災應，若是
translation_en:
…be entrusted with the realm. Now the realm under Heaven is a great vessel. Since Heaven has entrusted it to me, and I receive it in my own puny person, there must surely be a way to fulfill that trust. How much more so when Heaven reveals omens of fortune and misfortune to me, and manifests celestial patterns and phenomena to me, doing all this solely to give weight to its trust and to show its benevolent love for me! Yet if I do not reflect on embodying Heaven's mind in order to repay its favor, what then becomes of the trust Heaven has placed in me? Even so, what is meant by "embodying its mind" is not merely seeking it in the Heaven that is up in the sky and busying oneself with the exaltation of empty ritual forms; rather, it is simply striving to do good so as to keep the Heaven within my own mind pure, and nothing more. When the Heaven within my mind is pure, the realm is at peace; when the realm is at peace, only then is that for which Heaven entrusted it to me fulfilled, and thereafter Heaven's mind is reached and moved. This is what is meant by being one who well upholds Heaven.

Mr. Zhen of Xishan [Zhen Dexiu 真德秀] regarded calamities and auspicious omens as Heaven's love for the ruler, saying, "How could one who is a ruler not take the mind of Heaven as his own mind?" Truly, how rich in meaning are his words! Now Heaven's relationship to the ruler is like that of parents to their child. With a child, when parents soothe and nurture him, that is of course love; when at times they grow angry and admonish him, that too is love. Parents do not abandon their kindness because they are angry and admonishing; and if the one who is their child can fear their anger and follow their instruction, then the parents will cherish and nurture him all the more. This being so, the ruler of men is indeed the eldest son by lineage of Heaven; to what lengths does the benevolent love of Heaven's mind not reach? And how much more so when the greatness of the ancestral temples, the numinous power of the hundred spirits, the multitude of the millions of living people, and the distant expanses of the central states within and the barbarian tribes without are all entrusted to the ruler—how could Heaven not wish always to display auspicious omens, instead displaying anomalies? Yet when there is goodness, auspicious omens respond, and when there is lack of goodness, calamities respond. Why is it thus…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
乎其不僭者何耶蓋其祥也將福我之為善也
愛也其災也將儆我以為善也亦愛也惟人君
以其心為心而善應之則不拂乎天之所以愛
我者斯可為天之孝子能仰副乎天之所以仁
我者斯可為天之仁人故書曰克謹天戒詩曰
畏天之威于時保之又曰敬天之怒無敢戲豫
敬天之渝無敢馳驅春秋係王于天紀災異不
紀祥瑞無非欲人君以天心為心而善承天者
其善承天也乃所以善託天下者也然所謂以
===
天心為心者豈在于郊祀燔殽之典避殿減膳
之末金泥玉檢之文哉蓋君人者位曰天位祿
曰天祿職曰天職民曰天民則其心亦曰天心
而其尊亦天之尊也其威雷霆也其高日月也
復巍巍之勢挾赫赫之威惟其所欲而莫之禁
也則出入起居得無有循吾天者乎深宮燕閒
得無有累吾天者乎綴衣侍從得無有惑吾天
者乎好大喜功之私得無有雜吾天者乎慶賞
刑威之施得無有拂吾天而上干和氣者乎一
punctuated: 乎其不僭者，何耶？蓋其祥也，將福我之為善也，愛也；其災也，將儆我以為善也，亦愛也。惟人君以其心為心而善應之，則不拂乎天之所以愛我者，斯可為天之孝子；能仰副乎天之所以仁我者，斯可為天之仁人。故《書》曰：「克謹天戒。」《詩》曰：「畏天之威，于時保之。」又曰：「敬天之怒，無敢戲豫；敬天之渝，無敢馳驅。」《春秋》係王于天，紀災異不紀祥瑞，無非欲人君以天心為心而善承天者。其善承天也，乃所以善託天下者也。然所謂以天心為心者，豈在于郊祀燔殽之典、避殿減膳之末、金泥玉檢之文哉？蓋君人者，位曰天位，祿曰天祿，職曰天職，民曰天民，則其心亦曰天心，而其尊亦天之尊也。其威雷霆也，其高日月也。履巍巍之勢，挾赫赫之威，惟其所欲而莫之禁也。則出入起居，得無有循吾天者乎？深宮燕閒，得無有累吾天者乎？綴衣侍從，得無有惑吾天者乎？好大喜功之私，得無有雜吾天者乎？慶賞刑威之施，得無有拂吾天而上干和氣者乎？一
translation_en: …so unerring—why is this? Indeed, when Heaven sends auspicious omens, it is about to bless us for doing good, which is out of love; when it sends calamities, it is about to admonish us to do good, which is also out of love. Only when a ruler of men takes Heaven's mind as his own mind and responds to it properly will he not go against that whereby Heaven loves him, and thus can he be a filial son of Heaven; only when he can look up and fulfill that whereby Heaven shows benevolence to him can he thus be a benevolent man of Heaven. Therefore, the Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Be able to heed carefully the admonitions of Heaven." The Book of Odes (Shi) says: "Revere the majesty of Heaven, and thereby preserve its mandate." It also says: "Revere the wrath of Heaven, and dare not indulge in sport and idleness; revere the changing moods of Heaven, and dare not drive about at will." The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) links the King to Heaven and records calamities and anomalies rather than auspicious omens, for no other reason than desiring the ruler of men to take Heaven's mind as his own mind and properly uphold Heaven. Properly upholding Heaven is precisely the means by which one properly fulfills the trust of the realm. Yet how could what is called taking Heaven's mind as one's own mind lie merely in the ceremonies of suburban sacrifices and burnt offerings of meat, the superficialities of withdrawing from the main hall and reducing imperial meals, or the outward forms of golden mud seals and jade tablets? For in ruling over men, one's position is called the Heaven-ordained position, one's emolument is called the Heaven-ordained emolument, one's duty is called the Heaven-ordained duty, and one's people are called the Heaven-ordained people; thus one's mind is also called the mind of Heaven, and one's exaltedness is also the exaltedness of Heaven. One's majesty is that of thunder and lightning; one's loftiness is that of the sun and the moon. Occupying [reading 履 for 復][?] a towering position of power and wielding an awe-inspiring majesty, one does whatever one desires and none can forbid it. Then in going out and coming in, in daily activity and rest, might there not be something that transgresses [reading /斁 for 循][?] the Heaven within us? In the leisured seclusion of the deep palace, might there not be something that encumbers the Heaven within us? Among the robes-attendants and retinue, might there not be something that deludes the Heaven within us? In the selfish desires of loving grandeur and delighting in martial exploits, might there not be something that adulterates the Heaven within us? In the dispensation of rewards and punishments, might there not be something that goes against the Heaven within us and offends the harmonious ether above? If even once…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
有之即吾心之天有未純而天有未純則渾有
未究渾有未究則天之所以託我者以孤而又
何以格在天之天聖主知其然臨五位不異虎
尾撫盈成若履春冰以奉宗廟不謂祖功宗德
之可憑也而曰九鼎三恪之在列以事百神不
謂牲牷肥腯之足恃也而曰蘋蘩薀藻之當陳
以臨億兆生靈不謂惟吾頤氣之所指使也而
曰朽索六馬之難馭以主內夏外夷不謂貢享
重譯之在道也而曰復隍履霜之可憂故神動
===
而天隨合六氣之精以育羣生麤而不可不陳
者法也吾彰天則以示之紀遠而不可不居者
義也吾裁天理以示之宜親而不可不廣者仁
也吾本天眞以示之惠節而不可不積者禮也
吾緣天秩以示之中自昧爽而日昃自燕居而
大庭自百工而庶職靡莫得以淆而累之惑而
雜且拂之而無一事不與天俱無一念不與天
通皇皇焉常若天鑒之在茲而與之出王游衍
者豈故爲是過計哉勉于爲善以仰副乎天心
punctuated: 有之，即吾心之天有未純；而天有未純，則渾有未究；渾有未究，則天之所以託我者以孤，而又何以格在天之天？聖主知其然，臨五位不異虎尾，撫盈成若履春冰。以奉宗廟，不謂祖功宗德之可憑也，而曰九鼎三恪之在列；以事百神，不謂牲牷肥腯之足恃也，而曰蘋蘩薀藻之當陳；以臨億兆生靈，不謂惟吾頤氣之所指使也，而曰朽索六馬之難馭；以主內夏外夷，不謂貢享重譯之在道也，而曰復隍履霜之可憂。故神動而天隨，合六氣之精以育羣生。麤而不可不陳者，法也，吾彰天則以示之紀；遠而不可不居者，義也，吾裁天理以示之宜；親而不可不廣者，仁也，吾本天眞以示之惠；節而不可不積者，禮也，吾緣天秩以示之中。自昧爽而日昃，自燕居而大庭，自百工而庶職，靡莫得以淆而累之、惑而雜且拂之，而無一事不與天俱，無一念不與天通。皇皇焉常若天鑒之在茲，而與之出王游衍者，豈故爲是過計哉？勉于爲善以仰副乎天心
translation_en:
…even a single one of these be present, the Heaven within my own mind is not yet pure; when that Heaven is not yet pure, its wholeness is not yet fully realized; and when its wholeness is not yet fully realized, the charge that Heaven has entrusted to me is betrayed—how then could one move and reach the Heaven above?

The sage ruler knows that this is so. Occupying the royal throne, he regards it as no different from treading on a tiger's tail; presiding over an age of fullness and accomplishment, he acts as if walking on spring ice. In serving the ancestral temple, he does not say that the merits and virtues of the ancestors can be presumed upon, but rather declares that the Nine Tripods and the Three Revered Guests stand arrayed before him. In serving the hundred spirits, he does not say that fat and unblemished sacrificial beasts are enough to rely on, but rather declares that humble water plants—duckweed, white southernwood, and pondweed—must be reverently set forth. In governing the countless millions of living souls, he does not say that they are merely there to be ordered about at a nod of his chin and a breath of his voice, but rather declares that six horses held by rotten reins are difficult to drive. In ruling over China within and the non-Chinese peoples without, he does not say that tribute bearers with multiple interpreters are already on the roads, but rather declares that a城 wall collapsing back into its moat and the first treading on frost are cause for anxiety.

Therefore, when his spirit moves, Heaven follows, uniting the essence of the six atmospheric energies to nurture all living things. What is coarse yet cannot go unproclaimed is law: I make manifest the patterns of Heaven to show them regulation. What is distant yet cannot go uninhabited is righteousness: I tailor the principles of Heaven to show them what is fitting. What is intimate yet cannot go unbroadened is benevolence: I ground myself in the genuine truth of Heaven to show them kindness. What is restrictive yet cannot go unaccumulated is ritual: I follow the hierarchy of Heaven to show them equilibrium. From dawn until the sun inclines toward the west, from private leisure to the great court, from the hundred artisans to the multitudinous officials, nothing is allowed to confuse and encumber it, or to delude, adulterate, and contravene it. There is not a single affair in which he does not abide with Heaven, nor a single thought that does not communicate with Heaven. Anxiously and reverently, he acts always as though Heaven's scrutiny were right here, accompanying him in all his goings out and wanderings about. Why would he deliberately indulge in such excessive worry? He simply strives to do good so as to look up and fulfill the mind of Heaven…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
耳故曰盥而不薦有孚顒若夫惟有顒若之存
而後有不薦之孚惟有純天之心而後有格天
之治故天愛之聖君脩之天心益加
愛焉雉升之異易而爲蓂莢之祥矣旱魃之虐
轉而爲嘉禾之瑞矣彗孛之變弭而爲三台之
平斗柄之順七政之齊矣以承宗廟而天之祚
我者永以事百神而天之祐我者至以育蒼生
而天之與我者固以莅中國撫四夷而天之助
我者順然則天之所以儆我者寧非所以福我
===
乎而向之示我以咎徵者寧不轉而爲休徵乎
眞如子之於親承顔順志怡然日諭于道而未
始有違者故曰太上脩德其次脩政其次脩數
其次脩禳無非以仰承天心而求不負天之所
託也彼儆予之憂下車之泣六事之責雲漢之
歌側身之行帝王之所以憂勤惕厲而不遑寧
處者何莫非以純吾心之天耶固未嘗取必于
天而天之福之也常有捷於影響者其心通而
其感召之者自不容誣也故人君惟愼所感者
punctuated: 耳。故曰：「盥而不薦，有孚顒若。」夫惟有顒若之存，而後有不薦之孚；惟有純天之心，而後有格天之治。故天愛之，聖君脩之，天心益加愛焉。雉升之異，易而爲蓂莢之祥矣；旱魃之虐，轉而爲嘉禾之瑞矣；彗孛之變，弭而爲三台之平、斗柄之順、七政之齊矣。以承宗廟，而天之祚我者永；以事百神，而天之祐我者至；以育蒼生，而天之與我者固；以莅中國、撫四夷，而天之助我者順。然則天之所以儆我者，寧非所以福我乎？而向之示我以咎徵者，寧不轉而爲休徵乎？眞如子之於親，承顔順志，怡然日諭于道，而未始有違者。故曰：「太上脩德，其次脩政，其次脩數，其次脩禳。」無非以仰承天心，而求不負天之所託也。彼「儆予」之憂、下車之泣、六事之責、《雲漢》之歌、側身之行，帝王之所以憂勤惕厲而不遑寧處者，何莫非以純吾心之天耶？固未嘗取必于天，而天之福之也，常有捷於影響者，其心通而其感召之者自不容誣也。故人君惟愼所感者，
translation_en: … that is all. Therefore it is said: "The ablution has been made, but not yet the offering; there is sincerity and an aspect of solemn reverence." Indeed, only when one maintains that solemn reverence within does one possess the sincerity that precedes the offering; only when one has a heart pure as Heaven does one achieve governance that reaches and moves Heaven. Therefore, when Heaven shows its love through warnings and the sage ruler cultivates himself in response, Heaven's heart cherishes him all the more. The anomaly of the pheasant alighting on the sacrificial cauldron is transformed into the auspicious sign of the calendar-pod plant (mingjia); the ravages of the drought demon turn into the propitious omen of wondrous grain; the portents of comets and扫-stars subside into the equilibrium of the Three Terraces, the regular rotation of the Dipper's handle, and the harmony of the Seven Regulators. Thereby serving the ancestral temple, Heaven's blessing upon our dynastic line is made eternal; thereby serving the hundred spirits, Heaven's protection of us is made complete; thereby nurturing the common people, Heaven's support for us is made secure; thereby presiding over the Central Kingdom and pacifying the four borderlands, Heaven's assistance to us is made compliant. If so, then is not that whereby Heaven admonishes us precisely that whereby it blesses us? And are not the inauspicious signs previously shown to us transformed into auspicious signs? It is truly like a son before his parents, attending to their countenance and obeying their wishes, harmoniously comprehending the Way day by day without ever acting in defiance. Therefore it is said: "The highest course is to cultivate virtue; the next is to cultivate governance; the next is to cultivate calculations and measures; the next is to cultivate exorcistic prayers." All of this is nothing other than reverently receiving Heaven's mind and seeking not to fail what Heaven has entrusted to us. As for the anxiety of "admonishing me," weeping upon alighting from the carriage, blaming oneself for the six matters, the song of the "Milky Way" (Yunhan), and the conduct of humbling oneself in trepidation—whereby the emperors and kings of old were anxious, diligent, vigilant, and allowed themselves no leisure to rest—what part of this was not aimed at purifying the Heaven within one's own heart? Assuredly they never demanded certainty from Heaven, yet Heaven's blessing upon them was often swifter than shadow following form or echo following sound; because their hearts were in communion with Heaven, what they moved and summoned forth naturally admitted of no deception. Thus a ruler need only be cautious about that by which he moves Heaven; …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
彼災異何足諱哉古之賢君一歲無災則曰天
忘我耶諸祥迭見則曰吾何德以堪之非故辭
祥而就災也無亦心天心而求所以感格之者
也雖然必君臣交儆而後可以格天心亦必善
人是親而後可以格吾心故善人者天篤生以
福我國家者也災異者天垂象以愛我國家者
也必親其所以福我者而後能承其所以愛我
者故曰純心要矣用賢急焉然則體天心者盍
亦急於親賢哉
===
表
擬宋以李昉張齊賢同平章事賈黃中李
沆參知政事謝表〔淳化二年〕
苟自新
同考試官教諭王　批〔詞雅體莊而靖共之意〕
發揮得出
考試官教諭戴　批〔駢麗而有典則〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔鋪敘得體〕
淳化二年某月某日伏蒙
punctuated:
彼災異何足諱哉！古之賢君，一歲無災，則曰：「天忘我耶？」諸祥迭見，則曰：「吾何德以堪之？」非故辭祥而就災也，無亦心天心，而求所以感格之者也。雖然，必君臣交儆而後可以格天心，亦必善人是親而後可以格吾心。故善人者，天篤生以福我國家者也；災異者，天垂象以愛我國家者也。必親其所以福我者，而後能承其所以愛我者。故曰：「純心要矣，用賢急焉。」然則體天心者，盍亦急於親賢哉！

表
擬宋以李昉、張齊賢同平章事，賈黃中、李沆參知政事謝表〔淳化二年〕
苟自新
同考試官教諭王　批：〔詞雅體莊，而靖共之意發揮得出。〕
考試官教諭戴　批：〔駢麗而有典則。〕
考試官教諭楊　批：〔鋪敘得體。〕
淳化二年某月某日，伏蒙
translation_en:
…As for those calamities and anomalies, why should they be worth treating as taboo? When the worthy rulers of antiquity went a whole year without a calamity, they would say, "Has Heaven forgotten me?" When various auspicious omens appeared in succession, they would say, "What virtue do I possess to be worthy of them?" It was not that they deliberately rejected auspicious signs and courted calamities; rather, they took the mind of Heaven as their own mind and sought the means to move and reach it. Even so, only when ruler and ministers mutually admonish one another can the mind of Heaven be reached, and only when one draws close to good men can one's own mind be rectified. Therefore, good men are those whom Heaven has specially brought forth to bless our state; calamities and anomalies are the signs that Heaven displays from above out of love for our state. Only by drawing close to that whereby Heaven blesses us can we fittingly receive that whereby Heaven shows its love for us. Thus it is said: "Purifying the mind is essential; employing the worthy is urgent." That being so, for one who seeks to embody the mind of Heaven, why not also make it an urgent priority to draw close to the worthy?

Memorial
A Memorial Written in the Persona of Song Officials Expressing Gratitude for Appointing Li Fang 李昉 and Zhang Qixian 張齊賢 as Jointly Manager of Affairs, and Jia Huangzhong 賈黃中 and Li Hang 李沆 as Participant in Determining Governmental Matters [Second Year of the Chunhua Reign (991)]
By Gou Zixin 苟自新

Examiner, Instructor Dai, comments: [Parallel and ornate, yet adhering to classical standards.]
Examiner, Instructor Yang, comments: [The exposition is well-proportioned and appropriate.]
