title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
聖恩以臣昉臣齊賢同平章事臣黃中臣沆參
知政事者伏以
元鼎均調隆秩重
黃扉之寄
筦樞協贊清華聯
紫府之班位望特冠乎三臺儀表卒先于百
辟懇懇速官謗忝竊
恩榮臣昉等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊惟
天子撫蒞萬邦德隆丕冒宰臣節宣四氣職司
===
代終盛世建官百揆與四岳而竝設明王
立政三公聯三少而宣猷政本是端化機
攸賴自昔黃廷順紀六相協心爰考虞治
無爲五臣熙載阿衡任重伊傅同作商霖
師保義隆旦奭共培姬籙慨秦置相德選
希聞漢鑒秦權則增御史大夫之制唐裁
周典遂定中書門下之員宰相咸共平章
前朝著籍參政亞班聯署
昭代鴻摹論道銅螭
punctuated: 聖恩，以臣昉、臣齊賢同平章事，臣黃中、臣沆參知政事者。伏以元鼎均調，隆秩重黃扉之寄；筦樞協贊，清華聯紫府之班。位望特冠乎三臺，儀表卒先于百辟。懇懇速官謗，忝竊恩榮。臣昉等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟天子撫蒞萬邦，德隆丕冒；宰臣節宣四氣，職司代終。盛世建官，百揆與四岳而竝設；明王立政，三公聯三少而宣猷。政本是端，化機攸賴。自昔黃廷順紀，六相協心；爰考虞治無爲，五臣熙載。阿衡任重，伊、傅同作商霖；師保義隆，旦、奭共培姬籙。慨秦置相，德選希聞。漢鑒秦權，則增御史大夫之制；唐裁周典，遂定中書門下之員。宰相咸共平章，前朝著籍；參政亞班聯署，昭代鴻摹。論道銅螭，
translation_en:
…Imperial grace, appointing Your Servants [Li] Fang and [Zhang] Qixian as Jointly Manager of Affairs, and Your Servants [Jia] Huangzhong and [Li] Hang as Participant in Determining Governmental Matters.

Your Servants humbly consider that in harmonizing the Great Tripod of state, exalted rank attaches weighty trust to the Yellow Door [the Secretariat-Chancellery]; in assisting at the pivot of government, pure and illustrious offices join the court ranks of the Purple Palace. In position and prestige they stand foremost above the Three Terraces; in demeanor and example they lead the hundred officials [reading 卒 as 率]. Earnestly fearing that we may invite criticism for failing our offices, we are ashamed to have unworthily received such gracious honor. Your Servants Fang and the others, in utmost awe and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground again and again.

We humbly reflect that the Son of Heaven rules over the myriad states, his exalted virtue overspreading all; the chief ministers regulate and diffuse the four seasonal airs, their office charged with bringing the ruler's work to completion. When flourishing ages established offices, the General Regulator (baikui) was instituted alongside the Four Mountains (siyue); when enlightened kings ordered governance, the Three Dukes (sangong) were joined with the Three Juniors (sanshao) to set forth grand plans. Herein lies the rectification of the root of governance, and upon this depends the pivot of transforming influence. From of old, when the court of the Yellow Emperor harmonized the cosmic order, six ministers united their hearts; examining how Yu [Shun] governed through non-action, five ministers brightened his undertakings. Heavy was the charge of the Reliance and Balance (Aheng), as Yi [Yin] and Fu [Yue] alike became the timely rain of Shang; lofty was the duty of Tutor and Protector, as [the Duke of] Zhou (Dan) and [the Duke of] Shao (Shi) together nurtured the dynastic mandate of Ji [Zhou]. Alas, when Qin established chancellors, selection based on virtue was rarely heard of. Han, taking warning from Qin's concentration of power, added the institution of the Censor-in-chief (yushi dafu); Tang, adapting the canons of Zhou, thereupon fixed the personnel of the Secretariat and Chancellery (zhongshu menxia). That the chief ministers all jointly manage affairs is recorded in the registers of previous dynasties; that the Participants in Determining Governmental Matters sign jointly in the next rank is the grand design of our Illustrious Dynasty. Discussing the Way beside the bronze dragons…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
龍袞共瞻于
五位書銜玉尺鵷行首出乎六卿犄朝野之具
瞻宜儒林之碩彥詎意爰立叨及迂庸謀
斷莫効于兼資調燮愈知其難稱恭惟
○○○
應期出震
握紀御乾
帝驟王馳冠古今而爲烈
文經武緯參天地以成能
===
迪簡俊良侃直盡登于言路崇尚經術耆宿
悉置之周行謂毗贊
朝政之端于今宜慎而論思
密勿之地自古匪輕旣圖任于台垣復
留神于參府疇咨二職謬拔四臣〔臣臣齊賢昉〕
翰苑兩遷敢市恩于薦舉河東十策猥彼
召于
行宮〔臣中臣沆黃臣〕就
日握銓誓竭擬除之當占雲侍
punctuated: 龍袞共瞻于五位，書銜玉尺，鵷行首出乎六卿。犄朝野之具瞻，宜儒林之碩彥。詎意爰立，叨及迂庸；謀斷莫効于兼資，調燮愈知其難稱。恭惟○○○應期出震，握紀御乾。帝驟王馳，冠古今而爲烈；文經武緯，參天地以成能。迪簡俊良，侃直盡登于言路；崇尚經術，耆宿悉置之周行。謂毗贊朝政之端，于今宜慎；而論思密勿之地，自古匪輕。旣圖任于台垣，復留神于參府。疇咨二職，謬拔四臣。〔臣臣齊賢昉〕翰苑兩遷，敢市恩于薦舉；河東十策，猥彼召于行宮。〔臣中臣沆黃臣〕就日握銓，誓竭擬除之當；占雲侍
translation_en:
…and near the Dragon Robe, all look up to the sovereign on the throne; signing one's title by the jade ruler, in the courtly ranks of the simurghs they stand at the very head of the Six Ministers. Being the focus of the gaze of both court and countryside [?], these posts ought to be filled by eminent worthies from the forest of scholars. How could we have expected that this appointment as chief ministers would undeservedly fall upon us, who are pedantic and mediocre? Unable to offer both resourcefulness in counsel and decisiveness in action, we know all the more how hard it is to be worthy of the task of harmonizing the governance of the realm.

We reverently reflect that Your Majesty [○○○] has emerged in the East in response to the auspicious age, grasping the royal laws and ruling from the heavenly throne. Galloping on the path of the Five Emperors and Three Kings, Your illustrious achievements surpass both antiquity and the present; with civil administration as the warp and military might as the woof, You form a triad with Heaven and Earth in bringing all capabilities to completion. Selecting and promoting men of outstanding talent and goodness, the outspoken and upright are all raised to the avenues of remonstrance; venerating classicist statecraft, venerable scholars are all placed in the ranks of the court. You consider that assisting at the very source of court governance must today be handled with caution, and that the place of confidential deliberation and counsel has since antiquity never been taken lightly. Having sought out men to entrust with the Chief Council, You again turned Your attentive mind to the office of the Participant in Determining Governmental Matters. Inquiring after men for these two offices, You have mistakenly selected us four servants. [Your servants Qi Xian 齊賢 and Fang 昉][?] Having been twice promoted in the Hanlin Academy, how would I dare to curry personal favor through recommendations? Having submitted ten policy essays in Hedong, I was undeservedly summoned to the Auxiliary Palace [?]. [Your servants Zhong 中 and Hang 沆][?] Approaching the sun and holding the scales of personnel evaluation, I swear to exhaust my strength in making proper nominations and appointments; gazing at the auspicious clouds while attending…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
彩深赦風範之褒顪惟草茅之微均覩
旒黈之盛依光莫荚恐玷跡于鴛班接翼鳳
條益滋兢于蚊負臣等敢不靖共爾位同
寅協恭道眞本自皇王務底弼諧之績治
效莫踰論語益抒節愛之懷秉貢舉之公
無遺寒畯抑浮薄之習嚴杜倖途麴糵鹽
梅三五交照醇飴藥石忠順相將調
玉燭以亮功符宣兩兩保
金甌以弘化念切巖巖休玆四鄰之共欽庶
===
期
一德之交泰伏願
皇猷遐暢
帝祚永昌
履豐亨而宜照日中
賁文明以化成天下
峻德光于四表而四靈效順翕歸王會之圖
神功覆于萬年而萬國驩心永戴獻商之令臣
等無任瞻
punctuated: 彩，深赦風範之褒。顪惟草茅之微，均覩旒黈之盛。依光莫荚，恐玷跡于鴛班；接翼鳳條，益滋兢于蚊負。臣等敢不靖共爾位，同寅協恭！道眞本自皇王，務底弼諧之績；治效莫踰《論語》，益抒節愛之懷。秉貢舉之公，無遺寒畯；抑浮薄之習，嚴杜倖途。麴糵鹽梅，三五交照；醇飴藥石，忠順相將。調玉燭以亮功，符宣兩兩；保金甌以弘化，念切巖巖。休玆四鄰之共欽，庶期一德之交泰。伏願皇猷遐暢，帝祚永昌。履豐亨而宜照日中，賁文明以化成天下。峻德光于四表，而四靈效順，翕歸王會之圖；神功覆于萬年，而萬國驩心，永戴獻商之令。臣等無任瞻
translation_en: … clouds, deeply moved [?] by the praise of my demeanor. Ashamed that in our humble rustic origins we have all witnessed the splendor of the imperial crown and ear-plugs; leaning on the radiance of the calendar plant [?], we fear sullying the ranks of the court; joining wings on the phoenix branch, we feel ever more trepidation, like a mosquito bearing a mountain. How could your servants dare not quietly fulfill the duties of our offices and work together in reverent harmony! The true Way stems from the sovereigns and kings of old—we shall strive to achieve the merit of assisting and harmonizing; the efficacy of governance does not go beyond the Analects (Lunyu)—we shall further give expression to the ideal of economy in expenditure and love for the people. Upholding fairness in recommendation and selection, we shall leave behind no talent of humble birth; curbing frivolous and shallow customs, we shall strictly close off avenues of opportunistic advancement. Like yeast and malt, salt and plum, may the Three Lords and Five Emperors shine upon one another; like sweet wine and medicinal stone, may loyalty and compliance go hand in hand. Harmonizing the Jade Candle of the seasons to brighten meritorious achievements, as the stars of the Taisui constellation shine in pairs; preserving the Golden Urn of the empire to broaden transformation, our thoughts remain earnestly fixed on the lofty peaks. May this excellence be jointly revered by the four neighboring auxiliaries, so as to hope for the mutual flourishing of pure, unified virtue. We humbly pray that the Imperial plan may spread far and wide, and the Imperial throne may prosper forever. Treading in abundance and success, may Your Majesty fittingly shine like the sun at midday; adorning the realm with civilizing brightness, may You transform all under Heaven. May Your lofty virtue illuminate the four extremities, while the four numinous creatures render obedience and gather into the Illustrations of the King's Convocation (Wanghui tu); may Your divine achievements shelter ten thousand ages, while the myriad states rejoice in heart and forever uphold the commands presented as to Shang [?]. Your servants are beyond measure in gazing…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策五道
第一問
劉三才
===
同考試官訓導吳　批〔論和同之辨以揄揚我〕
皇上明良一德之交纚纚足觀矣而忠讜之忱溢于言外宜錄之
考試官教諭戴　批〔殞不忘規有忘尚友魏陸者〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔博古之學匡時之猷具見〕
盛矣哉君臣相得之際乎是故聚精神以
隆交泰之誼而其盛斯彰廣聽納以弘交
儆之謨而其盛斯永夫君臣之會猶天地
然乾施坤受則和協益而生類蕃矣主聖
臣良則籌策合而恩施溥矣以故冠履雖
punctuated:
天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叄場
策五道
第一問
劉三才
同考試官訓導吳　批〔論和同之辨，以揄揚我〕皇上明良一德之交，纚纚足觀矣，而忠讜之忱溢于言外，宜錄之。
考試官教諭戴　批〔殞不忘規，有忘尚友魏、陸者。〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔博古之學，匡時之猷，具見。〕

盛矣哉！君臣相得之際乎！是故聚精神以隆交泰之誼，而其盛斯彰；廣聽納以弘交儆之謨，而其盛斯永。夫君臣之會，猶天地然。乾施坤受，則和協益而生類蕃矣；主聖臣良，則籌策合而恩施溥矣。以故冠履雖
translation_en:
… up to Heaven and looking up to the Sage, overcome with the utmost earnestness and trepidation, respectfully present this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions (ce)
First Question
Liu Sancai 劉三才
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Wu: 〔He discusses the distinction between harmony and conformity in order to extol our〕 August Emperor's communion of enlightened ruler and worthy ministers sharing a single virtue. It flows articulately and is well worth reading, while his loyal and forthright sincerity overflows beyond the words; it ought to be selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Dai: 〔In praising [颂?] he does not forget to offer admonition, aspiring [志?] to befriend the ancients Wei Zheng 魏徵 and Lu Zhi 陸贄.〕
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Yang: 〔Learning that encompasses antiquity and counsels for rectifying the age are both evident here.〕

How magnificent is the occasion when ruler and minister are in mutual accord! Therefore, when they concentrate their vital spirit to exalt the bond of harmonious communion, its magnificence is made manifest; when they broaden their heed and acceptance of counsel to enlarge plans of mutual admonition, its magnificence is made enduring. Now, the meeting of ruler and minister is just like that of Heaven and Earth. When the Creative (qian) bestows and the Receptive (kun) receives, harmony and cooperation increase and living things flourish; when the sovereign is sage and the ministers are worthy, their deliberations and plans coincide and the bestowal of grace becomes universal. For this reason, although cap and shoes…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
分而精神自貫意氣雖洽而臣拂靡遺嚴
非立異和不黨同功業竝乎兩儀聲光垂
于千禩茲非曠古之一値哉愚不敏請述
唐虞商周君臣相得之盛而後鋪張我
昭代麻烈於萬一可乎甞讀易至大有之五爻
曰厥孚交如威如吉而九三曰公用享于
天子小人弗克夫五君道也三臣道也君
交於臣則手足腹心萃爲一體主伯亞旅
聯爲一家藹然乎其和之極矣而周公猶
===
有取於享獻之誼惟恐憂危之論不徹於
廉堂藥石之規或壅於耳目茲豈聖人之
私憂過計也哉蓋隆盛之極則瑕釁易萌
志氣之投則阿徇易起此三爻之享獻所
以成五爻之交孚大有之隆永保無斁職
斯之故矣盍自古帝王徵之夫羲軒而降
語君臣相得之盛者莫虞庭若矣當其時
君曰俞臣曰都君曰吁臣曰咈堂陛不閡
而志意流通形骸罔拘而真精貫徹即寠
punctuated: 分，而精神自貫；意氣雖洽，而臣拂靡遺。嚴非立異，和不黨同，功業竝乎兩儀，聲光垂于千禩，茲非曠古之一値哉？愚不敏，請述唐、虞、商、周君臣相得之盛，而後鋪張我昭代麻烈於萬一，可乎？甞讀《易》至《大有》之五爻，曰：「厥孚交如，威如，吉。」而九三曰：「公用享于天子，小人弗克。」夫五，君道也；三，臣道也。君交於臣，則手足腹心萃爲一體，主伯亞旅聯爲一家，藹然乎其和之極矣。而周公猶有取於享獻之誼，惟恐憂危之論不徹於廉堂，藥石之規或壅於耳目，茲豈聖人之私憂過計也哉？蓋隆盛之極，則瑕釁易萌；志氣之投，則阿徇易起。此三爻之享獻，所以成五爻之交孚，《大有》之隆，永保無斁，職斯之故矣。盍自古帝王徵之？夫羲、軒而降，語君臣相得之盛者，莫虞庭若矣。當其時，君曰「俞」，臣曰「都」；君曰「吁」，臣曰「咈」。堂陛不閡而志意流通，形骸罔拘而真精貫徹，即寠…
translation_en:
…are distinct, yet their spirit naturally interpenetrates; though their dispositions and aspirations are in harmony, remonstrance and correction by ministers are never omitted. Strictness is not for the sake of standing apart, and harmony is not for the sake of partisan conformity. Their achievements rival Heaven and Earth, and their renown shines down through a thousand generations—is this not an encounter seen only once in ages? Unworthy though I am, may I recount the flourishing harmony between ruler and minister in the Tang, Yu, Shang, and Zhou eras, and thereafter set forth one ten-thousandth of the glorious achievements [reading 休烈 for 麻烈] of our illustrious dynasty?

I have read the Book of Changes (Yi) up to the fifth line of the Dayou ("Great Possession") hexagram, which says: "His sincerity is reciprocated, and he has majesty; auspicious." And the Nine in the Third place says: "A duke presents offerings to the Son of Heaven; a petty man cannot do this." Now, the fifth line is the way of the ruler, and the third line is the way of the minister. When the ruler enters into fellowship with his ministers, hands, feet, heart, and belly are gathered into a single body; the master, the eldest son, the younger sons, and the multitude of laborers are joined into a single family—how genial is the utmost reach of their harmony! Yet the Duke of Zhou still drew upon the principle of presenting offerings, fearing only that discussions of anxiety and peril might not penetrate to the high hall [reading 廟堂 for 廉堂], or that admonitions as salutary as medicine and acupuncture stone might be blocked from the ruler's ears and eyes. How could this be merely a sage's private worry or excessive calculation? Indeed, at the height of flourishing prosperity, flaws and rifts easily sprout; when wills and dispositions are congenial, flattery and compliance easily arise. Thus, the offering presented by the third line is what brings to completion the mutual sincerity of the fifth line; that the flourishing of Great Possession is forever preserved without weariness is precisely for this reason.

Why not verify this from the emperors and kings of antiquity? From Fuxi and Xuan辕 (the Yellow Emperor) onward, in speaking of the flourishing harmony between ruler and minister, nothing matched the court of Yu (Shun). At that time, the ruler said "Yes (yu)," and the minister said "Oh, admirable (du)!"; the ruler said "Alas (xu)," and the minister said "No, I object (fu)!" The hall and the steps did not separate them, so their wills and intentions flowed freely between them; physical forms did not constrain them, so their true spirit penetrated through and through. Even clouds and [reading 雲龍 for 寠龍]…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
龍何以狀其遇魚水何以悉其懽哉然禹
臯陶之告其君者一則曰后克艱厥后臣
克艱厥臣又曰惠迪吉從逆凶惟影響一
則曰無敎逸欲有邦兢兢業業一日二日
萬幾又曰元首叢脞哉股肱惰哉庶事墮
哉此其交相儆戒日勤兢業何其危也自
是而降若太甲成王稱商周之令主矣乃
伊尹之告太甲曰無輕民事惟難無安厥
位惟危周公之告成王曰所其無逸先知
===
稼穡之艱難迄今讀太甲無逸二書凜凜
乎朽索之馭而盤水之持也夫商周二主
罔敢逸豫宜已乃重華協帝若舜風動四
方若舜雖日使其臣諷嵩祝之詞稱萬年
之觴亦奚不可者而顧往往勒危箴達聰
聽覩亂亡于指掌視熙洽于渺茫此所以
臣主一心諫聽不貳恩從祥風翺而德與
和氣游與故劉向曰舜命九官濟濟相讓
和之至也衆賢和於朝則萬物和於野而
punctuated: 龍何以狀其遇，魚水何以悉其懽哉！然禹、臯陶之告其君者，一則曰：「后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣。」又曰：「惠迪吉，從逆凶，惟影響。」一則曰：「無敎逸欲有邦，兢兢業業，一日二日萬幾。」又曰：「元首叢脞哉！股肱惰哉！庶事墮哉！」此其交相儆戒，日勤兢業，何其危也！自是而降，若太甲、成王，稱商、周之令主矣。乃伊尹之告太甲曰：「無輕民事惟難，無安厥位惟危。」周公之告成王曰：「所其無逸，先知稼穡之艱難。」迄今讀《太甲》、《無逸》二書，凜凜乎朽索之馭而盤水之持也。夫商、周二主罔敢逸豫，宜已；乃重華協帝若舜，風動四方若舜，雖日使其臣諷嵩祝之詞、稱萬年之觴，亦奚不可者？而顧往往勒危箴、達聰聽，覩亂亡于指掌，視熙洽于渺茫，此所以臣主一心，諫聽不貳，恩從祥風翺而德與和氣游與！故劉向曰：「舜命九官，濟濟相讓，和之至也。衆賢和於朝，則萬物和於野。」而
translation_en: …clouds and the dragon [?] could suffice to describe their encounter, or how fish and water could fully express their joy! Yet when Yu 禹 and Gao Yao 臯陶 admonished their sovereign, the one said, "If the sovereign can appreciate the difficulty of being sovereign, and the minister can appreciate the difficulty of being minister," and again, "Accordance with the right leads to good fortune; following the perverse leads to misfortune—just like shadow and echo." The other said, "Do not set an example of indolence and desires to the possessors of states; be cautious and conscientious, for in one day or two days there are ten thousand springs of things," and again, "When the head is petty and vexatious, the limbs are idle, and all affairs fall into ruin!" In thus mutually warning and cautioning one another, daily diligent in their cautious labor, how acutely aware of danger they were! Coming down from this era, rulers such as Tai Jia 太甲 and King Cheng 成王 were acclaimed as exemplary sovereigns of the Shang and Zhou dynasties. Yet Yi Yin 伊尹 admonished Tai Jia, saying, "Do not slight the affairs of the people—think only of their difficulty; do not rest idly in your position—think only of its peril." And the Duke of Zhou 周公 admonished King Cheng, saying, "Abide in diligence without idleness; first know the hardships of sowing and reaping." Even today, when one reads the two documents Tai Jia (Tai Jia) and Against Luxurious Ease (Wuyi 無逸), one feels the awe of driving horses with rotten reins or holding a basin filled to the brim with water. Now, that those two sovereigns of Shang and Zhou dared not indulge in idleness and pleasure is only fitting. But as for one like Shun 舜, whose double splendor matched the Di, or one like Shun, whose transforming wind moved the four quarters—even if he had daily caused his ministers to recite celebratory prayers heavy as Mount Song and raise toasts for ten thousand years of longevity, what harm would there have been? Instead, he constantly inscribed admonitions on peril and opened wide his keen hearing, beholding disorder and ruin as clearly as on the palm of his hand while viewing peace and harmony as something distant and uncertain. Is this not why sovereign and minister were of one mind, why remonstrance and its reception were without duplicity, why grace soared on auspicious winds and virtue roamed with harmonious ether? Thus Liu Xiang 劉向 said, "When Shun appointed the nine officers, in dignified array they yielded to one another: this was the culmination of harmony. When the many worthies are harmonious at court, the myriad things are harmonious in the wilds." And…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
其言周文武之盛亦曰以和致和獲天助
也明主有見於此是故尊居五位而納矇
瞽之箴宰制六合而訊芻蕘之口拔之疏
蹻寘之顯融所以示用也而砭熨不以爲
迂褒之九章食之萬石所以示尊也而韋
弦不以爲拂造膝而談霽顔而受所以洽
情也而忌諱之語日陳於前日晏侍食夜
分徹炬所以優禮也而荼蓼之詞不絕於
耳君臣上下之間雝雝然忘猜嫌披肝膈
===
固不得議其爲異而其是非媺惡之辨又
犂犂然各殫所長而相濟以出之亦豈得
訾其爲同哉譬之和羹焉醯醢鹽梅各一
其味而宰夫調之罔有不適口者也譬之
和樂焉五音六律各一其聲而樂師調之
罔有不適聽者也不然以水濟水雖易牙
不能使人嗜矣琴瑟專一雖師曠不能使
樂諧矣然則和同之辨齊晏子獻可替否
之論燗然其無所眊與卽禹皐伊周之事
punctuated: 其言周文、武之盛，亦曰：「以和致和，獲天助也。」明主有見於此，是故尊居五位，而納矇瞽之箴；宰制六合，而訊芻蕘之口。拔之疏蹻，寘之顯融，所以示用也，而砭熨不以爲迂；褒之九章，食之萬石，所以示尊也，而韋弦不以爲拂；造膝而談，霽顔而受，所以洽情也，而忌諱之語日陳於前；日晏侍食，夜分徹炬，所以優禮也，而荼蓼之詞不絕於耳。君臣上下之間，雝雝然忘猜嫌、披肝膈，固不得議其爲異；而其是非媺惡之辨，又犂犂然各殫所長而相濟以出之，亦豈得訾其爲同哉？譬之和羹焉，醯醢鹽梅各一其味，而宰夫調之，罔有不適口者也。譬之和樂焉，五音六律各一其聲，而樂師調之，罔有不適聽者也。不然，以水濟水，雖易牙不能使人嗜矣；琴瑟專一，雖師曠不能使樂諧矣。然則和同之辨，齊晏子獻可替否之論，燗然其無所眊與！卽禹、皐、伊、周之事…
translation_en: …and when he spoke of the flourishing of Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou, he also said: "Using harmony to bring about harmony, they obtained the assistance of Heaven." Enlightened rulers perceive this. Therefore, though occupying the supreme fifth position in dignity, they accept the admonitions of blind musicians; though governing the six directions of the universe, they inquire into the words of grass- and firewood-gatherers. Raising men from coarse sandals and placing them in illustrious positions is how they show employment, yet they do not regard probing needles and hot irons of criticism as pedantic; honoring them with nine-emblem robes and feeding them with salaries of ten thousand piculs is how they show respect, yet they do not regard the soft leather and taut bowstrings of remonstrance as perverse; conversing knee-to-knee and receiving them with a cleared countenance is how they cultivate affection, yet taboo and unpleasant words are daily set forth before them; having them attend meals late in the day and removing the torches at midnight is how they accord generous courtesy, yet bitter words like smartweed never cease in their ears. Between ruler and minister, superior and inferior, they harmoniously forget suspicion and resentment and bare their hearts and minds, so one certainly cannot criticize them for being divided; yet in distinguishing right and wrong, good and bad, they clearly exhaust their respective strengths and complement one another in bringing them forth—how could one disparage them for mere conformity? Take for example blending a soup: vinegar, meat sauce, salt, and plum each have their own distinct flavor, yet when the master chef blends them, there is none that does not suit the palate. Take for example harmonizing music: the five notes and six pitch-pipes each have their own distinct sound, yet when the music master blends them, there is none that does not suit the ear. Otherwise, if one supplements water with water, even Yi Ya 易牙 could not make people relish it; if the zithers play only a single note, even Music Master Kuang 師曠 could not make the music harmonious. Such being the case, the distinction between harmony and conformity, and Yanzi 晏子 of Qi's discourse on presenting what is acceptable andempotently rejecting what is objectionable—how brilliantly clear and free of confusion they are! Even in the way Yu 禹, Gao Yao 皐陶, Yi Yin 伊尹, and the Duke of Zhou 周公 served…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
其君者孰能違哉秦漢以來愚無容置喙
已我
皇上茂齡撫運
講學親賢朝乾夕惕日不暇給此其心即危
微之戒兢業之旨也商太甲周成王之事
烏足道耶乃一二輔臣相與交儆於下以
共登太平之理儼乎鹽梅之濟獻替之規
也而
天子又虛己南面以聽之靡善弗登無言不錄
千載泰交之會希前覯矣諸所贊畫
===
廟謨啓沃
宸聽縷縷乎不可更僕數也即如頃者
後宮土木之罷監局織造之減旱災虔禱星
變致戒厥所入告靡匪敬
天勤民之要
皇上悉見嘉納不崇朝而見之行事此其聚精
會神相得益章雖伯牙操邃鍾逢門子彎
烏號猶未足以喻其意者豈非虞廷聽納
punctuated:
其君者，孰能違哉？秦漢以來，愚無容置喙已。
我皇上茂齡撫運，講學親賢，朝乾夕惕，日不暇給。此其心，即危微之戒、兢業之旨也，商太甲、周成王之事，烏足道耶！乃一二輔臣，相與交儆於下，以共登太平之理，儼乎鹽梅之濟、獻替之規也。而天子又虛己南面以聽之，靡善弗登，無言不錄，千載泰交之會，希前覯矣。諸所贊畫廟謨、啓沃宸聽，縷縷乎不可更僕數也。即如頃者後宮土木之罷，監局織造之減，旱災虔禱，星變致戒，厥所入告，靡匪敬天勤民之要；皇上悉見嘉納，不崇朝而見之行事。此其聚精會神，相得益章，雖伯牙操邃鍾，逢門子彎烏號，猶未足以喻其意者，豈非虞廷聽納
translation_en:
… in serving their rulers—who could depart from it? As for the eras since Qin and Han, I have no need to interpose a word.

Our August Emperor, in the prime of his youth, holds sway over the dynastic destiny. He engages in scholarly lectures and draws close to the worthy; diligent by day and vigilant by night, he scarcely has a moment's leisure. This mind of his embodies the very admonition regarding the precarious and the subtle, and the principle of cautious reverence—how could the deeds of Taijia of Shang or King Cheng of Zhou even be worth mentioning by comparison! Meanwhile, one or two Grand Secretaries mutually admonish and encourage one another below so as to jointly ascend to the governance of Great Peace, truly exemplifying the complementary blending of salt and plum and the norm of presenting what is acceptable andinya rejecting what is objectionable. Moreover, the Son of Heaven humbles himself, facing south to listen to them: no goodness goes unpromoted, and no counsel goes unrecorded. Such a thousand-year confluence of harmonious communion between ruler and ministers has rarely been witnessed in the past. All the ways in which they have assisted in planning court counsels and enlightened the imperial hearing are so detailed and numerous that one could not count them all even by changing attendants. Take, for instance, recent events: the halting of construction works in the rear palaces, the reduction of textile manufacturing in the Directorate and Bureaus, the devout prayers offered during drought disasters, and the solemn warnings heeded upon celestial anomalies. Everything they have entered to report to the throne consists of nothing less than the essentials of revering Heaven and laboring for the people; and the August Emperor has praised and accepted it all, putting it into action before a single morning has passed. In this concentration of spirit and energy, whereby ruler and ministers bring out the best in one another, even Boya playing the Haozhong lute [?] or Pengmenzi drawing the Wuhao bow would still be insufficient to illustrate their rapport. Is this not indeed the fine virtue of attentive acceptance at the court of Yu…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
之庥美
君臣和德之極致哉薄海內外民恬物熙九夷
君長奉琛款塞斯誠太和充塞唐虞宇宙
間而漢人所稱天之所以相天之所以順
者在此也已然執事猶欲聞忠言讜論以
裨
當代之盛美愚也何能明習
國家事然以區區芹曝之念竊一籌之則有
四說焉講讀之當勤也覽斷之當親也言
路之當廣也直宿之當慎也夫今之
===
經筵日講儀制非不井井具也然肅然而臨
儼然而退講官所横經而議論者其能一
一當
聖心乎凡有疑義當
渙發綸音
特降清問必求其洞然豁暢而後已則庶乎旁
引曲證得悉其詞而
睿智其益廣乎
punctuated: 之庥美，君臣和德之極致哉！薄海內外，民恬物熙，九夷君長，奉琛款塞。斯誠太和充塞唐虞宇宙間，而漢人所稱「天之所以相，天之所以順」者，在此也已。然執事猶欲聞忠言讜論，以裨當代之盛美。愚也，何能明習國家事？然以區區芹曝之念，竊一籌之，則有四說焉：講讀之當勤也，覽斷之當親也，言路之當廣也，直宿之當慎也。夫今之經筵日講，儀制非不井井具也；然肅然而臨，儼然而退，講官所横經而議論者，其能一一當聖心乎？凡有疑義，當渙發綸音，特降清問，必求其洞然豁暢而後已；則庶乎旁引曲證，得悉其詞，而睿智其益廣乎！
translation_en: …the splendid beauty [of accepting remonstrance in the court of Shun] and the ultimate perfection of harmonious virtue between ruler and minister! Within and beyond the four seas, the people are content and all things flourish; the chieftains of the Nine Yi tribes present treasures and knock at the frontier passes in submission. Truly, this is a case of Supreme Harmony filling a universe like that of Yao and Shun, and what the men of Han called "that whereby Heaven assists, and that whereby Heaven complies" lies right here. Yet Your Excellency still wishes to hear loyal words and forthright counsel to supplement the flourishing beauty of the present era. Foolish as I am, how could I be well-versed in the affairs of the state? Nevertheless, out of my humble desire—like offering wild celery or basking in the sun—if I may venture to reckon the matter, there are four points: first, that exposition and reading in the Classics Colloquium ought to be diligent; second, that reviewing memorials and making decisions ought to be done in person; third, that the avenues of speech ought to be broadened; and fourth, that night-duty attendance ought to be treated with care. Now, as for the present Classics Colloquia (jingyan) and Daily Lectures (rijiang), their ceremonial regulations are not without orderly completeness. Yet if the sovereign approaches in solemn silence and withdraws with grave dignity, can what the Lecturers expound across the open Classics correspond in every detail to the Sage Mind? Whenever there is a doubtful point of meaning, His Majesty ought to issue his silken words and specially hand down clear inquiries, insisting on reaching a thorough and unobstructed comprehension before stopping. Then, perhaps, through wide-ranging citations and detailed proofs, the lecturers will be able to present their explanations in full, and the Imperial wisdom will be broadened all the more!

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
人主雖至神聖閭閻細務弗能周也今百官奏
疏四方之利弊具焉誠不厭旁午
躬親覽閱於其關繫
國是者時
召二三大臣咨詢可否而
裁度之則凡邊防國計刑獄災祥之類日達于
九重而
天聽其益擴乎古者諫無常官自公卿百執事
下至瞽御工師之賤皆諫也
===
今制寧無太狹乎誠倣周官遺意廣開言路
以招致之而止輦以受其言虛懷以納其
議如此而
主闕不補臣忠不宣者吾未之信也古者官必
擇人卽侍御僕從罔非吉士今之直宿果
皆若人乎誠於斯時嚴擇人以充其選俾
燕寢閒懿戒之儆出入有剪桐之規如此
而非幾或貢
天德弗純者吾未之信也凡此四者皆所以昭
punctuated: 人主雖至神聖，閭閻細務弗能周也。今百官奏疏，四方之利弊具焉。誠不厭旁午，躬親覽閱，於其關繫國是者，時召二三大臣，咨詢可否而裁度之，則凡邊防、國計、刑獄、災祥之類，日達于九重，而天聽其益擴乎！古者諫無常官，自公卿、百執事，下至瞽御、工師之賤，皆諫也。今制寧無太狹乎？誠倣《周官》遺意，廣開言路以招致之，而止輦以受其言，虛懷以納其議。如此，而主闕不補、臣忠不宣者，吾未之信也。古者官必擇人，卽侍御、僕從罔非吉士；今之直宿，果皆若人乎？誠於斯時嚴擇人以充其選，俾燕寢閒《懿戒》之儆，出入有剪桐之規。如此，而非幾或貢、天德弗純者，吾未之信也。凡此四者，皆所以昭
translation_en:
Even when a ruler is most divinely sage, he cannot be thoroughly familiar with all the minute affairs of the common people's alleys and lanes. Today, in the memorials submitted by the hundred officials, the advantages and abuses of the four quarters are all set forth. If he truly does not weary of their profusion, personally peruses and examines them, and, regarding those matters that bear upon fundamental state policy, from time to time summons two or three great ministers to consult them on what should be approved or rejected and then weighs and decides upon them, then all matters such as frontier defense, state finances, criminal administration, and portents of disaster or good fortune will daily reach the ninefold palace, and will not the imperial hearing thereby be broadened even further?

In antiquity, remonstrance was not confined to regular speaking officials; from the dukes, ministers, and hundred officeholders down to lowly blind musicians, attendants, and master artisans, all offered remonstrance. Is not the present system perhaps too narrow? If we truly emulate the legacy of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), throw open the avenues of speech to invite and attract them, halt the imperial carriage to receive their words, and keep an open mind to accept their deliberations—if this is done, I cannot believe that the ruler's faults would go unrectified or the ministers' loyalty go unexpressed.

In antiquity, in filling offices one invariably selected the right men, so that even among close attendants and personal retinue there were none who were not worthy gentlemen; are those who keep night watch in the palace today really all such men? If at this time we strictly select men to fill these posts, so that in moments of private leisure in the imperial chambers there is the admonition of the "Ode of Reverent Warning" (Yijie), and in going out and coming in there is the corrective counsel of the "cutting of the paulownia leaf" (jiantong)—if this is done, I cannot believe that improper impulses would ever be presented [?] or that the sovereign's heavenly virtue would fail to be pure.

All four of these measures are the means by which to manifest…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
宣
令德嘉納讜謨兢業日塵以共臻夫太和之
治焉盛世君臣所以建無窮之基垂無窮
之聞者率茲道哉率茲道哉雖然其本則
君心繫之矣宋儒有言曰惟學可以養此
心惟敬可以存此心惟親近君子可以維
持此心故魏徵有十漸之戒陸贄勤九弊
之陳豫養防微因事納誨其道固如此
今日格心之功固賴二三大臣在也愚何敢
===
臆說焉
第二問
王　蓋
同考試官訓導孫　批〔論周禮者准裁靡定子獨以識其大爲言其見卓矣且据摭詳而議論確〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔獨見大意而詞足以發之〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔具見博雅〕
聖人有可傳之道而無盡傳之法道本大
中至正而不易法則隨時變易以從道也
punctuated:
宣令德、嘉納讜謨，兢業日塵，以共臻夫太和之治焉。盛世君臣所以建無窮之基、垂無窮之聞者，率茲道哉！率茲道哉！雖然，其本則君心繫之矣。宋儒有言曰：「惟學可以養此心，惟敬可以存此心，惟親近君子可以維持此心。」故魏徵有十漸之戒，陸贄勤九弊之陳，豫養防微，因事納誨，其道固如此。今日格心之功，固賴二三大臣在也，愚何敢臆說焉！

第二問
王　蓋
同考試官訓導孫　批〔論《周禮》者准裁靡定，子獨以「識其大」爲言，其見卓矣，且据摭詳而議論確。〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔獨見大意，而詞足以發之。〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔具見博雅。〕

聖人有可傳之道，而無盡傳之法。道本大中至正而不易，法則隨時變易以從道也。
translation_en:
… manifest and proclaim his fine virtue, welcome and accept upright counsel, and maintain cautious diligence day after day [? 日塵, likely for 日昪 or 日慎], so as to jointly attain governance of supreme harmony. That whereby sovereign and ministers of a flourishing age establish a boundless foundation and hand down a boundless reputation is by following this Way! Is by following this Way! Even so, its root depends upon the mind of the ruler. A Song-dynasty Confucian once said: "Only through learning can one nourish this mind; only through reverence can one preserve this mind; only through drawing close to noble men can one sustain this mind." Thus Wei Zheng 魏徵 offered his admonition on the "Ten Gradual Lapses," and Lu Zhi 陸贄 earnestly presented his "Nine Malpractices"—nurturing in advance and guarding against subtleincipient faults, tendering instruction as matters arose: such was indeed their Way. Today, the work of rectifying the ruler's mind surely relies upon the two or three great ministers in office; how would a foolish person like me dare to speak from mere conjecture!

Second Question
By Wang Gai 王蓋
Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor (xundao): [Those who discuss the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) have no fixed standard of judgment; you alone speak in terms of "grasping its great principles." Your insight is outstanding, and moreover your citations are detailed and your arguments sound.]
Comment by Examiner Dai, Instructor (jiaoyu): [He perceives the grand meaning with singular insight, and his words are sufficient to bring it forth.]
Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor (jiaoyu): [This fully demonstrates breadth of learning and elegance.]

The sages had a Way that could be transmitted, but no institutions (fa) that could be transmitted in every detail. The Way is fundamentally supreme in centrality and utmost in rectitude, and does not change; institutions, however, change with the times in order to follow the Way. …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
夫法之立也非不經畫盡制錯綜盡宜以
爲維持天下之具然不知其法雖善而歷
久則窮故必有與世推移者以神其用於
不匱譬之權衡設於此而低昻進退之隨
其物也故道可以該法法不足以盡道善
用經者惟能緣法以求心由心而會法則
可識其大於千載之上而聖人之精見矣
請因明問而敬陳之周禮一書儒先謂周
公致治之大法在其中姬聖極由衷之典
===
法天地而行教化以成文武之德監列聖
之制昭郁郁之文若大猷而垂彝憲者也
當其時四國順焉百辟刑焉旣醉嘉其太
平行葦歌其忠厚迨至康昭之後紀綱尚
明爰及春秋之世法度猶在若韓宣子齊
仲孫湫咸知周禮之足興可鏡也今考其
所載惟王建國辨方正位體國經野設官
分職以爲民極極者道之中也即五官之
中皆冠以數語此其大本大原孰非其法
punctuated: 夫法之立也，非不經畫盡制、錯綜盡宜，以爲維持天下之具；然不知其法雖善，而歷久則窮，故必有與世推移者，以神其用於不匱。譬之權衡設於此，而低昻進退之隨其物也。故道可以該法，法不足以盡道。善用經者，惟能緣法以求心，由心而會法，則可識其大於千載之上，而聖人之精見矣。請因明問而敬陳之。《周禮》一書，儒先謂周公致治之大法在其中。姬聖極由衷之典，法天地而行教化，以成文、武之德；監列聖之制，昭郁郁之文，若大猷而垂彝憲者也。當其時，四國順焉，百辟刑焉，《旣醉》嘉其太平，《行葦》歌其忠厚。迨至康、昭之後，紀綱尚明；爰及春秋之世，法度猶在。若韓宣子、齊仲孫湫，咸知周禮之足興，可鏡也。今考其所載：「惟王建國，辨方正位，體國經野，設官分職，以爲民極。」極者，道之中也。即五官之中，皆冠以數語，此其大本大原，孰非其法…
translation_en:
Now, when institutions are established, it is not that their planning fails to perfect the system or that their intricate arrangements fail to achieve full appropriateness as instruments for sustaining the realm. Yet if one fails to recognize that even good institutions become exhausted over the course of time, then there must be that which shifts with the ages in order to render their application wondrously inexhaustible. It is like a steelyard and balance set up here, while the rising and falling, advancing and retreating of the weight follow the object being weighed. Therefore, the Way can encompass institutions, whereas institutions are insufficient to exhaust the Way. Those skilled in applying the Classics are simply able to trace the institutions to seek the mind behind them, and from that mind to comprehend the institutions; thus they can recognize what is great in them across a thousand years above, and the essence of the sages becomes manifest. Allow me to respectfully set this forth in response to your enlightened question.

Regarding the work the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), earlier Confucians stated that the Duke of Zhou's great institutions for bringing about order are contained within it. The sage of the Ji clan brought forth canons from the depths of his heart, modeling them on Heaven and Earth to carry out moral transformation and thereby complete the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu; surveying the systems of the succession of former sages, he displayed a richly flourishing culture, conforming to the great plan and handing down enduring norms. In those times, the states of the four quarters were compliant, and the hundred lords took him as their model; the ode "Already Drunk with Wine" (Jizui) praised that era's great peace, and "Roadside Reeds" (Xingwei) sang of its loyal generosity. Down to the reigns after Kings Kang and Zhao, the foundational order was still clear; and even into the Spring and Autumn period, its laws and measures remained in place. Figures such as Han Xuanzi 韓宣子 and Zhongsun Qiu 仲孫湫 of Qi both knew that the rites of Zhou were sufficient to bring about a revival—this can serve as a mirror. If we now examine what is recorded therein: "It is the king who establishes the state, distinguishes the directions and rectifies the positions, gives structure to the capital and lays out the countryside, establishes offices and apportions duties, so as to serve as the standard for the people." This "standard" (ji) is the centrality of the Way. Indeed, each of the five offices is headed by these few phrases; as for this great foundation and great source, which part of it is not that from which its institutions…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
之所自出者故其布之爲制則井牧始於
黃帝而九夫經畫之制建弼服肪於唐堯
而九畿分國之制詳象刑做於舜而五刑
麗民之制具貢賦創於夏而典式法則之
制行官刑肇於商而廢置誅賞之制立唯
其義之精也朱子曰周官徧布周密乃周
公運用天理爛熟之書誠哉是言也柰經
秦火之後散逸無存自漢除挾書之律衆
書往往頗出諸儒執經競進周禮遂列於
===
九經矣維時顓門持業者非其師說不從
各立門戶者互相詆毀求勝或索諸儀章
度數之間或泥乎文字訓詁之末甚至援
引曲說竊取聖人之迹而强附之昔人謂
秦人焚經而經存諸儒窮經而經絕良有
以也故在劉歆信其爲是則以爲周公致
太平之迹林孝存排其爲非則以爲戰國
陰謀之書王安石作周官義而謂成周理
財之書則見以爲徧漢武帝得周官五篇
punctuated: 之所自出者？故其布之爲制，則井牧始於黃帝，而九夫經畫之制建；弼服肪於唐堯，而九畿分國之制詳；象刑做於舜，而五刑麗民之制具；貢賦創於夏，而典式法則之制行；官刑肇於商，而廢置誅賞之制立。唯其義之精也，朱子曰：「《周官》徧布周密，乃周公運用天理爛熟之書。」誠哉是言也！柰經秦火之後，散逸無存。自漢除挾書之律，衆書往往頗出，諸儒執經競進，《周禮》遂列於九經矣。維時顓門持業者，非其師說不從；各立門戶者，互相詆毀求勝。或索諸儀章度數之間，或泥乎文字訓詁之末，甚至援引曲說，竊取聖人之迹而强附之。昔人謂：「秦人焚經而經存，諸儒窮經而經絕。」良有以也！故在劉歆信其爲是，則以爲周公致太平之迹；林孝存排其爲非，則以爲戰國陰謀之書。王安石作《周官義》，而謂成周理財之書，則見以爲徧；漢武帝得《周官》五篇，
translation_en: …from which its laws derived? Therefore, when it was set forth as a system of institutions: the well-field and pasture divisions began with the Yellow Emperor, and here the system of laying out land by nine-householder units was established; the assisting five zones originated [reading 昉 for 肪] with Yao of Tang, and here the system of dividing the realm into nine domains was elaborated in detail; symbolic punishments started [reading 作 or 倣 for 做] with Shun, and here the system of applying the five punishments to the people was made complete; tribute and taxes were initiated in the Xia, and here the system of canons, models, laws, and rules was put into practice; punishments for officials began in the Shang, and here the system of dismissal, appointment, execution, and reward was set up. Simply because its principles are so refined, Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) said: "The Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) is comprehensive and thoroughly detailed; it is truly a book in which the Duke of Zhou applied the Principle of Heaven with complete mastery." How true are these words! Yet after going through the fires of Qin, it was scattered and lost so that nothing remained. Once the Han repealed the statute against possessing books, the various texts gradually reappeared here and there, the scholars clutches their classics and competed to advance them, and the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) was consequently ranked among the Nine Classics. At that time, those who specialized in a single school refused to follow anything other than their master's doctrines, while those who set up rival factions disparaged one another in order to prevail. Some sought its meaning merely among ceremonial emblems and numerical measures, while others got bogged down in the trivialities of wording and glosses; some even went so far as to cite crooked theories, appropriating the traces of the Sage and forcibly attaching their own ideas to them. Someone in the past said: "When the men of Qin burned the Classics, the Classics survived; when the scholars exhaustively analyzed the Classics, the Classics were destroyed." There is truly good reason for this! Thus, because Liu Xin 劉歆 believed it to be authentic, he regarded it as the traces by which the Duke of Zhou brought about Great Peace; whereas because Lin Xiaocun 林孝存 rejected it as spurious, he regarded it as a book of Warring States intrigues. When Wang Anshi 王安石 composed the Meaning of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan yi) and called it a book by which the成周 (Cheng Zhou) regime managed finances, his view was one-sided [reading 偏 for 徧]; and when Emperor Wu of Han 漢武帝 obtained the five sections of the Offices of Zhou…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
而謂瀆亂不經之書則見以爲謬是非紛
錯準裁靡定其曷能運通方之至理而獨
觀乎昭曠之道哉蓋自河間購以千金而
上之祕府可謂能表章矣然工匠器械何
取於考工遂使其書不信於天下故世儒
譏之曰累周禮者劉德也其有激之言乎
劉歆校理祕書而著之錄略可謂能發明
矣然六幹五均託名於泉府遂使其義不
明於天下胡氏父子曰周禮是王莽令劉
===
歆撰出其排斥之論乎近世說周禮者非
一人也宋淳熙中俞廷椿謂司空之篇實
襍出于五官之屬而著復古編王次點作
周官補遺元泰定中丘葵乃參訂二家之
說以爲成書吴澄則謂冬官未嘗亡而地
官之文實亡又欲以遂人入司空此非其
獨見與近世用周禮者非一人也王莽託
五均以立錢府官天下騷動是爲假用蘇
綽取以輔宇文周六官定而民叛是爲輕
punctuated: 而謂「瀆亂不經之書」，則見以爲謬。是非紛錯，準裁靡定，其曷能運通方之至理，而獨觀乎昭曠之道哉？蓋自河間購以千金而上之祕府，可謂能表章矣；然工匠器械何取於《考工》，遂使其書不信於天下。故世儒譏之曰：「累《周禮》者，劉德也。」其有激之言乎？劉歆校理祕書而著之《錄略》，可謂能發明矣；然六幹、五均託名於《泉府》，遂使其義不明於天下。胡氏父子曰：「《周禮》是王莽令劉歆撰出。」其排斥之論乎？近世說《周禮》者，非一人也。宋淳熙中，俞廷椿謂《司空》之篇實襍出于五官之屬，而著《復古編》；王次點作《周官補遺》。元泰定中，丘葵乃參訂二家之說以爲成書。吴澄則謂《冬官》未嘗亡，而《地官》之文實亡，又欲以《遂人》入《司空》。此非其獨見與？近世用《周禮》者，非一人也。王莽託五均以立錢府官，天下騷動，是爲假用；蘇綽取以輔宇文周，六官定而民叛，是爲輕…
translation_en: …and called it "a corrupt and uncanonical book," thus viewing it as erroneous. With right and wrong so confusedly entangled and standards of judgment unsettled, how can one grasp the ultimate principle of comprehensive understanding and perceive alone the bright and broad Way? Ever since Prince Xian of Hejian (Liu De 劉德) purchased it for a thousand pieces of gold and presented it to the Imperial Library, he could well be said to have brought it to prominence. Yet what was the point of drawing upon the "Record of Trades" (Kaogong ji 考工記) with its artisans and implements, thereby causing the book to be distrusted throughout the realm? Hence, scholars of the world ridiculed him, saying, "He who compromised the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli 周禮) was Liu De." Was this not an impassioned remark? Liu Xin (劉歆) collated the imperial library's texts and recorded it in the Summaries of the Seven Categories (Qilüe 七略), so he could well be said to have elucidated it. Yet the six monopolies (liugan 六幹) and five equalizations (wujun 五均) were falsely attributed to the "Treasury of Coinage" (Quanfu 泉府) section, thereby causing its true meaning to become obscured throughout the realm. The Hu father and son (Hu Anguo 胡安國 and Hu Hong 胡宏) said, "The Rites of Zhou was fabricated by Liu Xin at Wang Mang's (王莽) order." Was this not an argument meant to reject it? In recent ages, those who have expounded upon the Rites of Zhou have not been just one person. During the Chunxi era (1174–1189) of the Song, Yu Tingchun (俞廷椿) argued that the "Minister of Works" (Sikong 司空) section was actually mixed in among the subordinates of the other five offices, and he composed the Compilation for Returning to Antiquity (Fugu bian 復古編), while Wang Cidian (王次點) wrote the Supplement to the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan buyi 周官補遺). During the Taiding era (1324–1328) of the Yuan, Qiu Kui (丘葵) then consulted and collated the theories of both scholars to form a complete book. Wu Cheng (吳澄), for his part, argued that the "Winter Offices" (Dongguan 冬官) was never lost, whereas text from the "Earth Offices" (Diguan 地官) was actually what was lost, and he further wished to place the "Grandee of the Outlying Districts" (Suiren 遂人) into the "Minister of Works." Were these not their own unique views? In recent ages, those who have put the Rites of Zhou into practice have also not been just one person. Wang Mang used the pretext of the five equalizations to establish officials of the Treasury of Coinage, throwing the realm into turmoil—this was a fraudulent application. Su Chuo (蘇綽) adopted it to assist the Yuwen regime of Northern Zhou, and once the Six Offices were established, the people rebelled—this was a reckless…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
用王安石之用周官師心妬眞黨同伐異
新法之行無異公卿以下至於庶人咸指
湯矣乃妄引聖經敝精神於訓詁而卒以
其術誤天下此非其尤甚歟至於設官不
與王制合封建不與孟子合緣王制所說
朝聘或以爲文襄時事去籍之後煨燼之
餘中間互相抵牾不無焉先儒謂其間必
有末世增入者良有見矣夫說周禮者既
如此用周禮者又如此然則聖人之道終
===
不可明且行乎嗚呼聖人經世之書聖人
之心法爲之也聖人以其精義妙道而著
之爲大經大法其藝極不專于名數其議
制不局于比詳甚明矣譚之者庸可剽其
外邪而昧其內竅用之者庸可摹其耿指
而遺其弘猷哉是故六典九賦十二物之
教保息六之養以至頒比瀍經土地之類
此其彰彰大者也其間掌炭掌蜃哲蔟赤
犮與夫蟈氏焚牡鞠壺涿氏牡橰午之類
punctuated: 用。王安石之用《周官》，師心妬眞，黨同伐異；新法之行，無異公卿以下至於庶人咸指湯矣，乃妄引聖經，敝精神於訓詁，而卒以其術誤天下，此非其尤甚歟？至於設官不與《王制》合，封建不與《孟子》合，緣《王制》所說朝聘，或以爲文、襄時事，去籍之後、煨燼之餘，中間互相抵牾，不無焉。先儒謂其間必有末世增入者，良有見矣。夫說《周禮》者既如此，用《周禮》者又如此，然則聖人之道終不可明且行乎？嗚呼！聖人經世之書，聖人之心法爲之也。聖人以其精義妙道，而著之爲大經大法，其藝極不專于名數，其議制不局于比詳，甚明矣。譚之者庸可剽其外邪而昧其內竅，用之者庸可摹其耿指而遺其弘猷哉？是故六典、九賦、十二物之教、保息六之養，以至頒比、瀍、經土地之類，此其彰彰大者也；其間掌炭、掌蜃、哲蔟、赤犮，與夫蟈氏焚牡鞠、壺涿氏牡橰午之類，
translation_en:
… adoption. As for Wang Anshi's 王安石 application of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), he trusted only his own mind and was jealous of the truth, forming cliques with like-minded men and attacking dissenters. When his New Policies were put into effect, from the high ministers and nobles down to the common people, all felt as if they were being plunged into boiling water [?]. Yet he recklessly cited the sage's classic, exhausting his mental energy on scholastic glosses, and in the end misled the entire empire with his statecraft—was this not the most extreme case of all?

As for the fact that its establishment of offices does not accord with the "Royal Regulations" (Wangzhi), and its system of enfeoffment does not accord with the Mencius (Mengzi): because the court audiences and diplomatic missions described in the "Royal Regulations" are considered by some to be the affairs of the era of Dukes Wen and Xiang of Jin, after the feudal lords removed the records and among the remnants of the Qin fires, it is not without mutual contradictions. Earlier Confucians held that there must be later-age interpolations within them, which is truly an insightful view.

Now, since those who expound the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) are like this, and those who apply the Rites of Zhou are like that, can the Way of the Sages ultimately neither be elucidated nor put into practice? Alas! The book by which the Sages ordered the world was produced from the mind-method of the Sages. The Sages took their subtle principles and wondrous Way and set them forth as great standards and grand laws; it is abundantly clear that the ultimate standard of their art does not lie exclusively in names and numbers, and their deliberated institutions are not confined to minute details. How could those who discuss it merely plagiarize its external husks while remaining blind to its inner core, and how could those who apply it merely imitate its petty pointers while neglecting its grand plan?

Therefore, the six statutes, the nine revenues, the instruction in the twelve things, the nurturing through the six measures for preserving and resting the people, and down to the promulgation of registers, residential plots [?], and the division of lands—these are its manifestly great matters. Meanwhile, offices among them such as the Masters of Charcoal (Zhangtan), the Masters of Clam-shells (Zhangshen), the Destroyers of Nests (Zhecu [?]), and the Exterminators of Vermin (Chiba), along with matters like the Frog-Exterminators (Guoshi) burning male chrysanthemums and the Water-Pest Exterminators (Huzhuoshi) using elm-wood rods and ivory [?]…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
此其區區細者也河間獻王之初得此書
也典則煥乎可宗矣乃祚氏銜枚之疑其
隸司甲都則之闕其文渠豈慮不及此而
不敢以聰明加焉其冬官亡而得考工記
附補之也文采爛然可觀矣然知創巧述
之語嘉量寧侯之銘因文附見不敢爲五
官溷焉其猶有夏五郭公之思乎初安石
使還上書仁宗大要謂法先王之政當法
其意亹亹有稽及行新法何其悖所聞也
===
其均輸青苗之法往往捃摭周禮而附會
之比徵斂于民又何與周公意異也夫周
公敷大德于天下厚生正德利用備是矣
然且孅其宮室而驩愉之時其讀法而諄
誨之計其時之民不在於田廬則在族師
閭胥之庭不治稼穡則聞孝弟婣睦之教
民享樂利久矣復念民恐有不足於貿遷
者于是有司市辨物及國服爲息之法焉
惠民而不盡其財者如此是周公之理財
punctuated: 此其區區細者也。河間獻王之初得此書也，典則煥乎可宗矣；乃柞氏、銜枚之疑其隸，司甲、都則之闕其文，渠豈慮不及此，而不敢以聰明加焉？其冬官亡而得《考工記》附補之也，文采爛然可觀矣；然「知創巧述」之語、嘉量寧侯之銘，因文附見，不敢爲五官溷焉，其猶有「夏五」、「郭公」之思乎？初，安石使還，上書仁宗，大要謂：「法先王之政，當法其意。」亹亹有稽；及行新法，何其悖所聞也！其均輸、青苗之法，往往捃摭《周禮》而附會之；比徵斂于民，又何與周公意異也！夫周公敷大德于天下，厚生、正德、利用備是矣。然且孅其宮室而驩愉之，時其讀法而諄誨之；計其時之民，不在於田廬，則在族師、閭胥之庭，不治稼穡，則聞孝弟婣睦之教。民享樂利久矣，復念民恐有不足於貿遷者，于是有司市辨物及「國服爲息」之法焉。惠民而不盡其財者如此，是周公之理財，
translation_en: …these are its petty, minor details. When King Xian of Hejian 河間獻王 first obtained this book [the *Rites of Zhou* (*Zhouli* 周禮)], its canons and rules were brilliantly worthy of veneration; yet where the Tree-clearers (*Zeshi* 祚氏 [柞氏]) and the Gag-bearers (*Xianmei* 銜枚) were of doubtful affiliation, and where the texts for the Director of Armor (*Sijia* 司甲) and the Regulations of the Capital Dependencies (*Duze* 都則) were missing, was it that his thought failed to reach these points, so that he dared not impose his own cleverness upon them? And when the Office of Winter (*Dongguan* 冬官) was lost and the *Record of Artificers* (*Kaogong ji* 考工記) was obtained and appended to supplement it, its literary brilliance was splendid to behold; yet the sayings about "the wise creating and the skillful transmitting" and the inscriptions on the Standard Measure (*Jialiang* 嘉量) and the Peaceful Target (*Ninghou* 寧侯) were merely appended along with the text, without daring to confound them with the other five offices—did this not still carry the cautious spirit of leaving blanks like "Fifth Month of Xia" (*Xia wu* 夏五) and "Duke of Guo" (*Guo gong* 郭公) [in the *Spring and Autumn Annals*]? Earlier, when [Wang] Anshi 王安石 returned from a mission and submitted a memorial to Emperor Renzong 仁宗, his main point was that "in modeling oneself on the governance of the Former Kings, one ought to model oneself on their intent," which was tirelessly reasoned and well-founded; yet when he implemented his New Laws, how utterly he violated what he had learned! His methods of Equitable Transport (*junshu* 均輸) and Green Sprouts (*qingmiao* 青苗) time and again plucked phrases from the *Rites of Zhou* and strained to match them; yet when it came to exacting levies from the people, how different they were from the intent of the Duke of Zhou 周公! Now, when the Duke of Zhou spread his great virtue across the realm, the enrichment of livelihood, the rectification of virtue, and the provision of useful tools were all complete therein. Moreover, he refined their dwellings to bring them joy and comfort, and set regular times for reading the laws to instruct them earnestly; if one reckons the people of that age, when they were not in their field huts, they were in the courtyards of the Clan Preceptors (*zushi* 族師) and Neighborhood Assistants (*lüxu* 閭胥), and when they were not tending to sowing and reaping, they were hearing teachings of filial piety, brotherly respect, friendliness in marriage relations, and harmony. After the people had long enjoyed peace and benefit, he further bethought himself that the people might still face shortages in trade and exchange, and thereupon instituted the methods of the Market Supervisor (*Sishi* 司市) distinguishing goods and of "taking national service as the rate of interest" (*guofu wei xi* 國服爲息). To benefit the people without exhausting their wealth was like this; thus the Duke of Zhou's management of finances…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
乃導利而布之上下也安石于周禮所以
爲民極者將蔑其官而棄其制唯藉口於
國服爲息一言以便其掊剋富國之計內
之則設制置三司條例司外之則歸利權
於發運使心計者日夜持籌講畫突梯者
分行馳逐營幹卽桑弘羊孔僅輩筭利析
秋毫者不苛于此矣以此倣周禮致太平
何異于坐井闚天見一斑而以爲全豹與
上之誤天子下之誤蒼生甚矣安石之謬
===
也故先正有言曰制其產使無不均詳其
敎使無不學文武周公之大意也法古者
取其大意所屬而行之奚患于財之不足
哉不治其本而以理財爲先此周官所棄
也是故房琯以車戰致敗議者罪琯可也
罪車戰不可也安石以周禮貽毒議者罪
安石可也罪周禮不可也善夫朱子之言
曰周禮其間細碎處雖可疑其大體直非
聖人做不得而其讀孟子經界章亦曰孟
punctuated: 乃導利而布之上下也。安石于《周禮》所以爲民極者，將蔑其官而棄其制，唯藉口於「國服爲息」一言，以便其掊剋富國之計。內之則設制置三司條例司，外之則歸利權於發運使。心計者日夜持籌講畫，突梯者分行馳逐營幹，卽桑弘羊、孔僅輩筭利析秋毫者，不苛于此矣。以此倣《周禮》致太平，何異于坐井闚天、見一斑而以爲全豹與？上之誤天子，下之誤蒼生，甚矣安石之謬也！故先正有言曰：「制其產使無不均，詳其敎使無不學，文、武、周公之大意也。法古者，取其大意所屬而行之，奚患于財之不足哉？」不治其本，而以理財爲先，此《周官》所棄也。是故房琯以車戰致敗，議者罪琯可也，罪車戰不可也；安石以《周禮》貽毒，議者罪安石可也，罪《周禮》不可也。善夫朱子之言曰：「《周禮》其間細碎處雖可疑，其大體直非聖人做不得。」而其讀《孟子》經界章亦曰：「孟
translation_en: … was to channel benefits and distribute them between above and below. As for that by which the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) established the standard for the people, [Wang] Anshi 王安石 disregarded its offices and discarded its institutions, using as his pretext only the single phrase "taking state service as interest" to facilitate his schemes for enriching the state through extortionate exactions. At court, he established the Finance Planning Commission (Zhizhi sansi tiaoli si); in the provinces, he concentrated fiscal authority in the hands of the Transport Commissioners (Fayun shi). Scheming calculators held their counting-rods day and night to deliberate and plan, while slick opportunists fanned out to race about and manage affairs; even the likes of Sang Hongyang 桑弘羊 and Kong Jin 孔僅, who calculated profit down to the tip of an autumn hair, were no more harsh than this. To imitate the Rites of Zhou in this manner in order to bring about Great Peace—how is it any different from sitting in a well to peer at the sky, or catching sight of a single spot and taking it for the whole leopard? Above, he misled the Son of Heaven; below, he brought ruin to the common people. Extreme indeed was Anshi's folly! Therefore a former worthy said: "To regulate their livelihood so that there is no inequality, and to elaborate their instruction so that no one goes unlearned—this was the grand intent of Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou. Those who model themselves on antiquity should grasp where that grand intent lies and put it into practice; what worry would there be over an insufficiency of wealth?" Failing to attend to the root while making fiscal administration the priority—this is what the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) rejected. Thus, when Fang Guan 房琯 suffered defeat by using chariot warfare, for critics to blame Guan is permissible, but to blame chariot warfare is not; when Anshi left a poisonous legacy by using the Rites of Zhou, for critics to blame Anshi is permissible, but to blame the Rites of Zhou is not. Admirable indeed are the words of Master Zhu [Xi 朱熹]: "Although the minute details within the Rites of Zhou may be open to doubt, its grand framework truly could not have been made by anyone other than a sage." title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
子之學識其大若朱子者可謂洞見周公
之大者乎讀周禮者亦惟得其大以會通
其意得其意以妙用其法則周禮固可維
持萬世無弊也愚于是竊有望焉
第三問
何偉
同考試官教諭湯　批〔論兩漢士風各得忠厚正直一偏而要之中行此確論也宜錄之〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔論士風而歸重於陶鑄世道之說誠致行非漫言者〕
===
考試官教諭楊　批〔議論正大有裨風教〕
士君子所以受天下之大者存乎量所以
荷天下之艱者存乎節夫士之有量如山
之能藏疾也如海之能納汙也士之有節
如劍之利而耀鍔也如弓之勁而及遠也
量匪徒也泰山惟高而後土壤藏焉滄海
惟深而後細流納焉茍一於茹納而失之
薄植則汚汚祇足以為汙節匪徒也莫邪
punctuated:
子之學識其大。」若朱子者，可謂洞見周公之大者乎！讀《周禮》者，亦惟得其大以會通其意，得其意以妙用其法，則《周禮》固可維持萬世無弊也。愚于是竊有望焉。

第三問
何偉
同考試官教諭湯　批：〔論兩漢士風，各得忠厚、正直一偏，而要之中行，此確論也，宜錄之。〕
考試官教諭戴　批：〔論士風而歸重於陶鑄世道之說，誠致行，非漫言者。〕
考試官教諭楊　批：〔議論正大，有裨風教。〕

士君子所以受天下之大者，存乎量；所以荷天下之艱者，存乎節。夫士之有量，如山之能藏疾也，如海之能納汙也；士之有節，如劍之利而耀鍔也，如弓之勁而及遠也。量匪徒也，泰山惟高而後土壤藏焉，滄海惟深而後細流納焉。茍一於茹納而失之薄植，則汚汚祇足以為汙。節匪徒也，莫邪
translation_en:
… [Meng]zi's learning recognized what is great." Someone like Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) may truly be said to have penetratingly perceived the greatness of the Duke of Zhou! If those who read the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli 周禮) likewise grasp only what is great in it so as to thoroughly comprehend its intent, and grasp its intent so as to marvelously apply its methods, then the Rites of Zhou can surely sustain ten thousand generations without abuse. In this I humbly place my hopes.

Third Policy Question
He Wei 何偉
Associate Examiner, Instructor Tang 湯 comments: [This essay argues that the literati ethos of the Western and Eastern Han each attained only one side—either loyal magnanimity or uprightness—and brings them back to the mean of balanced conduct. This is an unassailable argument; it ought to be selected for publication.]
Examiner, Instructor Dai 戴 comments: [In discussing the literati ethos, it places ultimate weight on the doctrine of molding the ways of the world. It truly aims at practical implementation and is not mere idle talk.]
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊 comments: [The argument is upright and grand, beneficial to moral customs and education.]

That whereby a scholar-gentleman accommodates the greatness of the world lies in his capacity for tolerance; that whereby he shoulders the hardships of the world lies in his moral integrity. Now, a scholar's possessing tolerance is like a mountain's ability to harbor imperfections, or the sea's ability to take in filth; a scholar's possessing integrity is like a sword's being sharp and gleaming at the edge, or a bow's being strong and reaching afar. Yet tolerance does not exist in vain: Mount Tai is first lofty, and only then is earth sheltered within it; the vast sea is first deep, and only then are trickling streams received into it. If one is solely bent on taking everything in while failing due to shallow foundations, then what is filthy will merely suffice to defile. Nor does integrity exist in vain: the Moye 莫邪 sword's…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
之鋒百鍊而後試焉虞機之張省括而後
釋焉茍一於剛勁而失之淺衷則嶢嶢適
所以爲缺故量合於節斯其量不淆而受
大者有其地節出於量斯其節不激而荷
艱者有其基明於此義然後可以觀形察
質而定天下士矣執事發策以兩漢習尚
爲問得非以輿㶚佔俾有閎覽而高議者
乎愚非其人也請得述其涯略以對夫光
岳之氣代有厚薄風會之流世有升降人
===
生其間習焉而得其性之所近故其剛柔
淺深不可以一律齊也惟聖人兼淳耀之
美而學體天地之純其制行隨時變易同
歸於道皆可以教後世自中庸以下則沉
潛高明之不能自克箕子固以㣧之况乎
叔季之世漸漬於失教被服於成俗者哉
昔虞夏殷周之盛九官相讓三事推賢和
之至也而不以度量名弼直欽於四鄰正
直聞於四國節甚偉也而不以氣節名蓋
punctuated:
之鋒，百鍊而後試焉；虞機之張，省括而後釋焉。茍一於剛勁而失之淺衷，則嶢嶢適所以爲缺。故量合於節，斯其量不淆，而受大者有其地；節出於量，斯其節不激，而荷艱者有其基。明於此義，然後可以觀形察質，而定天下士矣。

執事發策，以兩漢習尚爲問，得非以輿㶚佔俾有閎覽而高議者乎？愚非其人也，請得述其涯略以對。

夫光岳之氣，代有厚薄；風會之流，世有升降。人生其間，習焉而得其性之所近，故其剛柔淺深不可以一律齊也。惟聖人兼淳耀之美，而學體天地之純，其制行隨時變易，同歸於道，皆可以教後世。自中庸以下，則沉潛高明之不能自克，箕子固以㣧之，况乎叔季之世，漸漬於失教，被服於成俗者哉？昔虞、夏、殷、周之盛，九官相讓，三事推賢，和之至也，而不以度量名；弼直欽於四鄰，正直聞於四國，節甚偉也，而不以氣節名。蓋…
translation_en:
… edge is tested only after a hundred temperings; the Forester's crossbow trigger, once drawn, is released only after inspecting the nock. If one is solely bent on unyielding strength while erring through a shallow heart, then towering rigidity is precisely what leads to shattering. Therefore, when magnanimity is joined with integrity, one's magnanimity does not become muddled, and he who takes on great responsibilities has the capacity to do so; when integrity arises out of magnanimity, one's integrity does not become extreme, and he who shoulders difficulties has the foundation to do so. Only when one understands this principle can one observe appearances, examine inner substance, and appraise the scholars of the realm.

Your Excellency has posed a policy question asking about the customs and ethos of the Western and Eastern Han dynasties—could it not be that you expect among the students reciting texts by the Yu and Ba rivers [?] someone of broad learning and lofty discourse? I am not such a person, yet I beg leave to set forth a general outline in reply.

Now, the vital energy of thecelestial lights and sacred peaks is thick or thin depending on the era; the currents of custom and convention rise or fall depending on the age. People born amidst them become habituated and attain what is closest to their own nature; thus their firmness or gentleness, their shallowness or depth, cannot be made uniform by a single standard. Only the sage combines the beauties of pure brilliance, and his learning embodies the wholeness of Heaven and Earth; his conduct changes in accordance with the times yet returns alike to the Way, so that in all cases it can instruct posterity. From the level of the mean downward, however, those who are reserved or those who are high-minded cannot overcome their own biases—Jizi (Viscount of Ji) indeed already worried over this [?], how much more so in later, declining ages, when people are steeped in failed instruction and clothed in established customs! In ancient times, during the flourishing of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou, the Nine Offices yielded to one another and the Three Ministers promoted the worthy—this was the culmination of harmony, yet they were not famed merely for "magnanimity"; assisting rectitude was revered by the four neighboring associates, and uprightness was heard of throughout the four quarters of the realm—this was magnificent integrity, yet they were not famed merely for "moral integrity."
