title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
太和渾龐之氣融液於當時宇宙間未雕
未琢故人稟全賦世多全才不可以偏長
目也代之衰也眞淳漓而大道隱學士大
夫言風俗近古者蓋推兩漢云西漢自高
祖滌煩苛孝文脩玄默一時開國論議務
破觚爲圜斵雕爲朴故士專以長厚相訐
慕時則有見人有過掩匿覆蓋而斥文言
刻深者曹參氏之以清淨蒙譽也有郎官
有譴常蒙其罪有功常讓他將者衛綰之
===
以醇謹得幸也買金償同舍爲官掩吏迹
非直不疑之稱爲長者乎爲吏不案人官
屬不敢欺非張叔之號爲愛人乎之數子
者類以德量名若自託於忠厚矣然和光
同塵之習勝而彈冠振衣之風微君子譏
其近於佞則所少者正直也東漢自世祖
首褒勸顯宗尚察慧赫然中興氣象雲蒸
飈馳嚮風隨流故士爭以行誼相頡頏時
則有少厲清節而贓汙解印綬者范孟博
punctuated: 太和渾龐之氣，融液於當時宇宙間，未雕未琢，故人稟全賦，世多全才，不可以偏長目也。代之衰也，眞淳漓而大道隱。學士大夫言風俗近古者，蓋推兩漢云。西漢自高祖滌煩苛，孝文脩玄默，一時開國論議，務破觚爲圜、斵雕爲朴，故士專以長厚相訐慕。時則有見人有過，掩匿覆蓋，而斥文言刻深者，曹參氏之以清淨蒙譽也；有郎官有譴，常蒙其罪，有功，常讓他將者，衛綰之以醇謹得幸也。買金償同舍，爲官掩吏迹，非直不疑之稱爲長者乎？爲吏不案人，官屬不敢欺，非張叔之號爲愛人乎？之數子者，類以德量名，若自託於忠厚矣。然和光同塵之習勝，而彈冠振衣之風微，君子譏其近於佞，則所少者正直也。東漢自世祖首褒勸，顯宗尚察慧，赫然中興氣象，雲蒸飈馳，嚮風隨流，故士爭以行誼相頡頏。時則有少厲清節，而贓汙解印綬者，范孟博
translation_en:
… the qi of supreme harmony and vast wholeness melted and flowed throughout the cosmos at that time, uncarved and unpolished. Therefore, people were endowed with complete natures, the age had many complete talents, and one could not label them by any partial strength. When the ages declined, true purity thinned out and the Great Way became obscured. Scholars and grandees who speak of customs approaching antiquity generally point to the Two Han dynasties.

In the Western Han, after Gaozu (Emperor Gaozu) swept away vexatious harshness and Xiaowen (Emperor Wen) cultivated mysterious quietude, the founding discussions of the era strove to round off corners and hew ornateness back into simplicity. Consequently, gentlemen exclusively admired one another [?] for being generous and magnanimous. At that time, there was one who, upon seeing others' faults, covered and concealed them, while dismissing those whose written words were harsh and severe—this was Cao Can 曹參 winning praise through quiet purity. There was one who, when Court Gentlemen were reprimanded, always took the blame upon himself, and when there was merit, always yielded it to other generals—this was Wei Wan 衛綰 gaining favor through pure caution. Buying gold to repay a roommate, and as an official covering up the tracks of his subordinates—was this not Zhi Buyi 直不疑 being acclaimed as a man of generous virtue? Serving as an official without prosecuting people, yet his subordinates did not dare to deceive him—was this not Zhang Shu 張叔 (Zhang Ou 張歐) being known for loving the people? These several gentlemen were all famed for their moral capacity, as if entrusting themselves to loyalty and generosity. Yet the habit of softening one's light and mingling with the dust prevailed, while the ethos of dusting off one's cap and shaking out one's robes grew faint. Superior men criticized them as being close to flattery; thus what they lacked was uprightness.

In the Eastern Han, after Shizu (Emperor Guangwu) first promoted praise and encouragement and Xianzong (Emperor Ming) esteemed perceptive discernment, the glorious atmosphere of dynastic restoration rose like clouds and raced like a whirlwind. Turning toward the wind and following the current, gentlemen vied with one another in righteous conduct. At that time, there was one who honed pure integrity from his youth, and before whom corrupt officials untied their seal cords and resigned—this was Fan Mengbo 范孟博 (Fan Pang 范滂)…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
之慊慨澄清也有聲名自高而士號爲登
龍門者李元禮之模楷天下也不接賓客
一榻常懸者非陳仲舉之不畏强禦乎曉
譬曲直爭者無怨非陳太丘之表正鄉閭
乎之數子者類以氣節名若自負於正直
矣然洗垢索瘢之俗熾而磨稜合罅之義
疎君子譏其過於激則所少者忠厚也當
其時士固有特立獨行不苟同於俗者吾
於武帝之朝得一汲長孺焉招不來麾不
===
去面折公孫之飾詐斥張湯以刀筆謣謣
一士足以寢淮南之謀而當社稷臣之許
者其誠頹波中之砥柱哉吾於安帝之朝
得一黄叔度焉澄不清撓不濁倨傲者見
之正容鄙吝者聞之潛消汪汪千頃足以
陋奉高汎濫之器而飄然於汙世矰繳之
外者其誠鴻冥中之鳳凰哉嘗因是而反
覆兩漢之國勢士風始未嘗不崇大雅後
稍陵夷也西京之俗重朴茂猶有大羹不
punctuated: 之慊慨澄清也；有聲名自高，而士號爲登龍門者，李元禮之模楷天下也；不接賓客，一榻常懸者，非陳仲舉之不畏强禦乎？曉譬曲直，爭者無怨，非陳太丘之表正鄉閭乎？之數子者，類以氣節名，若自負於正直矣；然洗垢索瘢之俗熾，而磨稜合罅之義疎，君子譏其過於激，則所少者忠厚也。當其時，士固有特立獨行、不苟同於俗者。吾於武帝之朝，得一汲長孺焉：招不來，麾不去，面折公孫之飾詐，斥張湯以刀筆，謣謣一士，足以寢淮南之謀，而當社稷臣之許者，其誠頹波中之砥柱哉！吾於安帝之朝，得一黄叔度焉：澄不清，撓不濁，倨傲者見之正容，鄙吝者聞之潛消，汪汪千頃，足以陋奉高汎濫之器，而飄然於汙世矰繳之外者，其誠鴻冥中之鳳凰哉！嘗因是而反覆兩漢之國勢士風，始未嘗不崇大雅，後稍陵夷也。西京之俗重朴茂，猶有大羹不
translation_en:
… impassioned aspiration to purify the realm. As for holding one's reputation aloft so that scholars called being received by him "ascending the Dragon Gate," that was Li Yuanli 李元禮 (Li Ying 李膺) serving as a model for the entire realm. Receiving no guests yet keeping a single couch perpetually hung up—was that not Chen Zhongju 陳仲舉 (Chen Fan 陳蕃), who never feared the powerful and tyrannical? Explaining right and wrong so clearly that disputants harbored no resentment—was that not Chen Taiqiu 陳太丘 (Chen Shi 陳寔) setting a righteous standard for his local community? These several gentlemen were all famed for their moral courage and integrity, as though priding themselves on uprightness. Yet the custom of washing away dirt only to search for scars burned fiercely, while the principle of smoothing sharp edges and mending rifts grew tenuous; the superior man criticizes them for being overly extreme, for what they lacked was loyal generosity.

In those times, there were indeed scholars who stood independent and walked alone, refusing to conform lightly to popular custom. At the court of Emperor Wu 武帝, I find one Ji Changru 汲長孺 (Ji An 汲黯): summoned, he would not come; waved away, he would not leave. To his face he rebuked Gongsun弘 (Gongsun Hong 公孫弘) for his affected deceit, and he denounced Zhang Tang 張湯 as a mere pettifogging clerk. A single outspoken scholar [? 謣謣, for 諤諤], sufficient to put to rest the treasonous plot of the King of Huainan 淮南 and worthy of the praise of being a "minister of the altars of soil and grain"—was he not truly a pillar rock amid the collapsing waves! At the court of Emperor An 安帝, I find one Huang Shudu 黃叔度 (Huang Xian 黃憲): clarify him and he becomes no clearer; stir him and he becomes no murkier. Seeing him, the arrogant straightened their countenance; hearing of him, mean and petty thoughts melted away unseen. Vast and deep like a thousand acres of water, sufficient to make Dai Fenggao's 戴奉高 (Dai Liang 戴良) overflowing vessel seem shallow, and soaring freely beyond the tethered arrows of a sullied world—was he not truly a phoenix high in the vast firmament!

Because of this, I have repeatedly reflected upon the national momentum and the ethos of the literati in the Two Han dynasties: in the beginning, they never failed to revere great elegance, though later they gradually declined. The customs of the Western Capital (Western Han) valued unadorned substance; they still retained the spirit of the sacrificial broth left…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
和大圭不琢之意足以培國之元氣其弊
也習爲卑論儕俗而博榮名雖以孔光劉
歆之通經宿儒猶甘心僭僞之羽翼而不
耻則積弱易廢之勢也東京之俗貴高潔
猶之虎豹在山鵰鶚在霄足以張國之神
氣其弊也務爲噓枯吹生而眛幾先至於
俊廚顧及之號興歘然扞當世之文罔而
不悔則過剛易折之勢也元始之季舉國
若狂坐視乎大厦之顛熹平之後名義凜
===
然猶足懾夫問鼎之雄識者殆不無軒輊
於其中矣第律諸周行則槩乎未聞道耳
楊中立有言西漢之士喜功名而不務奇
節東漢之士貴節義而不通時變皆爲世
變所移而眛夫中行其於二代人物之權
衡審矣今世之命爲士者動稱引隆古而
卑視近代迨叀考其操行乃有大謬不然
者以爲懦也則又疑於枝媚以爲矯也則
復類於鉤進蓋俗之漸人波流風靡視兩
punctuated: 和、大圭不琢之意，足以培國之元氣。其弊也，習爲卑論，儕俗而博榮名，雖以孔光、劉歆之通經宿儒，猶甘心僭僞之羽翼而不耻，則積弱易廢之勢也。東京之俗貴高潔，猶之虎豹在山，鵰鶚在霄，足以張國之神氣。其弊也，務爲噓枯吹生，而眛幾先，至於「俊、廚、顧、及」之號興，歘然扞當世之文罔而不悔，則過剛易折之勢也。元始之季，舉國若狂，坐視乎大厦之顛；熹平之後，名義凜然，猶足懾夫問鼎之雄。識者殆不無軒輊於其中矣，第律諸周行，則槩乎未聞道耳。楊中立有言：「西漢之士，喜功名而不務奇節；東漢之士，貴節義而不通時變。皆爲世變所移，而眛夫中行。」其於二代人物之權衡審矣。今世之命爲士者，動稱引隆古而卑視近代；迨叀考其操行，乃有大謬不然者。以爲懦也，則又疑於枝媚；以爲矯也，則復類於鉤進。蓋俗之漸人，波流風靡，視兩…
translation_en: … remain unseasoned and the grand jade tablet remains uncarved, which was sufficient to cultivate the vital energy of the state. Yet its defect was that men grew accustomed to humble discourse, conforming to vulgarity to win glorious reputation; even venerable Confucians thoroughly versed in the classics like Kong Guang 孔光 and Liu Xin 劉歆 willingly acted as the wings of a usurper without shame—such was the tendency of accumulated weakness easily falling into ruin. The customs of the Eastern Capital valued lofty purity, like tigers and leopards in the mountains or eagles and ospreys in the sky, which was sufficient to expand the spiritual vigor of the state. Yet its defect was that men strove to breathe life into the withered and blow breath into the living [through partisan praise and blame] while remaining blind to early portents; by the time the designations of the "Eminent, Treasured, Steadfast, and Guides" (Jun, Chu, Gu, Ji) arose, they abruptly defied the legal net of the age without regret—such was the tendency of excessive rigidity easily snapping. At the close of the Yuanshi reign [1–5 CE], the whole country went as if mad, sitting idly by while the great edifice toppled; after the Xiping reign [172–178 CE], moral duty remained awe-inspiring, still enough to cow ambitious warlords who would inquire after the imperial tripods. Discerning observers can hardly avoid ranking one above the other, yet if measured against the highway of the Zhou, neither had heard of the true Way at all. Yang Zhongli 楊中立 [Yang Shi 楊時] had a saying: "The scholars of the Western Han delighted in merit and fame and did not strive for extraordinary integrity; the scholars of the Eastern Han valued integrity and righteousness and did not understand changing circumstances. Both were shifted by the transformations of their ages and remained blind to the Middle Way." His weighing of the figures of the two dynasties is precise indeed. Those who are called scholars in the present age constantly cite high antiquity and look down upon recent eras; yet when one specifically [?] examines their conduct, it turns out to be utterly contrary to their words. If one considers them timid, they also seem suspiciously close to fawning and flattery [?]; if one considers them uncompromising, they again resemble those who angle for advancement. Indeed, as customs steep into men, they drift with the waves and bend with the wind; compared to the scholars of the two [Han dynasties]…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
漢之士又不知遷庭何如毋亦所以風之
者有未至乎昔董仲舒曰不素養士而求
賢猶不琢玉而求文采也夫四代之學考
諸經可見矣曰直溫寬栗之謨也曰智仁
中和之訓也于時日宣日嚴克稱有常之
吉無偏無陂咸遵蕩平之路者豈獨淳風
攸萃哉蓋得於輔翼綱紀之所陶成者居
多焉後世之養士非古之所以養士矣居
今而志古者將安所度哉夫善調瑟者
===
更其浾灋要於和而已善持衡者權其低
昂要於平而已是故上之養士也抑詭恠
崇本實識極重之勢貴未然之防時尚包
荒則旌別以倡之使柔而不流於懦時尚
雕琢則惇大以覆之使剛而不淪於虐勵
世者此其亦憾乎士之自養也析義理變
氣質知欲其圓行欲其方舉世偷薄吾帥
以厚有瑾瑜匿瑕之意而不失廉隅舉世
混濁吾振以清有萬仞壁立之操而不□
punctuated: 漢之士，又不知遷庭何如，毋亦所以風之者有未至乎？昔董仲舒曰：「不素養士而求賢，猶不琢玉而求文采也。」夫四代之學，考諸經可見矣。曰「直溫寬栗」之謨也，曰「智仁中和」之訓也。于時日宣日嚴，克稱有常之吉；無偏無陂，咸遵蕩平之路者，豈獨淳風攸萃哉？蓋得於輔翼綱紀之所陶成者居多焉。後世之養士，非古之所以養士矣。居今而志古者，將安所度哉？夫善調瑟者，更其浾灋，要於和而已；善持衡者，權其低昂，要於平而已。是故上之養士也，抑詭恠，崇本實，識極重之勢，貴未然之防。時尚包荒，則旌別以倡之，使柔而不流於懦；時尚雕琢，則惇大以覆之，使剛而不淪於虐。勵世者，此其亦憾乎？士之自養也，析義理，變氣質，知欲其圓，行欲其方。舉世偷薄，吾帥以厚，有瑾瑜匿瑕之意，而不失廉隅；舉世混濁，吾振以清，有萬仞壁立之操，而不□
translation_en: … the scholars of the Western and Eastern Han, one knows not how much farther removed they are! Could it not be that the means of influencing them have fallen short? In the past, Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 said: "Not cultivating scholars beforehand while seeking the worthy is like not carving jade while seeking fine luster." Now, the learning of the Four Dynasties can be seen by examining the Classics. There is the counsel of being "straightforward yet mild, broad-minded yet reverent," and there is the instruction of "wisdom, benevolence, equilibrium, and harmony." At that time, daily manifesting and daily revering virtues so as to match the auspiciousness of constancy, and being without偏 (partiality) or obliquity so that all followed the broad and level road—was this merely because pure customs gathered there? Rather, for the most part it was achieved through the molding and guidance of supportive institutions and fundamental principles. The way later ages cultivate scholars is not the way antiquity cultivated scholars. For those who live in the present yet set their minds on antiquity, by what measure shall they proceed? Now, one who is skilled at tuning a zither alters the stringing method [?] (浾灋), aiming only at harmony; one who is skilled at holding a balance weighs its rise and fall, aiming only at levelness. Therefore, when superiors cultivate scholars, they suppress the deceitful and strange, exalt the fundamental and substantial, recognize trends of extreme imbalance, and value precautions taken before things come to pass. When the times favor indiscriminate tolerance, they distinguish the good and the bad to lead the way, making people gentle without degenerating into weakness; when the times favor harsh carving, they shelter them with generous magnanimity, making people firm without sinking into cruelty. For those who encourage the world, is this not the plumb line [?] (憾)? When scholars cultivate themselves, they analyze moral principles and transform their physical temperament, desiring their knowledge to be well-rounded and their conduct to be square. When the whole world is frivolous and mean, I lead it with generosity, holding the spirit of fine jade that conceals flaws without losing my sharp integrity; when the whole world is muddy and turbid, I rouse it with purity, maintaining the integrity of a cliff standing ten thousand ren high without [?]…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
門戶祇行者此其正鵠乎雖然士風之轉
移非文法禁令所能及也昔孔子觀河梁
之厲水而出者曰水猶可以忠信誠身親
之而況人乎古之化天下者神凝於穆清
之上而意流於海隅之遠浸潤如雨露鼓
動如雷霆以之駕馭寰宇鼓舞英豪如桴
鼓之相應臂指之相使故不下堂室而海
內之情舉得者誠使然也不此之務而偈
偈於法禁之末日提耳而令之曰吾將以
===
移風將以易俗則亦近於朝四暮三之術
矣天下其孰能信之蓋聞九皐之鶴鳴則
四野聞其聲海上之人機心一生則從游
之漚鳥翔舞而不下天不容偽其幾固如
此也後之君子有陶鑄世道之責者其設
誠於內而致行之也宛然鶴鳴之在皐而
無若好漚鳥之人然則幾矣
第四問
賈應舉
punctuated:
門戶，祇行者此其正鵠乎？雖然，士風之轉移，非文法禁令所能及也。昔孔子觀河梁之厲水而出者，曰：「水猶可以忠信誠身親之，而況人乎？」古之化天下者，神凝於穆清之上，而意流於海隅之遠，浸潤如雨露，鼓動如雷霆，以之駕馭寰宇，鼓舞英豪，如桴鼓之相應、臂指之相使，故不下堂室而海內之情舉得者，誠使然也。不此之務，而偈偈於法禁之末，日提耳而令之曰：「吾將以移風，將以易俗。」則亦近於朝四暮三之術矣，天下其孰能信之？蓋聞九皐之鶴鳴，則四野聞其聲；海上之人，機心一生，則從游之漚鳥翔舞而不下。天不容偽，其幾固如此也。後之君子有陶鑄世道之責者，其設誠於內而致行之也，宛然鶴鳴之在皐，而無若好漚鳥之人然，則幾矣。
第四問
賈應舉
translation_en:
…factional cliques. Is this not the true target for those who cultivate reverent conduct? Even so, the transformation of scholars' ethos is not something that legalistic regulations and prohibitions can achieve. Long ago, when Confucius observed a man crossing the surging waters at the river weir and emerging safely, he said: "If even water can be approached through loyalty, trustworthiness, and personal sincerity, how much more so human beings!" Those in antiquity who transformed the world concentrated their spirit in serene purity on high, while their intentions flowed out to the distant corners of the seas, soaking in like rain and dew and stirring like thunder and lightning. With this they directed the realm and inspired heroic talents, like drumstick and drum answering each other or the arm commanding the fingers. Thus, without descending from the hall or chamber, they fully grasped the sentiments of all within the seas—it was sincerity that made it so. If one does not attend to this, but instead bustles anxiously over the trivialities of laws and prohibitions, pulling people by the ear every day to command them, saying, "I am going to transform the ethos; I am going to change the customs!"—this comes close to the trick of "four in the morning and three in the evening." Who in the world would believe it? For we have heard that when the crane cries in the nine marshes, its voice is heard across the four wilds; yet the moment a scheming thought arose in the man by the sea, the seagulls that used to Frolic with him wheeled in the air and would not alight. Heaven does not tolerate falsehood; its subtle workings are inherently like this. If gentlemen of later times who bear the responsibility of molding the ways of the world establish sincerity within and carry it out in practice—just like the crane crying in the marsh, and not like the man who was fond of seagulls—then they will be near the mark.

Fourth Policy Question
Jia Yingju 賈應舉

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導李　批〔論久任之法宜行而要之維持以善用其法書生而明習世務者耶〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔論久任超遷之法卓有定見〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔馭吏之法援証得體〕
甞歷觀古今之理道其要在於馭吏之有
法而古今之馭吏其法恒相習而爲用乃
吏之善敗迥然今與古殊者非人之盡不
可與古匹也時有所不能盡同也其法之
良窳迥然終與始異者非法之不可必行
===
也而所以用是法者未能使人以必信也
是故馭吏之法不可不講也用此法也莫
先於通滯變通而鼓舞之審其機而握其
衡俾不泥於古之迹而直師其意者善馭
吏者也法之行也莫先於示信昭示而維
持之始如是而終亦如是俾不起疑貳之
端而使之一意無回慮者善用法也然則
久任之法馭吏之善經而圖治之要術也
乃古行之而今效之其意務以便民不計
punctuated:
同考試官訓導李　批〔論久任之法宜行，而要之維持以善用其法，書生而明習世務者耶！〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔論久任超遷之法，卓有定見。〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔馭吏之法，援証得體。〕

甞歷觀古今之理道，其要在於馭吏之有法；而古今之馭吏，其法恒相習而爲用。乃吏之善敗迥然今與古殊者，非人之盡不可與古匹也，時有所不能盡同也；其法之良窳迥然終與始異者，非法之不可必行也，而所以用是法者未能使人以必信也。是故馭吏之法，不可不講也。用此法也，莫先於通滯，變通而鼓舞之，審其機而握其衡，俾不泥於古之迹而直師其意者，善馭吏者也；法之行也，莫先於示信，昭示而維持之，始如是而終亦如是，俾不起疑貳之端，而使之一意無回慮者，善用法也。然則久任之法，馭吏之善經而圖治之要術也。乃古行之而今效之，其意務以便民，不計
translation_en:
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Li, comments: [He argues that the policy of long tenure ought to be implemented, and sums it up with sustaining it so as to make good use of the policy—truly a scholar who clearly understands practical affairs!]
Examiner, Instructor Dai, comments: [In discussing the policies of long tenure and rapid promotion, he shows outstanding and settled insight.]
Examiner, Instructor Yang, comments: [On the methods of managing officials, his citations and evidence are fitting.]

I have observed throughout history the principles of governance, and their essence lies in having a method for managing officials; and in the management of officials past and present, those methods have constantly been inherited and put to use. Yet the reason why the success and failure of officials today are vastly different from antiquity is not that men are entirely unable to match those of old, but that the times cannot be entirely the same; and the reason why the effectiveness of a policy at the end is vastly different from its beginning is not that the policy cannot necessarily be carried out, but that those who employ the policy have failed to make men place certain trust in it. Therefore, the method of managing officials must be carefully examined. In employing this method, nothing takes precedence over clearing bottlenecks—adapting flexibly and inspiring officials, assessing the pivotal mechanisms and holding the balance, so as not to cling rigidly to the outward traces of antiquity but directly emulate its underlying intent: such is one who excels at managing officials. In carrying out a policy, nothing takes precedence over demonstrating trustworthiness—proclaiming it clearly and upholding it, keeping it the same at the end as it was at the beginning, so that no cause for doubt or duplicity arises and men are made single-minded without backward glances: such is knowing how to employ a policy well. This being so, the policy of long tenure is a sound principle for managing officials and an essential art for pursuing good governance. Yet when antiquity practiced it and the present imitates it, the intent was to prioritize the convenience of the people, without calculating…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
其吏之便與不便也其終不惟不便於吏
且未見其有益於民此豈其法之悖謬而
不可行哉繇操持而策馭者無通滯之術
不足以信人之心而使人以不肖之心應
之爾明問所及敢論述其時勢之異與吏
道之詭然後及其法之所以不行與其所
以可行者俟採擇焉夫是法之行始之者
唐虞也三載考績三考黜陟其典具在三
代而下行之輒效者西漢也良吏蔡盛治
===
化郅隆吏牒可稽試觀今之時與唐虞之
時同乎今之用法與西京之用同乎四岳
九官十二牧僅若人爾今則岳牧官聯非
特夏商之官倍其倍于成周者又何如也
宣帝之世二千石以治狀聞者賜金下璽
書增秩至入拜公卿今即超卓其能一一
優崇乎此時勢之異至明矣今之時非古
之時而吏道之詭視古遠甚故無才賢智
譎而深取名於世無澡身潔志而厚矯飾
punctuated:
其吏之便與不便也。其終不惟不便於吏，且未見其有益於民。此豈其法之悖謬而不可行哉？繇操持而策馭者無通滯之術，不足以信人之心，而使人以不肖之心應之爾。明問所及，敢論述其時勢之異與吏道之詭，然後及其法之所以不行與其所以可行者，俟採擇焉。

夫是法之行，始之者唐虞也。三載考績，三考黜陟，其典具在。三代而下，行之輒效者西漢也。良吏蔡盛，治化郅隆，吏牒可稽。試觀今之時，與唐虞之時同乎？今之用法，與西京之用同乎？四岳、九官、十二牧，僅若人爾。今則岳牧官聯，非特夏商之官倍，其倍于成周者又何如也？宣帝之世，二千石以治狀聞者，賜金、下璽書、增秩，至入拜公卿。今即超卓，其能一一優崇乎？此時勢之異至明矣。

今之時非古之時，而吏道之詭視古遠甚。故無才賢，智譎而深取名於世；無澡身潔志，而厚矯飾
translation_en:
…whether it is convenient or inconvenient for the officials. In the end, not only is it inconvenient for the officials, it has not even been seen to be beneficial to the people. How could this be because the method itself is perverse and unworkable? It is only because those who hold the reins and direct them lack the art of clearing bottlenecks; they are unable to inspire trust in men's hearts, and thus cause men to respond with unworthy intentions. Addressing what Your Enlightened Inquiry has touched upon, I venture to discuss the differences in times and circumstances and the deceitfulness of official ways, and then proceed to why the method fails to work and how it can be made to work, awaiting Your selection.

Now, the practice of this method was begun under Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun]. Every three years achievements were evaluated, and after three evaluations promotions and demotions were made; those canons are still extant in full. From the Three Dynasties onward, the era when practicing it always brought results was the Western Han. Good officials flourished in abundance [? 蔡盛], and governance and transformation reached the utmost prosperity, as can be verified in the official records. Yet let us consider: are the present times the same as the times of Tang and Yu? Is the present application of the method the same as its application in the Western Capital [Western Han]? The Four Peaks, Nine Officials, and Twelve Pastors were only so many men. Today, however, the interconnected ranks of regional and local officials are not merely double the officials of the Xia and Shang—how many times more numerous are they than even those of the flourishing Zhou! In the reign of Emperor Xuan, Two-Thousand-Bushel officials [GrandAdministrators] whose administrative achievements were reported to the throne were bestowed gold, sent imperial letters under the玺 seal, and granted increases in rank, even to the point of being summoned to the court and appointed as Excellencies and Ministers. Today, even when officials are outstanding, can every single one of them be so generously honored? This difference in times and circumstances is utterly clear.

The present time is not the ancient time, and the deceitfulness of official ways far exceeds that of antiquity. Thus, lacking true talent and worth, men use cleverness and guile to deeply curry fame in the world; lacking pure conduct and clean aspirations, they heavily adorn themselves with hypocrisy…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
於外圓環謝請以爲獵取之計建說興事
以徼肩任之譽此情險于山川而明蔽于
眉睫胡可云較也夫吏之建置凡以爲民
也而吏之久任亦凡以爲民也民誠便矣
何顧于吏之不便誠有如明問所及者愚
則竊謂未有吏不便而有益於民者夫安
其志以行其道勵其心以宣其力卽受一
民一社之寄而精神心術無一不與境土
相流通措注設施無一不與黎庶相聯屬
===
由是而事體益周民志益定惠澤益深此
久任之於民良便也然進取之情銳而安
民之譽遲吾恐損實事以養名者多鐘鳴
之迫侵百姓以利己者志社錢之營官寧
有長子孫之驩民寧有借寇君之願乎以
此而欲吏稱民安是却行而求及前人也
此吏不便柰之何於民便也然法之所以
不行又有在焉今之仕進之途日廣闒茸
之流未汰缺裁則入滓於位途壅則新積
punctuated: 於外；圓環謝請，以爲獵取之計；建說興事，以徼肩任之譽。此情險于山川，而明蔽于眉睫，胡可云較也？夫吏之建置，凡以爲民也；而吏之久任，亦凡以爲民也。民誠便矣，何顧于吏之不便？誠有如明問所及者。愚則竊謂未有吏不便而有益於民者。夫安其志以行其道，勵其心以宣其力，卽受一民一社之寄，而精神心術無一不與境土相流通，措注設施無一不與黎庶相聯屬。由是而事體益周，民志益定，惠澤益深，此久任之於民良便也。然進取之情銳而安民之譽遲，吾恐損實事以養名者，多鐘鳴之迫；侵百姓以利己者，志社錢之營。官寧有長子孫之驩？民寧有借寇君之願乎？以此而欲吏稱民安，是却行而求及前人也。此吏不便，柰之何於民便也？然法之所以不行，又有在焉。今之仕進之途日廣，闒茸之流未汰。缺裁則入滓於位，途壅則新積
translation_en:
…on the outside; they go around declining or soliciting favors as a scheme to hunt for promotion, and propose theories and stir up projects to angle for a reputation of shouldering responsibility. When such intentions are more treacherous than mountains and rivers, and clear sight is obscured right before one's eyelashes, how can one even speak of comparing them?

Now, the establishment of officials is entirely for the sake of the people, and long tenure for officials is likewise entirely for the sake of the people. If it truly benefits the people, why care whether it is inconvenient for the officials? Indeed, it is just as Your brilliant question touches upon. Yet I would humbly venture to say that there has never been a case where something was inconvenient for officials and yet beneficial to the people. When an official settles his ambition to carry out his Way and rouses his mind to exert his strength, even if entrusted with only a single populace and a single local altar, his spirit and intentions are in every respect in communion with the territory, and his measures and arrangements are in every respect connected with the common people. Through this, administrative affairs become ever more thorough, the people's minds ever more settled, and benevolent grace ever deeper—this is how long tenure is truly beneficial to the people.

However, when the desire for advancement is keen and the reputation for bringing peace to the people is slow in coming, I fear that those who harm practical affairs to cultivate fame are often pressed by the urgency of the tolling bell [of advancing age], while those who encroach upon the commoners to profit themselves set their minds on scheming for community funds. How could officials have the joy of raising their children and grandchildren in office [as in Han times], and how could the people have the wish to "borrow Master Kou" [Kou Xun 寇恂, to retain a good magistrate]? To desire under these conditions that officials match their duties and the people enjoy peace is like walking backward while seeking to catch up with those ahead. When it is thus inconvenient for the officials, how could it possibly be beneficial for the people?

Yet there is another reason why the law cannot be put into practice. Today, the paths into officialdom grow wider by the day, and base and mediocre sorts have not been weeded out. When posts are reduced, entrants stagnate like dregs in their positions; when the path of promotion is clogged, newcomers pile up…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
於舊蘇軾所謂一官而三人共者居者一
人去者一人而伺之者又一人今慮不止
此也况埋於外者久則有意外之虞優游
於內者久則有樞要之望間又以虛冒而
獵取貪緣而倖致蘇軾所謂得者不以僥
倖自名不得者則以沉淪爲恨此又何怪
其然也此久任之所不行者非法之弊也
用之者弊也
聖天子嘉念黎元
===
納宰臣之議斷然以久任爲必可行其欲追
隆唐虞之至治而遠邁西漢之盛際其德
惠之在寰宇中者匪淺矣顧超遷與久任
相爲表裏蓋非久任則無以便民而使之
安而習之非超遷則無以便吏以庶幾激
而酬之此不易之論也乃君子出而委質
於君何內何外何久何近惟
天子使耳安敢計沉淪務速化厭雌伏跂華顯
而自處爲躍冶之金犇乘之騎哉顧恐天
punctuated:
於舊。蘇軾所謂「一官而三人共者，居者一人，去者一人，而伺之者又一人」，今慮不止此也。况埋於外者，久則有意外之虞；優游於內者，久則有樞要之望。間又以虛冒而獵取，貪緣而倖致。蘇軾所謂「得者不以僥倖自名，不得者則以沉淪爲恨」，此又何怪其然也！此久任之所不行者，非法之弊也，用之者弊也。
聖天子嘉念黎元，納宰臣之議，斷然以久任爲必可行，其欲追隆唐虞之至治，而遠邁西漢之盛際，其德惠之在寰宇中者匪淺矣。顧超遷與久任相爲表裏，蓋非久任則無以便民，而使之安而習之；非超遷則無以便吏，以庶幾激而酬之，此不易之論也。乃君子出而委質於君，何內何外，何久何近，惟天子使耳！安敢計沉淪、務速化、厭雌伏、跂華顯，而自處爲躍冶之金、犇乘之騎哉！顧恐天
translation_en:
…upon the old. What Su Shi 蘇軾 spoke of—"one post shared by three men: one currently occupying it, one departing it, and yet another waiting in the wings for it"—nowadays, I fear, does not stop even at that. Moreover, those buried in provincial posts for a long time face the peril of unforeseen mishaps, while those enjoying leisure at the capital for a long time entertain hopes of reaching pivotal positions of power. At times, too, men hunt for advancement through false claims or attain it by luck through corrupt connections [?]. As Su Shi said, "Those who succeed do not call themselves fortunate opportunists, while those who fail resent being left to sink into obscurity"—what wonder is it that things are so! That long tenure of office cannot be put into practice here is not a flaw of the law itself, but a flaw in how it is applied.

Our Sacred Son of Heaven, with gracious concern for the common people, has accepted the counsel of his Chief Minister and resolutely determined that long tenure in office must be put into effect. In his desire to match the supreme governance of Tang 唐 and Yu 虞 and far surpass the flourishing era of the Western Han, the moral grace and benevolence he extends throughout the realm are profound indeed. Yet extraordinary promotion and long tenure are two sides of the same coin. For without long tenure, there is no way to benefit the people and allow them to rest secure and grow accustomed to their officials; without extraordinary promotion, there is no way to benefit the officials and thereby inspire and reward them. This is an immutable principle. Now, when a gentleman goes forth and pledges his service to his ruler, what matters "inner" or "outer," what matters "long" or "brief"? He simply serves wherever the Son of Heaven employs him! How could he dare calculate his own obscurity, strive for rapid advancement, chafe at lying low, or stand on tiptoe for splendid prominence—conducting himself like metal leaping from the smelter's mold or a horse bolting from its team? Yet I fear that in the empire…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
下不皆忠良自許之夫則所以用法以制
馭之者不可少也所當維持以善用此法
者不可少也愚則謂要莫先於通滯本莫
先於示信而所以通滯而示信者又不出
於責循良之效嚴名實之辨寬督責之令
杜僥倖之門與夫汰冗流崇優異數者而
已夫漢志循良所傳其稱寵異最著者惟
黃次公之尚寛和韓延壽之敎禮讓者數
人至於發奸摘伏武健自快者類皆無取
則循良之效不可不尚也齊威積衰之國
一旦綜察精嚴呼卽墨大夫而封之呼阿
大夫而烹之卒之鄰人慴伏國中大治齊
用稱霸則名實之核不可不嚴也甞觀漢
世之用人也破觚而爲圜斲彫以爲朴故
吏治蒸蒸不至於姦今之郡邑日困於簿
書之繁惴惴幸無事以需次猝而有一細
故遂蝟舉而苛督之使之前功盡棄此畏
縮者所以怯前而顧後保名者所以計旦
punctuated: 下不皆忠良自許之夫，則所以用法以制馭之者不可少也；所當維持以善用此法者不可少也。愚則謂要莫先於通滯，本莫先於示信；而所以通滯而示信者，又不出於責循良之效、嚴名實之辨、寬督責之令、杜僥倖之門，與夫汰冗流、崇優異數者而已。夫漢志循良所傳，其稱寵異最著者，惟黃次公之尚寛和、韓延壽之敎禮讓者數人；至於發奸摘伏、武健自快者，類皆無取。則循良之效不可不尚也。齊威積衰之國，一旦綜察精嚴，呼卽墨大夫而封之，呼阿大夫而烹之，卒之鄰人慴伏，國中大治，齊用稱霸。則名實之核不可不嚴也。甞觀漢世之用人也，破觚而爲圜，斲彫以爲朴，故吏治蒸蒸，不至於姦。今之郡邑，日困於簿書之繁，惴惴幸無事以需次；猝而有一細故，遂蝟舉而苛督之，使之前功盡棄。此畏縮者所以怯前而顧後，保名者所以計旦
translation_en:
… not all men in the empire are those who pride themselves on loyalty and goodness, and therefore the means of using laws to control and govern them cannot be dispensed with; nor can the means by which we must uphold and skillfully apply these laws be dispensed with. In my humble opinion, the key lies first of all in clearing away stagnation in promotion, and the root lies first of all in demonstrating trustworthiness. Furthermore, the means of clearing away stagnation and demonstrating trustworthiness go no further than several measures: demanding the results of benevolent and law-abiding governance, strictly distinguishing between reputation and reality, relaxing orders of harsh reprimand, closing the gates of opportunistic advancement, as well as weeding out superfluous personnel and honoring outstanding merit.

In the biographies of benevolent and law-abiding officials recorded in the Han histories, those most famously cited for receiving special favor and distinction were only a few men, such as Huang Cigong (Huang Ba 黃霸), who valued leniency and harmony, and Han Yanshou 韓延壽, who taught ritual propriety and deference. As for those who exposed hidden villainy and took pleasure in their own aggressive rigor, none of that sort were chosen. Thus, the results of benevolent and law-abiding governance must be esteemed.

King Wei of Qi 齊威王 inherited a state in long-standing decline, yet once he conducted thorough and strict verification, he summoned the Grand Master of Jimo 卽墨 and enfeoffed him, and summoned the Grand Master of E 阿 and boiled him alive. In the end, neighboring states were cowed into submission, the state was brought to great order, and Qi thereby achieved hegemony. Thus, the verification of reputation and reality must be made strict.

I have observed how the Han dynasty employed men: it broke off sharp corners to make things round and carved away ornate embellishments to return to simplicity; hence official governance flourished and did not degenerate into wickedness. Today, prefectures and counties are daily exhausted by the proliferation of administrative documents, anxiously hoping only to avoid trouble while waiting for their turn at promotion. Should some minor mishap suddenly occur, critics swarm up like hedgehog spines to harshly censure them, causing all their previous achievements to be completely discarded. This is why timid officials are afraid to step forward and constantly look behind them, and why those who seek to preserve their reputation calculate from morning…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
而憂夕則苛細不可不蠲也又聞宦道猶
之市也眞僞無常權在駔驓利否無常機
在善趨故敦朴寡援之吏恒坐趑趄而便
儇突梯之徒每遷遠化其端不可勝詰此
執𢹂者所以窺閒而造瑕未亮者所以增
嫌而導惑則僥倖不可不絕也賢才跧伏
無盡雖難以類求而入貲之途額外之員
其冒濫又不可勝計漢時入財者補郎而
郎選遂衰厚貲者爲吏而吏道益襍今未
===
邊有此而冗襍之汰可不銳意行之乎臣
子鞠躬盡瘁何敢望報然而爵以勵世賞
以酬勞即聖帝所不容已漢時守吏有賢
能異等者優賜至補公卿之缺前固言之
今邊難行此然其歷任久而功效著超擢
之典可不必然行之乎夫責循良則彼知
不務赫赫以爲旦夕計也覈名實則彼知
不可蔽匿而以虛罔爲也苛細蠲則彼知
竭志宣力而無不測憂也倖進杜則彼知
punctuated: 而憂夕，則苛細不可不蠲也。又聞宦道猶之市也，眞僞無常，權在駔驓；利否無常，機在善趨。故敦朴寡援之吏，恒坐趑趄；而便儇突梯之徒，每遷遠化，其端不可勝詰。此執𢹂者所以窺閒而造瑕，未亮者所以增嫌而導惑，則僥倖不可不絕也。賢才跧伏無盡，雖難以類求，而入貲之途、額外之員，其冒濫又不可勝計。漢時入財者補郎，而郎選遂衰；厚貲者爲吏，而吏道益襍。今未邊有此，而冗襍之汰，可不銳意行之乎？臣子鞠躬盡瘁，何敢望報？然而爵以勵世，賞以酬勞，即聖帝所不容已。漢時守吏有賢能異等者，優賜至補公卿之缺，前固言之。今邊難行此，然其歷任久而功效著，超擢之典，可不必然行之乎？夫責循良，則彼知不務赫赫以爲旦夕計也；覈名實，則彼知不可蔽匿而以虛罔爲也；苛細蠲，則彼知竭志宣力而無不測憂也；倖進杜，則彼知
translation_en: … and worry at nightfall; therefore, petty and harsh scrutiny cannot but be eliminated. I have also heard that the path of officialdom is like a marketplace: authenticity and falsity are inconstant, for the power lies with the brokers; profit and loss are inconstant, for the opportunity lies in skillful maneuvering. Thus, honest, simple officials with few backers constantly suffer from hesitation and stagnation, whereas glib, accommodating fellows are regularly promoted to high and distant transformations, through maneuvers too numerous to investigate fully. This is why those with ulterior motives [?] watch for openings to fabricate flaws, and those lacking clear discernment heap up suspicions and invite confusion; therefore, opportunistic advancement cannot but be cut off. Worthy talents lie hidden in inexhaustible numbers; although it is difficult to seek them out by fixed categories, as for the path of purchasing office through wealth and supernumerary personnel, their fraudulent excesses are beyond calculation. In Han times, those who contributed wealth filled vacancies as Court Gentlemen, and the selection of Court Gentlemen consequently declined; those with substantial fortunes became officials, and the way of officialdom grew increasingly mixed. Even if today we have not suddenly [?] reached this point, can we fail to carry out the culling of superfluous and mixed personnel with keen determination? When a minister bends his body and exhausts his strength in service, how could he dare hope for repayment? Yet using noble rank to encourage the world and rewards to recompense toil is something even a sage emperor cannot dispense with. In Han times, local officials who were of exceptional worth and ability were generously rewarded, even to the point of filling vacancies among the Ducal Ministers—this has indeed been stated before. Today it is difficult to suddenly [?] put this into practice; yet when an official has served through a long tenure and his achievements are manifest, can the statute for extraordinary promotion not be resolutely carried out? Now, if we demand upright and benevolent governance, they will know not to pursue flashy renown as a scheme for morning and evening; if we verify reputation against reality, they will know they cannot conceal things and act with empty deceit; if petty harshness is eliminated, they will know to exhaust their will and exert their strength without fear of the unforeseen; if opportunistic advancement is blocked, they will know to …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
積日累勞而無壅淤處也汰冗嚴則蠹敗
免于噂沓優異崇則人心興於鼓舞如是
而久任行之不恤于羣言之翕訾不格于
衆情之牽滯推一世至千百世可也然又
有本焉在上而不在下有機焉在近而不
在遠夫立鵠行賞靡不爭射矣設標命趨
靡不爭赴矣何者言有以示之也一夫挽
强百夫決拾一人持罾千人臨淵何者言
有以倡之也是在
主上與秉衡者加之意焉愚生何敢竟其說
===
余　僴
同考試官訓導龔　批〔農桑生民大命也子論蜀之瀩田植桑而援古以酌今之宜行燦然可睹識時務之俊傑也〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔論事卓有定見非勦說者〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔該博之學精練之才〕
第五問
執事策蜀士而以蜀大利問亡亦以諸生
居恒有意於民事乎顧不佞業佔俾者流
punctuated:
積日累勞而無壅淤處也。汰冗嚴則蠹敗免于噂沓，優異崇則人心興於鼓舞。如是而久任行之，不恤于羣言之翕訾，不格于衆情之牽滯，推一世至千百世可也。然又有本焉，在上而不在下；有機焉，在近而不在遠。夫立鵠行賞，靡不爭射矣；設標命趨，靡不爭赴矣。何者？言有以示之也。一夫挽强，百夫決拾；一人持罾，千人臨淵。何者？言有以倡之也。是在主上與秉衡者加之意焉，愚生何敢竟其說。
余僴
同考試官訓導龔批〔農桑，生民大命也。子論蜀之瀩田、植桑，而援古以酌今之宜行，燦然可睹，識時務之俊傑也。〕
考試官教諭戴批〔論事卓有定見，非勦說者。〕
考試官教諭楊批〔該博之學，精練之才。〕
第五問
執事策蜀士而以蜀大利問，亡亦以諸生居恒有意於民事乎？顧不佞業佔俾者流，
translation_en:
…to accumulate days and build up merit without any stagnation or blockage. If the weeding out of superfluous personnel is strict, then corrupt and ruinous elements will be spared from chattering in cliques; if exceptional promotions are honored, then people's hearts will be aroused to enthusiastic encouragement. If long tenure in office is practiced in this manner—unmoved by the shifting praises and slanders of the crowd, and unhindered by the entanglements and delays of popular sentiment—it could be extended from one generation to a hundred or a thousand generations. Yet there is also a fundamental root to this, which lies above and not below; and there is a pivotal mechanism to this, which lies near and not far. When a target is set up and rewards are offered, everyone competes to shoot at it; when a marker is erected and the order is given to run, everyone competes to rush toward it. Why is this? It means there is something shown to guide them. When one man draws a strong bow, a hundred men put on their archer's thimbles and arm-guards; when one person holds a fishing net, a thousand people approach the deep water. Why is this? It means there is someone taking the lead for them. This depends on the Sovereign above and those who hold the scales of authority paying special heed to it; how dare this foolish student exhaust his argument?

Yu Xian
Comment by Associate Examiner Gong, Assistant Instructor: [Agriculture and sericulture are the great lifelines of the people. You discuss irrigating fields [?] and planting mulberries in Shu, citing antiquity to deliberate on what is appropriate to put into practice today. It is brilliantly clear to see—you are truly an outstanding talent who understands the affairs of the times.]
Comment by Examiner Dai, Instructor: [In discussing affairs, he has outstanding and firm views; he is not one who merely plagiarizes others' words.]
Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: [Comprehensive and broad learning; refined and practiced talent.]

Fifth Policy Question
Your Excellency puts a policy question to the scholars of Shu and asks about the great benefits of Shu—is it not because you suppose that the students ordinarily take an interest in the affairs of the people? Yet I, an unworthy one, am merely the sort who drones over his textbooks, …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
計畫無復之耳雖然地志所載故老所傳
聞竊耳之矣蓋蜀在天下故稱陸海其食
貨之利未易一二更僕指數姑勿論論其
大者有二一水利也一蠶桑也夫二者利
之所出而衣食之源也衣食者人之所資
以爲命奈之何其諱言之也蓋今蜀之田
畯莫急于水利而紅女莫要於蠶桑古人
有言一夫不耕或受之饑一女不織或受
之寒故聖王在上而民不凍餒者非能耕
===
而食之織而衣之也爲得其興利之道也
興利之道粟米布帛生於地長於時聚於
力非可以安坐而得之而麤錯所謂民貧
則姦邪生貧生於不足不足生于不農有
味乎其言之哉良有司者知其然也故務
民於農桑引水溉田植桑飼蠶爲勞民勸
相計也夫穿渠溉注之所資也居數歲而
水溢則潰奔匝溯瞨則淤閼不流蠶桑絲
帛之所出也均一鄉而彼則餘以貨外郡
punctuated: 計畫無復之耳。雖然，地志所載、故老所傳聞，竊耳之矣。蓋蜀在天下，故稱「陸海」，其食貨之利，未易一二更僕指數。姑勿論，論其大者有二：一水利也，一蠶桑也。夫二者，利之所出，而衣食之源也。衣食者，人之所資以爲命，奈之何其諱言之也？蓋今蜀之田畯莫急于水利，而紅女莫要於蠶桑。古人有言：「一夫不耕，或受之饑；一女不織，或受之寒。」故聖王在上，而民不凍餒者，非能耕而食之、織而衣之也，爲得其興利之道也。興利之道，粟米布帛，生於地，長於時，聚於力，非可以安坐而得之。而麤錯所謂「民貧則姦邪生，貧生於不足，不足生于不農」，有味乎其言之哉！良有司者知其然也，故務民於農桑，引水溉田，植桑飼蠶，爲勞民勸相計也。夫穿渠，溉注之所資也，居數歲而水溢則潰奔，匝溯瞨則淤閼不流；蠶桑，絲帛之所出也，均一鄉而彼則餘以貨外郡，
translation_en: … lacks further resources for planning [after the manner of Wu Fuzhi 無復之]. Even so, what is recorded in the local gazetteers and passed down by the elders, I have privately heard. Indeed, within the realm, Shu (Sichuan) has of old been called an "inland sea" (luhai), and its benefits in food and goods are not easily counted out in full even if one changes attending servants one after another. Setting the rest aside for now, if we discuss the greatest of them, there are two: one is water conservancy, and the other is sericulture and mulberry cultivation. These two are the sources from which benefit arises and the wellsprings of clothing and food. Clothing and food are what people rely upon for their very lives—how can one shrink from speaking of them? Today among the farmers of Shu nothing is more urgent than water conservancy, and among the weaving women nothing is more vital than sericulture and mulberry cultivation. The ancients had a saying: "If one man does not plow, someone will suffer hunger from it; if one woman does not weave, someone will suffer cold from it." Therefore, when a sage-king is above and the people do not freeze or starve, it is not because he is able to plow to feed them or weave to clothe them himself, but because he has grasped the Way of promoting benefits. As for the Way of promoting benefits: grain, rice, cloth, and silk are born of the earth, grow according to the seasons, and are gathered through human labor; they cannot be obtained by sitting idly by. And what Chao Cuo 鼂錯 [transcribed 麤錯] said—"When the people are poor, villainy and wickedness arise; poverty arises from insufficiency, and insufficiency arises from not farming"—how deeply meaningful are those words! Good local officials know this to be so; therefore they direct the people to agriculture and sericulture, drawing water to irrigate the fields and planting mulberries to feed silkworms, as a plan to encourage, comfort, and assist the toiling people. Now, digging canals is what irrigation relies upon, yet after several years, when the waters overflow they breach the banks and rush away, and when they eddy or encounter drought [?] they silt up and cease to flow. Sericulture and mulberry cultivation are whence silk fabrics come, yet even within the same district, that place has a surplus to trade to outside prefectures, …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
此則貨彼郡之餘故夫欲興已穿渠之利
易而興未穿渠之利則地勢高下水性順
逆不可不度也度之而議或格於盈庭興
已蠶桑之利易而興未蠶桑之利則地利
有無民情勤惰不可不審也審之而議或
奪于築舍此蜀之利民二事不能無靡執
事問也蓋蜀爲天府之地諸葛亮爲昭烈
告之矣其言曰益州險塞沃野千里夫險
塞則可以守沃野則可以出軍需亮蓋得
===
策矣是建邦啓土之始也乃今觀蜀自秦
守李冰鑿離堆辟沫水之害穿二江成都
之中此渠皆可行舟有餘則用溉浸百姓
饗其利今其堆在灌縣西一里許巋然立
水中可覩也蓋始未鑿堆地勢下壅沫水
奔突不可控揣爲居民害而今則順流而
東而水之利膜則藉以灌溉雨則不過其
流故其記曰水旱從人不知饑饉其謂是
也而二江則蜀志以爲一汶江一流江蓋
punctuated: 此則貨彼郡之餘。故夫欲興已穿渠之利易，而興未穿渠之利，則地勢高下、水性順逆不可不度也，度之而議或格於盈庭；興已蠶桑之利易，而興未蠶桑之利，則地利有無、民情勤惰不可不審也，審之而議或奪于築舍。此蜀之利民二事，不能無靡執事問也。蓋蜀爲天府之地，諸葛亮爲昭烈告之矣。其言曰：「益州險塞，沃野千里。」夫險塞則可以守，沃野則可以出軍需，亮蓋得策矣，是建邦啓土之始也。乃今觀蜀，自秦守李冰鑿離堆，辟沫水之害，穿二江成都之中，此渠皆可行舟，有餘則用溉浸，百姓饗其利。今其堆在灌縣西一里許，巋然立水中可覩也。蓋始未鑿堆，地勢下壅，沫水奔突不可控揣，爲居民害；而今則順流而東，而水之利，膜則藉以灌溉，雨則不過其流。故其記曰：「水旱從人，不知饑饉。」其謂是也。而二江，則《蜀志》以爲一汶江、一流江，蓋
translation_en:
… while this one must buy the surplus of that prefecture. Therefore, to promote the benefits of canals already dug is easy, whereas to promote the benefits of canals not yet dug, one cannot fail to measure the elevation of the terrain and whether the nature of the water runs with or against the course; and even when one measures them, deliberations may be obstructed by a court full of conflicting opinions. To promote the benefits of sericulture already practiced is easy, whereas to promote the benefits of sericulture not yet practiced, one cannot fail to examine the presence or absence of terrestrial advantages and the diligence or indolence of popular sentiment; and even when one examines them, deliberations may be derailed like building a house by the roadside. These two matters of benefiting the people in Shu cannot but trouble Your Excellency with questions.

Now, that Shu is a "Land of Heavenly Abundance" (Tianfu) was already told by Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮 to Zhaolie 昭烈 [Liu Bei 劉備]. His words were: "Yizhou has strategic fastnesses and a thousand li of fertile plains." With strategic fastnesses it can be defended, and with fertile plains it can supply military needs; Liang indeed grasped the right strategy, and this was the beginning of founding the state and opening up the territory. 

If we now observe Shu: ever since the Qin Governor (shou) Li Bing 李冰 cut through the Separated Mound (Lidui 離堆) to avert the harm of the Mo River (Moshui 沫水) and dug the Two Rivers through the midst of Chengdu, these canals have all been navigable by boat, and when there is surplus water it is used for irrigation, so the common people enjoy their benefit. Today that mound is a little more than one li west of Guan County 灌縣, standing toweringly in the middle of the water where it can be seen. For in the beginning, before the mound was cut through, the terrain below was blocked up, and the Mo River rushed and surged uncontrollably, bringing harm to the inhabitants; whereas now it flows smoothly eastward, and as for the benefit of the water, in drought [reading 膜 as 暵/旱] one relies on it for irrigation, and in rain it does not overflow its course [?]. Thus the record of it says: "Flood and drought follow human will, and people do not know famine." This is what it refers to. As for the Two Rivers, the Record of Shu (Shuzhi 蜀志) considers them to be one the Wen River (Wenjiang 汶江) and one the Liu River (Liujiang 流江), which…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
經郡城南七里者卽氷所穿耳宋郡縣志
謂一由永康過新繁入成都謂之外江一
由永康過郫入成都謂之內江者永康卽
今灌縣而所用灌溉則曰灌曰溫曰郫曰
雙流曰崇慶曰成都凡一州七縣皆利之
天下謂之天府也蓋昔魏襄王爲羣臣祝
而曰令吾臣皆如西門豹之爲人臣也史
起進曰魏氏之行田也以百畝鄴獨二百
畝是田惡也漳水在其旁而豹不知用是
===
仁智未盡何足法也及起爲鄴令乃引漳
溉鄴以富魏之河內而民歌之以亮其智
豈少區區史起之見乎然亮初慕蜀之沃
野而身自爲相江水亡恙也獨不聞與羣
下謀鑿引以溉旁近田畝何也蓋沙河以
南其原野雖廣平可田畝而地高江下不
可引水卽鑿之亦不得利故亮置弗爲坐
此耳蜀志有之蜀古蠶叢之國若曰地宜
蠶也所從來遠矣乃張詠則蜀賢守也先
punctuated: 經郡城南七里者，卽氷所穿耳。宋《郡縣志》謂：「一由永康過新繁入成都，謂之外江；一由永康過郫入成都，謂之內江」者，永康卽今灌縣，而所用灌溉，則曰灌、曰溫、曰郫、曰雙流、曰崇慶、曰成都，凡一州七縣皆利之，天下謂之天府也。蓋昔魏襄王爲羣臣祝而曰：「令吾臣皆如西門豹之爲人臣也。」史起進曰：「魏氏之行田也以百畝，鄴獨二百畝，是田惡也。漳水在其旁，而豹不知用，是仁智未盡，何足法也？」及起爲鄴令，乃引漳溉鄴，以富魏之河內，而民歌之。以亮其智，豈少區區史起之見乎？然亮初慕蜀之沃野，而身自爲相，江水亡恙也，獨不聞與羣下謀鑿引以溉旁近田畝，何也？蓋沙河以南，其原野雖廣平可田畝，而地高江下，不可引水，卽鑿之亦不得利，故亮置弗爲，坐此耳。《蜀志》有之：「蜀，古蠶叢之國。」若曰地宜蠶也，所從來遠矣。乃張詠則蜀賢守也，先
translation_en:
… passing seven li south of the prefectural city are simply those excavated by [Li] Bing. The Song-dynasty Treatise on Commandery and County Geography (Junxian zhi) states: "One flows from Yongkang past Xinfan and enters Chengdu, and is called the Outer River; one flows from Yongkang past Pi and enters Chengdu, and is called the Inner River." Yongkang is present-day Guan County, and as for the places they irrigate—namely Guan, Wen[jiang], Pi, Shuangliu, Chongqing, and Chengdu—in all, one subprefecture and seven counties benefit from them, and the world calls it the "Storehouse of Heaven" (Tianfu).

In the past, King Xiang of Wei offered a toast to his assembled ministers and said, "May all my ministers be true servants like Ximen Bao!" Shi Qi stepped forward and said, "In the Wei clan's distribution of land, the standard allotment is one hundred mu, yet in Ye alone it is two hundred mu; this is because the soil is poor. The Zhang River flows right beside it, yet Ximen Bao did not know to make use of it. This shows a failure to fulfill benevolence and wisdom—how is he worthy of emulation?" When Shi Qi became District Magistrate of Ye, he channeled the Zhang River to irrigate Ye, thereby enriching the Henei region of Wei, and the people sang his praises.

Given [Zhuge] Liang's wisdom, how could he have lacked the paltry insight of a Shi Qi? Yet although Liang at first admired the fertile plains of Shu, when he personally served as Counselor-in-Chief, the river waters were intact as ever, and we alone do not hear of him consulting with his subordinates to excavate channels and draw water to irrigate the adjacent farmlands. Why was this? It is because south of the Sha River, although the plains are broad, flat, and suitable for farming, the land is high and the river lies low; water cannot be drawn up, and even if one excavated channels, no benefit would be gained. Thus Liang left it alone and did not attempt it, precisely for this reason.

The Record of Shu (Shu zhi) has it that "Shu is the ancient state of Cancong [Silkworm Thicket]." This is as much as to say that its land is suited to sericulture, a tradition of very long standing. Now, Zhang Yong was a worthy Prefect of Shu. Previously…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
是知鄂州時旣以敎民拔茶植桑矣而至
爲蜀宋史第稱其減鹽價以足軍餉督驕
將以討叛賊吏不伏牽出斬之民苦饑豫
折米以待之而獨不聞其勸民植桑豈詠
不知蜀地宜桑而不以鄂治耶特以于時
四郊多壘桑株悉膏釜爨不可復植或蠶
桑故業民自利爲之不煩督勸云耳乃今
保寧諸縣則家植桑而人飼蠶其絲絁綾
絹旣用以自衣被而其餘且以貨諸他郡
===
利云厚矣而錦官以南千里而無一桑株
何也是末必皆出於避稅或者由惰農廢
業又無所督勸之故至于今而無復占是
業耳乃執事又謂欲用史起智而鑿山引
水灌溉沙河以南之田申張詠見而勸民
植桑脩復蠶叢以來之業意柔柔厚也其
爲蜀家人計生產殷矣而愚則以爲江水
不可引也陂塘獨不可鑿乎民稅可避也
蠶桑獨可廢乎有如鑿塘一畝深一丈可
punctuated:
是知鄂州時，旣以敎民拔茶植桑矣，而至爲蜀，《宋史》第稱其減鹽價以足軍餉，督驕將以討叛賊，吏不伏牽出斬之，民苦饑豫折米以待之，而獨不聞其勸民植桑。豈詠不知蜀地宜桑而不以鄂治耶？特以于時四郊多壘，桑株悉膏釜爨，不可復植；或蠶桑故業，民自利爲之，不煩督勸云耳。乃今保寧諸縣，則家植桑而人飼蠶，其絲、絁、綾、絹旣用以自衣被，而其餘且以貨諸他郡，利云厚矣；而錦官以南千里而無一桑株，何也？是末必皆出於避稅，或者由惰農廢業，又無所督勸之故，至于今而無復占是業耳。

乃執事又謂欲用史起智，而鑿山引水，灌溉沙河以南之田；申張詠見，而勸民植桑，脩復蠶叢以來之業。意柔柔厚也，其爲蜀家人計生產殷矣。而愚則以爲江水不可引也，陂塘獨不可鑿乎？民稅可避也，蠶桑獨可廢乎？有如鑿塘一畝，深一丈，可
translation_en:
…Previously, when he served as Prefect of Ezhou 鄂州, he had already taught the people to uproot tea bushes and plant mulberry trees. Yet when he came to govern Shu 蜀, the History of the Song (Songshi 宋史) merely praises him for lowering salt prices to suffice military provisions, supervising arrogant generals to suppress rebel bandits, dragging out and beheading refractory subofficial functionaries, and commuting grain taxes in advance to provide for the people when they suffered from famine—while nothing is heard of his encouraging the people to plant mulberries. Could it be that Zhang Yong 張詠 did not know that the land of Shu was suited for mulberries, and thus did not govern it as he had Ezhou? It was simply that at the time, there were many fortifications across the surrounding countryside, and the mulberry trunks had all gone to feed the cooking pots and fires and could not be replanted; or perhaps sericulture was an old livelihood that the people pursued for their own profit without needing supervision or encouragement. Nowadays, in the various counties of Baoning 保寧, every household plants mulberries and every person raises silkworms; their raw silk, coarse pongee, damask, and tabby silk are not only used to clothe themselves, but the surplus is even sold to other commanderies, yielding handsome profits indeed. Yet for a thousand li south of Jinguan 錦官 (Chengdu), there is not a single mulberry tree—why is this? This does not necessarily [reading 末 as 未] all stem from evading taxes; perhaps it is because lazy farmers abandoned the livelihood, and with no one to supervise or encourage them, down to the present day no one engages in this occupation anymore.

Now you, sir, further state that you wish to employ the wisdom of Shi Qi 史起 by cutting through mountains to channel water and irrigate the fields south of the Sha River 沙河, and to extend the insight of Zhang Yong by encouraging the people to plant mulberries and restore the livelihood handed down since the days of Cancong 蠶叢. Your intentions are gentle and generous [? 柔柔厚, likely a graphic error for 良厚 "truly generous"], and your planning for the household production of the people of Shu is earnest indeed. Yet in my humble view, if the river water cannot be channeled, can reservoirs and ponds alone not be excavated? Even if people might evade taxes, can sericulture alone be abandoned? Suppose one excavates a pond of one mu in area and one zhang in depth; it can…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
灌田十畝鑿塘百畝深一丈可灌田千畝
則自沙河以抵龍泉皆沃壤也如是行之
數年而陂塘之利不與一州七縣相埒吾
不信也植桑十株可供一女之蠶植桑百
株可供十女之蠶則自錦官以及戎渝皆
桑陌也如是行之數年而蠶桑之利不與
保寧諸縣相等吾不信也古人有云民不
可與慮始而可與樂成在事者誠計在必
行行矣而遲之歲月疏之鑿之而惰不鑿
===
者與鑿不深者從而法加焉督之勸之而
惰不植者與植不勤者從而罰及焉而又
時其疾苦毋苛責其稅則於興是二利若
承蜩而掇之也莞子曰倉廩實而知禮節
如是行之十年而教化不成風俗不美盜
不息奸不止而閭閻無揖讓之風吾又不
信也不佞生于窮巷之中愚陋無以經世
務乃承下詢以鄉土之利敬述所聞於長
老者以進若其權衡便宜之法是在執事
punctuated: 灌田十畝，鑿塘百畝、深一丈，可灌田千畝，則自沙河以抵龍泉，皆沃壤也。如是行之數年，而陂塘之利不與一州七縣相埒，吾不信也。植桑十株，可供一女之蠶；植桑百株，可供十女之蠶，則自錦官以及戎、渝，皆桑陌也。如是行之數年，而蠶桑之利不與保寧諸縣相等，吾不信也。古人有云：「民不可與慮始，而可與樂成。」在事者誠計在必行，行矣而遲之歲月：疏之鑿之，而惰不鑿者與鑿不深者，從而法加焉；督之勸之，而惰不植者與植不勤者，從而罰及焉；而又時其疾苦，毋苛責其稅，則於興是二利，若承蜩而掇之也。莞子曰：「倉廩實而知禮節。」如是行之十年，而教化不成，風俗不美，盜不息，奸不止，而閭閻無揖讓之風，吾又不信也。不佞生于窮巷之中，愚陋無以經世務，乃承下詢以鄉土之利，敬述所聞於長老者以進。若其權衡便宜之法，是在執事
translation_en:
…irrigate ten mu of fields, and if one digs a hundred mu of ponds to a depth of one zhang, it can irrigate a thousand mu of fields. Then from the Sha River (Shahe 沙河) all the way to Longquan 龍泉, all will be fertile soil. If this is carried out for several years, and the benefits of reservoirs and ponds do not rival those of the one subprefecture and seven counties, I would not believe it. If one plants ten mulberry trees, they can supply the silkworms of one woman; if one plants a hundred mulberry trees, they can supply the silkworms of ten women. Then from Jinguan 錦官 (Chengdu) all the way to Rong 戎 (Xuzhou) and Yu 渝 (Chongqing), all the field paths will be lined with mulberries. If this is carried out for several years, and the benefits of sericulture and mulberry cultivation do not equal those of the counties of Baoning 保寧, I would not believe it.

The ancients had a saying: "The common people cannot be consulted when planning the beginning of an undertaking, but one can rejoice with them in its completion." If those in authority truly resolve that it must be carried out, and having put it into practice, give it time over the months and years—dredging and digging, while applying the law to those who are lazy and do not dig, or who do not dig deeply; supervising and encouraging, while visiting punishment upon those who are lazy and do not plant, or who do not plant diligently; and at the same time attending seasonably to their hardships and sufferings without harshly demanding taxes from them—then promoting these two benefits will be as effortless as catching cicadas on a sticky pole and picking them off. Master Guan (Guanzi 莞子 [管子]) said: "When the granaries are full, people know ritual and moderation." If this is carried out for ten years, and moral transformation is not achieved, customs do not become fine, banditry does not cease, wickedness does not stop, and the village lanes lack an atmosphere of courteous deference, I again would not believe it.

I, your unworthy servant, was born in a humble lane, and am too ignorant and crude to manage the affairs of the world. Yet having received your condescension in inquiring about the benefits of our native land, I respectfully recount what I have heard from the elders to present to you. As for the methods of weighing circumstances and acting as expediency requires, that rests with Your Excellency…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text: 者矣是在執事者矣
punctuated: 者矣，是在執事者矣。
translation_en: … those in authority; this rests with those in authority.

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試錄後序
嘗觀左太冲之賦蜀都也曰
江漢炳靈世載其英則以長
卿子雲爲稱最初甚壯之旣
而竊疑焉夫蜀岷山之精下
蟠坤維上應井絡峙劒閣而
包玉壘帶二江而阻峨眉鬱
===
乎萃川岳之神秀矣其間沃
野千里蔚爲奧區瓌奇紛綸
不可勝紀所謂陸海天府豈
虛哉信推地靈人傑而論宜
以才藪聞舊矣顧志記蠶叢
魚鳧以來僻陋未除肇儒雅
縣文翁始漢已前惟尹吉甫
punctuated:
四川鄉試錄後序

嘗觀左太冲之賦蜀都也，曰：「江漢炳靈，世載其英。」則以長卿、子雲爲稱最。初甚壯之，旣而竊疑焉。夫蜀，岷山之精，下蟠坤維，上應井絡，峙劒閣而包玉壘，帶二江而阻峨眉，鬱乎萃川岳之神秀矣。其間沃野千里，蔚爲奧區，瓌奇紛綸，不可勝紀。所謂陸海、天府，豈虛哉？信推地靈人傑而論，宜以才藪聞舊矣。顧志記蠶叢、魚鳧以來，僻陋未除，肇儒雅繇文翁始。漢已前，惟尹吉甫
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

I once read Zuo Taichong's [Zuo Si 左思] rhapsody on the Capital of Shu, in which he says: "The Jiang and the Han shine with numinous spirit; generation after generation bears forth their finest." Yet he cites only Changqing [Sima Xiangru 司馬相如] and Ziyun [Yang Xiong 揚雄] as the foremost examples. At first I found his words quite grand, but afterward I privately came to doubt them. Now Shu, as the essence of Mount Min, coils below at the southwestern corner of the earth and corresponds above to the Jing constellation; it stands towering with the Jiange pass and encompasses Mount Yulei, is girdled by the Two Rivers and guarded by the fastness of Mount Emei—how richly it gathers the divine beauty of rivers and mountains! Within it lie a thousand li of fertile plains, flourishing as a favored heartland, where rare wonders and abundant treasures are too numerous to record. When it is called an "inland sea" and a "storehouse of Heaven," is that an empty boast? Truly, if one reasons that numinous land brings forth outstanding heroes, it ought long since to have been renowned as a marshaling ground of talent. Yet the records note that from the times of Cancong and Yufu onward, its remote rusticity had not been dispelled, and the inauguration of Confucian refinement began only with Wen Weng. Before the Han dynasty, only Yin Jifu…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
挺生其鄉爲百代冠吉甫之
外不概見何耶左生詞人也
則奚怪乎第謂楊馬云爾嗣
是而子昂太白以風雅鳴於
唐要亦馬楊之流亞焉至宋
有眉山三蘇華陽諸范漢州
二張德業風猷差足爲蜀重
===
蓋人才之難如此於鑠
明興大化湛醲人文旁洽以蜀
居寰宇西南陲至遐遜矣
神聖在上執粹精愷悌之惪照臨
而覆露之若近郊然故自蹇
忠定而下科不乏人往往軼
蘇駕范漪芳於吉甫甚盛斯
punctuated: 挺生其鄉，爲百代冠。吉甫之外不概見，何耶？左生詞人也，則奚怪乎第謂楊、馬云爾。嗣是而子昂、太白以風雅鳴於唐，要亦馬、楊之流亞焉。至宋有眉山三蘇、華陽諸范、漢州二張，德業風猷，差足爲蜀重，蓋人才之難如此。於鑠明興，大化湛醲，人文旁洽。以蜀居寰宇西南陲，至遐遜矣，神聖在上，執粹精愷悌之惪，照臨而覆露之，若近郊然。故自蹇忠定而下，科不乏人，往往軼蘇駕范，漪芳於吉甫，甚盛。斯
translation_en:
… rose outstandingly from this native place, crowning a hundred generations. Why is it that apart from Jifu, others are scarcely seen? Scholar Zuo [Zuo Si 左思] was a literary writer, so what wonder is it that he merely spoke of Yang [Yang Xiong 揚雄] and Ma [Sima Xiangru 司馬相如]? Thereafter, Zi'ang [Chen Zi'ang 陳子昂] and Taibai [Li Bai 李白] won renown for poetic elegance in the Tang, yet in essence they too were of the same literary lineage as Ma and Yang. Down to the Song, there were the three Su [Su Xun 蘇洵, Su Shi 蘇軾, and Su轍] of Meishan, the several Fan [such as Fan Zhen 范鎮 and Fan Zuyu 范祖禹] of Huayang, and the two Zhang [Zhang Shi 張栻 and Zhang杓, or Zhang Jun 張浚 and Zhang Shi] of Hanzhou, whose virtuous achievements and moral Conduct were somewhat sufficient to bring weight to Shu. Such, indeed, is the difficulty of finding talent!

Oh, how glorious the rise of the Ming! Its great transformative influence is deep and rich, and cultural refinement has spread far and wide. Although Shu lies in the southwestern borderlands of the realm, most distant and remote, the divine sages on high hold fast to pure, refined, and benevolent virtue, shining upon it and sheltering it with moistening grace just as if it were the near suburbs of the capital. Thus, from Jian Zhongding [Jian Yi 蹇義] onward, the examination rosters have never lacked men of worth, who time and again surpass the Su, outstrip the Fan, and rival the fragrant reputation of Jifu in great abundance. This…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
其才不啻爲蜀重而蜀才且
重天下詎非
久道郅隆雲蒸霞變遂卓犖特
抗於在昔與迺說者以爲嘉
隆之際文勝綦焉物盛則返
固其理也我
皇上睿明獨運洞燭化機曩取
===
功令申飭之挽頹風以還之大
雅一時翕然丕變於文質相
扶可謂近之矣間有曲學之
士務巧發奇中刻削纖新失
則詭庸者效之虛薄益甚失
則浮浮詭之習傷乎雅道安
在其爲士也頃
punctuated: 其才不啻爲蜀重，而蜀才且重天下。詎非久道郅隆，雲蒸霞變，遂卓犖特抗於在昔與？迺說者以爲嘉、隆之際，文勝綦焉。物盛則返，固其理也。我皇上睿明獨運，洞燭化機，曩取功令申飭之，挽頹風以還之大雅。一時翕然丕變，於文質相扶，可謂近之矣。間有曲學之士，務巧發奇中，刻削纖新，失則詭；庸者效之，虛薄益甚，失則浮。浮詭之習，傷乎雅道，安在其爲士也？頃
translation_en: … their talent does not merely bring weight to Sichuan, for the talent of Sichuan now carries weight throughout the empire. Is this not because enduring moral instruction has reached the pinnacle of flourishing, rising like clouds and transforming like rosy mists, so that they stand out brilliantly and surpass those of former times? Yet commentators hold that between the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) reigns, literary embellishment prevailed to an extreme. That things return to their root once they reach their peak is indeed a natural principle. Our August Emperor, exercising his sagely wisdom alone and penetratingly illuminating the mechanisms of transformation, previously took the examination regulations and reiterated their strict enforcement, turning back the decadent trend to restore great elegance. All at once, the literary world harmoniously underwent a great transformation; as for form and substance mutually supporting one another, it may be said to have come close to that ideal. Occasionally there are scholars of crooked learning who strive for clever thrusts and strange hits, carving out petty novelties, whose failing is perversity; mediocre men imitate them, becoming ever more hollow and superficial, whose failing is frivolity. Frivolous and perverse habits injure the way of elegance—how then can such men be considered scholars? Recently …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試錄序
上萬曆之十年四川當論秀士於
鄉巡按御史宋〔仕〕秉憲度而
監臨之兢兢翼翼如也先是
馳檄徵四方文學博士至則
以〔應科〕及教諭戴〔震亨〕司考
試教諭湯〔欽聞〕王〔顯先〕張〔道〕
===
深〔訓導李與杜〕孫〔紀〕吳〔中禎〕
龔〔棹〕司同考試提調則左布
政使蔡〔汝賢〕右叅議萬〔一貫〕
監試則按察使鄭〔旻〕副使范
崙百執事慎簡惟其人比入
闈御史申䟽要束矢精白以
從事諰諰懇懇如也於是進
punctuated:
四川鄉試錄序
上萬曆之十年，四川當論秀士於鄉，巡按御史宋〔仕〕秉憲度而監臨之，兢兢翼翼如也。先是，馳檄徵四方文學博士，至則以〔應科〕及教諭戴〔震亨〕司考試，教諭湯〔欽聞〕、王〔顯先〕、張〔道〕深、〔訓導李與杜〕、孫〔紀〕、吳〔中禎〕、龔〔棹〕司同考試。提調則左布政使蔡〔汝賢〕、右叅議萬〔一貫〕，監試則按察使鄭〔旻〕、副使范崙，百執事慎簡惟其人。比入闈，御史申䟽要束，矢精白以從事，諰諰懇懇如也。於是進
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

In the tenth year of the Wanli reign of His Majesty (1582), when Sichuan was due to evaluate and select cultivated scholars at the provincial level, Regional Inspector Song [Shi 仕] upheld the statutory regulations and served as Supervising Official over the proceedings, acting with the utmost caution and reverence. Prior to this, dispatches had been sent by fast courier to summon Confucian instructors and erudites from all quarters. Upon their arrival, [I, Yingke 應科] and Instructor Dai [Zhenheng 震亨] were appointed to take charge as Examiners, while Instructors Tang [Qinwen 欽聞], Wang [Xianxian 顯先], and Zhang [Dao]shen [道深], along with [Assistant Instructors Li Yudu 李與杜], Sun [Ji 紀], Wu [Zhongzhen 中禎], and Gong [Zhao 棹], were appointed to take charge as Associate Examiners. Serving as Proctors were Left Administration Commissioner Cai [Ruxian 汝賢] and Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Wan [Yiguan 一貫]; serving as Surveillance Officials of the Examination were Surveillance Commissioner Zheng [Min 旻] and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Fan Lun 范崙; and for the hundred functional posts, only the right men were carefully selected. When the time came to enter the examination compound, the Censor reiterated and set forth the binding regulations, and all swore to carry out their duties with pure integrity, acting with earnestness and conscientious care. Thereupon, there were brought forward…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
提學副使楊〔節〕今署提學事
左叅議王〔佩祥〕先後所選士
二千有奇三試之得儁者七
十人詩鹿鳴而賓興之濟濟
顒顒如也士當籍
奏〔應科〕不佞宜首颺言以諗諸
士始〔應科〕讀上林甘泉之賦
===
緬焉慕之以爲蜀士翩翩文
章鉅麗雖其人之贍辭哉儻
亦山川奇秀之助乎而無從
覩之也頃幸而攬名都之勝
岷峨表其鎮大江濬其源是
帝以會昌而神聖所爲鍾毓也扶
輿淳淑之氣洋洋乎攸稡矣
punctuated: 提學副使楊〔節〕、今署提學事左叅議王〔佩祥〕先後所選士二千有奇，三試之，得儁者七十人，詩《鹿鳴》而賓興之，濟濟顒顒如也。士當籍奏，〔應科〕不佞，宜首颺言以諗諸士。始〔應科〕讀《上林》、《甘泉》之賦，緬焉慕之，以爲蜀士翩翩，文章鉅麗，雖其人之贍辭哉，儻亦山川奇秀之助乎？而無從覩之也。頃幸而攬名都之勝，岷、峨表其鎮，大江濬其源，是帝以會昌而神聖所爲鍾毓也，扶輿淳淑之氣洋洋乎攸稡矣。
translation_en:
… the slightly more than two thousand scholars selected successively by the Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education Yang Jie 楊節 and the Left Assistant Administration Commissioner currently Acting in Charge of Education Affairs Wang Peixiang 王佩祥, and tested them in three sessions, obtaining seventy men of outstanding talent. Singing the ode "Deer Cry" (Luming 鹿鳴), they presented them as honored guests, numerous and dignified in demeanor. Now that the roster of scholars is to be submitted in a memorial to the throne, I, Yingke 應科, though unworthy, ought to lead off with an opening address to counsel the scholars.

At first, when I, Yingke, read the rhapsodies on the "Supreme Forest" (Shanglin 上林) and "Sweet Springs" (Ganquan 甘泉) palaces, I admired them from afar, thinking how graceful and refined the scholars of Shu 蜀 were, and how grand and magnificent their writings! Yet while this was due to the rich eloquence of the men themselves, might it not also have been aided by the wondrous beauty of their mountains and rivers? Still, I had no way to behold them for myself. Recently, I have had the good fortune to take in the scenic splendors of this famed metropolis: Mount Min 岷 and Mount Emei 峨眉 stand forth as its guardian peaks, and the Great River (Yangzi) dredges out its source. This is where the Sovereign brings together flourishing fortune and where divine sages are nurtured and brought forth; the pure and virtuous ether of the cosmos gathers here in vast abundance! …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
既有事校矾則又瞿然嘆蜀
士本實醇粹不第扶疎於枝
葉信斌斌兼有其質文焉而
嚮之豔慕卿雲爲黼黻河漢
者曾未睹大方之全也
本朝用經術取士士斟酌道德
之淵源以效諸實既其稍渝
===
則有繡鞶悅剽諸子百家以
炫衆驚愚者蜀人士顧獨斤
斤先民是程蓋其愼也邇歲
明詔沛然屢下匠鑄文體歸之雅
正海內操觚之徒意製蹐馳
猶然躍溢於治而令諸士之
業則皆規摹矱矩允哉知言
punctuated: 既有事校矾，則又瞿然嘆蜀士本實醇粹，不第扶疎於枝葉，信斌斌兼有其質文焉。而嚮之豔慕卿、雲爲黼黻河漢者，曾未睹大方之全也。本朝用經術取士，士斟酌道德之淵源，以效諸實。既其稍渝，則有繡鞶悅，剽諸子百家以炫衆驚愚者；蜀人士顧獨斤斤先民是程，蓋其愼也。邇歲明詔沛然屢下，匠鑄文體，歸之雅正。海內操觚之徒，意製蹐馳，猶然躍溢於治；而令諸士之業，則皆規摹矱矩，允哉知言
translation_en: When I then became engaged in grading the examination papers [?], I sighed in astonished admiration that the scholars of Shu are fundamentally substantial and pure, not merely luxuriant in branches and leaves, and truly possess both substance and refinement in harmonious balance. Thus my earlier admiring envy of Sima Xiangru (Qing 卿) and Yang Xiong (Yun 雲) as ornate embroideries and celestial rivers had in fact failed to see the entirety of great accomplishment. Our dynasty selects scholars through the study of the Classics, and scholars draw upon the fountainhead of morality and virtue to apply them in practical reality. Later, as standards somewhat declined, there were those who embroidered belt-pouches and kerchiefs [?], plagiarizing the Various Masters and Hundred Schools to dazzle the crowd and startle the ignorant; yet the scholars of Shu alone remained scrupulously devoted to taking the ancients as their model—such was their caution. In recent years, enlightened imperial edicts have repeatedly rained down in abundance, molding and forging literary style to return it to elegance and orthodoxy. Across the realm, those who wield the writing tablet, though checked in their willful fabrications and headlong galloping [?], still leap and overflow out of the mold; yet the essays of these present scholars all conform to the compass, square, and standard measures—truly a selection of those who understand words…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
之選已非夫乘
昌會而濟聖眞也抑何其涵煦
純懿靡然顧化之捷如此哉且非
獨於騂也馬之探前趹後蹄
間三尋者非梁益所產也乃
江源龍湖之種步驟中繩無
佚銜轡者多有冰紈霧縠文
犀翠翰明璣紫貝蜀鮮稱哉
而深山長谷楩柟松栢往往
勝
===
廟堂之棟榦唯士亦然今天下俶
儻異倫秀蔚有美者奚讁至
足要以小心奉法樸茂良實
稱任使蜀人士亦有足多者
punctuated: 之選已。非夫乘昌會而濟聖眞也，抑何其涵煦純懿、靡然顧化之捷如此哉？且非獨於騂也。馬之探前趹後、蹄間三尋者，非梁、益所產也；乃江源、龍湖之種，步驟中繩、無佚銜轡者多有。冰紈霧縠、文犀翠翰、明璣紫貝，蜀鮮稱哉；而深山長谷，楩柟松栢，往往勝廟堂之棟榦。唯士亦然。今天下俶儻異倫、秀蔚有美者奚讁至足，要以小心奉法、樸茂良實、稱任使，蜀人士亦有足多者
translation_en: …choice of those who understand words. Were it not for availing themselves of this flourishing era to aid the sage truth, how else could they have been nurtured into pure excellence and swept along in transformation so swiftly as this? Moreover, this is not only true of their literary expression [?]. Horses that reach forward and kick backward, covering three xun in a single stride, are not bred in Liangzhou and Yizhou; yet among the breeds of Jiangyuan and Longhu, there are many whose paces conform to the measure and that never slip bit or bridle. Ice-white silk and mist-fine gauze, patterned rhino horn and kingfisher feathers, bright pearls and purple cowries—Sichuan is rarely noted for these; yet in its deep mountains and long valleys, the pian, nan, pine, and cypress trees often prove equal to serving as pillars and beams for the imperial temple and court. It is just the same with scholars. In the empire today, extraordinary and unconventional men of luxuriant talent and fine quality are no doubt more than plentiful; yet when it comes to scrupulously upholding the law, being simple, substantial, honest, and sincere, and proving equal to official commissions, the scholars and gentlemen of Sichuan also have much to be praised for…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
焉前代無論焉耳
高皇帝天造草昧劉文成爲帷幄
子房而蚤授妙略以垂開濟
之勳者非蜀士也乎
文皇帝鼎建鴻基總銓衡之任而
謀謩太平者又蜀士也
肅皇帝中興景運首鉉台而斧藻
===
維新之化者又蜀士也蓋至
于今而炯聲茂實表樹
當世者軏躅相望此亦足明士適
用之效已且夫二三君子所
謂鉅儒元工故皆緜縫掖起
而諸士鳩山川之靈粹比肩
聯翩而興於
punctuated: 焉。前代無論焉耳，高皇帝天造草昧，劉文成爲帷幄子房，而蚤授妙略以垂開濟之勳者，非蜀士也乎？文皇帝鼎建鴻基，總銓衡之任而謀謩太平者，又蜀士也。肅皇帝中興景運，首鉉台而斧藻維新之化者，又蜀士也。蓋至于今，而炯聲茂實、表樹當世者，軏躅相望，此亦足明士適用之效已。且夫二三君子，所謂鉅儒元工，故皆緜縫掖起；而諸士鳩山川之靈粹，比肩聯翩而興於
translation_en: … therein. Setting aside previous dynasties, when the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi, i.e., the Hongwu Emperor) created the empire out of chaos, Liu Wencheng (Liu Ji 劉基) served as the Zifang (Zhang Liang 張良) within the command tent, yet was the one who early on imparted marvelous strategies to leave behind foundational and world-saving achievements not a scholar of Shu (Sichuan)? When the Cultured Emperor (Wen Huangdi, i.e., the Yongle Emperor) established the great enterprise anew, the one who held overall charge of personnel evaluation and appointments and planned for great peace was also a scholar of Shu. When the Reverent Emperor (Su Huangdi, i.e., the Jiajing Emperor) brought about a restoration of glorious fortune, the one who headed the Grand Secretariat and adorned the transformative rule of renewal was likewise a scholar of Shu. Indeed, down to the present day, those of shining reputation and flourishing substance who have distinguished themselves in the current age follow closely in one another's wheel-tracks in unbroken succession; this too suffices to demonstrate the efficacy of scholars being suited for practical service. Moreover, those few gentlemen—the so-called great Confucians and premier statesmen—all originally rose from the ranks of scholars wearing the plain robes of students; and now the various scholars, gathering the numinous essence of the mountains and rivers, stand shoulder to shoulder and soar together, rising up in…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
文明之旦寧渠無傑然自期許以
前哲者哉〔應科〕誠望之矣不
聞賢者在治其着鳳乎止則
梧棲而竹食飛則翽羽而噰
鳴故處奧濮而稱良士則學
有檢押必不爲雕蔓離奇以
詭正資適逢時而稱良臣則
===
業有衡量必不爲駘蕩儇巧
以踰節夫爲臣者亦奚以加
于士哉直取居平所誦法設
誠致行之道如是足也諸士
醇脩而敏迪徵諸辭華實相
章則信乎蜀之良也已方將
濯清流翔天衢耀
punctuated: 文明之旦，寧渠無傑然自期許以前哲者哉？〔應科〕誠望之矣！不聞賢者在治，其着鳳乎？止則梧棲而竹食，飛則翽羽而噰鳴。故處奧濮而稱良士，則學有檢押，必不爲雕蔓離奇以詭正；資適逢時而稱良臣，則業有衡量，必不爲駘蕩儇巧以踰節。夫爲臣者，亦奚以加于士哉？直取居平所誦法，設誠致行之道，如是足也。諸士醇脩而敏迪，徵諸辭，華實相章，則信乎蜀之良也已！方將濯清流、翔天衢，耀
translation_en: … the dawn of a flourishing civilization, how could there not be among you those who stand out boldly and hold themselves to the standard of those former worthies? I, Yingke, truly hope for this from you! Have you not heard that a worthy man in an age of good governance is like the phoenix[?]? When at rest, it roosts in the parasol tree and feeds on bamboo; when in flight, its wings rustle and its call is harmonious. Therefore, when one dwells in retirement in obscure places and is called a fine scholar, one's learning has restraint and discipline, and one certainly does not indulge in ornate, rambling, or bizarre expressions to pervert what is orthodox. When one's talents happen to meet the right moment and one is called a fine minister, one's achievements have measure and standard, and one certainly does not engage in reckless indulgence or clever opportunism to overstep moral bounds. Indeed, how does being a minister add anything beyond what is already in the scholar? It is simply a matter of taking what one ordinarily recites and models oneself upon, establishing sincerity and carrying out the Way in practice—that much suffices. You gentlemen cultivate yourselves with purity and advance with diligence; verified in your writings, flower and substance illuminate one another, so you are truly the finest of Shu! You are just now about to bathe in the clear stream, soar along the heavenly thoroughfare, and shine in …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
日月之末光以展宷錯事殫精悉
忠激卬名世之烈斯自雅志
素所蓄也其何讓哉雖然〔應〕
〔科〕懔懔懼焉周地賤媒非謂
其爲訑而偏於譽耶今主司
於諸士之升輒津津曰良士
良士誠中心愛之信之猶列
===
眉乃不量其譽之過也太阿
剖型觀者神竦燕石緹緡容
乃盧胡士或索之實而無益
主上之理與今所稱詡相繆盭則
安歸責乎諸士勗矣脩爾邦
人之素毋異趣以爲高寧範
我馳驅毋詭遇而關人以捷
punctuated: 日月之末光，以展宷錯事，殫精悉忠，激卬名世之烈，斯自雅志素所蓄也，其何讓哉！雖然，〔應科〕懔懔懼焉。周地賤媒，非謂其爲訑而偏於譽耶？今主司於諸士之升，輒津津曰：「良士！良士！」誠中心愛之、信之，猶列眉，乃不量其譽之過也。太阿剖型，觀者神竦；燕石緹緡，容乃盧胡。士或索之實而無益主上之理，與今所稱詡相繆盭，則安歸責乎？諸士勗矣！脩爾邦人之素，毋異趣以爲高；寧範我馳驅，毋詭遇而關人以捷；
translation_en: … the reflected radiance of the sun and moon, so as to display your talents and attend to affairs, exhausting your vigor and devoting your utmost loyalty to rouse the illustrious achievements of an age-renowned figure—this is naturally the noble ambition you have long cherished; why should you yield in this? Even so, I, Yingke, am filled with trembling dread. When in the land of Zhou matchmakers were held in low esteem, was it not because they indulged in boastful exaggeration and were partial to praise? Now, upon the advancement of these scholars, the examiners tirelessly exclaim, "Fine scholars! Fine scholars!" Truly, we love them and trust them from the bottom of our hearts, seeing their worth as clearly as eyebrows set in a row, yet without measuring whether our praise is excessive. When the Tai'e sword is broken from its mold, onlookers are awestruck in spirit; when a mere stone from Yan is wrapped in red silk and cords, people only laugh behind their hands. Should these scholars, when examined in reality, prove of no benefit to His Majesty's governance, contradicting what we now praise and boast of, then where will the blame fall? Exert yourselves, gentlemen! Cultivate the accustomed virtues of the predecessors of your native land, and do not pursue divergent paths to affect loftiness. Rather drive your chariot strictly according to the rules than intercept game by trickery to vie with others in swiftness; …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
寧爲楩柟松栢需其成于久
大毋若譁囂之玩取衒目睫
庶幾哉前哲可企以爲爾山
川重而主司竊徼榮附於以
人事
君逭訕者之誚幸矣夫語有之信
言不華〔凡應科所切磋度諸〕
士能行者具以質告亦猶以
奉
===
明詔也毋婣曰畢畢無甚高論哉
是舉也巡撫右副都御史今
陞吏部右侍郎侯代張〔士佩〕
飭治經文聲教布濩巡撫貴
州兼督湖北川東右僉都御
punctuated:
寧爲楩柟松栢，需其成于久大，毋若譁囂之玩，取衒目睫。庶幾哉前哲可企，以爲爾山川重，而主司竊徼榮附於以人事君，逭訕者之誚，幸矣夫！語有之：「信言不華。」〔凡應科所切磋，度諸〕士能行者，具以質告，亦猶以奉明詔也，毋婣曰畢畢無甚高論哉！
是舉也，巡撫右副都御史今陞吏部右侍郎侯代張〔士佩〕，飭治經文，聲教布濩；巡撫貴州兼督湖北川東右僉都御
translation_en:
… Rather be like the *pian* and *nan* cedars, or the pines and cypresses, awaiting maturity in enduring greatness, and do not be like flashy trinkets that merely dazzle the eyes for a moment. Thus you may nearly hope to emulate the former worthies and add weight to the mountains and rivers of your homeland; while we, the examination officials, may humbly share in the glory of serving our Lord by recommending worthy men, and fortunate indeed to escape the reproach of critics! As the saying goes: "Trustworthy words are not ornate." [All that I, Yingke, have discussed in earnest here is measured by what you] scholars can actually put into practice, and I have set it forth plainly, just as a way of upholding the August Edict. Do not disdainfully say that these are commonplace words devoid of lofty discourse!

In this examination, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, now promoted to Right Vice Minister of Personnel awaiting replacement, Zhang [Shipei 張士佩], ordered the administration and regulated literary culture, spreading transformative teaching far and wide; Grand Coordinator of Guizhou and Concurrent Controller of Hubei and Eastern Sichuan, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
史今陞南贛汀韶右副都御
史王〔縉〕右副都御史劉〔庠〕先
後保釐章縫漸被巡理茶法
監察御史赫〔瀛〕風猷卓遠興
起譽髦禮科給事中聶〔良杞〕
大理寺右寺正祁〔鯨〕行人司
行人林〔士弘〕以使事至樂觀
===
盛典鎮守總兵官中軍都督府都
督同知郭〔成〕保禦疆土裨益
人文其綜理防檢於外則左
叅政賴〔庭檜〕右叅政淩〔琯〕右
叅政兼僉事楊〔一桂〕右叅議
兼僉事陳〔用賓〕副使鄭〔一信〕
戴〔燿〕張〔稽古〕僉事王〔言〕李〔士〕
punctuated: 史、今陞南贛汀韶右副都御史王〔縉〕，右副都御史劉〔庠〕，先後保釐，章縫漸被；巡理茶法監察御史赫〔瀛〕風猷卓遠，興起譽髦；禮科給事中聶〔良杞〕、大理寺右寺正祁〔鯨〕、行人司行人林〔士弘〕以使事至，樂觀盛典；鎮守總兵官、中軍都督府都督同知郭〔成〕保禦疆土，裨益人文；其綜理防檢於外，則左叅政賴〔庭檜〕，右叅政淩〔琯〕，右叅政兼僉事楊〔一桂〕，右叅議兼僉事陳〔用賓〕，副使鄭〔一信〕、戴〔燿〕、張〔稽古〕，僉事王〔言〕、李〔士〕
translation_en: … [Grand Coordinator of Guizhou and Concurrent Supervisor of Northern Huguang and Eastern Sichuan, Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief], now promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief for Nan'gan, Tingzhou, and Shaozhou, Wang Jin 王縉, and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiang 劉庠, successively safeguarded and governed the region, so that the robed scholars gradually received their beneficent influence. Inspecting Censor for Tea-Law Supervision He Ying 赫瀛, whose moral example and plans are lofty and far-reaching, inspired and roused the renowned talents. Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Rites Nie Liangqi 聶良杞, Right Case Reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review Qi Jing 祁鯨, and Messenger of the Messenger Office Lin Shihong 林士弘 arrived on imperial missions and were delighted to witness this grand ceremony. Regional Commander for Defense and Vice Commissioner-in-Chief of the Central Military Commission Guo Cheng 郭成 protected and defended the territory, bringing benefit to literary culture. As for those who managed overall administration and security precautions on the outside, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Lai Tinggui 賴庭檜, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Ling Guan 淩琯, Right Administration Vice Commissioner concurrently serving as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Yang Yigui 楊一桂, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner concurrently serving as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Chen Yongbin 陳用賓, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zheng Yixin 鄭一信, Dai Yao 戴燿, and Zhang Jigu 張稽古, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Wang Yan 王言 and Li Shi[da] 李士…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
達署都指揮僉事李贇蘇民
望協恭宣力咸有司存右叅
議高任重僉事費尚伊署都
指揮僉事汪東之以入
賀行與勞始事法宜書書之
河南懷慶府脩武縣儒學教
諭楊應科謹序
punctuated:
達、署都指揮僉事李贇、蘇民望，協恭宣力，咸有司存。右叅議高任重、僉事費尚伊、署都指揮僉事汪東之，以入賀行，與勞始事，法宜書，書之。
河南懷慶府脩武縣儒學教諭楊應科謹序。
translation_en:
…da (Li Shida 李士達), and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Li Yun 李贇 and Su Minwang 蘇民望 worked together in reverent harmony and exerted their strength, each fulfilling his official duties. Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Gao Renzhong 高任重, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Fei Shangyi 費尚伊, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Wang Dongzhi 汪東之 departed to present congratulations at court, having shared in the labors of initiating the affair; by rule they ought to be recorded, and so I record them.

Respectfully written as a postface by Yang Yingke 楊應科, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xiuwu County 脩武縣, Huaiqing Prefecture 懷慶府, Henan 河南.

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
重慶府巴縣知縣張文耀〔叅疇湖廣沅陵縣人丁丑進士〕
彌封官
敘州府推官胡喬岱〔道宗江西廬陵縣人癸酉貢士〕
嘉定州知州徐學周〔尚文浙江嘉興縣人甲子貢士〕
邛州知州朱繼魯〔克一湖廣麻城縣人乙卯貢士〕
成都府崇慶州知州陳邦謨〔明甫雲南太和縣人庚午貢士〕
重慶府忠州知州戰符〔廷信湖廣蘄州人戊午貢士〕
成都府新繁縣知縣李聞馨〔德華雲南昆陽州人癸酉貢士〕
夔州府萬縣知縣李植〔良材湖廣黃岡縣人辛酉貢士〕
===
順慶府蓬州判官王致中〔懋和陝西寧羌衛籍直隸無錫縣人甲戌進士〕
謄錄官
保寧府同知桑橋初〔汝培貴州永寧衛籍直隸亳州人戊午貢士〕

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
善政政在養民
學于古訓乃有獲事不師古以克永世匪
說攸聞惟學遜志務時敏厥脩乃來允
懷于茲道積于厥躬惟斆學半念終始
典于學厥德脩罔覺監于先王成憲其
永無愆
嚴惟丕式克用三宅三俊
惟周公克慎厥始惟君陳克和厥中惟公
克成厥終
===
詩
匪東方則明月出之光
彤弓弨兮受言藏之我有嘉賓中心貺之
鍾鼓既設一朝饗之
子孫千億穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
有飶其香邦家之光有椒其馨胡考之寧
匪且有且匪今斯今振古如茲
春秋
秋及江人黃人伐陳僖公四年九月戊辰
punctuated:
善政，政在養民。
學于古訓，乃有獲；事不師古，以克永世，匪說攸聞。惟學遜志，務時敏，厥脩乃來。允懷于茲，道積于厥躬。惟斆學半，念終始典于學，厥德脩罔覺。監于先王成憲，其永無愆。
嚴惟丕式，克用三宅、三俊。
惟周公克慎厥始，惟君陳克和厥中，惟公克成厥終。

詩
匪東方則明，月出之光。
彤弓弨兮，受言藏之。我有嘉賓，中心貺之。鍾鼓既設，一朝饗之。
子孫千億，穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。
有飶其香，邦家之光。有椒其馨，胡考之寧。匪且有且，匪今斯今，振古如茲。

春秋
秋，及江人、黃人伐陳，〔僖公四年〕九月戊辰，
translation_en:
…good government, and government consists in nourishing the people."
"One should study the ancient precepts, and then one will make attainments. That affairs not modeled on antiquity can be maintained for long generations is not what I, Yue, have heard. In learning, one must have a humble will and strive to be constantly diligent; then one's cultivation will come. Truly cherishing this, the Way will accumulate in one's person. Teaching is half of learning; if one's thoughts from end to beginning are constantly fixed on learning, one's virtue will be cultivated without one's being conscious of it. Taking as one's mirror the established statutes of the former kings, one will forever be free from error."
"Sternly pondering the great model, he was able to employ the three appointees to office and the three men of eminence."
"Only the Duke of Zhou was able to be cautious at the beginning; only Jun Chen was able to bring harmony to the middle; only you, Duke, can bring completion to the end."

Book of Odes (Shi):
"It is not the east that is bright; it is the light of the rising moon."
"The red bow is unbent; upon receiving it, it is stored away. I have an honored guest; from the bottom of my heart I bestow it upon him. The bells and drums have been set up; for a whole morning I feast him."
"Sons and grandsons in thousands and ratusan millions, solemn and august, fit to be lords, fit to be kings."
"Fragrant is the aroma, the glory of the state and the clan. Peppery is the scent, the comfort of longevity. Not only here is it thus, not only now is it so; from ancient times it has been like this."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
"In autumn, [we] together with the men of Jiang and the men of Huang attacked Chen" [Fourth year of Duke Xi]; "In the ninth month, on the wuchen day, …"

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
