衛侯使甯俞來聘〔文公四年〕
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子齊世
子光滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭〔襄公〕
〔十年〕公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子
光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐
鄭　公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子
光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐
鄭〔俱襄公十有一年〕
夏五月宋人及楚人平〔宣公十有五年〕春
王正月暨齊平〔昭公七年〕
===
禮記
德成而教尊教尊而官正官正而國治君
之謂也
一命緼韍幽衡再命赤韍幽衡三命赤韍
葱衡
夫肅肅敬也雝雝和也夫敬以和何事不
行
punctuated:
諸侯盟于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕
衛侯使甯俞來聘。〔文公四年〕
公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。〔襄公〕〔十年〕公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。〔俱襄公十有一年〕
夏五月，宋人及楚人平。〔宣公十有五年〕春王正月，暨齊平。〔昭公七年〕

禮記
德成而教尊，教尊而官正，官正而國治，君之謂也。
一命緼韍幽衡，再命赤韍幽衡，三命赤韍葱衡。
夫肅肅，敬也；雝雝，和也。夫敬以和，何事不行？
translation_en:
…"the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu." (Ninth year of Duke Xi)
"The Marquis of Wei sent Ning Yu to come on a mission of friendly inquiries." (Fourth year of Duke Wen)
"The Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, Guang, Heir Apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng." (Tenth year of Duke Xiang) "The Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, Heir Apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng." "The Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, Heir Apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng." (Both in the eleventh year of Duke Xiang)
"In summer, in the fifth month, the people of Song and the people of Chu made peace." (Fifteenth year of Duke Xuan) "In spring, in the King's first month, peace was made with Qi." (Seventh year of Duke Zhao)

Record of Rites (Liji)
"When virtue is perfected, teaching is honored; when teaching is honored, officials are upright; when officials are upright, the state is well governed: this is what is meant by a ruler."
"One of the first grade of commission wears an orange-red knee-cover and a dark-colored girdle pendant; one of the second grade of commission wears a scarlet knee-cover and a dark-colored girdle pendant; one of the third grade of commission wears a scarlet knee-cover and a cerulean-green girdle pendant."
"Now 'solemn, solemn' means reverence; 'harmonious, harmonious' means harmony. When there is reverence combined with harmony, what affair cannot be carried out?"

Imitation of a Song-dynasty memorial of gratitude upon the appointment of Li Fang 李昉 and Zhang Qixian 張齊賢 as Jointly Managers of Affairs (tong pingzhangshi), and Jia Huangzhong 賈黃中 and Li Hang 李沆 as Participants in Determining Governmental Matters (canzhi zhengshi) [2nd year of the Chunhua era (991 CE)]

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
治者然其道豈上下合同之謂哉齊晏
子評梁丘據而有和同之論其於君臣
相須之道辨至悉矣其説可指而言與
執是而求之往古舜爲天子禹皐爲輔
相交相儆戒日勤兢業至於太甲之篇
無逸之訓亦莫非逆耳之言觸鱗之語
彼所謂聖君賢相者相與之際何其艱
哉而譚者率謂太和元氣在唐虞成周
宇宙間則同與和果不相謀也可歷數
===
之與我
皇上茂齡撫運
講學親賢朝乾夕惕日不暇給其心卽舜之
心也商周令主固不敢望下風矣而一
二輔臣鹽梅交濟獻替相成如頃者罷
土木減織造旱災有禱星變有戒其他
憂盛危明之説靡不備至
主上悉以其説見諸行事回視虞廷商周泰和
之景象固千載一日也爾諸士得於躬
punctuated: 治者。然其道豈上下合同之謂哉？齊晏子評梁丘據而有和同之論，其於君臣相須之道，辨至悉矣，其説可指而言與？執是而求之往古：舜爲天子，禹、皐爲輔相，交相儆戒，日勤兢業；至於《太甲》之篇、《無逸》之訓，亦莫非逆耳之言、觸鱗之語。彼所謂聖君賢相者，相與之際，何其艱哉！而譚者率謂太和元氣在唐、虞、成周宇宙間，則同與和果不相謀也，可歷數之與？我皇上茂齡撫運，講學親賢，朝乾夕惕，日不暇給，其心卽舜之心也，商、周令主固不敢望下風矣。而一二輔臣，鹽梅交濟，獻替相成，如頃者罷土木、減織造，旱災有禱、星變有戒，其他憂盛危明之説，靡不備至。主上悉以其説見諸行事，回視虞廷、商、周泰和之景象，固千載一日也。爾諸士得於躬
translation_en:
… governance. Yet how could this Way merely mean ruler and minister echoing one another in uniformity? Master Yan of Qi (Yanzi 晏子), in criticizing Liangqiu Ju 梁丘據, set forth his discourse on harmony versus uniformity (hetong 和同); in it, he distinguished the Way of mutual dependence between ruler and minister in the utmost detail. Can his argument be pointed out and explained?

Holding to this standard and seeking examples in antiquity: when Shun 舜 was the Son of Heaven and Yu 禹 and Gao Yao 皐陶 were his assisting ministers, they mutually admonished and cautioned one another, laboring diligently with wariness and reverence every day. Coming down to the chapters of the Tai Jia 太甲 ("Tai Jia") and the instructions of the Wu Yi 無逸 ("Against Luxurious Ease"), these too consisted entirely of words grating to the ear and speech that brushed against the dragon's reverse scales. In the interactions between those whom we call sage rulers and worthy chief ministers, how difficult and demanding it was! Yet commentators generally say that the primordial vitality of Great Harmony resided in the cosmos during the eras of Tang 唐 (Yao 堯), Yu 虞 (Shun), and Accomplished Zhou 成周. Thus uniformity and harmony truly have nothing in common with each other—can you enumerate the reasons for this one by one?

Our Sovereign, taking up the Mandate in his flourishing youth, expounds upon learning and draws close to the worthy. Diligent by day and vigilant by night, his days are scarcely long enough for all his tasks. His mind is none other than the mind of Shun; the admirable rulers of the Shang 商 and Zhou 周 dynasties could certainly not presume to measure up even to his leeward shadow! Meanwhile, his one or two Grand Secretaries (fuchen 輔臣) blend their efforts like salt and plum to season the state, offering the good and replacing the bad to bring about mutual completion. For instance, recently they have halted construction projects and reduced imperial textile quotas; there have been prayers during droughts and solemn warnings upon the appearance of celestial anomalies; and all other manner of counsels expressing anxiety in times of flourishing and caution in an age of enlightenment have been presented in full. The Sovereign has put every one of their proposals into actual practice. Looking back upon the scenes of Supreme Harmony in the court of Yu (Shun) and in the Shang and Zhou dynasties, this is truly a moment that comes once in a thousand years! You gentlemen have personally…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
逢久矣試颺言於篇用紀盛美即更有
直言讜論其畢陳之以觀忠愛毋諱
問周禮一書備載經略巨細畢舉此聖人
致治之迹也自經秦火其書多散失錯
雜而異議蜂起焉或以爲周公作或以
爲非或謂成周理財之書或謂瀆亂不
經之書其何所據與購得五篇而獻之
祕府校理祕書而著之錄略若能表章
發明之矣乃議者訾之豈別有見乎說
===
周禮者非一人有著復古編者有著補
遺者有謂冬官未嘗亡而地官之文實
亡者果孰爲得與用周禮者亦非一人
或謂其假用之者或謂其輕用之者或
謂其誤用之者果孰爲甚與至於設官
不與王制合封建不與孟子合先儒謂
其間必有末世增入者是固無庸瑣議
也宋朱熹讀孟子經界章稱之曰學識
其大然則善論周禮者亦惟得其大而
punctuated:
逢久矣，試颺言於篇，用紀盛美。即更有直言讜論，其畢陳之，以觀忠愛，毋諱。
問：《周禮》一書，備載經略，巨細畢舉，此聖人致治之迹也。自經秦火，其書多散失錯雜，而異議蜂起焉。或以爲周公作，或以爲非；或謂成周理財之書，或謂瀆亂不經之書，其何所據與？購得五篇而獻之祕府，校理祕書而著之《錄》《略》，若能表章發明之矣，乃議者訾之，豈別有見乎？說《周禮》者非一人：有著《復古編》者，有著《補遺》者，有謂〈冬官〉未嘗亡而〈地官〉之文實亡者，果孰爲得與？用《周禮》者亦非一人：或謂其假用之者，或謂其輕用之者，或謂其誤用之者，果孰爲甚與？至於設官不與〈王制〉合，封建不與《孟子》合，先儒謂其間必有末世增入者，是固無庸瑣議也。宋朱熹讀《孟子》「經界」章，稱之曰：「學識其大。」然則善論《周禮》者，亦惟得其大而
translation_en:
…personally encountered it for a long time. Try setting forth your words in an essay to record this flourishing excellence. And if you have further forthright words and honest counsel, lay them out in full so that we may observe your loyalty and devotion; hold nothing back.

Question: The book Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) comprehensively records the grand designs of governance, encompassing everything great and small; these are the traces of how the sages brought about order. Ever since it passed through the fires of Qin, the book has suffered much loss and scrambling, and divergent opinions have risen like a swarm of bees. Some consider it the work of the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong), while others consider it not to be; some call it a book on fiscal administration from the flourishing Zhou era, while others call it a muddled, disordered, and uncanonical book—what are the grounds for these views? Those who purchased and obtained five sections and presented them to the Imperial Library, and who collated the palace books and recorded it in the Seven略 (Qilüe) and Separate Records (Bielu), seemed able to bring it to light and elucidate it; yet critics disparaged them—did they have some other insight? Those who have expounded on the Rites of Zhou are not just one person: there was one who wrote the Restoration of Antiquity Edition (Fugubian), one who wrote the Supplement to Omissions (Buyi), and one who argued that the "Offices of Winter" (Dongguan) was never lost while text from the "Offices of Earth" (Diguan) was in fact lost—which of them actually got it right? Those who have put the Rites of Zhou into practice are likewise not just one person: some are said to have used it as a pretext, some are said to have used it rashly, and some are said to have used it mistakenly—which of these cases was in fact the worst? As for the fact that its establishment of offices does not accord with the "Royal Regulations" (Wangzhi), and its enfeoffment system does not accord with the Mencius (Mengzi), earlier Confucians said there must be interpolations from a declining age in it, so there is certainly no need for petty disputation over such points. When Zhu Xi of the Song read the chapter on "defining boundaries" (jingjie) in the Mencius, he praised him, saying: "In learning, he grasped the great essentials." If that is so, then one who is good at discussing the Rites of Zhou likewise only grasps its great essentials and…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
已玆欲師周公之意而不泥其迹諸生
必有會通其大指者願切磋究之
問儒者有言士人以正直忠厚爲本貴節
與量也虞夏商周以前尚矣自是而後
惟兩漢士風最爲近古西漢尚長厚東
漢尚奇節姑撮其著者言之有見人有
過専務覆匿者有郎官有譴常蒙其罪
者有買金償同舍恐人知吏迹者有爲
吏未甞案人官屬不敢爲欺者以量名
===
也果有得於正直與有少厲清節而贓
汙解綬者有聲名自高而士號登龍門
者有性方峻厲一榻常懸者有表正鄉
閭不願爲所短者以節名也果有得於
忠厚與士生其時亦有卓然不受變於
俗者其人可得而指與兩漢風聲氣習
大抵與理道運祚相維繫其得失利害
可得而評與當今士習比前代何似論
世者擇術而趨作人者樹風而倡將何
punctuated:
已。玆欲師周公之意而不泥其迹，諸生必有會通其大指者，願切磋究之。

問：儒者有言：「士人以正直忠厚爲本，貴節與量也。」虞、夏、商、周以前尚矣，自是而後，惟兩漢士風最爲近古。西漢尚長厚，東漢尚奇節。姑撮其著者言之：有見人有過，専務覆匿者；有郎官有譴，常蒙其罪者；有買金償同舍，恐人知吏迹者；有爲吏未甞案人，官屬不敢爲欺者。以量名也，果有得於正直與？有少厲清節，而贓汙解綬者；有聲名自高，而士號登龍門者；有性方峻厲，一榻常懸者；有表正鄉閭，不願爲所短者。以節名也，果有得於忠厚與？士生其時，亦有卓然不受變於俗者，其人可得而指與？兩漢風聲氣習，大抵與理道運祚相維繫，其得失利害，可得而評與？當今士習比前代何似？論世者擇術而趨，作人者樹風而倡，將何…
translation_en:
…only. Now, if we wish to take the Duke of Zhou's intentions as our model without clinging rigidly to his outward traces, you students must surely have a thorough grasp of the overarching purport; I hope you will carefully examine and discuss it.

Question: Confucian scholars have a saying: "For the literatus, uprightness and loyal generosity are the foundation; what is prized are moral integrity and magnanimity." The eras of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou are remote in antiquity; from that time onward, only the ethos of the literati in the Two Han dynasties was closest to antiquity. The Western Han esteemed generous magnanimity, whereas the Eastern Han esteemed extraordinary integrity. Let us tentatively gather the most prominent examples to speak of them: there was one who, upon seeing others' faults, made it his sole business to cover and conceal them; there was one who, when Court Gentlemen incurred reprimands, regularly took their blame upon himself; there was one who bought gold to repay a roommate, fearing that others might learn of the clerk's investigation; and there was one who, serving as an official, never investigated or prosecuted anyone, yet whose subordinates dared not deceive him. These men were renowned for their magnanimity—did they truly attain uprightness? Then there were those before whom corrupt officials untied their seal-ribbons and resigned upon hearing of the strict purity they cultivated in youth; there was one who held his own reputation in high esteem, such that scholars called being received by him "ascending the Dragon Gate"; there was one whose nature was square, stern, and severe, keeping a single couch constantly hung up except for a worthy guest; and there was one who stood as a paragon of rectitude in his home community, such that wrongdoers wished not to be disparaged by him. These men were renowned for their moral integrity—did they truly attain loyal generosity? Among the literati born in those times, were there also those who stood out independently and were not altered by prevailing customs, and can those individuals be pointed out? The moral influence and prevailing ethos of the Two Han dynasties were on the whole bound up with their principles of governance and the destiny and longevity of the throne; can their successes and failures, advantages and disadvantages, be evaluated? How do the customs of the literati today compare with those of former dynasties? For those who assess the age in choosing the path they pursue, and for those who cultivate men by establishing the ethos they champion, where…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
居焉其詳言之以觀向往
問守令數易則民不安任官之必要於久
也尚矣史遷稱漢之盛以居官者長子
孫爲言漢宣之治史贊其吏稱民安者
正以久任之法行上下莫有苟且之意
也歷代論治者卒歸重於此詎不然哉
我
皇上鑒古圖治首用輔臣議
明詔有司力行久任期復唐虞三考黜陟庶績
===
咸熙之効
神明之化洽矣或者有謂久任便民不便吏何
與夫張官置吏以爲民也民誠便矣何
以吏之不便爲顧乃蘇軾復言得者旣
不肯以僥倖自名則不得者必以沉淪
爲恨何以故乎先正謂久任與超遷相
爲表裏信斯言也吏民俱得其便與其
說亦可得聞與
皇朝稽古定制於斯二者實兼用之其在今日
punctuated:
居焉？其詳言之，以觀向往。
問：守令數易則民不安，任官之必要於久也尚矣。史遷稱漢之盛，以居官者長子孫爲言；漢宣之治，史贊其吏稱民安者，正以久任之法行，上下莫有苟且之意也。歷代論治者，卒歸重於此，詎不然哉？我皇上鑒古圖治，首用輔臣議，明詔有司力行久任，期復唐、虞三考黜陟、庶績咸熙之効，神明之化洽矣。或者有謂久任便民不便吏，何與？夫張官置吏以爲民也，民誠便矣，何以吏之不便爲？顧乃蘇軾復言「得者旣不肯以僥倖自名，則不得者必以沉淪爲恨」，何以故乎？先正謂久任與超遷相爲表裏，信斯言也，吏民俱得其便與？其說亦可得聞與？皇朝稽古定制，於斯二者實兼用之，其在今日，
translation_en:
…position should one take? Explain this in detail so that we may observe your aspirations.

Question: When prefects and magistrates are frequently replaced, the common people cannot rest in peace; the necessity of long tenure in official appointments has been recognized since antiquity. When Sima Qian 史遷 praised the flourishing of the Han dynasty, he cited the fact that those holding office raised their sons and grandsons in their posts; and regarding the governance of Emperor Xuan of Han 漢宣, the histories praised it by saying that officials were equal to their duties and the people were at peace, precisely because the policy of long tenure was practiced and neither superiors nor subordinates harbored any perfunctory intentions. Those who have discussed governance through the ages have ultimately placed great weight upon this—how could it not be so?

Our August Emperor, examining antiquity and planning for good governance, first adopted the deliberations of his Grand Secretaries and issued a clear decree to the authorities to vigorously implement long tenure in office, hoping to restore the efficacy of the Tang 唐 and Yu 虞 eras, when demotions and promotions were carried out after three triennial evaluations and all official achievements were resplendent. His divine and enlightened transformative influence has spread far and wide! Yet some say that long tenure is convenient for the people, but inconvenient for the officials—why is that? Now, offices are established and officials are appointed for the sake of the people; if it is truly convenient for the people, why should one care about its inconvenience for the officials? And yet Su Shi 蘇軾 further remarked that "since those who succeed are unwilling to call themselves lucky, those who fail will inevitably resent sinking into obscurity"—for what reason is this? Worthies of earlier generations said that long tenure and rapid promotion are two sides of the same coin. If we trust these words, do both officials and the people obtain convenience from this? May we also hear an explanation of that? Our August Dynasty examined antiquity to establish its institutions, and in fact employed both of these methods together. At the present day,…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
可因而行之否茲欲使服官牧民者樂
於久任以維其法於無窮其道何繇與
請攄所藴以竟其說
問立國莫先於爲民興利蜀之利民無如
水利蠶桑茲試相與籌之夫益州沃野
千里天府之地諸葛亮言也攷史漢蜀
守李冰鑿離堆辟沬水穿二江成都中
行舟而餘以用溉今堆猶巋立水間而
沬水不言害矣第不審二江謂何而經
===
行灌溉何縣何畝也夫亮稱沃野矣而
自爲蜀相江水無恙旁近地皆引注爲
畝乃廢不講其少史起引漳灌鄴智耶
抑有說也蜀志曰蜀古蠶叢國謂其地
宜蠶舊矣乃張詠教植桑於知鄂時而
事蹟不具於爲蜀何也且今閬之北家
蠶户桑而錦官以南不覩一植又何也
或曰民辟稅說果然否今成都自沙河
牴龍泉皆可田而乏水利自錦官及戎
punctuated:
可因而行之否？茲欲使服官牧民者樂於久任，以維其法於無窮，其道何繇與？請攄所藴，以竟其說。

問：立國莫先於爲民興利。蜀之利民，無如水利、蠶桑，茲試相與籌之。夫「益州沃野千里，天府之地」，諸葛亮言也。攷《史》、《漢》，蜀守李冰鑿離堆，辟沬水，穿二江成都中，行舟而餘以用溉。今堆猶巋立水間，而沬水不言害矣，第不審二江謂何？而經行灌溉，何縣何畝也？夫亮稱沃野矣，而自爲蜀相，江水無恙，旁近地皆引注爲畝，乃廢不講，其少史起引漳灌鄴智耶？抑有說也？《蜀志》曰：「蜀，古蠶叢國。」謂其地宜蠶舊矣。乃張詠教植桑於知鄂時，而事蹟不具於爲蜀，何也？且今閬之北，家蠶户桑，而錦官以南不覩一植，又何也？或曰民辟稅，說果然否？今成都自沙河牴龍泉，皆可田而乏水利；自錦官及戎、
translation_en:
… can we follow and put them into practice? Now, if we wish to make those who hold office and shepherd the people happy with long tenures of office, so as to maintain the system in perpetuity, by what way can this be achieved? Please set forth your accumulated learning to complete this discussion.

Question: In establishing the state, nothing takes precedence over promoting what benefits the people. In Shu [Sichuan], nothing benefits the people more than water conservancy and sericulture; let us now deliberate on them together. That "Yizhou has a thousand li of fertile fields, a land of heavenly abundance" were the words of Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮. Examining the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji) and the History of the Han (Hanshu), the Grand Administrator of Shu, Li Bing 李冰, cut through the Separated Mound (Lidui 離堆) to ward off the harms of the Mo River (Moshui 沬水), and dug two canals through the midst of Chengdu 成都, allowing boats to navigate while the surplus water was used for irrigation. Today the mound still stands towering amid the waters, and the Mo River is no longer spoken of as a hazard; yet we do not clearly know what the "two rivers" refer to, nor through which counties and across which fields they flow and irrigate. Now, Zhuge Liang praised the fertile fields, yet when he himself served as Chancellor of Shu, although the river waters were intact and the nearby lands could all draw water to irrigate the fields, this was neglected and not attended to—did he lack the wisdom of Shi Qi 史起 in drawing water from the Zhang River to irrigate Ye 鄴? Or is there another explanation? The Record of Shu (Shuzhi) says: "Shu is the ancient state of Cancong 蠶叢," meaning that its land has long been suitable for sericulture. Yet Zhang Yong 張詠 taught the planting of mulberry trees when he served as Prefect of E [Ezhou 鄂州], whereas no such deeds are recorded from his governance of Shu—why is that? Moreover, today north of Lang [Langzhong 閬中], every family raises silkworms and every household cultivates mulberries, while south of Jinguan 錦官 [Chengdu] not a single planted mulberry tree is to be seen—why is this so as well? Some say the people are evading taxes; is this explanation truly correct or not? Today in Chengdu, from the Sha River (Shahe 沙河) reaching to Longquan 龍泉, all the land can be farmed, yet it lacks water conservancy; from Jinguan reaching to Rong [Rongzhou 戎州] and…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
渝皆可桑而罕勸課誠欲在事者用史
起智而申張詠之見奚策而可諸生蜀
產宜習蜀掌故其具言之
punctuated: 渝皆可桑而罕勸課。誠欲在事者用史起智，而申張詠之見，奚策而可？諸生蜀產，宜習蜀掌故，其具言之。
translation_en: … Yu 渝 [Chongqing] is all suited to cultivating mulberry trees, yet encouragement and supervision are rare. If we truly wish for those in office to employ the wisdom of Shi Qi 史起 and carry forward the insight of Zhang Yong 張詠, what policy would make this possible? You students are natives of Shu 蜀 [Sichuan] and ought to be familiar with its historical precedents; set forth your views in full.

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
所謂誠其意者毋自欺也
劉三才
同考試官教諭湯　批〔講毋自欺透徹題旨躍然宜錄〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔切當〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔典實〕
答
傳者釋誠意惟戒其累吾誠者而已夫意之不
===
誠自欺累之也欲誠其意者可不知所戒哉且
夫天下有實理自脩有實功而一毫之欺不與
焉知此則經文之所謂誠意者可識矣何則意
發於人心之動其初何有於欺也意雜於人欲
之私其欺於是乎生焉誠則不欺欺則不可以
語誠矣故誠意者不必他有所求也眞妄之辨
旣以晰於知至之餘則防檢之功自當加於有
感之際善知所當爲矣而爲之不力將誰欺乎
是自欺其好也非所以誠吾好善之意也吾其
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「所謂誠其意者，毋自欺也。」

劉三才
同考試官教諭湯　批〔講毋自欺透徹，題旨躍然，宜錄。〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔切當。〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔典實。〕

答：
傳者釋誠意，惟戒其累吾誠者而已。夫意之不誠，自欺累之也。欲誠其意者，可不知所戒哉？且夫天下有實理，自脩有實功，而一毫之欺不與焉。知此，則經文之所謂誠意者可識矣。何則？意發於人心之動，其初何有於欺也？意雜於人欲之私，其欺於是乎生焉。誠則不欺，欺則不可以語誠矣。故誠意者，不必他有所求也。眞妄之辨，旣以晰於知至之餘；則防檢之功，自當加於有感之際。善知所當爲矣，而爲之不力，將誰欺乎？是自欺其好也，非所以誠吾好善之意也。吾其

First Session

The Four Books

"What is meant by 'making one's thoughts sincere' is allowing no self-deception."

Liu Sancai 劉三才
Associate Examiner, Instructor Tang 湯, comments: [The explanation of "allowing no self-deception" is thorough; the import of the theme leaps out vividly. It ought to be selected.]
Examiner, Instructor Dai 戴, comments: [Pertinent and apt.]
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊, comments: [Grounded in the classics and substantial.]

Answer:
In explaining how to make one's thoughts sincere, the commentator simply warns against that which compromises our sincerity. Now, when thoughts are not sincere, it is self-deception that compromises them. How can one who wishes to make his thoughts sincere not know what to guard against? Moreover, in the world there is real principle, and in self-cultivation there is real effort, in which not a hair's breadth of deception has any part. Once one understands this, what the classic text means by "making the thoughts sincere" can be recognized. Why is this? Thoughts issue from the stirrings of the human mind; in the beginning, what deception is there in them? Only when thoughts become adulterated by the selfishness of human desires does deception arise therein. Where there is sincerity, there is no deception; where there is deception, one cannot speak of sincerity. Therefore, one who would make his thoughts sincere need not seek anything elsewhere. Since the distinction between the true and the false has already been clearly discerned after knowledge has been extended to the utmost, the work of vigilance and restraint ought naturally to be applied at the moment when thoughts are stirred. When one knows that a good ought to be done, yet does not do it with all one's strength, whom would one be deceiving? This is to deceive oneself in one's own love of the good, and is not the way to make sincere one's intention to love the good. Should I…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
一言而興邦乎
苟自新
同考試官教諭王批轉折起伏曲盡其妙且氣度冠
冕擅塲之作也
考試官教諭戴批精粹
考試官教諭楊批正大
時君求治於一言聖人因進以克艱之道焉甚
矣君道惟艱也知其艱而圖之邦其可幾而興
乎此夫子一言以迪定公也且為君者豈不欲
===
其邦之興哉顧治道成於憂勤而隳於逸樂難
易之間人君不可以不知也定公志於興邦而
取必於一言焉蓋知所以期其效而未知所以
圖其難者孔子則對之曰君欲一言以興邦也
言可若是其期哉必也其人言乎曰為君難為
臣不易蓋以代天理物者君也日御萬幾之煩
代君終事者臣也身膺百責之萃故言君難而
幷及臣之不易也思深哉其言之也誠萬世興
邦之要道矣君人者特患未之知耳如其聞斯

punctuated:
「一言而興邦乎？」
苟自新
同考試官教諭王批：轉折起伏，曲盡其妙，且氣度冠冕，擅塲之作也。
考試官教諭戴批：精粹。
考試官教諭楊批：正大。
時君求治於一言，聖人因進以克艱之道焉。甚矣，君道惟艱也！知其艱而圖之，邦其可幾而興乎？此夫子一言以迪定公也。且為君者，豈不欲其邦之興哉？顧治道成於憂勤而隳於逸樂，難易之間，人君不可以不知也。定公志於興邦，而取必於一言焉，蓋知所以期其效，而未知所以圖其難者。孔子則對之曰：君欲一言以興邦也，言可若是其期哉？必也其人言乎，曰：「為君難，為臣不易。」蓋以代天理物者，君也，日御萬幾之煩；代君終事者，臣也，身膺百責之萃。故言君難，而幷及臣之不易也。思深哉其言之也！誠萬世興邦之要道矣。君人者，特患未之知耳。如其聞斯
translation_en:
"[Is there] a single saying that can cause a state to flourish?" (Analects 13.15)
Gou Zixin 苟自新
Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Wang comments: Its twists, turns, rises, and falls exhaust every subtlety; moreover, its bearing is stately and dignified—a piece that dominates the examination compound.
Examiner Instructor Dai comments: Pure and refined.
Examiner Instructor Yang comments: Upright and grand.
When the ruler of the time sought good governance in a single saying, the Sage accordingly presented him with the Way of overcoming difficulties. Profound indeed is the difficulty of the Way of the ruler! If one recognizes its difficulty and plans accordingly, may one not hope for the state to flourish? This was how the Master enlightened Duke Ding 定公 through a single saying.
Moreover, how could anyone who acts as a ruler not wish for his state to flourish? Yet the Way of governance is achieved through anxious diligence and ruined through idle pleasure; the distinction between difficulty and ease is something a ruler of men cannot fail to understand. Duke Ding set his ambition on causing his state to flourish, yet sought to guarantee it through a single saying; this was because he knew how to hope for the effect, but did not yet know how to grapple with the difficulty. Confucius therefore replied to him: You, my lord, wish for a single saying by which to cause your state to flourish, yet can a saying be counted upon like that? If there must be one, is it not the popular saying, which runs: "To be a ruler is difficult; to be a minister is not easy"? For he who governs all things on behalf of Heaven is the ruler, who daily presides over the complexity of a myriad affairs; and he who brings tasks to completion on behalf of the ruler is the minister, who personally shoulders the convergence of a hundred responsibilities. Therefore, in speaking of the difficulty of being a ruler, the saying also extends to how it is not easy to be a minister. How deeply considered are the words of that saying! Truly, it is the essential Way for causing a state to flourish for ten thousand generations. Those who rule over men suffer only from not yet knowing it. If indeed one hears this…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
人主雖至神聖閭閻細務弗能周也今百官奏
疏四方之利弊具焉誠不厭旁午
躬親覽閱於其關繫
國是者時
召二三大臣咨詢可否而
裁度之則凡邊防國計刑獄災祥之類日達于
九重而
天聽其益擴乎古者諫無常官自公卿百執事
下至瞽御工師之賤皆諫也
===
今制寧無太狹乎誠倣周官遺意廣開言路
以招致之而止輦以受其言虛懷以納其
議如此而
主闕不補臣忠不宣者吾未之信也古者官必
擇人卽侍御僕從罔非吉士今之直宿果
皆若人乎誠於斯時嚴擇人以充其選俾
燕寢閒懿戒之儆出入有剪桐之規如此
而非幾或貢
天德弗純者吾未之信也凡此四者皆所以昭
punctuated: 人主雖至神聖，閭閻細務弗能周也。今百官奏疏，四方之利弊具焉。誠不厭旁午，躬親覽閱，於其關繫國是者，時召二三大臣咨詢可否而裁度之，則凡邊防、國計、刑獄、災祥之類日達于九重，而天聽其益擴乎！古者諫無常官，自公卿、百執事，下至瞽御、工師之賤，皆諫也。今制寧無太狹乎？誠倣《周官》遺意，廣開言路以招致之，而止輦以受其言，虛懷以納其議，如此而主闕不補、臣忠不宣者，吾未之信也。古者官必擇人，卽侍御僕從罔非吉士，今之直宿果皆若人乎？誠於斯時嚴擇人以充其選，俾燕寢閒懿戒之儆，出入有剪桐之規，如此而非幾或貢、天德弗純者，吾未之信也。凡此四者，皆所以昭
translation_en:
Even if a sovereign is supremely sagely and divine, he cannot be thoroughly acquainted with the minute affairs of the common villages. Nowadays, the memorials submitted by the hundred officials contain all the advantages and abuses of the four quarters. If he truly does not tire of their multiplicity and personally reads through them, and regarding matters that bear upon policies of state, frequently summons two or three grand ministers to consult on their feasibility and make his decisions upon them, then everything concerning frontier defense, state finances, penal administration, and portents of disaster or good fortune will daily reach the Ninefold Palace, and will not the imperial hearing be ever more broadened?

In antiquity, remonstrance was not confined to regular offices; from the Dukes, Ministers, and hundred functionaries down to the lowly blind musicians, attendants, and artisans, all offered remonstrance. Is the present system not perhaps too narrow? If he truly emulates the surviving intent of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), broadly opens the avenue of speech to invite them in, halts his imperial carriage to receive their words, and keeps an open mind to adopt their deliberations—that if he acts thus the sovereign's failings will still not be mended and the ministers' loyalty not be expressed, I cannot believe it.

In antiquity, in filling offices one necessarily selected the right men, so that even among close attendants and retinue there were none who were not worthy gentlemen. Are those who keep night watch in the palace today truly all such men? If at this time he strictly selects men to fill these appointments, so that in the leisure of his private chambers there are the warnings of the "Admirable Admonitions" [?], and in his goings and comings there is the corrective counsel of the "cutting of the paulownia leaf"—that if he acts thus improper inclinations might still be presented and the imperial virtue not remain pure, I cannot believe it.

All four of these are means by which to manifest…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
宣
令德嘉納讜謨兢業日虔以共臻夫太和之
治焉盛世君臣所以建無窮之基垂無窮
之聞者率茲道哉率茲道哉雖然其本則
君心繫之矣宋儒有言曰惟學可以養此
心惟敬可以存此心惟親近君子可以維
持此心故魏徵有十漸之戒陸贄勸九弊
之陳豫養防微因事納誨其道固如此
今日格心之功固賴二三大臣在也愚何敢
===
臆說焉
第二問　　　　　　　　王　藎
同考試官訓導孫　批〔論周禮者率裁靡定子獨以識其大爲言其見卓矣且据摭詳而議論確〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔獨見大意而詞足以發之〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔具見博雅〕
聖人有可傳之道而無盡傳之法道本大
中至正而不易法則隨時變易以從道也
punctuated:
宣令德、嘉納讜謨，兢業日虔，以共臻夫太和之治焉。盛世君臣所以建無窮之基、垂無窮之聞者，率茲道哉！率茲道哉！雖然，其本則君心繫之矣。宋儒有言曰：「惟學可以養此心，惟敬可以存此心，惟親近君子可以維持此心。」故魏徵有「十漸」之戒，陸贄勸「九弊」之陳，豫養防微，因事納誨，其道固如此。今日格心之功，固賴二三大臣在也，愚何敢臆說焉！

第二問　王藎
同考試官訓導孫　批〔論《周禮》者率裁靡定，子獨以識其大爲言，其見卓矣，且据摭詳而議論確。〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔獨見大意，而詞足以發之。〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔具見博雅。〕

聖人有可傳之道，而無盡傳之法。道本大中至正而不易，法則隨時變易以從道也。
translation_en:
…proclaim His illustrious virtue, favorably accept forthright counsels, and grow daily more reverent in cautious diligence, so as to reach together a governance of Supreme Harmony. That whereby sovereign and ministers in a flourishing age establish an endless foundation and hand down endless renown follows this very Way—follows this very Way indeed! Even so, its root is bound up with the sovereign's mind. A Song Confucian once said: "Only through learning can one nourish this mind; only through reverence can one preserve this mind; only through drawing close to noble men can one sustain this mind." Thus Wei Zheng 魏徵 offered his admonition on the "Ten Gradual Lapses," and Lu Zhi 陸贄 urged his presentation on the "Nine Abuses." Cultivating in advance and guarding against the incipient, offering instruction according to the matter at hand—such has ever been the Way. Today, the work of rectifying the sovereign's mind surely depends upon our two or three grand ministers; how dare an ignorant student like myself offer mere conjectures!

Second Policy Question — Wang Jin 王藎
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Sun 孫, comments: [Those who discuss the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli 周禮) generally arrive at no settled judgment, yet you alone speak of grasping its great essentials; your insight is lofty indeed, and moreover your citations are detailed and your arguments sound.]
Examiner, Instructor Dai 戴, comments: [He alone perceives the main import, and his words suffice to bring it forth.]
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊, comments: [Fully demonstrates breadth of learning and elegance.]

The sages possessed a Way that could be transmitted, yet had no institutions (fa 法) that could be transmitted in their entirety. The Way is by nature supremely central, utterly upright, and unchanging, whereas institutions change with the times in order to follow the Way. …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
夫法之立也非不經晝盡制錯綜盡宜以
爲維持天下之具然不知其法雖善而歷
久則窮故必有與世推移者以神其用於
不匱譬之權衡設於此而低昂進退之隨
其物也故道可以該法法不足以盡道善
用經者惟能緣法以求心由心而會法則
可識其大於千載之上而聖人之精見矣
請因明問而敬陳之周禮一書儒先謂周
公致治之大法在其中姬聖極由東之典
===
法天地而行教化以成文武之德監列聖
之制昭郁郁之文若大猷而垂彝憲者也
當其時四國順焉百辟刑焉旣醉嘉其太
平行葦歌其忠厚迨至康昭之後紀綱尚
明爰及春秋之世法度猶在若韓宣子齊
仲孫湫咸知周禮之足興可鏡也今考其
所載惟王建國辨方正位體國經野設官
分職以爲民極極者道之中也即五官之
中皆冠以數語此其大本大原孰非其法
punctuated: 夫法之立也，非不經晝盡制、錯綜盡宜，以爲維持天下之具；然不知其法雖善，而歷久則窮，故必有與世推移者，以神其用於不匱。譬之權衡設於此，而低昂進退之隨其物也。故道可以該法，法不足以盡道。善用經者，惟能緣法以求心，由心而會法，則可識其大於千載之上，而聖人之精見矣。請因明問而敬陳之：《周禮》一書，儒先謂周公致治之大法在其中，姬聖極由東之典，法天地而行教化，以成文、武之德；監列聖之制，昭郁郁之文，若大猷而垂彝憲者也。當其時，四國順焉，百辟刑焉，《旣醉》嘉其太平，《行葦》歌其忠厚。迨至康、昭之後，紀綱尚明；爰及春秋之世，法度猶在，若韓宣子、齊仲孫湫，咸知周禮之足興，可鏡也。今考其所載：「惟王建國，辨方正位，體國經野，設官分職，以爲民極。」極者，道之中也。即五官之中，皆冠以數語，此其大本大原，孰非其法
translation_en:
Now, when institutions are established, it is not that they fail to be thoroughly planned in every regulation and intricately arranged for every circumstance so as to serve as instruments for sustaining the realm. Yet if one does not understand that even though the institutions are good, over the course of time they reach an impasse, then there must be that which shifts with the ages in order to keep their operation wondrous and inexhaustible. It is like a steelyard and balance set up here: their rising and falling, advancing and retreating, simply follow the objects being weighed. Therefore, the Way can encompass institutions, whereas institutions are insufficient to exhaust the Way. Those skilled at using the Classics are simply able to trace the institutions to seek the mind behind them, and through that mind to comprehend the institutions; thus one can recognize what is great in them across a thousand years above, and the essence of the sages becomes manifest.

Allow me to respectfully set this forth in response to your perceptive question. Regarding the book the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), former Confucian scholars said that the Duke of Zhou's great institutions for bringing about order are contained within it. The sage of the Ji clan brought to perfection the canons from his eastern campaigns [? 極由東之典], modeling them on Heaven and Earth to carry out moral transformation, thereby completing the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu; surveying the systems of the successive sages to display a richly flourishing culture, conforming to the great plan and handing down constant statutes. At that time, the states of the four quarters were compliant, and the hundred lords took him as their model; the ode "Already Drunk" (Jizui) praised that era's great peace, and "Roadside Reeds" (Xingwei) sang of its loyal generosity. Down to the period after Kings Kang and Zhao, the guiding principles of order were still clear; and even reaching the Spring and Autumn era, the laws and measures still remained—men such as Han Xuanzi and Zhongsun Qiu of Qi both knew that the rites of Zhou were sufficient for a revival, which serves as a mirror.

If we now examine what is recorded therein: "It is the king who establishes the state, distinguishes the directions and rectifies the positions, gives structure to the capital and lays out the countryside, establishes offices and apportions duties, so as to serve as the supreme standard for the people." The "supreme standard" (ji) is the centrality of the Way. Indeed, each of the Five Offices (instead of six, as five survive) is prefaced with these few lines; as for this great foundation and great source, which part of it is not that from which its institutions…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
之所自出者故其布之爲制則井牧始於
黃帝而九夫經畫之制建弼服昉於唐堯
而九畿分國之制詳象刑儆於舜而五刑
麗民之制具貢賦創於夏而典式法則之
制行官刑肇於商而廢置誅賞之制立唯
其義之精也朱子曰周官徧布周密乃周
公運用天理爛熟之書誠哉是言也柰經
秦火之後散逸無存自漢除挾書之律衆
書往往頗出諸儒執經競進周禮遂列於
===
九經矣維時顓門持業者非其師說不從
各立門戶者互相詆毀求勝或索諸儀章
度數之間或泥乎文字訓詁之末甚至援
引曲說竊取聖人之迹而强附之昔人謂
秦人焚經而經存諸儒窮經而經絕良有
以也故在劉歆信其爲是則以爲周公致
太平之迹林孝存排其爲非則以爲戰國
陰謀之書王安石作周官義而謂成周理
財之書則見以爲偏漢武帝得周官五篇
punctuated: 之所自出者？故其布之爲制，則井牧始於黃帝，而九夫經畫之制建；弼服昉於唐堯，而九畿分國之制詳；象刑儆於舜，而五刑麗民之制具；貢賦創於夏，而典式法則之制行；官刑肇於商，而廢置誅賞之制立，唯其義之精也。朱子曰：「《周官》徧布周密，乃周公運用天理爛熟之書。」誠哉是言也！柰經秦火之後，散逸無存。自漢除挾書之律，衆書往往頗出，諸儒執經競進，《周禮》遂列於九經矣。維時顓門持業者，非其師說不從；各立門戶者，互相詆毀求勝。或索諸儀章度數之間，或泥乎文字訓詁之末，甚至援引曲說，竊取聖人之迹而强附之。昔人謂「秦人焚經而經存，諸儒窮經而經絕」，良有以也。故在劉歆信其爲是，則以爲周公致太平之迹；林孝存排其爲非，則以爲戰國陰謀之書；王安石作《周官義》，而謂成周理財之書，則見以爲偏；漢武帝得《周官》五篇，
translation_en:
…from which its laws derived? Therefore, when it was set forth as a system of institutions: the well-field and pasturage divisions began with the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黃帝), and thus the system of laying out boundaries for nine-husbandman plots was established; the assisting domains originated with Yao of Tang (Tang Yao 唐堯), and thus the system of dividing the realm into nine domains was elaborated; symbolic punishments were used as warnings by Shun 舜, and thus the system of applying the five punishments to the populace was completed; tribute and taxes were initiated in the Xia 夏 dynasty, and thus the system of statutory models and fiscal regulations was put into practice; official punishments commenced in the Shang 商 dynasty, and thus the system of dismissal, appointment, execution, and reward was instituted—all solely because its underlying principles were so refined. Master Zhu (Zhuzi 朱子, Zhu Xi 朱熹) said: "The Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan 周官) is comprehensive and meticulous; it is a book in which the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公) applied the principles of Heaven with complete mastery." How true are these words!

Yet after suffering the fires of Qin 秦, it was scattered and lost, with nothing remaining. Once the Han 漢 repealed the statute against possessing books, the various texts gradually reappeared in considerable numbers. Scholars grasped the classics and vied to advance them, and the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli 周禮) was consequently ranked among the Nine Classics. At that time, specialists who clung to their own traditions refused to follow anything other than their masters' explanations, while those who established rival schools slandered one another in pursuit of victory. Some sought meaning merely among ceremonial emblems and numerical measures, while others were bogged down in the trivialities of textual glosses and philology; some even cited convoluted theories, appropriating the traces of the sages and forcibly attaching their own ideas to them. Truly there was good reason for the ancients to say, "When the men of Qin burned the classics, the classics survived; when the scholars exhaustively analyzed the classics, the classics were destroyed."

Thus, because Liu Xin 劉歆 believed it to be authentic, he regarded it as the trace of how the Duke of Zhou achieved Great Peace; because Lin Xiaocun 林孝存 (Lin Shuo 林碩) rejected it as spurious, he regarded it as a book of Warring States intrigues; when Wang Anshi 王安石 composed the Meaning of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan yi 周官義) and called it a book on fiscal administration from the flourishing Zhou, his view was considered biased; and when Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wudi 漢武帝) obtained the five sections of the Offices of Zhou…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
而謂瀆亂不經之書則見以爲謬是非紛
錯準裁靡定其曷能運通方之至理而獨
觀乎昭曠之道哉蓋自河間購以千金而
上之祕府可謂能表章矣然工匠器械何
取於考工遂使其書不信於天下故世儒
譏之曰纍周禮者劉德也其有激之言乎
劉歆校理祕書而著之錄略可謂能發明
矣然六幹五均託名於泉府遂使其義不
明於天下胡氏父子曰周禮是王莽令劉
===
歆撰出其排斥之論乎近世說周禮者非
一人也宋淳熙中俞廷椿謂司空之篇實
襍出于五官之屬而著復古編王次點作
周官補遺元泰定中丘葵乃參訂二家之
說以爲成書吳澄則謂冬官未嘗亡而地
官之文實亡又欲以遂人入司空此非其
獨見與近世用周禮者非一人也王莽託
五均以立錢府官天下騷動是爲假用蘇
綽取以輔宇文周六官定而民叛是爲輕
punctuated: 而謂瀆亂不經之書，則見以爲謬。是非紛錯，準裁靡定，其曷能運通方之至理，而獨觀乎昭曠之道哉？蓋自河間購以千金，而上之祕府，可謂能表章矣；然工匠器械何取於《考工》，遂使其書不信於天下。故世儒譏之曰：「纍《周禮》者，劉德也。」其有激之言乎？劉歆校理祕書，而著之《錄》《略》，可謂能發明矣；然六幹五均託名於泉府，遂使其義不明於天下。胡氏父子曰：「《周禮》是王莽令劉歆撰出。」其排斥之論乎？近世說《周禮》者非一人也：宋淳熙中，俞廷椿謂司空之篇實襍出于五官之屬，而著《復古編》；王次點作《周官補遺》；元泰定中，丘葵乃參訂二家之說以爲成書；吳澄則謂《冬官》未嘗亡，而《地官》之文實亡，又欲以遂人入司空。此非其獨見與？近世用《周禮》者非一人也：王莽託五均以立錢府官，天下騷動，是爲假用；蘇綽取以輔宇文周，六官定而民叛，是爲輕
translation_en: …and called it a profane, disorderly, and uncanonical book, which shows a mistaken view. With judgments of right and wrong so confused and standards of evaluation unsettled, how can one wield the supreme principle of comprehensive understanding and behold alone the bright and spacious Way? Ever since Prince Xian of Hejian (Liu De 劉德) purchased the missing section for a thousand pieces of gold and presented it to the Imperial Library, he could well be said to have brought the work to prominence. Yet what was the point of taking artisans and implements from the Record of Trades (Kaogong ji 考工記) to fill the gap, thereby causing the book to be distrusted throughout the realm? Thus scholars of later generations criticized him, saying: "The one who marred the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli 周禮) was Liu De." Was this not a remark born of indignation? Liu Xin 劉歆 collated the imperial collection and recorded the text in his bibliographical summaries (the Qilüe 七略), so he could well be said to have elucidated it. Yet because the policies of the Six Monopolies (liugan 六幹) and Five Equalizations (wujun 五均) borrowed the name of its Treasury of Currency (Quanfu 泉府), the true meaning of the book became obscured throughout the realm. Father and son of the Hu 胡 clan (Hu Anguo 胡安國 and Hu Hong 胡宏) said: "The Rites of Zhou was fabricated by Liu Xin at Wang Mang's 王莽 command." Was this not an argument aimed at rejecting it? In more recent times, those who have expounded the Rites of Zhou have not been just one person. During the Chunxi era (1174–1189) of the Song, Yu Tingchun 俞廷椿 argued that the section on the Minister of Works (Sikong 司空) was in fact scattered and mixed among the subordinates of the other five offices, and he composed the Compilation for Restoring Antiquity (Fugu bian 復古編). Wang Cidian 王次點 wrote the Supplement to the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan buyi 周官補遺). During the Taiding era (1324–1328) of the Yuan, Qiu Kui 丘葵 collated and revised the theories of those two scholars to form a complete work. Wu Cheng 吳澄, for his part, maintained that the "Offices of Winter" (Dongguan 冬官) had never been lost whereas the text of the "Offices of Earth" (Diguan 地官) was actually lost, and he further wished to transfer the Grandee of the Outlying Districts (Suiren 遂人) into the office of the Minister of Works. Were these not their own idiosyncratic views? In recent eras, those who have applied the Rites of Zhou in governance have also not been just one person. Wang Mang used the pretext of the Five Equalizations to establish the offices of the Treasury of Coinage (Qianfu 錢府), throwing the realm into turmoil; this was a fraudulent application of it. Su Chuo 蘇綽 drew upon it to assist the Yuwen 宇文 regime of the Northern Zhou; the Six Offices were established, yet the people rebelled; this was a rash…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
用王安石之用周官師心妬眞黨同伐異
新法之行無異公卿以下至於庶人咸指
湯矣乃妄引聖經敝精神於訓詁而卒以
其術誤天下此非其尤甚歟至於設官不
與王制合封建不與孟子合緣王制所說
朝聘或以爲文襄時事去籍之後煨燼之
餘中間互相牴牾不無焉先儒謂其間必
有末世增入者良有見矣夫說周禮者旣
如此用周禮者又如此然則聖人之道終
不可明且行乎嗚呼聖人經世之書聖人
之心法爲之也聖人以其精義妙道而著
之爲大經大法其藝極不專于名數其議
制不局于比詳甚明矣譚之者庸可剽其
外郛而昧其內竅用之者庸可摹其緐指
而遺其弘猷哉是故六典九賦十二物之
教保息六之養以至須比灋經土地之類
此其彰彰大者也其間掌炭掌蜃硩蔟赤
犮與夫蟈氏焚牡蘜壺涿氏牡橭午之類
punctuated: 用。王安石之用《周官》，師心妬眞，黨同伐異，新法之行，無異公卿以下至於庶人咸指湯矣，乃妄引聖經，敝精神於訓詁，而卒以其術誤天下，此非其尤甚歟？至於設官不與《王制》合，封建不與《孟子》合，緣《王制》所說朝聘，或以爲文、襄時事，去籍之後，煨燼之餘，中間互相牴牾，不無焉。先儒謂其間必有末世增入者，良有見矣。夫說《周禮》者旣如此，用《周禮》者又如此，然則聖人之道終不可明且行乎？嗚呼！聖人經世之書，聖人之心法爲之也。聖人以其精義妙道，而著之爲大經大法，其藝極不專于名數，其議制不局于比詳，甚明矣。譚之者庸可剽其外郛而昧其內竅，用之者庸可摹其緐指而遺其弘猷哉？是故六典、九賦、十二物之教，保息六之養，以至須比灋、經土地之類，此其彰彰大者也；其間掌炭、掌蜃、硩蔟、赤犮，與夫蟈氏焚牡蘜、壺涿氏牡橭午之類，
translation_en:
… application. As for Wang Anshi’s 王安石 application of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), he relied on his own willful mind and was jealous of the truth, forming cliques with the like-minded and attacking dissenters. When his New Policies were put into effect, it was no different from everyone—from grandees and ministers down to the common people—all pointing at boiling water [in dread, or: pointing in complaint (?)]; yet he rashly cited the sacred Classic, exhausting his mental energy on exegetical glosses (Specifically, his *New Meanings of the Three Classics*), and in the end misled the empire with his statecraft. Was this not the most extreme case of all?

As for the fact that its establishment of offices does not accord with the "Royal Regulations" (Wangzhi) and its enfeoffment system does not accord with the Mencius (Mengzi): because the court audiences and diplomatic missions described in the "Royal Regulations" are considered by some to be affairs from the era of Dukes Wen and Xiang of Jin, after the feudal lords removed the records and among the remnants of the秦 fires, mutual contradictions among the texts are not absent. Former Confucian scholars said that among them there must be interpolations added in a later age, which is truly an insightful view.

Now, if those who explicate the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) are already like this, and those who apply the Rites of Zhou are also like this, then can the Way of the Sages ultimately neither be elucidated nor put into practice? Alas! The book by which the Sages ordered the world was created out of the Sages' method of the mind (xinfa). That the Sages took their subtle meanings and marvelous Way and set them forth as great statutes and grand laws—whose ultimate standard does not lie solely in titles and numbers, and whose deliberated institutions are not confined to minute details—is very clear indeed. How could those who discuss it merely plagiarize its outer ramparts while remaining blind to its inner essentials, and how could those who apply it merely imitate its intricate minutiae while neglecting its grand plan?

Therefore, the teachings of the six administrative statutes (liudian), the nine revenues (jiufu), and the twelve categories of things, the nurturing of the six measures for preserving and fostering the people (baoxi), all the way to the promulgation of the laws of neighborhood groupings [?] (bifa) and the surveying and division of lands—these are its manifestly great aspects. Meanwhile, such offices within it as the Charcoal Supervisors (Zhangtan), the Clam-ash Supervisors (Zhangshen), the Nest-Destroyers (Zhecu), and the Red-Pest-Exterminators (Chiba), along with such matters as the Frog-Exterminators (Guoshi) burning male chrysanthemum stalks and the Water-Pest-Exterminators (Huzhuoshi) driving away water spirits with rods of fruitless elm intersected like a cross…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
此其區區細者也河間獻王之初得此書
也典則煥乎可宗矣乃柞氏銜枚之疑其
隸司甲都則之闕其文渠豈慮不及此而
不敢以聰明加焉其冬官亡而得考工記
附補之也文采爛然可覩矣然知創巧述
之語嘉量寧侯之銘因文附見不敢爲五
官溷焉其猶有夏五郭公之思乎初安石
使還上書仁宗大要謂法先王之政當法
其意亹亹有稽及行新法何其悖所聞也
其均輸青苗之法往往捃摭周禮而附會
之比徵斂于民又何與周公意異也夫周
公敷大德于天下厚生正德利用備是矣
然且嬔其宮室而驩愉之時其讀法而諄
誨之計其時之民不在於田廬則在族師
閭胥之庭不治稼穡則聞孝弟婣睦之敎
民享樂利久矣復念民恐有不足於貿遷
者于是有司市辨物及國服爲息之法焉
惠民而不盡其財者如此是周公之理財
punctuated: 此其區區細者也。河間獻王之初得此書也，典則煥乎可宗矣；乃柞氏、銜枚之疑其隸，司甲、都則之闕其文，渠豈慮不及此，而不敢以聰明加焉？其冬官亡而得《考工記》附補之也，文采爛然可覩矣；然「知創巧述」之語、嘉量寧侯之銘，因文附見，不敢爲五官溷焉，其猶有「夏五」、「郭公」之思乎？初，安石使還，上書仁宗，大要謂「法先王之政，當法其意」，亹亹有稽；及行新法，何其悖所聞也！其均輸、青苗之法，往往捃摭《周禮》而附會之，比徵斂于民，又何與周公意異也！夫周公敷大德于天下，厚生、正德、利用備是矣。然且嬔其宮室而驩愉之，時其讀法而諄誨之；計其時之民，不在於田廬，則在族師、閭胥之庭；不治稼穡，則聞孝弟、婣睦之敎。民享樂利久矣，復念民恐有不足於貿遷者，于是有司市辨物及「國服爲息」之法焉。惠民而不盡其財者如此，是周公之理財，
translation_en: …these are its trivial minutiae. When Prince Xian of Hejian (Hejian Xianwang 河間獻王) first acquired this book, its statutes and models were resplendent and worthy of reverence. Yet where the affiliation of the Land-clearing Official (Zeshi 柞氏) and the Gag-bit Official (Xianmei 銜枚) was doubtful, and where the text for the Director of Armor (Sijia 司甲) and the Capital Regulations (Duze 都則) was missing, how could it be that his thoughts failed to reach these points? Rather, he did not dare impose his own cleverness upon them. When the "Winter Offices" (Dongguan 冬官) was lost and the Record of Trades (Kaogong ji 考工記) was obtained and appended to supplement it, its literary brilliance was resplendent to behold. Yet sayings such as "the wise create and the skillful transmit," and the inscriptions on the standard measure (jialiang 嘉量) and the target of peace (ninghou 寧侯), were appended by virtue of the text without daring to confound them with the Five Offices—did this not preserve the spirit of leaving lacunae like "fifth month of summer" (Xia wu 夏五) and "Lord of Guo" (Guo gong 郭公) in the Spring and Autumn Annals? Earlier, when Wang Anshi 王安石 returned from a mission and submitted a memorial to Emperor Renzong 仁宗, his main point was that "in modeling oneself on the governance of the former kings, one ought to model oneself on their intent"—an argument tireless and well-grounded. Yet when he implemented his New Policies, how utterly he contradicted what he had once professed! For his Price Equalization and Transport (junshu 均輸) and Green Sprouts (qingmiao 青苗) measures, he repeatedly plucked phrases from the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli 周禮) and strained to force a connection; yet when it came to levying exactions upon the people, how different this was from the intent of the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公)! Now, the Duke of Zhou spread great virtue throughout the realm, and the enrichment of livelihoods, rectification of virtue, and facilitation of utility were all complete therein. Moreover, he paired their dwellings [?] and brought them joy, and set regular times for reading the laws to instruct them earnestly. Reckoning the people of that age, if they were not in their field huts, they were in the courtyards of the Clan Preceptors (zushi 族師) and Neighborhood Scribes (lüxu 閭胥); if they were not tending to sowing and reaping, they were hearing teachings of filial piety, fraternal duty, affinity, and harmony. After the people had long enjoyed happiness and benefit, he further reflected with concern that the people might suffer insufficiencies in trade and exchange, and thereupon instituted the methods whereby the Market Director (Sishi 司市) distinguished goods and interest was reckoned according to the state's service-rates ("guofu wei xi" 國服爲息). Such was his way of benefiting the people without exhausting their wealth; thus, the Duke of Zhou's management of finances…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
乃導利而布之上下也安石于周禮所以
爲民極者將蔑其官而棄其制唯藉口於
國服爲息一言以便其掊剋富國之計內
之則設制置三司條例司外之則歸利權
於發運使心計者日夜持籌講畫突梯者
分行馳逐營幹即桑弘羊孔僅輩筭利析
秋毫者不苛于此矣以此做周禮致太平
何異于坐井闚天見一班而以爲全豹與
上之誤天子下之誤蒼生甚矣安石之謬
===
也故先正有言曰制其產使無不均詳其
教使無不學文武周公之大意也法古者
取其大意所屬而行之奚患于財之不足
哉不治其本而以理財爲先此周官所棄
也是故房琯以車戰致敗議者罪琯可也
罪車戰不可也安石以周禮貽毒議者罪
安石可也罪周禮不可也善夫朱子之言
曰周禮其間細碎處雖可疑其大體直非
聖人做不得而其讀孟子經界章亦曰孟
punctuated: 乃導利而布之上下也。安石于《周禮》所以爲民極者，將蔑其官而棄其制，唯藉口於「國服爲息」一言，以便其掊剋富國之計。內之則設制置三司條例司，外之則歸利權於發運使。心計者日夜持籌講畫，突梯者分行馳逐營幹，即桑弘羊、孔僅輩筭利析秋毫者，不苛于此矣。以此做《周禮》致太平，何異于坐井闚天，見一班而以爲全豹與？上之誤天子，下之誤蒼生，甚矣，安石之謬也！故先正有言曰：「制其產使無不均，詳其教使無不學，文、武、周公之大意也。法古者，取其大意所屬而行之，奚患于財之不足哉？」不治其本，而以理財爲先，此周官所棄也。是故房琯以車戰致敗，議者罪琯可也，罪車戰不可也；安石以《周禮》貽毒，議者罪安石可也，罪《周禮》不可也。善夫！朱子之言曰：「《周禮》其間細碎處雖可疑，其大體直非聖人做不得。」而其讀《孟子》經界章亦曰：「孟
translation_en:
…was to guide benefits and distribute them between those above and those below. As for that in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) which established the supreme standard for the people, [Wang] Anshi disdained its offices and discarded its institutions, using only the single phrase "taking the state's prescribed service as interest" as a pretext to facilitate his schemes of extortion and enriching the state. At court, he established the Finance Planning Commission (Zhizhi sansi tiaoli si); in the provinces, he concentrated fiscal authority in the hands of the Transport Commissioners (Fayun shi). Scheming calculators held their tally sticks day and night to deliberate and plan, while slick opportunists fanned out in all directions to race after profit and manage affairs. Even men like Sang Hongyang and Kong Jin, who calculated profits down to the tip of an autumn hair, were no more harsh than this! To act upon the Rites of Zhou in this manner to bring about Grand Tranquility—how is it any different from sitting in a well to peer at the sky, or seeing a single spot and taking it for the whole leopard? Above, he misled the Son of Heaven; below, he harmed the common people. Extreme indeed was Anshi's folly!

Therefore, a former worthy had a saying: "To regulate their livelihood so that none suffer inequality, and to elaborate their instruction so that none go untaught—this was the grand intention of Kings Wen and Wu and the Duke of Zhou. Those who model themselves on antiquity should grasp where this grand intention lies and put it into practice; what worry would there be over an insufficiency of wealth?" Not attending to the root while making fiscal administration the priority—this is what the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) rejected. For this reason, when Fang Guan suffered defeat by using chariot warfare, for critics to blame Guan is permissible, but to blame chariot warfare is not; when Anshi bequeathed a poison by using the Rites of Zhou, for critics to blame Anshi is permissible, but to blame the Rites of Zhou is not. Well spoken indeed were the words of Master Zhu [Xi]: "Although the minute details within the Rites of Zhou may be open to doubt, its grand structure truly could not have been made by anyone other than a sage." And when reading the chapter on defining boundaries in the Mencius (Mengzi), he also said: "Mencius's…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
子之學識其大若朱子者可謂洞見周公
之大者乎讀周禮者亦惟得其大以會通
其意得其意以妙用其法則周禮固可維
持萬世無弊也愚于是竊有望焉
第三問
何偉
同考試官教諭湯　批〔論兩漢士風各得忠厚正直一偏而處之中行此確論也宜錄之〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔論士風而歸重於陶鑄世〕
===
考試官教諭楊　批〔議論正大有裨風教之說誠致行非漫言者〕
士君子所以受天下之大者存乎量所以
荷天下之艱者存乎節夫士之有量如山
之能藏疾也如海之能納汙也士之有節
如劒之利而耀鋩也如弓之勁而及遠也
量匪徒也泰山惟高而後土壤藏焉滄海
惟深而後細流納焉苟一於茹納而失之
薄植則汎汎祇足以爲汙節匪徒也莫邪
punctuated:
子之學，識其大。」若朱子者，可謂洞見周公之大者乎！讀《周禮》者，亦惟得其大以會通其意，得其意以妙用其法，則《周禮》固可維持萬世無弊也。愚于是竊有望焉。
第三問
何偉
同考試官教諭湯　批〔論兩漢士風，各得忠厚、正直一偏，而處之中行，此確論也，宜錄之。〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔論士風而歸重於陶鑄世。〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔議論正大，有裨風教之說，誠致行非漫言者。〕
士君子所以受天下之大者存乎量，所以荷天下之艱者存乎節。夫士之有量，如山之能藏疾也，如海之能納汙也；士之有節，如劒之利而耀鋩也，如弓之勁而及遠也。量匪徒也，泰山惟高，而後土壤藏焉；滄海惟深，而後細流納焉。苟一於茹納而失之薄植，則汎汎祇足以爲汙。節匪徒也，莫邪
translation_en:
… [Meng]zi's learning recognized the great fundamentals." Someone like Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) may truly be said to have had a penetrating insight into the great fundamentals of the Duke of Zhou! If those who read the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli 周禮) likewise grasp only its great fundamentals in order to comprehend its intent as a whole, and grasp its intent in order to skillfully apply its methods, then the Rites of Zhou can surely be maintained for ten thousand generations without abuse. In this, I privately place my hopes.

Question Three
He Wei 何偉
Associate Examiner, Instructor Tang 湯, comments: [He discusses the ethos of literati in the Former and Later Han, showing how each attained a one-sided aspect of either loyal magnanimity or upright rectitude, while he situates himself in the balanced mean. This is a sound discourse; it should be recorded.]
Examiner, Instructor Dai 戴, comments: [He discusses the ethos of literati and places the ultimate emphasis on molding the age [?].]
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊, comments: [His argument is upright and grand, a doctrine beneficial to moral instruction—truly something that can be put into practice and not mere empty talk.]

Whereby a scholar-gentleman accommodates the greatness of the world lies in his capacity (liang 量); whereby he shoulders the difficulties of the world lies in his integrity (jie 節). Now, a scholar's possessing capacity is like a mountain's ability to shelter imperfections, and like the sea's ability to take in mire; a scholar's possessing integrity is like a sword's being sharp and flashing its point, and like a bow's being strong and reaching afar. Capacity does not stand alone: Mount Tai is first high, and only then is earth and soil sheltered therein; the vast sea is first deep, and only then are trickling streams taken in therein. If one is solely devoted to taking everything in while failing through shallow grounding, then drifting about aimlessly will only suffice to make one sullied. Integrity does not stand alone: the blade of the Moye 莫邪 sword…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
之鋒百鍊而後試焉虞機之張省括而後
釋焉茍一於剛勁而失之淺衷則嶢嶢適
所以爲缺故量合於節斯其量不淆而受
大者有其地節出於量斯其節不激而荷
艱者有其基明於此義然後可以觀形察
質而定天下士矣執事發策以兩漢習尚
爲問得非以奧㴱佔俾有閱覽而高議者
乎愚非其人也請得述其涯略以對夫光
岳之氣代有厚薄風會之流世有升降人
===
生其間習焉而得其性之所近故其剛柔
淺深不可以一律齊也惟聖人秉淳粹之
美而學體天地之純其制行隨時變易同
歸於道皆可以敎後世自中庸以下則沉
潛高明之不能自克箕子固以唏之況乎
叔季之世漸漬於失敎被服於成俗者哉
昔虞夏殷周之盛九官相讓三事推賢和
之至也而不以度量名弼直欽於四鄰正
直聞於四國節甚偉也而不以氣節名蓋
punctuated:
之鋒，百鍊而後試焉；虞機之張，省括而後釋焉。茍一於剛勁而失之淺衷，則嶢嶢適所以爲缺。故量合於節，斯其量不淆，而受大者有其地；節出於量，斯其節不激，而荷艱者有其基。明於此義，然後可以觀形察質，而定天下士矣。

執事發策，以兩漢習尚爲問，得非以奧㴱佔俾，有閱覽而高議者乎？愚非其人也，請得述其涯略以對。

夫光岳之氣，代有厚薄；風會之流，世有升降。人生其間，習焉而得其性之所近，故其剛柔淺深，不可以一律齊也。惟聖人秉淳粹之美，而學體天地之純，其制行隨時變易，同歸於道，皆可以敎後世。自中庸以下，則沉潛高明之不能自克，箕子固以唏之，況乎叔季之世，漸漬於失敎，被服於成俗者哉！昔虞、夏、殷、周之盛，九官相讓，三事推賢，和之至也，而不以度量名；弼直欽於四鄰，正直聞於四國，節甚偉也，而不以氣節名。蓋
translation_en:
…the edge [of the Moye sword] is tested only after being tempered a hundred times; the drawn crossbow of the forester is released only after inspecting the nock. If one is solely bent on unyielding strength and errs by being shallow at heart, then being towering and rigid is precisely what causes one to break. Therefore, when magnanimity is joined with integrity, that magnanimity does not become muddled, and he who takes on great responsibilities has the capacity for it; when integrity arises from magnanimity, that integrity does not become extreme, and he who shoulders difficulties has a foundation for it. Only when one understands this principle can one observe outward appearances, examine inner substance, and evaluate the scholars of the world.

Your Excellency has posed a policy question asking about the customs and ethos of the Two Han dynasties; could it not be that you seek someone of profound scholarship who is widely read and capable of lofty discourse? Though I, foolish as I am, am not such a person, allow me to outline the general points in reply.

Now, the vital energy of the cosmos and great mountains is thicker or thinner from age to age; the currents of custom and circumstance rise and fall from generation to generation. People born into their midst become habituated to them and develop according to what is closest to their nature; thus their firmness or softness, shallowness or depth, cannot be made uniform by a single rule. Only the sages possess pure and unadulterated excellence and through learning embody the perfection of Heaven and Earth; their conduct adapts to changing times yet returns alike to the Way, and all of it can serve to instruct later generations. Below the level of the Mean, however, the reserved and the lofty-minded are unable to overcome their own biases—something over which Jizi already sighed—how much more so in degenerate later ages, when people are steeped in failed instruction and clothed in established customs! In the flourishing eras of Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou in antiquity, the Nine Offices yielded to one another and the Three Ministers promoted the worthy: this was the ultimate in harmony, yet they were not famed for "magnanimity." Assisting uprightness was revered by the four neighboring associates, and rectitude was renowned throughout the four quarters of the realm: this was extraordinary integrity, yet they were not famed for "moral integrity." For indeed,…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
太和渾龐之氣融液於當時宇宙間未雕
未琢故人稟全賦世多全才不可以偏長
目也代之衰也眞淳漓而大道隱學士大
夫言風俗近古者蓋推兩漢云西漢自高
祖滌煩苛孝文脩玄默一時開國論議務
破觚爲圜斲雕爲朴故士專以長厚相訐
慕時則有見人有過掩匿覆蓋而斥文言
刻深者曹參氏之以淸淨蒙譽也有郎官
有譴常蒙其罪有功常讓他將者衞綰之
以醇謹得幸也買金償同舍爲官掩吏迹
非直不疑之稱爲長者乎爲吏不案人官
屬不敢欺非張叔之號爲愛人乎之數子
者類以德量名若自託於忠厚矣然和光
同塵之習勝而彈冠振衣之風微君子譏
其近於佞則所少者正直也東漢自世祖
首褒勸顯宗尚察慧赫然中興氣象雲蒸
飇馳嚮風隨流故士爭以行誼相頡頏時
則有少厲淸節而贓汙解印綬者范孟博
punctuated: 太和渾龐之氣，融液於當時宇宙間，未雕未琢，故人稟全賦，世多全才，不可以偏長目也。代之衰也，眞淳漓而大道隱。學士大夫言風俗近古者，蓋推兩漢云。西漢自高祖滌煩苛，孝文脩玄默，一時開國論議，務破觚爲圜，斲雕爲朴，故士專以長厚相訐慕。時則有見人有過，掩匿覆蓋，而斥文言刻深者，曹參氏之以淸淨蒙譽也；有郎官有譴，常蒙其罪，有功常讓他將者，衞綰之以醇謹得幸也；買金償同舍，爲官掩吏迹，非直不疑之稱爲長者乎？爲吏不案人，官屬不敢欺，非張叔之號爲愛人乎？之數子者，類以德量名，若自託於忠厚矣。然和光同塵之習勝，而彈冠振衣之風微，君子譏其近於佞，則所少者正直也。東漢自世祖首褒勸，顯宗尚察慧，赫然中興，氣象雲蒸飇馳，嚮風隨流，故士爭以行誼相頡頏。時則有少厲淸節，而贓汙解印綬者，范孟博
translation_en:
… the vital breath of supreme harmony and vast wholeness pervaded the cosmos at that time, uncarved and unpolished. Therefore, people were endowed with complete natures, and the age abounded with all-around talents who could not be categorized merely by a single specialty. When later ages declined, true purity thinned out and the Great Way was obscured. When scholar-officials speak of customs that approached antiquity, they generally praise the two Han dynasties.

In the Western Han, after Emperor Gaozu swept away vexatious and harsh laws and Emperor Xiaowen cultivated mysterious quietude, the discussions at the founding of the dynasty strove to round off sharp corners and pare away ornamentation in favor of simplicity. Thus, scholars single-mindedly admired [?] one another for magnanimity and generosity. At that time, there was one who, upon seeing others' faults, concealed and covered them up, while dismissing those whose written words were harsh and severe—such was Cao Can 曹參, who won praise through tranquil non-interference. There was one who, when Court Gentlemen were reprimanded, always took the blame upon himself, and when there was merit, always yielded it to other generals—such was Wei Wan 衞綰, who gained imperial favor through pure caution. Buying gold to repay a roommate, and as an official covering up the tracks of subordinate clerks—was this not how Zhi Buyi 直不疑 came to be called a man of generous virtue? Serving as an official without prosecuting people, yet his subordinates did not dare to deceive him—was this not how Zhang Shu 張叔 came to be known for loving others? These several gentlemen were all renowned for their virtuous capacity, as if entrusting themselves to loyalty and generosity. Yet when the habit of softening one's glare and mingling with the dust prevailed, and the spirit of dusting off one's cap and shaking out one's robes grew faint, superior men criticized them for bordering on flattery; what they lacked was uprightness.

In the Eastern Han, after Emperor Shizu first promoted praise and encouragement, and Emperor Xianzong esteemed perceptive acumen, in the glorious dynastic revival the atmosphere rose like clouds and raced like a whirlwind. Swept along by the trend, scholars vied with one another in righteous conduct. At that time, there was one who honed pure integrity from youth, and at whose approach corrupt officials untied their seal-ribbons and fled—such was Fan Mengbo 范孟博 [Fan Pang 范滂]…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
之慷慨澄清也有聲名自高而士號爲登
龍門者李元禮之模楷天下也不接賓客
一榻常懸者非陳仲舉之不畏强禦乎曉
譬曲直爭者無怨非陳太丘之表正鄉閭
乎之數子者類以氣節名若自負於正直
矣然洗垢索瘢之俗熾而磨稜合罅之義
疎君子譏其過於激則所少者忠厚也當
其時士固有特立獨行不苟同於俗者吾
於武帝之朝得一汲長孺焉招不來麾不
===
去面折公孫之飾詐斥張湯以刀筆詬譖
一士足以寢淮南之謀而當社稷臣之許
者其誠頽波中之砥柱哉吾於安帝之朝
得一黄叔度焉澄不清撓不濁倨傲者見
之正容鄙吝者聞之潛消汪汪千頃足以
陋奉高汎濫之器而飄然於汙世矰繳之
外者其誠鴻冥中之鳳凰哉嘗因是而反
覆兩漢之國勢士風始未嘗不崇大雅後
稍陵夷也西京之俗重朴茂猶有大獎不
punctuated: 之慷慨澄清也；有聲名自高而士號爲登龍門者，李元禮之模楷天下也；不接賓客、一榻常懸者，非陳仲舉之不畏强禦乎？曉譬曲直、爭者無怨，非陳太丘之表正鄉閭乎？之數子者，類以氣節名，若自負於正直矣。然洗垢索瘢之俗熾，而磨稜合罅之義疎，君子譏其過於激，則所少者忠厚也。當其時，士固有特立獨行，不苟同於俗者。吾於武帝之朝得一汲長孺焉：招不來，麾不去，面折公孫之飾詐，斥張湯以刀筆，詬譖一士，足以寢淮南之謀，而當社稷臣之許者，其誠頽波中之砥柱哉！吾於安帝之朝得一黄叔度焉：澄不清，撓不濁，倨傲者見之正容，鄙吝者聞之潛消，汪汪千頃，足以陋奉高汎濫之器，而飄然於汙世矰繳之外者，其誠鴻冥中之鳳凰哉！嘗因是而反覆兩漢之國勢士風，始未嘗不崇大雅，後稍陵夷也。西京之俗重朴茂，猶有大獎不
translation_en:
…impassioned aspiration to purify the realm; there was one who held his reputation lofty, such that scholars called being received by him "ascending the Dragon Gate"—this was Li Yuanli 李元禮 (Li Ying 李膺) serving as a paragon for the empire; as for he who did not receive guests save for a single couch kept suspended, was this not Chen Zhongju 陳仲舉 (Chen Fan 陳蕃), who did not fear powerful and overbearing men? And as for he who explained right and wrong so clearly that disputants harbored no resentment, was this not Chen Taiqiu 陳太丘 (Chen Shi 陳寔), who set an upright example for his local community? These several gentlemen were all generally renowned for their moral courage and integrity, as though priding themselves on uprightness. Yet when the custom of scrubbing away dirt to search for scars grew熾 rampant, and the principle of smoothing sharp edges and mending rifts grew distant, superior men criticized them for being overly extreme; thus, what they lacked was magnanimous厚道 kindness (zhonghou).

At those times, there were indeed scholars who stood independent and walked alone, refusing to carelessly conform to vulgar convention. In the court of Emperor Wu 武帝, I find one Ji Changru 汲長孺 (Ji黯 Ji An): summoned, he would not come; waved away, he would not leave; to his face he rebuked Gongsun 公孫 (Gongsun Hong 公孫弘) for his affected deceit, and he denounced Zhang Tang 張湯 as a mere pettifogging scribe; though reviled and slandered [?], this single scholar sufficed to put an end to the rebellion plotted by Huainan 淮南 and to merit praise as a "minister of the altars of soil and grain"—truly, was he not a bedrock pillar amidst a collapsing tide! In the court of Emperor An 安帝, I find one Huang Shudu 黄叔度 (Huang Xian 黃憲): clarify him and he does not become clearer, stir him and he does not grow turbid; the arrogant, upon seeing him, composed their countenances, while the mean and stingy, upon hearing of him, saw their baseness quietly melt away; vast and deep like a thousand acres of water, he sufficed to make Fenggao's 奉高 (Yuan Lang 袁閬) overflowing vessel seem narrow, soaring freely beyond the tethered arrows of a sullied world—truly, was he not a phoenix amidst the high-flying wild geese in the distant heavens!

Having on this account repeatedly reflected upon the national momentum and the ethos of the literati in the Two Han dynasties, in the beginning they never failed to revere great elegance, though later this gradually declined. The customs of the Western Capital (Western Han) valued unadorned substance, still retaining the sense of "great sacrificial broth [? written 大獎 for 大羹] is unseasoned…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
和大圭不琢之意足以培國之元氣其弊
也習爲卑論儕俗而博榮名雖以孔光劉
歆之通經宿儒猶甘心僭僞之羽翼而不
耻則積弱易廢之勢也東京之俗貴高潔
猶之虎豹在山鵰鶚在霄足以張國之神
氣其弊也務爲噓枯吹生而眛幾先至於
俊厨顧及之號興歘然扞當世之文罔而
不悔則過剛易折之勢也元始之季舉國
若狂坐視乎大厦之顛熹平之後名義凜
===
然猶足懾夫問鼎之雄識者殆不無軒輊
於其中矣第律諸周行則槩乎未聞道耳
楊中立有言西漢之士喜功名而不務奇
節東漢之士貴節義而不通時變皆爲世
變所移而眛夫中行其於二代人物之權
衡審矣今世之命爲士者動稱引隆古而
卑視近代迨叓考其操行乃有大謬不然
者以爲儒也則又疑於枝媚以爲矯也則
復類於鉤進葢俗之漸人波流風靡視兩
punctuated: 和大圭不琢之意，足以培國之元氣。其弊也，習爲卑論儕俗以博榮名，雖以孔光、劉歆之通經宿儒，猶甘心僭僞之羽翼而不耻，則積弱易廢之勢也。東京之俗貴高潔，猶之虎豹在山、鵰鶚在霄，足以張國之神氣。其弊也，務爲噓枯吹生而眛幾先，至於俊、厨、顧、及之號興，歘然扞當世之文罔而不悔，則過剛易折之勢也。元始之季，舉國若狂，坐視乎大厦之顛；熹平之後，名義凜然，猶足懾夫問鼎之雄。識者殆不無軒輊於其中矣，第律諸周行，則槩乎未聞道耳。楊中立有言：「西漢之士，喜功名而不務奇節；東漢之士，貴節義而不通時變。皆爲世變所移，而眛夫中行。」其於二代人物之權衡審矣。今世之命爲士者，動稱引隆古而卑視近代，迨叓考其操行，乃有大謬不然者。以爲儒也，則又疑於枝媚；以爲矯也，則復類於鉤進。葢俗之漸人，波流風靡，視兩…
translation_en: …the idea of the sacrificial broth left unseasoned [reading 大獎 as 大羹] and the great jade tablet left uncarved, which was sufficient to nourish the vital energy of the state. Its defect, however, was that men grew accustomed to lowly discourse and conforming to the vulgar crowd in order to win glorious reputation. Even venerable scholars thoroughly versed in the Classics like Kong Guang 孔光 and Liu Xin 劉歆 willingly served as the wings of a usurper without shame—such was the tendency of accumulated weakness easily leading to collapse. The ethos of the Eastern Capital prized lofty purity, like tigers and leopards in the mountains or eagles and ospreys in the skies, which was sufficient to expand the spiritual vigor of the state. Its defect, however, was that men strove to praise or disparage others—"breathing life into the withered and blowing frost on the living"—while remaining blind to the subtle signs of what was to come. Eventually, when the designations of the "Heroes" (jun 俊), "Kitchens" (chu 厨), "Guides" (gu 顧), and "Exemplars" (ji 及) arose, they suddenly defied the legal net of their age without regret—such was the tendency of excessive rigidity easily leading to fracture. At the close of the Yuanshi reign (1–5 CE), the whole country acted as if mad, sitting idly by while the great edifice toppled; whereas after the Xiping reign (172–178 CE), moral duty and honor remained awe-inspiring, still sufficient to cow ambitious warlords who would inquire after the imperial tripods. Discerning observers can hardly avoid ranking one above the other; yet if we measure them against the Great Way (zhouhang 周行), neither had truly heard the Way. Yang Zhongli 楊中立 (Yang Shi 楊時) once said: "The scholars of the Western Han delighted in merit and fame and did not strive for extraordinary integrity; the scholars of the Eastern Han prized integrity and righteousness and did not understand how to adapt to changing times. Both were shifted by the transformations of their age and were blind to the Way of the Mean." His weighing of the figures of the two dynasties is indeed judicious. Those in the present age who are called scholars at every turn cite high antiquity and look down upon recent eras, yet when one closely examines [?] their actual conduct, it turns out to be utterly contrary to their words. If one takes them to be pliant [reading 儒 as 懦], they seem suspect of fawning flattery [?]; if one takes them to be uncompromisingly upright, they resemble those who angle for advancement. Indeed, the way custom gradually saturates people, sweeping them along like waves and bending them like the wind, compared to the scholars of the two…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
漢之士又不知逕庭何如毋亦所以風之
者有未至乎昔董仲舒曰不素養士而求
賢猶不琢玉而求文采也夫四代之學考
諸經可見矣曰直溫寬栗之謨也曰智仁
中和之訓也于時曰宣曰嚴克稱有常之
吉無偏無陂咸遵蕩平之路者豈獨淳風
攸萃哉蓋得於輔翼綱紀之所陶成者居
多焉後世之養士非古之所以養士矣居
今而志古者將安所度束哉夫善調瑟者
===
更其浤灂要於和而已善持衡者權其低
昂要於平而已是故上之養士也抑詭惟
崇本實識極重之勢貴未然之防時尚包
荒則旌別以倡之使柔而不流於懦時尚
雕琢則惇大以覆之使剛而不淪於虐勵
世者此其亦幟乎士之自養也析義理變
氣質知欲其圓行欲其方舉世偷薄吾師
以厚有瑾瑜匿瑕之意而不失廉隅舉世
混濁吾振以清有萬仞壁立之操而不□
punctuated: 漢之士，又不知逕庭何如！毋亦所以風之者有未至乎？昔董仲舒曰：「不素養士而求賢，猶不琢玉而求文采也。」夫四代之學，考諸經可見矣。曰「直溫、寬栗」之謨也，曰「智、仁、中、和」之訓也。于時曰宣曰嚴，克稱有常之吉；無偏無陂，咸遵蕩平之路者，豈獨淳風攸萃哉？蓋得於輔翼綱紀之所陶成者居多焉。後世之養士，非古之所以養士矣；居今而志古者，將安所度束哉？夫善調瑟者，更其浤灂，要於和而已；善持衡者，權其低昂，要於平而已。是故上之養士也，抑詭惟崇本實，識極重之勢，貴未然之防。時尚包荒，則旌別以倡之，使柔而不流於懦；時尚雕琢，則惇大以覆之，使剛而不淪於虐。勵世者，此其亦幟乎！士之自養也，析義理，變氣質，知欲其圓，行欲其方。舉世偷薄，吾師以厚，有瑾瑜匿瑕之意，而不失廉隅；舉世混濁，吾振以清，有萬仞壁立之操，而不□
translation_en: … scholars of the [Western and Eastern] Han, one does not know how much further apart they are! Could it not be that the means of inspiring them have not yet reached perfection? In the past, Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 said: "Not cultivating scholars beforehand and yet seeking worthy men is like not carving jade and yet seeking brilliant patterns." Now, the schools of the Four Dynasties can be seen by examining the Classics: there was the counsel of being "straightforward yet mild, broad-minded yet reverent," and the instruction in "wisdom, benevolence, centrality, and harmony." At those times, whether displaying three virtues daily or six virtues strictly, men were able to match the auspiciousness of constancy; without偏頗 (partiality) or obliquity, all followed the broad and level road. Was this merely because pure customs gathered there? Rather, it was mostly achieved through the molding and shaping of supportive guidance and moral standards. The cultivation of scholars in later ages is no longer the way scholars were cultivated in antiquity; for those living in the present who set their minds on antiquity, by what measure and restraint shall they guide themselves? Now, one who is skilled at tuning a zither adjusts its booming or thin tones, aiming only at harmony; one who is skilled at holding a balance weighs its rise and fall, aiming only at levelness. Therefore, when superiors cultivate scholars, they suppress奇詭 (eccentricity) and esteem only fundamental substance; they recognize the momentum of extreme tendencies and value precautions taken before things come to pass. When the age prizes all-embracing tolerance, they lead it by distinguishing good and bad, making men gentle without lapsing into cowardice; when the age prizes ornate carving, they shelter it with generous magnanimity, making men firm without sinking into harshness. For those who encourage the world, is this not their red banner? As for how a scholar cultivates himself, he analyzes moral principles and transforms his temperament; he desires his knowledge to be round and adaptable, and his conduct to be square and upright. When the whole world is frivolous and shallow, I model myself on generosity, embracing the spirit of fine jade that conceals flaws without losing my sharp integrity; when the whole world is turbid and muddy, I rouse myself with purity, maintaining the integrity of a cliff standing ten thousand ren high without [setting up?]…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
門戶砥行者此其正鵠乎雖然士風之轉
移非文法禁令所能及也昔孔子觀河梁
之厲水而出者曰水猶可以忠信誠身親
之而况人乎古之化天下者神凝於穆清
之上而意流於海隅之遠浸潤如雨露鼓
動如雷霆以之駕馭寰宇鼓舞英豪如桴
鼓之相應臂指之相使故不下堂室而海
內之情舉得者誠使然也不此之務而偈
偈於法禁之末日提耳而令之曰吾將以
===
移風將以易俗則亦近於朝四暮三之術
矣天下其孰能信之蓋聞九皐之鶴鳴則
四野聞其聲海上之人機心一生則從游
之漚鳥翔舞而不下天不容僞其幾固如
此也後之君子有陶鑄世道之責者其設
誠於內而致行之也宛然鶴鳴之在皐而
無若好漚鳥之人然則幾矣
第四問
貫應舉
punctuated:
門戶。砥行者，此其正鵠乎？雖然，士風之轉移，非文法禁令所能及也。昔孔子觀河梁之厲水而出者，曰：「水猶可以忠信誠身親之，而况人乎？」古之化天下者，神凝於穆清之上，而意流於海隅之遠，浸潤如雨露，鼓動如雷霆。以之駕馭寰宇，鼓舞英豪，如桴鼓之相應、臂指之相使。故不下堂室，而海內之情舉得者，誠使然也。不此之務，而偈偈於法禁之末，日提耳而令之曰：「吾將以移風，將以易俗。」則亦近於朝四暮三之術矣，天下其孰能信之？蓋聞九皐之鶴鳴，則四野聞其聲；海上之人，機心一生，則從游之漚鳥翔舞而不下。天不容僞，其幾固如此也。後之君子，有陶鑄世道之責者，其設誠於內而致行之也，宛然鶴鳴之在皐，而無若好漚鳥之人然，則幾矣。

第四問
貫應舉
translation_en:
… [set up] factional gates. For those who hone their conduct, is this not the true target?

Even so, the transformation of literati customs is not something that legalistic regulations and prohibitions can achieve. In the past, when Confucius observed someone at the Lüliang rapids treading the water and emerging safely, he said: "If even water can be approached closely through loyalty, trustworthiness, and personal sincerity, how much more so human beings?" Those in antiquity who transformed the world concentrated their spirit on high in serene purity, while their intentions flowed out to the distant corners of the seas, soaking in like rain and dew, rousing like thunder and lightning. Using this to govern the realm and inspire heroes was like the mutual response of drumstick and drum, or the mutual coordination of arm and fingers. Therefore, without descending from their halls and chambers, they fully grasped the sentiments of all within the seas—it was sincerity that made it so. If one does not attend to this, but instead bustles anxiously after the trivialities of legal prohibitions, pulling people by the ear every day to command them, saying, "I am going to transform customs, I am going to change habits," this comes close to the trick of "four in the morning and three in the evening" [from the Zhuangzi]. Who in the world would believe it? For it is heard that when the crane cries in the九皋 (deep marshes), the four wilds hear its voice; whereas with the man by the sea, the moment a scheming thought arose in his mind, the seagulls that used to Frolic with him soared and danced in the air without alighting. Heaven does not tolerate falsehood; its subtle workings are inherently like this. If gentlemen of later times who bear the responsibility of molding the ways of the world establish sincerity within and carry it out in practice—just like the crane crying in the marsh, and not like the man who was fond of seagulls—then they will be near the mark.

Question Four
Guan Yingju 貫應舉

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導李　批〔論久任之法宜行而要之維持以善用其法書生而明習世務者耶〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔論久任超遷之法卓有定見〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔馭吏之法援証得體〕
甞歷觀古今之理道其要在於馭吏之有
法而古今之馭吏其法恒相習而爲用乃
吏之善敗迥然今與古殊者非人之盡不
可與古匹也時有所不能盡同也其法之
良窳迥然終與始異者非法之不可必行
===
也而所以用是法者未能使人以必信也
是故馭吏之法不可不講也用此法也莫
先於通滯變通而鼓舞之審其機而握其
衡俾不泥於古之迹而直師其意者善馭
吏者也法之行也莫先於示信昭示而維
持之始如是而終亦如是俾不起疑貳之
端而使之一意無回慮者善用法也然則
久任之法馭吏之善經而圖治之要術也
乃古行之而今效之其意務以便民不計
punctuated:
同考試官訓導李　批〔論久任之法宜行，而要之維持以善用其法，書生而明習世務者耶！〕
考試官教諭戴　批〔論久任、超遷之法，卓有定見。〕
考試官教諭楊　批〔馭吏之法，援証得體。〕

甞歷觀古今之理道，其要在於馭吏之有法；而古今之馭吏，其法恒相習而爲用。乃吏之善敗，迥然今與古殊者，非人之盡不可與古匹也，時有所不能盡同也；其法之良窳，迥然終與始異者，非法之不可必行也，而所以用是法者未能使人以必信也。是故馭吏之法不可不講也。用此法也，莫先於通滯。變通而鼓舞之，審其機而握其衡，俾不泥於古之迹而直師其意者，善馭吏者也。法之行也，莫先於示信。昭示而維持之，始如是而終亦如是，俾不起疑貳之端，而使之一意無回慮者，善用法也。然則久任之法，馭吏之善經而圖治之要術也。乃古行之而今效之，其意務以便民，不計
translation_en:
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Li, comments: [He argues that the system of long tenure ought to be put into practice, yet sums it up by emphasizing its maintenance so as to employ the system well—is he not a scholar who clearly understands and is well-versed in worldly affairs!]
Examiner, Instructor Dai, comments: [In discussing the systems of long tenure and rapid promotion, he possesses outstanding and settled views.]
Examiner, Instructor Yang, comments: [On the methods of managing officials, his citations of evidence are fitting.]

I have surveyed the principles of governance from antiquity to the present, and found that their essential point lies in having a method for managing officials; and in managing officials from antiquity to the present, the methods have constantly followed one another to be put to use. Yet the success and failure of officials today are vastly different from antiquity—not because men today are entirely unable to match those of antiquity, but because there are respects in which the times cannot be entirely the same. And the effectiveness or defectiveness of the methods turns out vastly different in the end from what it was at the beginning—not because the methods cannot necessarily be put into practice, but because those who employ these methods have failed to make men place certain trust in them. Therefore, the methods of managing officials must be carefully examined. In employing these methods, nothing takes precedence over relieving stagnation. To adapt flexibly and inspire officials, examining the pivot of affairs and holding the balance, so that one does not cling rigidly to the outward traces of antiquity but directly emulates its intent—this is what it means to be skilled at managing officials. In putting the methods into practice, nothing takes precedence over demonstrating trustworthiness. To proclaim them clearly and uphold them, being the same at the end as at the beginning, so that no cause for doubt or duplicity arises and officials are made single-minded without second thoughts—this is what it means to be skilled at employing the methods. This being so, the system of long tenure is a sound principle for managing officials and a vital art for planning governance. Now antiquity practiced it and the present imitates it; its intent is devoted to benefiting the people, without calculating…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
其吏之便與不便也其終不惟不便於吏
且未見其有益於民此豈其法之悖謬而
不可行哉繇操持而策馭者無通滯之術
不足以信人之心而使人以不肖之心應
之爾明問所及敢論述其時勢之異與吏
道之詭然後及其法之所以不行與其所
以可行者俟採擇焉夫是法之行始之者
唐虞也三載考績三考黜陟其典具在三
代而下行之輒效者西漢也良吏綦盛治
===
化郅隆史牒可稽試觀今之時與唐虞之
時同乎今之用法與西京之用同乎四岳
九官十二牧僅若人爾今則岳牧官聯非
特夏商之官倍其倍于成周者又何如也
宣帝之世二千石以治狀聞者賜金下璽
書增秩至入拜公卿令郎超卓其能一一
優崇乎此時勢之異至明矣今之時非古
之時而吏道之詭視古遠甚故無才賢智
譎而深取名於世無澡身潔志而厚矯飾
punctuated:
其吏之便與不便也，其終不惟不便於吏，且未見其有益於民。此豈其法之悖謬而不可行哉？繇操持而策馭者無通滯之術，不足以信人之心，而使人以不肖之心應之爾。明問所及，敢論述其時勢之異與吏道之詭，然後及其法之所以不行與其所以可行者，俟採擇焉。

夫是法之行，始之者唐、虞也。「三載考績，三考黜陟」，其典具在。三代而下，行之輒效者，西漢也。良吏綦盛，治化郅隆，史牒可稽。試觀今之時，與唐、虞之時同乎？今之用法，與西京之用同乎？四岳、九官、十二牧，僅若人爾。今則岳、牧官聯，非特夏、商之官倍，其倍于成周者又何如也？宣帝之世，二千石以治狀聞者，賜金、下璽書、增秩，至入拜公卿；令、郎超卓，其能一一優崇乎？此時勢之異，至明矣。

今之時非古之時，而吏道之詭視古遠甚。故無才賢智，譎而深取名於世；無澡身潔志，而厚矯飾…
translation_en:
…whether it is convenient or inconvenient for the officials. In the end, not only is it inconvenient for the officials, it is not even seen to be beneficial to the people. How could this be because the policy itself is perverse, flawed, and unworkable? Rather, it is simply because those who hold the reins and direct the officials lack the art of clearing bottlenecks, failing to win people's trust and instead prompting them to respond with unworthy intentions. Addressing the enlightened question, I venture to discuss the differences in historical circumstances and the deceitfulness in the ways of officials, and thereafter touch upon why this policy fails to work and how it can be made to work, awaiting your selection.

Now, the implementation of this policy began under Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun]. "Every three years there was an evaluation of merits, and after three evaluations there were demotions and promotions"—those canons remain intact. From the Three Dynasties onward, the era in which its implementation consistently proved effective was the Western Han. Good officials flourished abundantly and transformative governance reached the utmost height, as can be verified in the historical records. Yet let us consider: are the times of today the same as the times of Tang and Yu? Is today's application of the law the same as its application in the Western Capital [Western Han]? The Four Peaks, Nine Ministers, and Twelve Pastors were merely that handful of men. Today, however, the official ranks corresponding to those Peaks and Pastors do not merely double the offices of the Xia and Shang—how many times more are they than even those of the flourishing Zhou! In the reign of Emperor Xuan [of Han], Two-thousand-bushel officials [Commandery Governors] whose administrative achievements were reported to the throne were bestowed gold, granted imperial letters under the玺 seal, and promoted in rank, even to the point of entering the court to be appointed as Excellency or Minister. Today, when District Magistrates and Court Gentlemen are outstanding, can every single one of them be so specially honored and exalted? That the historical circumstances are different is abundantly clear.

The times of today are not the times of antiquity, and the deceitfulness in the ways of officials far exceeds that of antiquity. Thus, lacking genuine talent, worth, or wisdom, they use craftiness to deeply angle for reputation in the world; lacking cleansed conduct and pure intentions, they heavily cloak themselves in pretense…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
於外圓環謝請以爲獵取之計建說興事
以徼肩任之譽此情險于山川而明蔽于
眉睫胡可云較也夫吏之建置凡以爲民
也而吏之久任亦凡以爲民也民誠便矣
何顧于吏之不便誠有如明問所及者愚
則竊謂未有吏不便而有益於民者夫安
其志以行其道勵其心以宣其力卽受一
民一社之寄而精神心術無一不與境土
相流通措注設施無一不與黎庶相聯屬
===
由是而事體益周民志益定惠澤益深此
久任之於民良便也然進取之情銳而安
民之譽遲吾恐損實事以養名者多鐘鳴
之迫侵百姓以利己者志社錢之營官寧
有長子孫之驩民寧有借寇君之願乎以
此而欲吏稱民安是却行而求及前人也
此吏不便柰之何於民便也然法之所以
不行又有在焉今之仕進之途日廣闒茸
之流未汰缺裁則入淬於位途壅則新積
punctuated: 於外，圓環謝請以爲獵取之計，建說興事以徼肩任之譽。此情險于山川，而明蔽于眉睫，胡可云較也？夫吏之建置，凡以爲民也；而吏之久任，亦凡以爲民也。民誠便矣，何顧于吏之不便？誠有如明問所及者。愚則竊謂：未有吏不便而有益於民者。夫安其志以行其道，勵其心以宣其力，卽受一民一社之寄，而精神心術，無一不與境土相流通；措注設施，無一不與黎庶相聯屬。由是而事體益周，民志益定，惠澤益深，此久任之於民良便也。然進取之情銳，而安民之譽遲，吾恐損實事以養名者，多鐘鳴之迫；侵百姓以利己者，志社錢之營。官寧有長子孫之驩？民寧有借寇君之願乎？以此而欲吏稱民安，是却行而求及前人也。此吏不便，柰之何於民便也？然法之所以不行，又有在焉。今之仕進之途日廣，闒茸之流未汰。缺裁則入淬於位，途壅則新積…
translation_en:
…on the outside. They smoothly make rounds of polite visits and requests as a scheme to hunt for promotion, and they propose theories and initiate projects to angle for a reputation of shouldering responsibility. When human nature is more treacherous than mountains and rivers, and clear sight is obscured right before one's very eyelashes, how can we even speak of comparing [our times with antiquity]?

Now, the establishment of officials is entirely for the sake of the people, and keeping officials in office for long tenures is likewise entirely for the sake of the people. If it truly benefits the people, why care if it is inconvenient for the officials? This is indeed just as the Examiner's question has touched upon. Yet I would venture to say that there has never been a case where what is inconvenient for officials is beneficial to the people. Only when an official's ambition is settled so that he may carry out his Way, and his mind is encouraged so that he may exert his strength, can he—even when entrusted with a single community and its altars—have his spirit and intentions wholly connected with the territory, and his measures and policies wholly bound up with the common people. Through this, administrative affairs become ever more thorough, the people's minds ever more settled, and benevolent grace ever deeper—this is how long tenure in office is truly beneficial to the people.
