In putting a system into practice, nothing takes precedence over demonstrating trustworthiness—proclaiming it clearly and upholding it consistently, so that as it is at the beginning, so too it is at the end, giving rise to no cause for doubt or duplicity and making men single-minded without second thoughts: this is what it means to be skilled at employing a system. This being so, the system of long tenure is a sound principle for managing officials and an essential art for achieving good governance. Yet when antiquity practiced it and the present imitates it, the intention is to strive for the convenience of the people, without reckoning…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
其吏之便與不便也其終不惟不便於吏
且未見其有益於民此豈其法之悖謬而
不可行哉繇操持而策馭者無通滯之術
不足以信人之心而使人以不肖之心應
之爾明問所及敢論述其時勢之異與吏
道之詭然後及其法之所以不行與其所
以可行者俟採擇焉夫是法之行始之者
唐虞也三載考績三考黜陟其典具在三
代而下行之輒效者西漢也良吏蓁盛治
===
化郅隆史牒可稽試觀今之時與唐虞之
時同乎今之用法與西京之用同乎四岳
九官十二牧僅若人爾今則岳牧官聯非
特夏商之官倍其倍于成周者又何如也
宣帝之世二千石以治狀聞者賜金下璽
書增秩至入拜公卿令卽超卓其能一一
優崇乎此時勢之異至明矣今之時非古
之時而吏道之詭視古遠甚故無才賢智
譎而深取名於世無澡身潔志而厚矯飾
punctuated: 其吏之便與不便也，其終不惟不便於吏，且未見其有益於民。此豈其法之悖謬而不可行哉？繇操持而策馭者無通滯之術，不足以信人之心，而使人以不肖之心應之爾。明問所及，敢論述其時勢之異與吏道之詭，然後及其法之所以不行與其所以可行者，俟採擇焉。夫是法之行，始之者唐虞也。三載考績，三考黜陟，其典具在。三代而下，行之輒效者，西漢也。良吏蓁盛，治化郅隆，史牒可稽。試觀今之時，與唐虞之時同乎？今之用法，與西京之用同乎？四岳、九官、十二牧，僅若人爾。今則岳牧官聯，非特夏商之官倍，其倍于成周者，又何如也？宣帝之世，二千石以治狀聞者，賜金、下璽書、增秩，至入拜公卿。令卽超卓，其能一一優崇乎？此時勢之異，至明矣。今之時非古之時，而吏道之詭視古遠甚。故無才賢，智譎而深取名於世；無澡身潔志，而厚矯飾…
translation_en:
…whether it is convenient or inconvenient for the officials. In the end, not only is it inconvenient for the officials, it also has not been seen to be of any benefit to the people. How could this be because the method itself is perverse and unworkable? It is simply because those who hold the reins and direct the officials lack the art of clearing away stagnation; they are unable to win trust in people's hearts, and so cause men to respond with unworthy intentions. Regarding what your enlightened question touches upon, I venture to discuss the differences in the circumstances of the times and the deceitfulness of official ways, and then proceed to why the method does not work and how it can be made to work, awaiting your selection.

Now, the practice of this method began under Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun]. Every three years achievements were evaluated, and after three evaluations promotions and demotions were made—those canons are preserved in full. From the Three Dynasties onward, the era in which practicing it consistently brought results was the Western Han. Good officials flourished in abundance and transformative governance reached the utmost height, as can be verified in the historical records. Yet try to observe: is the present time the same as the time of Tang and Yu? Is the present application of the method the same as its application in the Western Capital [Western Han]? The Four Peaks, Nine Officials, and Twelve Pastors were only so many men. Today, however, the provincial and local officials and interlocking offices are not merely double the officials of the Xia and Shang—how many times more are they than those of the flourishing Zhou! In the reign of Emperor Xuan [of Han], Two-Thousand-Bushel Officials [Grand Administrators] whose administrative performance became known were granted gold, honored with imperial letters under the玺 seal, and given increased rank, even to the point of entering the court to be appointed among the Three Dukes and Nine Ministers. Even if [officials today][?] are outstanding, can they be favored and exalted one by one? This difference in the circumstances of the times is utterly clear.

The present time is not the ancient time, and the deceitfulness of official ways far exceeds that of antiquity. Thus, lacking talent and worth, men use cleverness and guile to deeplyfish for reputation in the world; lacking purified persons and clean aspirations, they heavily affect…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
於外圓環謝請以爲獵取之計建說興事
以徼肩任之譽此情險于山川而明蔽于
眉睫胡可云較也夫吏之建置凡以爲民
也而吏之久任亦凡以爲民也民誠便矣
何顧于吏之不便誠有如明問所及者愚
則竊謂未有吏不便而有益於民者夫安
其志以行其道勵其心以宣其力卽受一
民一社之寄而精神心術無一不與境土
相流通措注設施無一不與黎庶相聯屬
由是而事體益周民志益定惠澤益深此
===
久任之於民良便也然進取之情鋭而安
民之譽遲吾恐損實事以養名者多鐘鳴
之迫侵百姓以利己者志社錢之營官寧
有長子孫之驩民寧有借寇君之願乎以
此而欲吏稱民安是却行而求及前人也
此吏不便柰之何於民便也然法之所以
不行又有在焉今之仕進之途日廣闒茸
之流未汰缺裁則人浮於位途壅則新積
punctuated: 於外；圓環謝請，以爲獵取之計；建說興事，以徼肩任之譽。此情險于山川，而明蔽于眉睫，胡可云較也！夫吏之建置，凡以爲民也；而吏之久任，亦凡以爲民也。民誠便矣，何顧于吏之不便？誠有如明問所及者。愚則竊謂未有吏不便而有益於民者。夫安其志以行其道，勵其心以宣其力，卽受一民一社之寄，而精神心術，無一不與境土相流通；措注設施，無一不與黎庶相聯屬。由是而事體益周，民志益定，惠澤益深，此久任之於民良便也。然進取之情鋭，而安民之譽遲，吾恐損實事以養名者，多鐘鳴之迫；侵百姓以利己者，志社錢之營。官寧有長子孫之驩？民寧有借寇君之願乎？以此而欲吏稱民安，是却行而求及前人也。此吏不便，柰之何於民便也？然法之所以不行，又有在焉。今之仕進之途日廣，闒茸之流未汰；缺裁則人浮於位，途壅則新積
translation_en: …on the outside; they curry favor in circles and decline requests [for favours in a calculating way] as a scheme to hunt for promotion; they propose theories and initiate projects in order to court the reputation of shouldering responsibility. Their true dispositions are more treacherous than mountains and rivers, and clear sight is blinded right before one's very eyelashes—how can they even be compared [with the ancients]? Now, the establishment of officials is entirely for the sake of the people; and long tenure for officials is likewise entirely for the sake of the people. If it is truly convenient for the people, why care if it is inconvenient for the officials? It is indeed just as Your Enlightened Question has touched upon. Yet I would humbly suggest that there has never been a case where what is inconvenient for the officials proves beneficial to the people. When an official settles his ambition to carry out his Way and rouses his mind to exert his strength, even if he receives the charge of just a single populace and a single local altar of the soil, his spirit and mental craft will in every respect circulate through the territory, and his measures and arrangements will in every respect be bound together with the common people. Through this, the administration of affairs becomes ever more thorough, the minds of the people ever more settled, and benevolent grace ever deeper—this is how long tenure is genuinely advantageous to the people. Yet when the eagerness for advancement is sharp while the reputation gained from pacifying the people comes slowly, I fear that those who harm actual affairs in order to cultivate their own fame are often pressed by the urgency of the tolling bell [of passing time], and those who encroach upon the common people to profit themselves set their minds on scheming for community funds [?]. How then could officials have the joy of raising sons and grandsons in their posts, or the people have the wish to "borrow Master Kou [Kou Xun]" for another term? To desire through such means that officials match their duties and the people enjoy peace is like walking backward while seeking to catch up with the person ahead. When the officials find it inconvenient like this, how could it possibly be advantageous to the people? Moreover, there is another reason why the law cannot be carried out. Today the avenues of official advancement grow wider by the day, while base and mediocre sorts have not been weeded out; when posts are reduced, there are more men than positions, and when the path is congested, new candidates pile up…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
於舊蘇軾所謂一官而三人共者居者一
人去者一人而伺之者又一人令慮不止
此也况埋於外者久則有意外之虞優游
於內者久則有樞要之望間又以虛冏而
獵取貪緣而倖致蘇軾所謂得者不以僥
倖自名不得者則以沉淪爲恨此又何怪
其然也此久任之所不行者非法之弊也
用之者弊也
聖天子嘉念黎元
===
納宰臣之議斷然以久任爲必可行其欲追
隆唐虞之至治而遠邁西漢之盛際其德
惠之在寰宇中者匪淺矣顧超遷與久任
相爲表裏蓋非久任則無以便民而使之
安而習之非超遷則無以便吏以庶幾激
而酬之此不易之論也乃君子出而委質
於君何內何外何久何近惟
天子使耳安敢計沉淪務速化厭雌伏跂華顯
而自處爲躍冶之金犇乘之騎哉顧恐天
punctuated: 於舊。蘇軾所謂「一官而三人共」者：居者一人，去者一人，而伺之者又一人；令慮不止此也。况埋於外者，久則有意外之虞；優游於內者，久則有樞要之望。間又以虛冏而獵取，貪緣而倖致。蘇軾所謂「得者不以僥倖自名，不得者則以沉淪爲恨」，此又何怪其然也？此久任之所不行者，非法之弊也，用之者弊也。聖天子嘉念黎元，納宰臣之議，斷然以久任爲必可行，其欲追隆唐、虞之至治，而遠邁西漢之盛際，其德惠之在寰宇中者匪淺矣。顧超遷與久任相爲表裏，蓋非久任則無以便民，而使之安而習之；非超遷則無以便吏，以庶幾激而酬之，此不易之論也。乃君子出而委質於君，何內何外？何久何近？惟天子使耳。安敢計沉淪、務速化、厭雌伏、跂華顯，而自處爲躍冶之金、犇乘之騎哉？顧恐天
translation_en:
…upon the old. As Su Shi (蘇軾) said of "three men sharing a single office": one occupies it, one is leaving it, and yet another is waiting in the wings for it; today [?], I fear it goes even beyond this. Moreover, those buried away in provincial posts, if kept there long, face the peril of unexpected misfortune; whereas those enjoying leisure at court, if kept there long, harbor expectations of pivotal positions. Occasionally, too, men hunt for advancement through empty reputation [?] and obtain it by lucky chance through corrupt connections [?]. As Su Shi said, "Those who succeed do not call themselves fortunate opportunists, while those who fail resent their obscurity"—what wonder is it that things are so? That long tenure cannot be put into practice is not the fault of the law itself, but the fault of those who administer it.

Our Sacred Son of Heaven, cherishing compassionate concern for the common people, has accepted the counsel of his chief ministers and resolutely deemed long tenure certain to be practicable. In his desire to rival the supreme governance of Tang and Yu and far surpass the flourishing era of the Western Han, the moral bounty he bestows throughout the empire is by no means shallow. Yet extraordinary promotion and long tenure are two sides of the same coin. Without long tenure, there is no way to benefit the people, allowing them to live in peace and grow accustomed to their officials; without extraordinary promotion, there is no way to benefit the officials, whereby one may hope to rouse and reward them. This is an immutable principle.

Now, when a gentleman goes forth and pledges his service to his sovereign, what matters inner or outer, long or brief? He simply obeys the command of the Son of Heaven. How could he dare calculate his obscurity, strive for rapid advancement, disdain humble subordination, or stand on tiptoe for splendid eminence—conducting himself like metal leaping from the smelter's mold or a horse bolting from its team? Yet I fear that in the empire…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
下不皆忠良自許之夫則所以用法以制
馭之者不可少也所當維持以善用此法
者不可少也愚則謂要莫先於通滯本莫
先於示信而所以通滯而示信者又不出
於責循良之效嚴名實之辨寬督責之令
杜僥倖之門與夫汰冗流崇優異數者而
已夫漢志循良所傳其稱寵異最著者惟
黃次公之尚寬和韓延壽之教禮讓者數
人至於發奸擿伏武健自快者類皆無取
===
則循良之效不可不尚也齊威積衰之國
一旦綜察精嚴呼卽墨大夫而封之呼阿
大夫而烹之卒之鄰人懾伏國中大治齊
用稱霸則名實之核不可不嚴也甞觀漢
世之用人也破觚而爲圜斲彫以爲朴故
吏治蒸蒸不至於姦今之郡邑日困於簿
書之繁惴惴幸無事以需次猝而有一細
故遂蝟舉而苛督之使之前功盡棄此畏
縮者所以怯前而顧後保名者所以計旦
punctuated: 下不皆忠良自許之夫，則所以用法以制馭之者，不可少也；所當維持以善用此法者，不可少也。愚則謂要莫先於通滯，本莫先於示信，而所以通滯而示信者，又不出於責循良之效、嚴名實之辨、寬督責之令、杜僥倖之門，與夫汰冗流、崇優異數者而已。夫漢志循良所傳，其稱寵異最著者，惟黃次公之尚寬和、韓延壽之教禮讓者數人；至於發奸擿伏、武健自快者，類皆無取，則循良之效不可不尚也。齊威積衰之國，一旦綜察精嚴，呼卽墨大夫而封之，呼阿大夫而烹之，卒之鄰人懾伏，國中大治，齊用稱霸，則名實之核不可不嚴也。甞觀漢世之用人也，破觚而爲圜，斲彫以爲朴，故吏治蒸蒸，不至於姦。今之郡邑，日困於簿書之繁，惴惴幸無事以需次，猝而有一細故，遂蝟舉而苛督之，使之前功盡棄，此畏縮者所以怯前而顧後，保名者所以計旦…
translation_en:
…the empire does not consist entirely of men who consider themselves loyal and virtuous; therefore, the means of using laws to control and govern them cannot be dispensed with, and what ought to be upheld in order to use these laws well cannot be dispensed with either. In my humble view, nothing is more essential than clearing stagnation in promotions, and nothing is more fundamental than demonstrating trustworthiness. And the means to clear stagnation and demonstrate trustworthiness lie in nothing more than these several measures: demanding the results of upright and benevolent administration, strictly distinguishing between reputation and reality, relaxing the orders of harsh supervision and censure, closing the doors to opportunistic advancement, as well as weeding out superfluous officials and honoring outstanding merit.

In the biographies of upright officials recorded in the History of the Han (Hanzhi), those most notably praised and favored were only a few men, such as Huang Cigong (Huang Ba 黃霸), who valued leniency and harmony, and Han Yanshou 韓延壽, who taught ritual propriety and deference. As for those who exposed hidden villainy and took pleasure in ruthless severity, none were approved. Thus, the results of upright and benevolent administration must be esteemed.

King Wei of Qi 齊威王 inherited a state in long-standing decline, yet once he conducted thorough and strict verification, he summoned the Grand Master of Jimo 卽墨 and enfeoffed him, and summoned the Grand Master of E 阿 and boiled him alive. In the end, neighboring states submitted in awe, the state within was brought to great order, and Qi thereby achieved hegemony. Thus, the verification of reputation and reality must be made strict.

I have observed how the Han dynasty employed men: it broke off sharp corners to make things round, and planed away ornate carvings to restore simplicity; therefore, official administration flourished and did not degenerate into wickedness. Today's commanderies and counties are daily exhausted by the proliferation of administrative paperwork, anxiously hoping for no incidents while awaiting their turn for promotion. Should a minor fault suddenly occur, critics rise up like hedgehog spines to harshly censure them, causing all their previous achievements to be completely discarded. This is why the timid are afraid to advance and look anxiously behind them, and why those who seek to preserve their reputation calculate from morning…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
而憂夕則苛細不可不蠲也又聞官道猶
之市也眞僞無常權在駔驓利否無常機
在善趨故敦朴寡援之吏恒坐赼趄而便
儇突梯之徒每遂速化其端不可勝詰此
執攜者所以窺閒而造瑕未亮者所以增
嫌而導惑則僥倖不可不絕也賢才跧伏
無盡雖難以類求而入貲之途額外之員
其冒濫又不可勝計漢時入財者補郎而
郎選途衰厚貲者爲吏而吏道益襍今未
===
遽有此而宂襍之汰可不銳意行之乎臣
子鞠躬盡瘁何敢望報然而爵以勵世賞
以酬勞即聖帝所不容已漢時守吏有賢
能異等者優賜至補公卿之缺前固言之
今遽難行此然其歷任久而功效著超擢
之典可不必然行之乎夫責循良則彼知
不務赫赫以爲旦夕計也覈名實則彼知
不可蔽匿而以虛罔爲也苛細蠲則彼知
竭志宣力而無不測憂也倖進杜則彼知
punctuated: 而憂夕，則苛細不可不蠲也。又聞官道猶之市也，眞僞無常，權在駔驓；利否無常，機在善趨。故敦朴寡援之吏恒坐赼趄，而便儇突梯之徒每遂速化，其端不可勝詰。此執攜者所以窺閒而造瑕，未亮者所以增嫌而導惑，則僥倖不可不絕也。賢才跧伏無盡，雖難以類求，而入貲之途、額外之員，其冒濫又不可勝計。漢時入財者補郎，而郎選途衰；厚貲者爲吏，而吏道益襍。今未遽有此，而宂襍之汰，可不銳意行之乎？臣子鞠躬盡瘁，何敢望報？然而爵以勵世，賞以酬勞，即聖帝所不容已。漢時守吏有賢能異等者，優賜至補公卿之缺，前固言之。今遽難行此，然其歷任久而功效著，超擢之典，可不必然行之乎？夫責循良，則彼知不務赫赫以爲旦夕計也；覈名實，則彼知不可蔽匿而以虛罔爲也；苛細蠲，則彼知竭志宣力而無不測憂也；倖進杜，則彼知
translation_en: …and worry about the evening; thus, petty hairsplitting must be eliminated. I have also heard that the way of officialdom is like a marketplace: truth and falsehood are inconstant, for power lies with the brokers; profit and loss are inconstant, for opportunity lies with those skilled at chasing advantage. Therefore, honest, unadorned officials with few backers are constantly bogged down in hesitation, whereas slick and obsequious fellows always achieve rapid promotion—the ways this happens are too numerous to investigate. This is why those with ulterior motives [?] watch for openings to fabricate flaws, and those lacking integrity heighten suspicions and lead people astray; thus, opportunistic advancement must be cut off. Worthy talents lie hidden in inexhaustible numbers; although it is hard to seek them out by category, those who enter through the path of contributing wealth and the supernumerary personnel outside the quotas represent a fraudulent excess beyond calculation. In Han times, those who contributed wealth filled vacancies as Court Gentlemen, and the selection path for Court Gentlemen declined; those with ample wealth became officials, and the way of officialdom grew increasingly mixed. Even if it has not quite come to this today, how can we not resolutely carry out the culling of superfluous and miscellaneous personnel? When subjects bend their bodies and exhaust their strength in service, how dare they hope for recompense? Yet using noble rank to encourage the world and rewards to repay toil is something even a sage emperor cannot dispense with. In Han times, when territorial officials showed extraordinary worth and ability, generous rewards extended even to filling vacancies among the Ducal Ministers—as was indeed mentioned earlier. Today it would be difficult to suddenly implement this, yet when officials have served for a long time and their achievements are manifest, how can the statute for extraordinary promotion not be unfailingly carried out? Now, if we demand upright and良 (benevolent) administration, they will know not to pursue flashy renown as a scheme for morning and evening; if we verify reputation against reality, they will know they cannot conceal things and act with empty deceit; if petty hairsplitting is eliminated, they will know to exhaust their will and exert their strength without fear of the unexpected; if opportunistic advancement is blocked, they will know…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
積日累勞而無壅淤慮也汰宂嚴則蠹敗
免于噂沓優異崇則人心興於鼓舞如是
而久任行之不恤于羣言之翕訿不格于
衆情之牽滯推一世至千百世可也然又
有本焉在上而不在下有機焉在近而不
在遠夫立鵠行賞靡不爭射矣設標命趨
靡不爭赴矣何者言有以示之也一夫挽
强百夫決拾一人持罾千人臨淵何者言
有以倡之也是在
主上與秉衡者加之意焉愚生何敢竟其說
===
第五問
余僴
同考試官訓導龔 批〔農桑生民大命也子論蜀之瀧田植桑而援古以酌今之宜行燦然可睹識時務之俊傑也〕
考試官教諭戴 批〔論事卓有定見非勦說者〕
考試官教諭楊 批〔該博之學精練之才〕
執事策蜀士而以蜀大利問亡亦以諸生
居恒有意於民事乎顧不佞業佔僤者流
punctuated:
積日累勞而無壅淤慮也。汰宂嚴，則蠹敗免于噂沓；優異崇，則人心興於鼓舞。如是而久任行之，不恤于羣言之翕訿，不格于衆情之牽滯，推一世至千百世可也。然又有本焉，在上而不在下；有機焉，在近而不在遠。夫立鵠行賞，靡不爭射矣；設標命趨，靡不爭赴矣。何者？言有以示之也。一夫挽强，百夫決拾；一人持罾，千人臨淵。何者？言有以倡之也。是在主上與秉衡者加之意焉，愚生何敢竟其說！

第五問
余僴
同考試官訓導龔批〔農桑，生民大命也。子論蜀之瀧田植桑，而援古以酌今之宜行，燦然可睹，識時務之俊傑也。〕
考試官教諭戴批〔論事卓有定見，非勦說者。〕
考試官教諭楊批〔該博之學，精練之才。〕
執事策蜀士，而以蜀大利問，亡亦以諸生居恒有意於民事乎？顧不佞業佔僤者流，
translation_en:
…accumulate days and pile up merits without worrying about blockage or stagnation. When the weeding out of superfluous personnel is strict, corrupt and ruinous elements are kept from babbling in cliques; when special distinction is honored, people's minds are roused to encouragement. If long tenure of office is practiced in this way—unmoved by thewhispered slanders of the crowd and unhindered by the dragging hesitations of popular sentiment—it can be extended from one generation to a hundred or a thousand generations. Yet there is also a fundamental root to this, which lies above and not below; and there is a pivotal mechanism, which lies near and not far. Now, when a target is set up and rewards are offered, everyone competes to shoot at it; when a marker is erected and men are ordered to run toward it, everyone competes to rush to it. Why is this? It means there is something displayed to guide them. When one man draws a strong bow, a hundred men put on their thumb-rings and arm-guards; when one man holds a fishing net, a thousand men approach the deep pool. Why is this? It means there is someone taking the lead for them. This depends on the Sovereign above and those who hold the scales of authority paying special heed to it. How dare this foolish student exhaust his argument!

Fifth Question
Yu Xian 余僴
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Gong 龔 comments: [Agriculture and sericulture are the great lifeblood of the people. You discuss irrigating fields [?] and planting mulberries in Sichuan, citing antiquity to deliberate on what is appropriate to put into practice today. It is brilliantly clear to see—truly an outstanding talent who understands the affairs of the times.]
Examiner, Instructor Dai 戴 comments: [In discussing affairs, he possesses an outstanding and firm view; he is not one who merely plagiarizes others' words.]
Examiner, Instructor Yang 楊 comments: [Comprehensive and broad learning; refined and practiced talent.]

Your Excellency puts a policy question to the scholars of Sichuan and asks about the great advantages of Sichuan—is it not because you suppose that we students ordinarily take an interest in the affairs of the people? Yet I, an unworthy man, am merely one of those who drone over texts [?]…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
計畫無復之耳雖然地志所載故老所傳
聞竊耳之矣蓋蜀在天下故稱陸海其食
貨之利未易一二更僕指數姑勿論論其
大者有二一水利也一蠶桑也夫二者利
之所出而衣食之源也衣食者人之所資
以爲命柰之何其諱言之也蓋今蜀之田
�london
===
而食之織而衣之也爲得其興利之道也
興利之道粟米布帛生於地長於時聚於
力非可以安坐而得之而鼂錯所謂民貧
則姦邪生貧生於不足不足生于不農有
味乎其言之哉良有司者知其然也故務
民於農桑引水漑田植桑飼蠶爲勞民勸
相計也夫穿渠漑注之所資也居數歲而
水溢則潰奔叵測暵則淤閼不流蠶桑絲
帛之所出也均一鄉而彼則餘以貨外郡
punctuated: 計畫無復之耳。雖然，地志所載、故老所傳聞，竊耳之矣。蓋蜀在天下，故稱「陸海」，其食貨之利未易一二更僕指數，姑勿論。論其大者有二：一水利也，一蠶桑也。夫二者，利之所出而衣食之源也。衣食者，人之所資以爲命，柰之何其諱言之也？蓋今蜀之田london，而食之、織而衣之也，爲得其興利之道也。興利之道，粟米布帛，生於地，長於時，聚於力，非可以安坐而得之。而鼂錯所謂「民貧則姦邪生，貧生於不足，不足生于不農」，有味乎其言之哉！良有司者知其然也，故務民於農桑，引水漑田，植桑飼蠶，爲勞民勸相計也。夫穿渠，漑注之所資也；居數歲而水溢則潰奔叵測，暵則淤閼不流。蠶桑，絲帛之所出也；均一鄉，而彼則餘以貨外郡，
translation_en: … have no other practical plans to offer. Even so, as for what is recorded in the local gazetteers and passed down by the elders, I have privately heard something of it. Now, within the Empire, Sichuan has of old been called an “Inland Sea” of abundance; the benefits of its food and goods could not easily be enumerated in full even if one changed attendants repeatedly, so let us leave the minor ones aside. Speaking of the greatest among them, there are two: one is water conservancy, and the other is sericulture and mulberry cultivation. These two are the sources from which benefit issues and the fountainheads of clothing and food. Clothing and food are what people rely upon to sustain life—whyever should one shrink from speaking of them? Now, as for the fields of Sichuan today [? garbled: london, missing text likely to the effect of “it is not merely a matter of ploughing”] and eating from them, or weaving and clothing oneself with them; rather, it is a matter of grasping the way to promote their benefits. As for the way of promoting benefits: grain, rice, cloth, and silk are born of the earth, nurtured by the seasons, and gathered through human labor; they cannot be obtained by sitting idly at ease. How deeply meaningful are the words of Chao Cuo 鼂錯: “When the people are poor, villainy and wickedness arise; poverty arises from insufficiency, and insufficiency arises from not engaging in agriculture!” Good local officials understand that this is so, and therefore they direct the people to agriculture and sericulture, drawing water to irrigate the fields and planting mulberries to rear silkworms as a plan to encourage, comfort, and assist the toiling populace. Now, digging canals is what irrigation depends upon; yet after a few years pass, when the waters overflow, they burst their banks and rush forth unpredictably, and when there is drought, they silt up and become blocked so that they do not flow. Silkworms and mulberries are what silk fabrics come from; yet within the very same district, that place has a surplus with which to trade to outside prefectures, …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
此則貨彼郡之餘故夫欲興巳穿渠之利
易而興未穿渠之利則地勢高下水性順
逆不可不度也度之而議或格於盈庭興
巳蠶桑之利易而興未蠶桑之利則地利
有無民情勤惰不可不審也審之而議或
奪于築舍此蜀之利民二事不能無廑執
事問也蓋蜀爲天府之地諸葛亮爲昭烈
告之矣其言曰益州險塞沃野千里夫險
塞則可以守沃野則可以出軍需亮蓋得
===
策矣是建邦啓土之始也乃今觀蜀自秦
守李氷鑿離堆辟沫水之害穿二江成都
之中此渠皆可行舟有餘則用溉浸百姓
饗其利今其堆在灌縣西一里許巋然立
水中可覩也蓋始未鑿堆地勢下壅沫水
奔突不可控揣爲居民害而今則順流而
東而水之利溥則藉以灌溉雨則不過其
流故其記曰水旱從人不知饑饉其謂是
也而二江則蜀志以爲一汶江一流江蓋
punctuated: 此則貨彼郡之餘。故夫欲興巳穿渠之利易，而興未穿渠之利，則地勢高下、水性順逆，不可不度也；度之而議或格於盈庭。興巳蠶桑之利易，而興未蠶桑之利，則地利有無、民情勤惰，不可不審也；審之而議或奪于築舍。此蜀之利民二事，不能無廑執事問也。蓋蜀爲天府之地，諸葛亮爲昭烈告之矣。其言曰：「益州險塞，沃野千里。」夫險塞則可以守，沃野則可以出軍需，亮蓋得策矣，是建邦啓土之始也。乃今觀蜀，自秦守李氷鑿離堆，辟沫水之害，穿二江成都之中，此渠皆可行舟，有餘則用溉浸，百姓饗其利。今其堆在灌縣西一里許，巋然立水中，可覩也。蓋始未鑿堆，地勢下壅，沫水奔突，不可控揣，爲居民害；而今則順流而東，而水之利溥，則藉以灌溉，雨則不過其流。故其記曰：「水旱從人，不知饑饉。」其謂是也。而二江，則《蜀志》以爲一汶江、一流江，蓋
translation_en:
… while this place must purchase the surplus of that prefecture. Therefore, to promote the benefits where canals have already been dug is easy, whereas to promote the benefits where canals have not yet been dug, one cannot fail to measure the elevation of the terrain and whether the nature of the water is favorable or adverse; and even when one measures them, deliberations may be obstructed by a court full of conflicting opinions. To promote the benefits where sericulture is already practiced is easy, whereas to promote the benefits where sericulture is not yet practiced, one cannot fail to examine the presence or absence of terrestrial advantages and the diligence orlaziness of the people's disposition; and even when one examines them, deliberations may be thwarted like building a house by the roadside. These two matters for benefiting the people of Shu (Sichuan) could not but trouble Your Excellency to ask about them.

Indeed, that Shu is a "Storehouse of Heaven" (tianfu zhi di) was already declared by Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮 to Zhaolie 昭烈 (Liu Bei 劉備). His words were: "Yizhou 益州 has perilous passes and a thousand li of fertile plains." With perilous passes it can be defended, and with fertile plains it can supply military provisions; Liang indeed grasped the right strategy, and this was the beginning of founding the state and opening up the territory. Now if we observe Shu today, ever since the Qin Governor (shou) Li Bing 李氷 cut through Lidui 離堆 (Separated Mound) to avert the harm of the Mo River 沫水, and dug the Two Rivers (Erjiang 二江) through the midst of Chengdu 成都, these canals have all been navigable by boat, and when there is surplus water it is used for irrigation, so that the common people enjoy their benefits. Today that mound lies a mile or so (yi li xu) west of Guan County 灌縣, standing towering in the midst of the water, where it can be seen. For in the beginning, before the mound was cut through, the terrain below was blocked up, and the Mo River rushed and surged unpredictably beyond control, bringing harm to the inhabitants; whereas now it flows smoothly eastward, and the benefit of the water is widespread, so that in drought [?] one relies on it for irrigation, and in rain it does not overflow its course. Thus the record of it says: "Flood and drought follow human will, and people know nothing of famine." It refers to this. As for the Two Rivers, the Record of Shu (Shu zhi 蜀志) holds that one is the Wen River 汶江 and one is the Liu River 流江, which…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
經郡城南七里者即冰所穿耳宋郡縣志
謂一由永康過新繁入成都謂之外江一
由永康過郫入成都謂之內江者永康即
今灌縣而所用灌溉則曰灌曰溫曰郫曰
雙流曰崇慶曰成都凡一州七縣皆利之
天下謂之天府也蓋昔魏襄王爲羣臣祝
而曰令吾臣皆如西門豹之爲人臣也史
起進曰魏氏之行田也以百畝鄴獨二百
畝是田惡也漳水在其旁而豹不知用是
===
仁智未盡何足法也及起爲鄴令乃引漳
溉鄴以富魏之河內而民歌之以亮其智
豈少區區史起之見乎然亮初慕蜀之沃
野而身自爲相江水亡恙也獨不聞與羣
下謀鑿引以溉旁近田畝何也蓋沙河以
南其原野雖廣平可田畝而地高江下不
可引水即鑿之亦不得利故亮置弗爲坐
此耳蜀志有之蜀古蠶叢之國若曰地宜
蠶也所從來遠矣乃張詠則蜀賢守也先
punctuated: 經郡城南七里者，即冰所穿耳。宋《郡縣志》謂：「一由永康過新繁入成都，謂之外江；一由永康過郫入成都，謂之內江」者，永康即今灌縣，而所用灌溉，則曰灌、曰溫、曰郫、曰雙流、曰崇慶、曰成都，凡一州七縣皆利之，天下謂之天府也。蓋昔魏襄王爲羣臣祝而曰：「令吾臣皆如西門豹之爲人臣也。」史起進曰：「魏氏之行田也以百畝，鄴獨二百畝，是田惡也。漳水在其旁而豹不知用，是仁智未盡，何足法也？」及起爲鄴令，乃引漳溉鄴，以富魏之河內，而民歌之。以亮其智，豈少區區史起之見乎？然亮初慕蜀之沃野，而身自爲相，江水亡恙也，獨不聞與羣下謀鑿引以溉旁近田畝，何也？蓋沙河以南，其原野雖廣平可田畝，而地高江下，不可引水，即鑿之亦不得利，故亮置弗爲，坐此耳。《蜀志》有之：「蜀，古蠶叢之國。」若曰地宜蠶也，所從來遠矣。乃張詠則蜀賢守也，先
translation_en:
…that passes seven li south of the prefectural city is none other than what Bing excavated. The Song-dynasty Treatise on Commandery and County (Junxian zhi) states: "One flows from Yongkang past Xinfan and enters Chengdu, and is called the Outer River; one flows from Yongkang past Pi and enters Chengdu, and is called the Inner River." Yongkang is the present-day Guan County, and the places that use them for irrigation are Guan, Wen [Wenjiang], Pi, Shuangliu, Chongqing, and Chengdu—in all, one subprefecture and seven counties [note: six named here, though Chengdu had two attached counties, Chengdu and Huayang] derive benefit from them, and the empire calls this the Storehouse of Heaven.

In antiquity, King Xiang of Wei offered a toast to his assembled officials and said, "May my ministers all be like Ximen Bao in their service as ministers!" Shi Qi stepped forward and said, "In the house of Wei, land is allotted by the hundred mu, yet in Ye alone it is by two hundred mu; this is because the soil is poor. The Zhang River lies right beside it, yet Bao did not know how to make use of it. This shows his benevolence and wisdom were not complete—how is he worthy of emulation?" When Qi became Magistrate of Ye, he channeled the Zhang River to irrigate Ye, thereby enriching the Henei region of Wei, and the people sang his praises.

Given the wisdom of Liang [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮], how could he have lacked the paltry insight of a Shi Qi? Yet although Liang at first admired the fertile plains of Shu, when he himself served as Chancellor and the river waters were intact, we alone do not hear of him consulting with his subordinates to excavate channels and draw water to irrigate the nearby fields—why was this? It was because south of the Sha River, although the plains are broad, level, and suitable for farming, the land is high and the river is low, so water cannot be drawn up; even if one excavated channels, no benefit could be gained. That Liang left it alone and did not attempt it was simply on account of this.

The Record of Shu (Shu zhi) has it: "Shu is the ancient state of Cancong." This is as much as to say that the land is suited to sericulture, and that this has been the case since remote antiquity. Now Zhang Yong 張詠 was a worthy Prefect of Shu. Earlier…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
是知鄂州時旣以敎民拔茶植桑矣而至
爲蜀宋史第稱其減鹽價以足軍餉督驕
將以討叛賊吏不伏辜出斬之民苦饑豫
折米以待之而獨不聞其勸民植桑豈詠
不知蜀地宜桑而不以鄂治耶特以于時
四郊多壘桑株悉膏釜爨不可復植或蠶
桑故業民自利爲之不煩督勸云耳乃今
保寧諸縣則家植桑而入飼蠶其絲絁綾
絹旣用以自衣被而其餘且以貨諸他郡
===
利云厚矣而錦官以南千里而無一桑株
何也是未必皆出於避稅或者由惰農廢
業又無所督勸之故至于今而無復占是
業耳乃執事又謂欲用史起智而鑿山引
水灌漑沙河以南之田申張詠見而勸民
植桑脩復蠶叢以來之業意柔桑厚也其
爲蜀家入計生產殷矣而愚則以爲江水
不可引也陂塘獨不可鑿乎民稅可避也
蠶桑獨可廢乎有如鑿塘一畝深一丈可
punctuated: 是知鄂州時，旣以敎民拔茶植桑矣。而至爲蜀，《宋史》第稱其減鹽價以足軍餉，督驕將以討叛賊，吏不伏辜出斬之，民苦饑豫折米以待之，而獨不聞其勸民植桑。豈詠不知蜀地宜桑，而不以鄂治耶？特以于時四郊多壘，桑株悉膏釜爨，不可復植；或蠶桑故業，民自利爲之，不煩督勸云耳。乃今保寧諸縣，則家植桑而入飼蠶，其絲絁綾絹，旣用以自衣被，而其餘且以貨諸他郡，利云厚矣。而錦官以南，千里而無一桑株，何也？是未必皆出於避稅，或者由惰農廢業，又無所督勸之故，至于今而無復占是業耳。乃執事又謂欲用史起智，而鑿山引水，灌漑沙河以南之田；申張詠見，而勸民植桑，脩復蠶叢以來之業。意柔桑厚也，其爲蜀家入計生產殷矣。而愚則以爲江水不可引也，陂塘獨不可鑿乎？民稅可避也，蠶桑獨可廢乎？有如鑿塘一畝，深一丈，可
translation_en: … Prior to this, when he governed Ezhou, he had already taught the people to uproot tea bushes and plant mulberry trees. Yet when he came to govern Shu, the History of the Song (Songshi) merely praises him for lowering salt prices to suffice military provisions, supervising arrogant generals to suppress rebel bandits, bringing out and executing subofficial functionaries who refused to admit their guilt, and converting tax obligations into rice in advance to relieve the people when they suffered from famine—while uniquely making no mention of his encouraging the people to plant mulberries. Could it be that Zhang Yong did not know the land of Shu was suited for mulberries, and thus did not govern it as he did Ezhou? It was simply because at that time the surrounding countryside was full of military fortifications and the mulberry trees had all fed the cooking pots as firewood and could not be replanted; or perhaps sericulture was an old occupation that the people engaged in for their own profit, requiring no supervision or encouragement. Now, in the various counties of Baoning, every household plants mulberries and raises silkworms indoors [? 入, likely a misprint for 人 "everyone"]. Their fine silk, coarse silk, damask, and tabby are not only used to clothe themselves, but the surplus is even sold to other commanderies, yielding substantial profits indeed. Yet south of Jinguan [Chengdu], for a thousand li there is not a single mulberry tree—why is this? This does not necessarily all stem from evading taxes; perhaps it is because lazy farmers abandoned the occupation and there was no one to supervise or encourage them, so that down to the present day no one engages in this trade anymore. Now, Your Excellency further states that you wish to employ the wisdom of Shi Qi to cut through mountains and channel water to irrigate the fields south of the Sha River, and to extend the insight of Zhang Yong to encourage the people to plant mulberries and restore the occupation passed down since Cancong. Your intention toward the tender mulberries is generous [? 意柔桑厚, likely a misprint for 意甚厚 "your intention is most generous"], and your concern for the household income and livelihood of the people of Shu is profound. However, I foolishly consider that even if the river water cannot be channeled, can reservoirs and ponds alone not be dug? Even if taxes on the people might be evaded, should sericulture alone be abandoned? Suppose one digs a pond of one mu to a depth of one zhang; it can…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
溉田十畝鑿塘百畝深一丈可溉田千畝
則自沙河以抵龍泉皆沃壤也如是行之
數年而陂塘之利不與一州七縣相埒吾
不信也植桑十株可供一女之蠶植桑百
株可供十女之蠶則自錦官以及戎渝皆
桑陌也如是行之數年而蠶桑之利不與
保寧諸縣相等吾不信也古人有云民不
可與慮始而可與樂成在事者誠計在必
行行矣而遲之歲月疏之鑿之而惰不鑿
===
者與鑿不深者從而法加焉督之勸之而
惰不植者與植不勤者從而罰及焉而又
時其疾苦毋苛責其稅則於與是二利若
承蜩而掇之也筦子曰倉廩實而知禮節
如是行之十年而教化不成風俗不美盜
不息奸不止而閭閻無揖讓之風吾又不
信也不佞生于窮巷之中愚陋無以經世
務乃承下詢以鄉土之利敬述所聞於長
老者以進若其權衡便宜之法是在執事
punctuated: 溉田十畝，鑿塘百畝、深一丈，可溉田千畝，則自沙河以抵龍泉皆沃壤也。如是行之數年，而陂塘之利不與一州七縣相埒，吾不信也。植桑十株，可供一女之蠶；植桑百株，可供十女之蠶，則自錦官以及戎、渝皆桑陌也。如是行之數年，而蠶桑之利不與保寧諸縣相等，吾不信也。古人有云：「民不可與慮始，而可與樂成。」在事者誠計在必行，行矣而遲之歲月，疏之鑿之，而惰不鑿者與鑿不深者，從而法加焉；督之勸之，而惰不植者與植不勤者，從而罰及焉。而又時其疾苦，毋苛責其稅，則於與是二利，若承蜩而掇之也。筦子曰：「倉廩實而知禮節。」如是行之十年，而教化不成，風俗不美，盜不息，奸不止，而閭閻無揖讓之風，吾又不信也。不佞生于窮巷之中，愚陋無以經世務，乃承下詢以鄉土之利，敬述所聞於長老者以進。若其權衡便宜之法，是在執事
translation_en: …irrigate ten mu of fields; if one digs a hundred mu of ponds to a depth of one zhang, it can irrigate a thousand mu of fields. Then from Shahe all the way to Longquan, all will be fertile soil. If this is practiced in such a manner for several years, and the benefits of reservoirs and ponds do not equal those of the one subprefecture and seven counties, I would not believe it. If one plants ten mulberry trees, they can supply silkworms for one woman; if one plants a hundred mulberry trees, they can supply silkworms for ten women. Then from Jinguan (Chengdu) all the way to Rong (Xuzhou) and Yu (Chongqing), all the paths will be lined with mulberries. If this is practiced in such a manner for several years, and the benefits of sericulture and mulberries do not match those of the various counties of Baoning, I would not believe it. The ancients had a saying: "The people cannot be consulted when planning a beginning, but one can rejoice with them in the completion." If those in authority truly resolve that it must be carried out—carrying it out while allowing years and months for it to take effect—dredging and digging, and applying the law to those who are lazy and do not dig or who do not dig deeply; supervising and encouraging them, and visiting punishment upon those who are lazy and do not plant or who do not plant diligently; and furthermore, attending seasonably to their hardships and not harshly demanding taxes from them—then as for promoting [reading 與 as 興?] these two benefits, it will be like catching cicadas on a pole and picking them up. Master Guan (Guanzi) said: "When the granaries are full, people know ritual and moderation." If this is practiced in such a manner for ten years, and yet moral transformation is not achieved, customs do not become fine, banditry does not cease, wickedness does not stop, and the village lanes lack an atmosphere of courteous yielding, once again I would not believe it. Unworthy as I am, born in an impoverished lane, ignorant and rustic with no means to manage affairs of state, yet having received your gracious inquiry regarding the benefits of our local land, I respectfully recount what I have heard from the elders to present to you. As for the methods of weighing what is expedient and appropriate, that rests with Your Excellency…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text: 者矣是在執事者矣
punctuated: 者矣，是在執事者矣。
translation_en: … authorities; it rests with the authorities.

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試錄後序
甞觀左太冲之賦蜀都也曰
江漢炳靈世載其英則以長
卿子雲爲稱最初甚壯之旣
而竊疑焉夫蜀岷山之精下
蟠坤維上應井絡峙劒閣而
包玉壘帶二江而阻峩眉欝
===
乎萃川岳之神秀矣其間沃
野千里蔚爲奥區瓌奇紛綸
不可勝紀所謂陸海天府豈
虚哉信推地靈人傑而論宜
以才藪聞舊矣顧志記蠶叢
魚鳧以來僻陋未除肇儒雅
繇文翁始漢已前惟尹吉甫
punctuated:
四川鄉試錄後序

甞觀左太冲之賦《蜀都》也，曰：「江漢炳靈，世載其英。」則以長卿、子雲爲稱最。初甚壯之，旣而竊疑焉。夫蜀，岷山之精，下蟠坤維，上應井絡，峙劒閣而包玉壘，帶二江而阻峩眉，欝乎萃川岳之神秀矣。其間沃野千里，蔚爲奥區，瓌奇紛綸，不可勝紀。所謂陸海、天府，豈虚哉？信推地靈人傑而論，宜以才藪聞舊矣。顧志記蠶叢、魚鳧以來，僻陋未除，肇儒雅繇文翁始。漢已前惟尹吉甫
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

I once read Zuo Taichong's [Zuo Si 左思] rhapsody on the "Shu Capital" (Shu du), which says: "The Jiang and Han rivers shine with numinous power, and generation after generation bears forth their finest talents"—and he singled out Changqing [Sima Xiangru 司馬相如] and Ziyun [Yang Xiong 揚雄] as the foremost among them. At first I found this grand and stirring, yet later I came to harbor doubts about it. Now Shu is the essence of the Min Mountains: below, it coils around the Kun corner of the earth; above, it corresponds to the Well constellation (Jingluo). It rears up Jian'ge [Sword Gate] and encompasses Yulei [Jade Rampart], is girdled by the Two Rivers and guarded by Mount Emei—how luxuriantly it gathers the sacred beauty of rivers and mountains! Within it lie a thousand li of fertile plains, flourishing as a richly favored heartland, where rare wonders and abundant treasures are too numerous to record. When it is called an "inland sea" (luhai) and a "storehouse of Heaven" (tianfu), how could that be empty praise? Truly, if we reason from the principle that numinous terrain produces outstanding men, it ought to have been renowned as a gathering place of talent since antiquity. Yet the local gazetteers and records note that from the times of Cancong 蠶叢 and Yufu 魚鳧 onward, its rustic isolation had not been dispelled, and the inauguration of Confucian refinement began only with Wen Weng 文翁. Prior to the Han dynasty, only Yin Jifu 尹吉甫…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
挺生其鄉爲百代冠吉甫之
外不概見何耶左生詞人也
則奚怪乎第詡楊馬云爾嗣
是而子昂太白以風雅鳴於
唐要亦馬楊之流亞焉至宋
有眉山三蘇華陽諸范漢州
二張德業風猷差足爲蜀重
===
蓋人才之難如此於鑠
明興大化湛釀人文旁洽以蜀
居寰宇西南陲至遐遜矣
神聖在上執粹精愷悌之惪照臨
而覆露之若近郊然故自蹇
忠定而下科不乏人往往軼
蘇駕范㳽苐於吉甫甚盛斯
punctuated: 挺生其鄉，爲百代冠。吉甫之外不概見，何耶？左生詞人也，則奚怪乎第詡楊、馬云爾。嗣是而子昂、太白以風雅鳴於唐，要亦馬、楊之流亞焉。至宋有眉山三蘇、華陽諸范、漢州二張，德業風猷，差足爲蜀重。蓋人才之難如此。於鑠明興，大化湛釀，人文旁洽。以蜀居寰宇西南陲，至遐遜矣，神聖在上，執粹精愷悌之惪，照臨而覆露之，若近郊然。故自蹇忠定而下，科不乏人，往往軼蘇駕范，㳽苐於吉甫，甚盛。斯
translation_en:
… stood forth from this homeland as the crown of a hundred generations. Yet apart from Jifu, others are scarcely seen—why is that? Master Zuo [Zuo Si 左思] was a writer of belles-lettres, so what wonder is it that he merely boasted of Yang [Yang Xiong 揚雄] and Ma [Sima Xiangru 司馬相如] and left it at that? Thereafter, Zi'ang [Chen Zi'ang 陳子昂] and Taibai [Li Bai 李白] won renown for their poetic elegance in the Tang dynasty, yet in essence they too were of the same ilk as Ma and Yang. Down to the Song dynasty, there were the Three Sus of Meishan [Su Xun 蘇洵, Su Shi 蘇軾, and Su轍 Su Zhe], the various Fans of Huayang [such as Fan Zhen 范鎮 and Fan Zuyu 范祖禹], and the Two Zhangs of Hanzhou [Zhang Shi 張栻 and Zhang杓 Zhang Biao], whose moral achievements and illustrious statesmanship were just sufficient to bring weight to Shu [Sichuan]. Such, indeed, is the difficulty of producing men of talent!

Oh, how glorious is the rise of the Ming! Its great transforming influence has deeply steeped the realm, and cultural refinement has spread far and wide. Although Shu lies in the southwestern borderlands of the empire, at a most remote distance, the sacred Emperors on high, holding fast to pure, refined, and benevolent virtue, have shone upon it and sheltered it with their nourishing dew as though it were the immediate suburbs of the capital. Thus, from Jian Zhongding [Jian Yi 蹇義] onward, the examination rosters have never lacked for men; time and again they have surpassed the Sus, outstripped the Fans, and ranked as peers right next to Jifu in great abundance. Thus…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
其才不啻爲蜀重而蜀才且
重天下詎非
久道郅隆雲蒸霞變遂卓犖特
抗於在昔與迺說者以爲嘉
隆之際文勝綦焉物盛則返
固其理也我
皇上睿明獨運洞燭化機曩取
===
功令申飭之挽頹風以還之大
雅一時翕然丕變於文質相
扶可謂近之矣間有曲學之
士務巧發奇中刻削纖新失
則詭庸者效之虛薄益甚失
則浮浮詭之習傷乎雅道安
在其爲士也頃
punctuated: 其才不啻爲蜀重，而蜀才且重天下。詎非久道郅隆，雲蒸霞變，遂卓犖特抗於在昔與？迺說者以爲嘉隆之際，文勝綦焉，物盛則返，固其理也。我皇上睿明獨運，洞燭化機，曩取功令申飭之，挽頹風以還之大雅。一時翕然丕變，於文質相扶，可謂近之矣。間有曲學之士，務巧發奇中，刻削纖新，失則詭；庸者效之，虛薄益甚，失則浮。浮詭之習，傷乎雅道，安在其爲士也？頃
translation_en: …their talents have not merely brought prestige to Shu, for the talents of Shu have moreover brought prestige to the entire realm. Is this not because the enduring Way has reached supreme flourishing—rising like clouds and transforming like rosy mist—so that they stand out brilliantly and surpass those of former times? Yet commentators hold that during the transition between the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) reigns, literary embellishment reached an extreme; when things reach their peak, they inevitably revert—such is inherently the principle of things. Our August Emperor, exercising his sagely intelligence alone and penetratingly illuminating the mechanisms of transformation, previously took the examination regulations and reiterated their strict enforcement, turning back decadent trends to restore them to great elegance. All at once, there was a harmonious and grand transformation, which may well be called close to a mutual balance of refinement and substance. Occasionally, however, there have been scholars of crooked learning who strive for clever outbursts and surprise hits, carving and whittling away in pursuit of petty novelty, whose failing is perversity; mediocre men imitate them, becoming ever more hollow and superficial, whose failing is浮 frivolity. Habits of frivolity and perversity injure the Way of elegance—how then can such men be considered scholars? Recently, …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
上復用廷臣議
深詔所司取士以浮詭爲戒有不
如式者雖籍
奏禮官必察而
請黜之竝坐主者於是〔震亨〕聞
命稟稟殫夙夜之力閱諸士所爲
文浮者斥詭者亟斥其必實
且正也而後收焉猶懼其未
也從而紬繹焉則皆尊用先
聖之術曉暢當世之務侃侃
===
有經天下之氣寓焉夫
國家所託財器職業者粹於羣
下也今兹求士固將有以用
之自是與計偕對
punctuated: 上復用廷臣議，深詔所司：取士以浮詭爲戒，有不如式者，雖籍奏，禮官必察而請黜之，竝坐主者。於是〔震亨〕聞命稟稟，殫夙夜之力，閱諸士所爲文，浮者斥，詭者亟斥，其必實且正也而後收焉。猶懼其未也，從而紬繹焉，則皆尊用先聖之術，曉暢當世之務，侃侃有經天下之氣寓焉。夫國家所託財器、職業者，粹於羣下也。今兹求士，固將有以用之。自是與計偕，對
translation_en: … His Majesty again adopted the counsel of his court officials and issued a solemn decree to the competent authorities that in selecting scholars they must guard against superficiality and eccentricity; if there are any whose essays do not conform to the prescribed standards, even after their names have been registered and memorialized to the throne, the officials of the Ministry of Rites must investigate and request their dismissal, while also holding the examiners culpable. Thereupon, hearing this command with reverent trepidation, I, Zhenheng 〔震亨〕, exhausted my strength day and night in reviewing the essays composed by the candidates: those that were superficial I rejected, those that were eccentric I promptly rejected, and only when they were assuredly substantive and orthodox did I accept them. Still fearing that this was not enough, I proceeded to examine and draw out their deeper threads, and found that they all revered and applied the teachings of the former sages, clearly understood the affairs of the present age, and carried within them a forthright spirit capable of ordering the realm. Now, the talents, instruments, and official duties upon which the state relies are gathered in their purest form among its various subjects below. In seeking out scholars at this time, the state assuredly intends to put them to use. From here they will travel with the tribute reports to the capital, reply at …

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
大廷服官而受事迹其所自獻足
以爲效矣異日者果用之而
效則上之以楨幹
邦國不顓於楩枏豫章干霄之
材次之以衣被海內不顓於
煒燁璀璨濯江之錦又次之
以兼濟生民不顓於金莖瑶
===
草丹英碧實藥籠之良遺大
投艱歷險致遠無施而不可
如度雲棧瞿塘三峽之隘九
折之坂靡殊康衢衽席焉何
則所見者實所趨者正也此
眞方聞之士出入不悖其學
其眎爾鄉先達所以追往喆
alt_text:
大廷服官而受事迹其所自獻足
以爲效矣異日者果用之而
效則上之以楨幹
邦國不顓於楩柟豫章千霄之
材次之以衣被海内不顓於
煒燁燿爍濯江之錦又次之
以兼濟生民不顓於金莖瑤
===
草丹英�villain
大廷服官而受事迹其所自獻足
以爲效矣異日者果用之而
效則上之以楨幹
邦國不顓於楩柟豫章千霄之
材次之以衣被海内不顓於
煒燁燿爍濯江之錦又次之
以兼濟生民不顓於金莖瑤
===
草丹英珺實藥籠之良遺大
投艱歷險致遠無施而不可
如度雲棧瞿塘三峽之隘九
折之坂靡殊康衢袵席焉何
則所見者實所趨者正也此
眞方聞之士出入不悖其學
其睎爾鄉先達所以追往喆
punctuated: 大廷，服官而受事，迹其所自獻，足以爲效矣。異日者，果用之而效，則上之以楨幹邦國，不顓於楩枏、豫章干霄之材；次之以衣被海內，不顓於煒燁、璀璨濯江之錦；又次之以兼濟生民，不顓於金莖、瑶草、丹英、碧實藥籠之良。遺大投艱，歷險致遠，無施而不可，如度雲棧、瞿塘三峽之隘、九折之坂，靡殊康衢衽席焉。何則？所見者實，所趨者正也。此眞方聞之士，出入不悖其學，其眎爾鄉先達所以追往喆、
translation_en: …in the Great Court, assume office, and take up their duties; judging from what they have presented of themselves, it is sufficient to prove effective. In future days, if they are indeed employed and prove effective, then at the highest level they will serve as the pillars and framework of the state, not leaving that role exclusively to the sky-piercing timber of piannan and camphor trees; at the next level they will clothe and benefit all within the seas, not leaving that role exclusively to the brilliant, resplendent brocades washed in the Jiang; and at the level after that they will bring wide relief to the common people, not leaving that role exclusively to the fine medicines of golden stems, jade herbs, cinnabar blossoms, and azure fruits in the apothecary's basket. Entrusted with great responsibilities and cast into difficult tasks, traversing dangers and reaching distant places, there is nothing to which they cannot be applied—crossing the cloud-high plank roads, the narrows of Qutang and the Three Gorges, or the Nine-Turn Slope will be no different to them than a broad thoroughfare or a sleeping mat. Why is this? Because what they perceive is substantial, and what they pursue is orthodox. These are truly scholars of uprightness and learning, whose conduct at home and abroad does not contradict their study. Compared with the way the former worthies of your native region emulated the sages of the past…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
重
本朝者庶幾爲無愧豈與夫雕
蟲小技夸靡不經蘄馳愚耀
衆好奇爲名高者埒哉彼左
賦所揚搉曷足偉焉抑〔震亨〕
聞之口能言身能行國寶也
口不能言身能行國器也口
===
粲於言而身盭於行國蠹也
王者敬其寶愛其器而棄其
蠹脫或諸士不浮於言矣而
乃浮於行事不詭於言矣而
乃詭於心術萬有一焉出其
中是蠹之鄆也無論見棄爲
主者累如大負
punctuated: 重本朝者，庶幾爲無愧！豈與夫雕蟲小技、夸靡不經，蘄馳愚耀衆、好奇爲名高者埒哉？彼左賦所揚搉，曷足偉焉！抑〔震亨〕聞之：口能言、身能行，國寶也；口不能言、身能行，國器也；口粲於言而身盭於行，國蠹也。王者敬其寶，愛其器，而棄其蠹。脫或諸士不浮於言矣，而乃浮於行事；不詭於言矣，而乃詭於心術，萬有一焉出其中，是蠹之鄆也。無論見棄，爲主者累，如大負
translation_en: … bring weight to our reigning dynasty, one may well feel no shame! How could they be placed on a par with those who practice the petty craft of carving insects—boastful, extravagant, and uncanonical—seeking to dazzle the foolish and show off to the crowd, indulging in curiosities for the sake of a lofty reputation? As for what Zuo Si’s rhapsody lauded and assessed, how is that worthy of being considered great? Furthermore, I, [Zhenheng], have heard it said: he whose mouth can speak and whose person can act is a treasure of the state; he whose mouth cannot speak yet whose person can act is an instrument of the state; he whose mouth is brilliant in speech yet whose person is perverse in conduct is a pest of the state. A true king reveres his treasures, cherishes his instruments, and discards his pests. Should it happen that you gentlemen are not superficial in your words, yet are superficial in your deeds; are not deceitful in your words, yet are deceitful in the intentions of your mind—if even one in ten thousand among you turns out so, that would be the worst of pests [?]. Not to mention being discarded and becoming a burden to the examiners, what of gravely failing…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
清時何吾恐井絡貽譏坤維蒙誚
即蠶叢魚鳧僻陋之氓無可
與比數矣切爲諸士恥之夫
蜀才奇麗率類其山川麗如
長卿奇如子雲故古今所忻
豔者則蜀之所少非文也至
考兩人素行大節均無足道
===
使繩以
當代濂程縱甚麗而奇必且置浮
詭之列今諸士審能行脩節
立無寧文采愧之爾或謂文
行判久矣自漢不能必揚馬
今必之諸士乎然〔震亨〕知諸
士必不爾也人亦有言人心
punctuated: 清時何？吾恐井絡貽譏，坤維蒙誚，即蠶叢、魚鳧僻陋之氓，無可與比數矣。切爲諸士恥之。夫蜀才奇麗，率類其山川，麗如長卿，奇如子雲，故古今所忻豔者，則蜀之所少非文也。至考兩人素行大節，均無足道；使繩以當代濂、程，縱甚麗而奇，必且置浮詭之列。今諸士審能行脩節立，無寧文采愧之爾。或謂文行判久矣，自漢不能必揚、馬，今必之諸士乎？然〔震亨〕知諸士必不爾也。人亦有言：「人心
translation_en: … this era of clarity? I fear it would bring ridicule upon the region of Jingluo [Sichuan] and incur reproach across the Southwest; even the rustic folk of the ages of Cancong and Yufu would be beyond comparison with them. I would feel deeply ashamed on behalf of you scholars. Now, the talents of Shu [Sichuan] are marvelous and resplendent, generally resembling its mountains and rivers. Resplendent like Changqing [Sima Xiangru 司馬相如] and marvelous like Ziyun [Yang Xiong 揚雄], they have been admired and envied both past and present—thus what Shu lacks is not literary brilliance. Yet when one examines the everyday conduct and fundamental moral integrity of those two men, neither is worth mentioning. If measured by the standards of the contemporary masters of Lianxi [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤] and the Cheng brothers [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] [or: by our present dynasty's statutory standards of selection], even though their writings were exceedingly resplendent and marvelous, they would surely be placed in the ranks of the superficial and deceitful. Today, if you scholars can truly cultivate your conduct and establish your moral integrity, would it not be better even if your literary brilliance fell short of theirs? Someone might say that literary skill and moral conduct have long been separated: since the Han dynasty could not demand both of Yang Xiong and Sima Xiangru, can we demand it of the scholars of today? Yet I, Zhenheng, know that you scholars will certainly not be like that. People also have a saying: "The human heart…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
險於山川〔震亨〕獨明其非是
人固不易知豈其有險而如
山川也若其險如山川則人
之可信者尠矣是何其言之
不長厚乎而聖賢又何謂千
萬人之心即一人之心推一
心可以平天下乎蓋惟誠實
===
爲能成宇宙之事惟正大爲
能一天下之情故推一心可
以觀萬心者實也正也其不
易知者浮也詭也吾惟以實
且正待諸士而亦願諸士以
實且正終身自期待諸士而
以實且正自期待即今日之
punctuated: 險於山川」，〔震亨〕獨明其非是。人固不易知，豈其有險而如山川也？若其險如山川，則人之可信者尠矣，是何其言之不長厚乎！而聖賢又何謂「千萬人之心即一人之心，推一心可以平天下」乎？蓋惟誠實爲能成宇宙之事，惟正大爲能一天下之情。故推一心可以觀萬心者，實也，正也；其不易知者，浮也，詭也。吾惟以實且正待諸士，而亦願諸士以實且正終身自期待。諸士而以實且正自期待，即今日之…
translation_en: …is more treacherous than mountains and rivers,” yet I, [Zhenheng], alone declare that this is not so. People are indeed not easy to know, but how could they be as treacherous as mountains and rivers? If they were as treacherous as mountains and rivers, then those who could be trusted would be few indeed—how ungenerous such words are! And why then did the sages and worthies say that “the minds of tens of millions of people are the mind of one person, and by extending a single mind one can bring peace to all under Heaven”? Indeed, only sincerity and substance can accomplish the affairs of the universe, and only uprightness and magnanimity can unify the sentiments of all under Heaven. Therefore, that by which one can extend a single mind to observe ten thousand minds is substance and uprightness; that which makes them not easy to know is superficiality and deceit. I treat you gentlemen solely with substance and uprightness, and I also wish that you gentlemen will expect substance and uprightness of yourselves throughout your lives. If you gentlemen expect substance and uprightness of yourselves, then today’s…

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
言不浮不詭者悉乎天下之
具也而吾以實且正待諸士
則業已知其不浮詭於言矣
夫焉得設山川之險之疑耶
震亨非託長者之言而稱之
誠仰見
訓辭深厚恩施甚美慮淺聞者不
===
能究宣敢對揚
聖天子之德意爲諸士勸諸士慎
之矣昔者子路盛服見孔子孔子
曰江出於岷山其始可以
濫觴及放而之津則難涉也
以其流愈濫故也今汝被服
盛顏色充天下且孰肯諫汝
punctuated: 言不浮、不詭者，悉乎天下之具也；而吾以實且正待諸士，則業已知其不浮詭於言矣，夫焉得設山川之險之疑耶？震亨非託長者之言而稱之，誠仰見訓辭深厚，恩施甚美，慮淺聞者不能究宣，敢對揚聖天子之德意，爲諸士勸，諸士慎之矣！昔者子路盛服見孔子，孔子曰：「江出於岷山，其始可以濫觴，及放而之津，則難涉也，以其流愈濫故也。今汝被服盛，顏色充，天下且孰肯諫汝？」
translation_en: …words that are neither superficial nor deceitful are altogether the instruments for bringing peace to the world; and since I treat you scholars with sincerity and uprightness, I already know from your words that you are neither superficial nor deceitful—how, then, could I harbor suspicions of hidden perils like those of mountains and rivers? I, Zhenheng, do not merely borrow the words of an elder in saying this. Truly, looking up and beholding that the imperial instructions are profound and generous and the bestowal of grace is exceedingly fine, yet fearing that those of shallow learning might not be able to fully fathom and proclaim them, I have ventured to extol the virtuous intent of the Sacred Son of Heaven as an exhortation to you scholars. Be mindful of this, scholars! In olden times, when Zilu (子路) wore splendid attire to see Confucius (孔子), Confucius said: "When the Yangtze River emerges from Mount Min (岷山), at its source it can barely float a goblet; but when it spreads out and reaches the ferries, it becomes difficult to ford, because its flow has grown ever more expansive. Now your attire is splendid and your countenance is full of self-satisfaction—who in the world will be willing to remonstrate with you?"

title: 萬曆十年四川鄉試錄
text:
嗟乎諸士之始進江漢之在
岷嶓也賴其未濫而易入也
故致戒儻諸士輒盛氣自負
罔念於震亨之言則涓涓者
波其無乃遽而爲沱潛乎哉
其又以人心爲不山川也諸
士愼之矣録旣成震亨宜有
===
言申末簡謹次其勸戒之詞
備書之
江西九江府彭澤縣儒學教
諭戴震亨謹序
punctuated:
嗟乎！諸士之始進，江漢之在岷嶓也；賴其未濫而易入也，故致戒。儻諸士輒盛氣自負，罔念於震亨之言，則涓涓者波，其無乃遽而爲沱潛乎哉？其又以人心爲不山川也？諸士愼之矣！録旣成，震亨宜有言申末簡，謹次其勸戒之詞，備書之。
江西九江府彭澤縣儒學教諭戴震亨謹序。
translation_en:
Alas! When the gentlemen first enter upon their careers, it is like the Yangtze and Han rivers at Mount Min and Mount Bo; relying on the fact that the waters have not yet overflowed and that counsel may easily enter, I therefore offer this admonition. Should the gentlemen immediately become arrogant and self-important, paying no heed to my—Zhenheng's—words, then will not that trickling stream suddenly swell into the diverging torrents of the Tuo and Qian? Or would they take the human heart to be less perilous than mountains and rivers [?]? May the gentlemen be cautious! Now that the record is completed, it is fitting that I, Zhenheng, contribute a word at the final leaves; I have respectfully arranged my words of encouragement and admonition, and written them down in full.

Respectfully prefaced by Dai Zhenheng 戴震亨, Instructor of the Confucian School of Pengze County, Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi.
